I took French Tart's advice and grilled some chevre to serve alongside and I was very, very happy.

Frenchie - you are a goddess.  I think this has just become my favourite rendition of the classic.  The creme fraiche made all the difference (thank the Lord for Carrefours!).  Dare I say I will be having these again tomorrow? ;-)

This was so good and really hit the spot.  Very light and fluffy.  I added way more cheddar, but I am a cheese-a-holic.  Would never have thought to add sage and rosemary to a cheese omelette but, you know, it worked fine!  Thanks.

I so wish I hadn't discovered this recipe...I always have everything on hand and can whip up a loaf at any given time...WHICH MEANS I CAN EAT A WHOLE LOAF OF BUTTERY, HERBY, SLIGHTLY CHEESY BREAD ANY TIME I WANT.  Syd is a bad, bad man with a good, good recipe. (sprinkled the loaf with a little fleur de sel once baked for additional salty crunch)

This is a classic.  I used couverture chocolate as we don't like milk chocolate.  Made on Saturday morning 10am, gone on Saturday morning 10:45am.  Anyone else have the Joe Dassin earworm?  'Tous les matins, il achete son p'tit pain au chocolat-ai-yi-yi-yi-yi...'  Thanks.
This was really good.  The olives added an interesting note to the whole blend and I really liked it.  A little tarter than what I'm used to in a salsa, but very refreshing.  Thanks.
Absolutely refreshing and so pretty!

OK, I have to say I used this as a 'base' recipe and took off from there...I added chopped olives and a bit of chipotle in adobo sauce to the salsa for more kick.  At table, I sprinkled a bit of grated jack cheese on top and some sliced green onion and cilantro for colour.  Served with guac, sour cream and mexican rice and we were mm..mmming all over the place.

Couldn't cook today - it was too hot.  This is a real heat-buster.  Used roquefort in place of the bleu and creme fraiche in place of the sour cream.  Fleur de sel was my salt of choice.  Everything else as is.  Delicious.

Too hot to cook here so I made a couple of salads.  I used a bag of mixed baby lettuce/spinach leaves for this to make it even easier.  Also used roquefort instead of brie and fleur de sel.  Deliciously cooling.

Love grilled bread!  I used the suggestion of half butter/half olive oil and melted 2 cloves of real garlic into it before brushing on the bread.  Added a little dried oregano for good measure.  This was so good!
This was a delicious 'beat-the-heat' recipe that we all enjoyed.  The herb blend was delightful.  Dare I say I spiked mine with a little vodka???

Very refreshing.  I had a big pitcher of lemonade I'd made yesterday (good deal on lemons at the Market) and I used this just now as a 'pick-me-up'.  Loved it.  Tart and sweet and the brandy really gives a nice hit.

This recipe is so much better than the sum of its parts - one of those simple things that are perfection.  I used creme fraiche in place of the sour cream and a combo of Grand Marnier/Cointreau/Triple Sec just to provide varied orange essence.  I had also zested one of the oranges and zapped that with the demerara sugar before sprinkling on top, so we got orange flavour to the max!

A really great 'meal' salad, that is hearty and satisfying with a good use of contest ingredients. My only issue (and thus the loss of one star) is with the cheese...the cheddar cheese in the salad and the blue cheese in the dressing were really too much of a good thing, with the blue basically obliterating the taste of the cheddar (the contest ingredient). A tasty dressing could have been devised without the blue and the calorie count would have been significantly lower - 100 calories lower per serving! I would also have liked a bit more onion for this amount of salad. Very much enjoyed this for lunch today, and I know I'll be making it again! Good work, chef!

This was a hearty, warming soup for a cold day.  I really enjoyed all the veg and my only change was the addition of fresh, homemade meatballs rather than frozen.  The only thing I didn't care for (and I could really taste it!) was the addition of the sugar.  I would leave that out completely next time - and I will make this soup a next time.  Great use of contest ingredients, chef, and a very good recipe for the season.  Good luck!

What a perfect little recipe!  I splurged and bought a can of soup (hard to find here in Greece and 4 Euros for one can!!!) but it was totally worth it.  The addition of the horseradish is what got me.  Just so good.  I'm going to be making this a lot this winter, but I'll make my own homemade tomato soup next time. ;-)  You have a winner here, chef.

My kids are nuts about smoothie (and mom secretly drinks what's left in the blender) and I'm glad I tried this one.  Used light greek yoghurt with a dash of vanilla extract and thyme honey.  Deiicious.
A delicious wake-up jolt to start my day!  Loved the spice in the coffee.

A delicious and really filling breakfast that the kids and I really enjoyed.  The flavours and textural contrasts are dynamite - crisp and creamy from the outer and inner parts of the potato, smoky/salt from the bacon and sweetness from the onion.  Thanks for a great start to our day!
Nice and sweet and refreshing.  Made the kid-friendly version tonight.

This was major yum!  Very easy to make and so fresh-tasting...a lot of bang for the buck, so to speak.  The horseradish and dill really made this special, imo, and this recipe will be a regular on our table from now on.
Made this to accompany chicken schnitzel.  Had lovely, homemade egg noodles.  Fast and simple, with the caraway adding nice flavour, crunch and contrast.  Thanks, Kitty. :-)
Very refreshing!  My kids loved drinking their juice at breakfast out of champagne flutes.LOL
OK - great new healthy snack idea for the kids - plus they loved making them!  Easy, tasty and healthy.  What's not to love?
Absolute indulgence - and I'm all for that.  Who needs that major coffee chain?  Thanks.
I made the apple variation of this sandwich for our lunch today and we all enjoyed it.  Thanks.
Major yum happening with this lassi!  Used Greek thyme honey, and maybe a little more cardamom.  Kids and I loved it!
Delicious - got the kids to make it for tired, old mom.  We all loved this treat.

Excellent.  Edamame have become widely available at the markets here in Athens and I'm glad as I love them.  This was a deliciously-easy recipe, with lots of different tastes and textures happening.  Thanks.
This was such a pretty colour and went down far too easily.  Love Midori.  Love coconut rum.  Love this drink!

Terrific!  I'll definitely be doing this a lot as I bought a 1 lb container of miso (didn't have a smaller size and, in Greece, when you find something you BUY it.LOL).  Loved the savoury/sweet element - everyone enjoyed this.  Thanks.
Lovely smell wafting through the kitchen as I toasted the spice blend and smells absolutely authentic.  Sprinkled a bit on my eggs this morning and will enjoy experimenting with it more.  Thanks.

Made this for lunch today and it was very tasty, indeed.  My only 'problem' with it was that 5 minutes wasn't long enough to get the diced potato tender.  Next time, I'll just nuke the potato a couple of minutes before adding it.  Thanks.
Really lovely salad - and so pretty!  All the flavours complemented each other perfectly.  I'll be sure to make this again.

We really enjoyed this for supper tonight.  I made the sauce up earlier in the day and just thinned it with a little water as it thickened up some in the fridge.  I would smear the paste on the chicken a couple of hours before grilling just to get it to penetrate the meat more.  The instructions were easy to follow and dinner was on the table in no time.  Served with Recipe #427781 and Recipe #228680 for a lovely meal.  Thanks.
The salad we all know and love.  I added far less vinegar as I find the juices released by the tomato are usually acidic enough.  Good recipe.
A simple recipe for a simple couscous that you can then add to in many different ways.  Thanks, ~Rita~.
This is just one of those perfect things - especially if you are lucky enough to have greek yoghurt and thyme honey.  We can eat it 24/7.

Always having a supply of (homemade) hamburger patties in the freezer, lunch was a breeze for this working mom today!  I took out the patties before I went to work, put together the topping while I was grilling the burgers, toasted the pitas and assembled.  Couldn't have been easier - or tastier.  The kids thought they were way cool (even in Greece we're traditionalists and I usually use buns for my burgers).  Thanks.

So refreshing - lovely, bright and aromatic.  My Syrian brother-in-law supplied me with the tamarind syrup and it was go from there.  Made up a pitcher and filled it with ice and had it with our dinner.  It's fruity, sweet, floral and VERY refreshing.  Thanks for such a great recipe!

Lovely and fresh and good for you!  I had cooked the barley the night before and bought a rotisserie chicken, so this recipe literally came together in minutes.  Everything was so good - filled you up without stuffing you up.  Thanks for a great recipe.
Made this up with a combination of sage and chamomile - stronger than I'd drink for hot tea.  Iced it and added a squeeze of fresh lemon juice - VERY NICE iced tea to beat the heat.  Thanks.
Lovely - nothing like fresh fruit, simply prepared - to round out a meal.  Used canned peaches as fresh aren't in season yet.  Thank you for posting.
Diced Greek Salad!  Served this with pita crisps as a snack - we all thought it was a great way to incoporate more fresh veg into a diet.  Thanks.
Loved this.  It tasted as beautifully as it looked.  The harissa gave it a nice spark cooled down by the bursts of sweet/sour from the pomegranate.  Delicious.  Thanks.
Being a big fan of rose-flavoured rahat loukoum, I was looking forward to trying this drink - it did not disappoint.  Pretty and refreshing and with that lovely rose flavour.
Made these sandwiches for dinner using pita bread.  Simply great.
Got DH to grill a couple of swordfish steaks and spooned this on top - delicious.  I'm going to try this on all kinds of fillets.  Salmon's next.  Thanks. :-)
We make various versions of this delicious salad all the time - love it!  The addition of min was most refreshing.  Thanks.
Loved this couscous - lots of great flavours happening here and I really liked the crunch of the pistachios.  Thanks for a great recipe.

Very different from the Baba Ghanoush I usually make as my recipe does not incorporate beans.  Having said that - this is a great version!  I did add literally 2 drops of liquid smoke as I like to give baba ghanoush a slightly smoky flavour (and my family has come to expect it).  Lovely.  Thanks.

The best way to showcase our fabulous Greek honey - with our rich, creamy, tangy yoghurt and fresh, seasonal fruit.  I used strawberries, fresh melon and banana and sprinkled some granola over for crunch.  We all loved this for breakfast.  Thanks.
This was so good!  A few drops of the orange blossom water and you have the world's best lemonade!  Never thought of doing this and so glad I saw this recipe.  Thanks.
Made for breakfast and we really liked it - the cheese sauce is really good!  Thanks for a great recipe.
Made for breakfast today and we all really liked it.  Strange-looking but tasty - the custardy-crust was really good.  Thanks.
Excellent version of the ham and cheese.  Used HP for the steak sauce.  Thanks.
Fabulous!  I'll have another - and make it a double!  This is just perfect and DH and I will definitely be making these often over the summer.  Thanks.

Sign me up amongst the lovers of this recipe.  Yes, it's simple and what does that mean?  The fish shines through with awesome flavour that hasn't been obscured by a gazillion ingredients.  The herb butter is simply fabulous on the salmon.  We are a family of salmon lovers and I will definitely make this recipe again soon.  Thanks!
Excellent dessert - loved the combo of the rich/creamy/tart curd and the fresh fruit.  Thanks.

Made to drink while watching Greece play Argentina in the World Cup.  Greece lost but these drinks are a winner!  So refreshing.  Didn't bother to measure out the gin - just eyeballed it generously. ;-)  Thanks.

Very nice bar - the walnuts in the crust added a nice texture and flavour.  I made half the pan with apricot preserves and half with raspberry jam, as I had both on hand.  I liked the apricot best, but the kids enjoyed the 'red side' more.  Thanks.

I've had these several times at various homes, but had never made them myself.  Very glad I followed your recipe as the instructions were excellent.  These do taste very much like apple pie.  Enclosing the apple filling is the hardest (and messiest) part.  What worked best for me was to pat out the dough - rather like a burger patty or round spoon in the filling, pinch shut and then reshape into a ball, very gently.  Thanks.
So refreshing - loved the raspberry flavour.  Thanks.

I made a virgin version of this drink for the kids at our Greece-Argentian World Cup bash.  Greece lost but this drink won the kids over - the non-alcoholic version that is.  To be fair to alli, I poured myself a glass and added a healthy shot of rum just to drink it Mary Poppings would - excellent!  Thanks.

This recipe was much easier to make than I thought it would be - the chicken didn't have a chance to really crisp up on both sides in 10 minutes so I had to bake a bit longer (more like 15) and for this reason, I expect, it was a little dry.  Next time, I'd increase the oven temperature to speed up crisping.  I only mixed in 1 tablespoon red curry paste into the coconut milk dipping sauce, and it was plenty hot for us.  I would have liked more contrast in flavour in the dip - maybe a squeeze of lime and a little palm sugar mixed in to get that sweet/salt/tart thing that is so good in thai recipes?  Thanks.
Lovely little morsels of oniony-cheesy-bacon goodness.  Easy to make, too.  Thanks.
Made these to munch on while watching Greece play Argentina in the World Cup.  No one's scored yet, but this recipe scored big with the family and 5 child guests.  Thanks!
Very nice fruit salad.  Pantry ingredients and ready in a flash.  Thanks.

Took a bit of licence with this recipe - used full-fat feta and regular tomatoes, which I didn't feel compromised the recipe any.  I don't know what Cavender's greek seasoning is, so I just used a pinch each of oregano and basil (a little more generous on the oregano) as well as salt and pepper.  The kids and I really enjoyed this wrap for our breakfast - tasty and filling and fast.  Thanks.
Made to accompany Recipe #230043.  Real vegetable goodness - and so easy.  I loved how all the flavours melted into one another.  Thanks.

Excellent!  Smooth and creamy and oh-so-cool.  I used 2% greek yoghurt instead of sour cream and we didn't miss the calories at all!  (Plus the tangy flavour was great with the raspberries)  I will be making this dessert several times over the summer - so glad I tried it!  Thanks.
All 3 kids gave 2 thumbs up (total = 6) to this delicious pancake - mom can't ask for more.  I only used a tablespoon of sugar in the actual pancake and we drizzled golden syrup over top.  Thanks!

This was too sweet for us and I would just cut out the sugar next time (plenty of sweetness happening from the balsamic, honey-roasted peanuts and raisins).  Used greek kasseri for the white cheese.  We all liked!  Thanks.

First thing - I loved that this made a little cake and that there were no leftovers left for mom to eat, secretly.  Secondly - outstanding flavour!  A little more work than I'm used to in a cake (I hate getting out the 2nd mixing bowl) but so good and worth it.  When cool, I split in half and we ate it like shortcake, with lightly sweetened whipped cream and raspberry preserves in the middle, and a dollop of each on top for decoration.  Thanks for such a good recipe!

We really enjoyed this and I'm so glad it came together so quickly, although I did cook a couple of minutes longer than stated to make sure the chicken was cooked through.  My kids really liked that it was so much noodle to broth, and we all thought it tasted great.  Thanks.
Nice and healthy variation of 'ordinary' scrambled eggs.  I used a banana pepper.  Thanks.

Basically, I came in to review with the same comments already made - overwhelming vinegar and onion flavour - so much so, that you really couldn't taste the goodness of the beans.  After being tried by my family, the beans were basically just pushed back and forth on the plate, and ended up being thrown out.  I think this recipe needs some 'fine-tuning', because as an idea, it really should work.  Thanks for trying!

Very tasty but WAY too sweet for our tastes.  The sugar could definitely be cut back (atleast for us) to 1/3 of a cup as it, with the rootbeer, add a whole lot of sugar to the overall flavour.  Otherwise, I liked all the other additions and felt they would have been able to shine better had they been allowed to come past the sweet.  I used this recipe to sauce some baked chicken pieces (both during baking and at the table).  Thank you, chef.
Very good and healthy-tasting.  I used a little sriracha paste instead of the chili and pepper.
Yum!  The whole family loved this salad.
Tasty and easy.  We all gobbled it up.  Thanks.
I made this only with the chimichurri sauce - which was excellent, so I can't comment on the pineapple aioli.  Served with Recipe #307686 and Recipe #456917 alongside for a delicious dinner.  Thanks.

So good...using the first batch of vine-ripened tomatoes I have bought this year and fresh basil and oregano from my little pots on the balcony.  I could tell this was going to be more onion than my family would want and so I cut it down to 1 cup, which was perfect, imo.  Thanks for a yummy, healthy recipe.  Made for Italy- ZWT7 ~ Gardening, Herbs, & Spices Forum Challenge.
Very easy to make and a tasty side to our dinner of Recipe #456709 and Recipe #456917.  Thanks.
I do enjoy a caipirosca.  This is a classic recipe and very refreshing.
So good!  Coffee and cinnamon are perfect together.  I did forego the whipped cream and just added some milk to mine.  Thanks.
This was so easy and delicious!  I have to say that I am a fan of anchovies and that's what drew me to this salad.  The combination was perfect.  Thanks for posting this.
I really enjoyed this recipe.  I used a combo of spinach and swiss chard as I needed to use up both.  The addition of peanut butter was so unusual for me, but worked!  Thanks.
This delicious pilaf has so much going for it - fruity-sweet, spicy, slightly tart in bites...it was a delight to eat.  Thanks.

I made this over the weekend to have on hand for when the kids got hungry (all the time, lately!).  The tenderloin was cooked for me in 6 hours in my slow-cooker and I shredded it into the sauce with 2 forks.  We used the meat to stuff flour tortillas and topped with a fresh mango salsa, cheese and greek yoghurt instead of sour cream.  Delicious.
This was SOOOOOOO good!  I left out the bacon and did not miss it a bit.  A keeper.
Spaghetti with a simple tomato sauce is my kids' favourite - and this version was very well-received today.  It is a classic.  Thanks.

I'm always looking for healthy, economical recipes to fill up my boys with (2 teens - basically bottomless pits).  I make a huge tub of hummus every couple of weeks that they eat in a variety of ways, and I'm so pleased to have discovered this recipe as it was quick to make and they really enjoyed it.  Served with pita crisps for healthy after-school snacking.  Thanks.

We all love this healthy and great-tasting dish!  My Syrian brother-in-law first introduced it to us (I believe he called it m'jedereh) and we've been enjoying it ever since.  Mike your version is just as good.  I added some cumin and allspice as well, and served with greek yoghurt on the sides.  For anyone who hasn't tried this recipe and is considering it - first of all, make it - it's delicious!  Secondly, yes, you really need all that onion. ;-)
This was a delicious, tangy and very fresh-tasting salad.  Finally got to use my can of hearts of palm.  Thanks.

Such a great flavour combination.  I heeded alligirl's advice and cut the amount of cayenne way back - which  was a good thing...about 3/4 tsp of cayenne was plenty spicy for my heat-challenged family.  Thanks.

A positively winning combination.  I love strawberries dressed with balsamic vinegar, but I would never have thought to pair them with roka - absolutely terrific!  Parmesan shavings added just the right touch of savoury saltiness to this salad.  Thanks!
Delicious and refreshing.  I used greek yoghurt flavoured with honey and vanilla and toasted, dessicated (dry) coconut.  Loved that this used pantry ingredients and was ready in minutes!
Yummy.  I added a little chopped gherkin, just because we always do to macaroni salads.  Also added more tuna to make it a 'main course' salad.  My whole family really liked this.
Yummy.  I used thin slices of a local, fouantre ham.  Can't beat a grilled cheese sandwich!
Oh my, this was so good!  Served with buttered, toast soldiers to dip into the egg and creamy-cheese mixture.
I haven't had a mai tai in forever and seriously regret not making them more often - this version is delicious - and not too sweet.
Delightful!  I used greek yoghurt and fresh strawberries and some frozen blueberries.  I had toasted almond flakes and used those.

I knew I couldn't go wrong with grilled cheese and tomato sandwiches for lunch and chose this recipe.  Simple and delicious - I used good, vine-ripened tomatoes.  Grilled longer than stated as we like our sandwiches more toasty.  Thanks.
Maybe one of the easiest sides I've ever made.  DH and I really enjoyed it, the kids said it was 'OK', but ate it (yay!).  Thanks.
I made the hot version of this late last night.  Ovaltine and peppermint schnapps...who'd have thought?LOL
Very refreshing.

Excellent!  Made for the gluten-free ZWT#7 challenge.  These can be made gluten-free by 1 1/2 cups gluten-free flour mix and adding 1/4 tsp xantham gum (if the flour mix doesn't already contain it).  Follow the recipe as is.
Excellent!
This delicious chocolate fondue was a bit of an investment - but you pay for the really good things in life!  Served with chunks of sponge-cake, banana and strawberries.  My family adores me.LOL
This was very good - everything complemented.
alli - my kids LOVE you!  I have been ordered to make this again - fast!
This is an excellent, spiced coffee.   Loved the cardamom.
This was delicious!  The kids thought the colour was 'weird' (well - it does have blueberries!) but we all enjoyed it.
This was really good, and a nice complement to a grilled flank steak I'd made.  I used a fresh red pepper.
I loved these fries!  They were spicy-hot and salty and sweet all at once, and a breeze to make.  Thanks - I'll be making these often.

My whole family really enjoyed this refreshing drink.  I bruised some fresh spearmint leaves and added them to my pitcher and allowed the citrusade to sit in the refrigerator for a couple of hours before I served it.  The mint really gave a fresh taste that complimented the citrus combination.

This was so good!  I also added some mirin to the broth - toppings were SPAM (dare I admit I always have a can in the cupboard?LOL), egg (just broke it on top and let it lightly cook), bok choy, green onions, peas, carrot julienne and some frozen cocktail shrimp.  We love soba noodles and this was fast, easy, and tasty.
I used frozen blackberries, raspberries and blueberries to make this delicious cobbler.  The biscuit topping was so good and the fruit juicy, but not runny.  Thanks.
Tasty and simple!
This was very good but missing a bit of acid, so I added a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

Excellent.  I call cheese crisps 'fricos' and I've never made them with swiss (emmentaler) before - good!  The spinach-apple combo was perfect with the vinaigrette.  Looked and tasted completely 'gourmet'.  Thanks.
This was the green 'side' to a traditional roast chicken dinner and it was superb in its simplicity.  Complemented everything, and good for you.
Delicious!
Very yummy and easy with good, clear instructions.  I was only allowed a nibble off one drumstick as the kids ate them all up.  Clearly, they know a good thing when they taste it.

I have to agree with the other reviewers that this tuna salad was just a bit too drippy for comfort, and my kids did have a couple of accidents while eating it.  On the plus side, it is extremely tasty and a good use of contest ingredients.  Good luck, chef.
Delicious - like a greek puttanesca (minus the anchovies).  So simple to make and so tasty!

This is a tasty main for lunch today.  The simple ingredients lend themselves to a bright flavour that don't mask the flavour of the fish.  I had swordfish filets in the freezer, so that's what I used. :-)

I scaled this down to 2 servings for breakfast today for my son and myself, but used more of the tomato, parsley and olives than the scaled-down version called for.  We served this wonderfully-flavourful eggs in whole-wheat pita breads for a 'greek burrito' breakfast.  Yummy!

The tenderloins, prepared as per Lori's excellent instructions, were juicy and flavourful, but what was really outstanding was the fantastic glaze the tenderloins get doused with!  Both sweet and spicy hot, and with the undertone of the bourbon (which does not overwhelm), we were licking our forks!  Thanks Lori!
Yum!  Really well-seasoned mushrooms.  Were served with 2 other grilled meats, tzatziki and greek salada for our most awesome meal so far this summer!

Like I really needed to see this recipe!  I scaled down to 1 serving because I recognized the evil intent behind it, which was a good thing because my son and I ate all 6 rashers in, maybe, 2 minutes?  Unbelievably good.  Unbelievably messy.  I took aforementioned advice and lined my pan with aluminum foil so that there wouldn't be any clean-up.

Jostlori recommended this recipe to me and I'm glad I tried it out as it's very easy to make, good and just a 'tad' different.  I made a half batch.  The residual heat left by the cayenne is a very nice addition to the chocolate sauce.
As I can't get cajun spice mix here, it was nice to have a recipe to make my own.  Have used it in a few dishes thus far.  Very good.

Iced coffee is called a 'frappe' here (there should be an accent on the 'e', but my keyboard won't do it!LOL).  I think a very lightly-flavoured honey is more appropriate to allow the coffee to star.  I used greek thyme honey, which did overpower the drink.  I do love my iced coffee in summer, and I appreciated the little 'trick' of using honey instead of sugar.

We love 'kolokithokeftedes' and this version is quite authentic.  I did add one small, finely-minced onion to the mixture.  The feta and mint make it uniquely greek and so good.  Also served with tzatziki to scoop on or dip into.

This time of year, I can get beautiful fresh grape leaves at the farmer's market which I just blanch and use, as I did for this recipe.  Very easy to make, and lovely spritzed with the fresh lemon.  Definitely a meze I'll make again.
Good and fresh - everything a salad should be.

This was a very unusual breakfast for us, but nonetheless delicious.  I did as some reviewers commented and actually chopped up the bacon I used for dripping into the cornbread couche couche (love the name!).  The hit of sweet with savoury was yummy.
I wish I'd found this recipe a few days ago, when this heatwave started - we'd be eating it 24/7!  So good.  The salty, sweet of feta and fruit is classic.  Love the dressing.
Perfectly refreshing and delicious.
Very good.  The batter for this cake is very stiff but it does bake up tender, with a fine crumb.  The lingonberries were a lovely sweet-sour touch.  Perfect with coffee.

What a good idea to pour the hot oil on the onion to get rid of the 'raw' taste - going to put that in my little book of tricks.  Having said that, this recipe is OMG delicious!  Even though I halved the recipe, I used the full amount of scotch bonnet asked for.  The mango takes this to a whole new level with the sweet element.  Served with pita chips.  Will have to make some more soon.

Ha!  Learn something new every day!  In Greece, we make the same sugar 'crema' for our hot nescafes.  I MUCH prefer it with espresso.  One really good shot after breakfast and I'm going to be zippy and happy all day long!
Delicious and refreshing.  The instructions don't mention when to add the salt.  Experience told me to salt the cucumber slices before weighting because the salt helps them release their water.

I have to agree with twissis in that 4 oz of smoked salmon is not enough for 4 sandwiches.  I scaled down to 2 and used that amount just for the 2 and it was perfect.  This really is a 'special' sandwich.  We all love our smoked salmon in this house and it was a treat to have it in this way with the havarti.  Thanks for a good recipe (but up the salmon ;-) ).
Sweet and sour is what I look for in a drink and this one satisfies.  Perfect for a hot summer's night.  Make sure you use lots of ice and a long glass.
Very tasty.  I spritzed my sandwich lightly with lemon before biting in as I love what lemon does to a rich, fatty fish like herring.
I do love daiquiris and this tropical rendition is fantastic.  Loved the fresh mango in it.

Scaled this back to 2 servings.  Someone else described this as an 'eggy crepe' and I think that says it very well.  Served with lingonberry preserves purchased at IKEA (needed an excuse to go shopping, I guess ;-) ).
Super!  Very nicely-spiced.
Looks so cool but tastes so HOT!  This was a great blend of flavours.
All-out delicious.  I should have made a double batch.
The combo of spicy-rich salami, havarti and cole slaw (I used Recipe #264522) was fantastic!

I used a local grape juice.  Like a previous reviewer, I felt the grape juice was already sweet enough and, though I only used half the amount of honey called for, felt it really didn't need any added sweetener.  Loved the additions of orange flower water and cinnamon.
This is very refreshing on a hot day - tart and sweet and slightly musky from the hibiscus.  Stunning colour, too.  I scaled down to 1 quart but upped the amount of ginger.  Thanks, alli!
Made this using greek coffee.  Very fragrant.  A 'special' way to begin the day.
Great and different way to make oatmeal.  My two oatmeal-loving-kids and I ate it up.
Really special.  Glad I made it.
Really wonderful way to do roasted potatoes.  The ras el hanout was the bomb!

Being a family of iced-tea lovers, this didn't last very long in our home (especially thanks to son #2 who drank most of it all by himself!).  I used Darjeeling.  I felt the flavours of the lemongrass and ginger really did make this a 'cut above' regular iced tea.  Good instructions.  We sweetened a bit with sugar.
Different and delicious salad.  There is something 'new' happening in your mouth with every bite, which makes it a lot of fun to eat.  Loved the Asian flavour profile.  Will make again.

This is delicious but I had to 'read' quite a bit into the recipe.  First of all, I made the coffee VERY strong.  I drink a lot of iced coffee (popular in hot Greece) and know that I have to make it triple-strength because, as soon as you add the ice, it becomes quite diluted.
