What a treat.  The combination is just wonderful.  I will cut back on the red peppers next time.  I made a little extra dressing with the remaining pineapple juice which I'm glad I did because I don't think it would have been enough with the original stated amount.  I also let this marinade for about an hour and the flavors really came through and the slaw was not soggy at all.  I may add some red onion to the mix next time.  Thanks so much for sharing.  Made for PRMR :)

This was a nice different chicken dish.  I didn't care for the blue cheese in this though and I like blue cheese.  I skipped the browning in the butter and baked this at 400 degrees for about 40 minutes, spraying with some cooking spray half way through.  Crisped up nicely.  Had to use a lot of toothpicks and had 3 balls of the cheese mixture left over.  My three chicken breasts were 26 oz.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for PRMR :)

Excellent.  Loved the mustard although I did decrease it to half.  I've made mashed potatoes with buttermilk before and I really like the flavor it adds.  Thanks so much for sharing.  Made for March Aussie Swap 2010  :)

Excellent spice blend that made a wonderful light tasting Italian dressing with the perfect blend of spices.  I made this up today to use on my salads at work this coming week.  Instead of the EVOO I used Canola Oil and Extra Virgin Olive Oil Blend that had Omega-3 DHA added which worked so well with this recipe and made it a little healthier for me.  I used Splenda as a sub for the sugar to lower the calories a little more.  Thanks so much for sharing.  Made for PRMR :)

Excellent.  Loved the tartness the apple brought to this recipe.  I even think some sweet fruit would work well in this like dried apricots or some raisins.  The variations are endless.  Really liked the addition of the bacon.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for Aussie Swap Spring 2010 :)

My first try at Edamame and I really enjoyed it.  Great for a snake.  I used 12 oz of frozen edamame, cooked for 5 minutes then cooled as instructed.  I cut the chili and garlic powder to 1 tbls each and that was plenty for us.  I'll make this one again.  Made for Photo Forum Special :)

This was a total surprise in the flavor that was produced with the combination of ingredients.  We loved it, although it really wasn't sticky :)  The chicken turned out very moist and juicy cooking it for about 35 minutes.  I left out the cumin per DH request but other than that made as witten.  Thanks Saturn for a great recipe that I'll make again.  Made for PAC Spring 2010 :)

We loved this as an afternoon snack.  The flavors were just excellent as written and I don't think I'll change a thing about it except maybe put more on each tortilla.  I used this with our homemade salsa.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for PAC Spring 2010 :)
Really enjoyed this for brunch this morning.  I made as directed except added some crushed red pepper flakes.  Made for PRMR :)

This was so very good and so easy to put together.  Some of my favorite flavors, although this was my first experience with bok choy.  Very nice and I'll use that again.  Thanks for a great recipe.  Made for ZWT #6 )
I love mushrooms and any type of Teriyaki marinade so I knew I would love this recipe.  The flavors were spot on.  Thanks so much for sharing.  Made for ZWT 6 :)
Excellent sticky rice, which is one of my favorites.  The method worked great.  Served this with recipe #405625 and it was perfect.  Thanks  Made for ZWT #6 :)

Such fresh flavors that we always enjoy.  Loved the addition of the sesame seeds.  I used kosher salt and increased the garlic a little.  I made the whole recipe and it was just enough for the two of us.  I splashed a little lemon on it just before serving.  As you say sometimes Andi, Yummers :)  Made for ZWT #6

This was very good and fairly easy to put together.  I increased the eggs by 1 (DH loves eggs) and added a little cheese towards the end of cooking, but other than that made as directed.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for ZWT #6 :)

These were pretty good but I thought the sauce in the filling was a little on the strong side.  I think next time I'll just use the Hoisin sauce.  I would have liked more veggies and a little less chichen also.  I used Egg Roll wraps because they are easier for me to work with.  I really liked the dipping sauce and would make more of that next time.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for ZWT #6 :)

Just excellent flavor for a good baked potato.  I used regular 2% milk as that is what I had and that seemed to work great.  Creamy cheesy and delightful.  I agree with CarrolJ that this would be great with leftover baked potatoes.  Thanks katew for sharing.  Made for ZWT :)

Very nice light cookie.  Loved the combination of coconut and chocolate along with the almonds.  Vanilla is stated in the directions but is not listed as an ingredient.  I used 1 tsp.  My cookies didn't flatten out very much.  Overall very nice.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for ZWT 6 :)
These were absolutely deliciious.  So light and fluffy.  The creme fraiche made this dish for us.  Thanks diner for sharing.  Made for ZWT 6 :)

These were very good but the dough seemed a little difficult to work with.  I added additional flour and that helped some.  The flavor was perfect with the use of additional onion powder.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for ZWT #6 :)
It is so hot here that this was just perfect to cool us down.  The flavors were perfect.  thanks for sharing.  Made for ZWT #6 :)

I don't drink a lot of scotch but that may change in the future.  This was a delicious after dinner drink.  I used 2% milk and didn't miss the extra calories.  I'll make this one again.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for ZWT #6 :)

I made this for lunch today and we really enjoyed it.  I cut the mayo down to about 2 tablespoons (I think 1/2 cup would be way too much) but other than that made as directed.  I used some homemade wheat bread and we got 2 sandwiches out of this.  Loved the lemon flavor.  Thanks for sharing this great recipe.  Will make this one again.  Made for PRMR :)

This was very good and so easy to put together.  I added some basil and red pepper flakes to the meat mixture and only 1 tsp of splenda because we don't like it too sweet.  As other did I also used extra cheeses.  I'll make this one again.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for WTTM Tag Game :)

The chipotle chiles in adobo added such a great addition to an all time favorite.  I used a light buttermilk ranch over chopped iceberg lettuce with the last of our chopped tomatoes from the garden and some bacon bites.  Just wonderful.  thanks so much for sharing.  Made for Holiday Tag game :)

This was a great side dish but I wanted a little more flavor.  I think the bread you choose will make a big difference in this recipe.  I used plain white bread.  I think I might add some garlic next time.  I halved the recipe and still had enough for 2-3 more servings.  I baked this at 350 degrees for 30 minutes and I think I'll bake it another 5 or 10 minutes to get a good set on the eggs next time.  This recipe has great potential for us.  thanks for sharing.  Made for PRMR :)

OMG This was just excellent.  All the flavors went so well together.  My chicken turned out very crisp, which we loved.  I also added a little more red pepper flakes, cut the salt to 1/4 tsp for personal preferences and cut the peas (which I used frozen peas) to about 1/4 cup and used 2 green onions.  Thanks so much for sharing.  Will make this again.  Made for PRMR :)
Just excellent and so easy to put together.  I would add some garlic to the recipe next time but other than that wouldn't change a thing.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for Australia/NZ Swap event.  :)

We really enjoyed this recipe for baked fish.  I made as directed as far as the ingrediants and it was a perfect combination and amount of breading for 5 small Tailpia fillets.  I baked my fish for 20 minutes at 375 degrees then turned the oven to broil to brown the top for about 2 -3 minutes.  Loved the lime juice as I usually use lemon.  Thanks so much for sharing another great recipe for fish.  Made for PRMR

These skewers were excellent.  The meat was so tender, although a little dry as I think I cut mine too thin.  Great little bite to the sauce.  I added some red onion pieces but other than that made as directed.  I'll probably make this into a meat and veggie combination next time for our summer grilling.  The flavor of the sauce will be very good on chicken too I think.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for PRMR

This was so simple and easy to put together.  I did season my chicken with some salt and pepper before browning and I used the chicken and mushroom combination of cream of soup which we really like.  I also used 2% milk in place of the water as a personal preference.  The Dijon mustard added a nice flavor that we enjoyed.  Served this over Jasmine rice along with corn on the cobb and a nice salad.  In memory of Pets "R" us.

Excellent flavor and loved the cooking method.  Especially the grilled red onion.  Excellent.  The chimichuri sauce is on the stong tasting side and a little goes a long way for us.  Thanks so much for sharing.  :)

Very good but I would have liked a little more flavor.  I think I might use Italian bread crumbs next time.  I didn't have zucchini so I substituted straight neck squash with very nice results.  Thanks for sharing.

I giving this a 5 star because of the success of all the others and my failed blender experience, which as of today has been retired.  The flavor combination I loved much more than my DH but I don't really count him in my reviews lol.  The dressing was a little thicker than I would have liked, but was not sure what to add to it to compliment the recipe.  I used this on a spinach salad with red onions, tomatoes, real bacon bits and some hard boiled eggs aling with an Onion Soup to make our Friday night dinner.  thanks Andi for sharing.  I'll make this one again.  :)  Made for the Diabetic Forum

We really enjoyed the flavors in this recipe (we love sage).  I too didn't know how to measure a handful of sage so took the recommendation of Nif and used about 20 leaves and that seemed to work well for us.  I used peanut oil to fry the steaks and that worked well for us.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for PRMR

Excellent burger.  I used chili powder instead of the curry (personal preference) and left off the pickled cucumbers as I didn't have any and made my own fried onions and we loved it.  This was an excellent burger.  thanks for sharing.

We enjoyed these as a snake yesterday.  I did use chili seasoning in place of the cumin and added a little red pepper flakes to spice this up some.  Topped this with some cheese dip and slices of avocado and we really enjoyed.  I also used rotisserie chicken which made for a quick snack.  Thanks.  Made for the diabetic tailgate forum.  :)

OMG this is so rich and so sweet.  I would cut back on the sugar next time.  Maybe because I used splenda sugar that it turned out so sweet.  I also used 2% milk to help with the calorie count.  I did not add any of the options as I didn't think it needed any.  Thanks.  Made for Fall PAC 2011.

Excellent.  I can't say enough about this recipe.  All the flavors blended so well together that I would not add anything other than a pinch of extra salt.  And it didn't turn brown which I loved.  I'll use this later tonight for my chicken fajitas but it was excellent with just chips.  Thanks so much for sharing this great make again recipe :)  Made for Fall 2011 PAC

This was just delicious, but I will cut back on the potatoes next time by about a third.  Loved the flavor that the cajun seasoning added to the mixture although made it a little salty for us.  This made a huge amount and filled a 9x13 pan and would serve 6-8 people in my family or more.  Very rich and filling.  Thanks for sharing Made for PRMR :)

This was good but the marinade combination did not go well for us.  So strong............I could not find sirloin steaks either so used NY strips and did not think the marinade added much to tenderizing the steaks (but could be our quality of steaks).   I marinaded my steaks for about 18 hours. As for the side of onions and mushrooms, we love that with any steak.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for PRMR

I had this at Outback last night and just knew I'd find a similar recipe here and I did with this recipe.  Just absolutely wonderful and full of flavor.  I actually liked this better because I used cheese that I love like Provolone and cheddar instead of the Monterey Jack.  I also used recipe #373680 for the Honey Mustard which is much better than Outback.  Thanks so much for sharing.  Will be making this one again.  Made for "Let's Party" 2011

This is the best Honey Mustard Dressing that I have ever tried or made.  My DH said a couple of weeks ago that he had the best HMD at a resturant that he went to but he said this was even better.  The combination and balance was just perfect.  Used this to make recipe #348008 and it was perfect.  Thanks so much for sharing.  I'll make this one again.  Made for "Let's Party" 2011

I made this recipe for the dressing so used spinach, tomatoes, red onion, eggs, zucchini, and bacon as the salad.  The dressing was very, very tart so I added a tsp of splenda to try to mellow out the flavors and that worked somewhat but still very tart.  My dressing didn't get as thick as Andi's photo showed and didn't really stick to my salad.  I'll play with this one as I liked the base recipe.  Thanks Annacia.  Made for "Let's Party"

I'll give this recipe 5 stars for the great flavors.  I love this type combination.  I did however make some a few changes.  I used two 6 oz boxes of Stove Top Savory Herb Stuffing Mix (I prefer that  over the Pepperidge Farm) and only half the butter stated in the recipe and that was plenty for our liking.  I also covered the dish for the first 30 minutes of baking and then uncovered the last 15 minutes and it still got a little toasty on top.  There is a lot of stuffing mix in this recipe and boderline over-powering the chicken mixture. I did add a nice sprinkle of black papper and a thin layer of parmesan cheese to the chicken mixture before adding the final layer of stuffing.  I will make this again with some adjustments on the stuffing mix.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for Let's Party 2011.

Just delicious, especially with the two blends of sauces.  I had some spaghetti sauce in the freezer that I needed to use up so subed that for the tomato sauce.  Loved the flavor the sage gave to the chicken.  I used 2 chicken breast and had to make more of the breadcrumb mixture to get a good coating.  I'll make this one again for sure.  Made for I recommend tag game.

So so good.  The perfect amount of lemon flavor without overpowering the delicate taste of the Pork cutlet.  I did purchase a block of Parmesan Cheese for true grated Parmesan as suggested by the author and yes, it does make for a better sauce.  I used 1/2 and 1/2 instead of the heavy cream as that is what I usually have on hand.  I had a little over 1 pound of pork so the 6 tablespoons was not enough so adjusted for that.  I did add a couple of tablespoons of capers just because we love them with lemon suaces.  The meat was just tender and juicy. Thanks so much for sharing gailanng.  Will make this one again.

OMG this is just wonderful and so easy to put together.  I used different vegetables because of what I had on hand but no matter this is a very versital recipe (which makes it more awesome)  I used red peppers, mushrooms, the onions and for the tomatoes I used a can of Rotel well drained (added the perfect heat for our taste) Loved the red onion in this.  I did sautee the veggies in just a little butter.  As per another review, I added 1/4 tsp of garlic powder and 1/4 tsp onion powder to the crust mixture (nice addition I think)  And per another review, I used Cheddar, Mozzarella, and Parmesan as my cheese mixture..........So, so good.  My DH was so funny when the crust was baking......Wife, that thing is growing......No I mean it is distorted........Looks like a mountain range.....When it came out of the oven, it was deformed in height.  I used a spatula to press it down into shape.  Worked great.  Thanks loof for sharing.  Will make this one often.

This was good but I did not care for the sauce and I think it was the mint that we didn't like.  The Fiery Spice Blend was perfect for us.  I used this as a stir-fry and it made for a quick dinner.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for Healthy Choice Tag Game.

We really enjoyed this recipe with just a few changes for diatery reasons.  After pouring the 2% milk (which is what I used in place of the cream) over the chicken, and added the Parmesan cheese and let it refrigerate for about 6 hours, it seemed a little bland. I sprinkled some Southern Flavor Garlic Seasoning over the chicken and added just a taste of crushed red peppers and extra pepper and that seemed to perk it up for us. I simmered the mushrooms in a little Smart Balance Butter spread and that seemed to work very well.  Very nice flavor.  I'll be making this one again.  Thanks for sharing.  Made for I Recommend Tag Game.

We loved this combination even though I did sub bacon for the pancetta as I couldn't find that at the store.  I used splenda in place of the sugar and left out tyhe parsley as I didn't have any.   I'll made this one again.  Made for Best of The Best 2011
Just excellent.  Loved everything about this.  :)Made for Best of the Best 2011

Excellent flavor combination.  Made as directed except used whole wheat flour instead of the all purpose flour.  Loved the lemon.  Served with sweet potato and salad.  Thanks.  Made for Best of 2011 :)

This was so easy to put together and tastes just great.  Like others I used my own pizza crust and used some leftover steak and it was just delicious.  Thanks so much for sharing.  We will make this one again.  Made for PRMR tag game.

They had a funny twang for us.  I think I'll use only half of the mustard powder next time.  I left out the cilantro as I'm taking these to a friends house and they don't care for it.  The serrano chilies gave them a nice little bite.  Thanks.

Excellent recipe.  I did make some substitutions to use what I had on hand.  I replaced the cucumber with fresh zucchini and used 1/2 of the cumin and subed oregano for the marjoram.  Also increased the honey to suit our taste.  Just a beautiful combination of flavors.  One that will be made again this summer.  Thanks for sharing.

So easy yet so flavorful.  Loved the addition of the bay leaf.  I did have to use Mozzarella cheese as I didn't have any Parmesan but it worked out great for us.  Thenks for a great recipe.  Made for Fall PAC

This review is for the peaches and pork chops only as we didn't care for the pork stuffing mix which I knew we wouldn't.  But the peachy pork chops were excellent.  Cooked an extra 5 minutes with the peaches and the butter-flied chops turned out so moist and tender.  Just excellent.  I would like to try it with pineapple next time just as written to see if that works.  We served this with green beans and garlic bread and the stuffing mix.  Thanks so much for sharing your family recipe.  I'll make this again.  Thanks

Very good.  I did use 2% milk as that is all I had and the pan dripping from my fried venison which added a lot of flavor to the gravy, but even without that, this gravy is delicious and so simple to make.  I had to add just a little more milk to mine as it was a little thick.  This thickens up very quickly.  Thanks Ms Sally  Made for I Recommend

Excellent flavor combination in the marinade.  I also added minced garlic to the mixture.  Loved the peanut mixture.  I used additional garlic powder instead of the minced which worked well for me.  I doubled the breading mixture and had just a little left over after breading 2 large chicken breast that I cut in half and split length-wise to make them thinner.  Thanks so much Susie for sharing.  Made for New Kids on the Block tag game.

OMG this is just wonderful.  The flavors combination was right on.  I could not find the mesquite powder so used Grill Mates Mesquite which probably gave it a little more kick which we didn't mind at all.  I used a 2.22 pound pork tenderloin roast which is what I had and used  all the spice mixture and all of the barbeque sauce as written.  Just excellent.  I'll make this one again for sure.  Thanks for posting.  Excellent recipe.

Love my chili dogs made this way.  I did toast the buns and added mustard and a little relish.  I also fried the split hot dogs.  I used my own Chili recipe #146288 that I had in the freezer.  Made in memory of Pammy.

Although I way over cooked mine in the oven at 375 for 40 minutes, the flavor was just delicious.  Next time I'll make on the grill as directed.  A wonderful recipe and I highly recommend it.  Flavor combination was perfect.  I only marinated mine for about 6 hours.   Thanks DrG for sharing.

This had such a wonderful flavor with the added bacon.  However, I did use tomato sauce with basil and garlic which added a lot of flavor I think that otherwise would have been missed.  I made half the recipe for the two of us with plenty of leftovers for the weekend.  As it cooked for the 1 hour it seemed to dry out a lot so I doubled the sauce about half-way through the 1 hour cooking time and it thickened up perfectly.  I wish I had doubled the bacon since I added double the sauce.  The flavors were so good and DH loved it.  I'll be making this again   Thanks loof.

This was a very unique salad for us.  I had never had Quinoa before but I think I like it.  Loved the combination of spices although I cut back on the Cilantro, personal preference.  Thanks for sharing.

We thought this was very tasty.  The recipe worked well.  I didn't have seedless raspberry preserves, so I pressed through a sieve.  Reduced the amount of cayenne because kids were eating.  This needed a garnish for presentation, perhaps orange slices and fresh parsley (if serving to company).  It is not too sweet a dish, and went well with brown pecan rice.  Thanks for the recipe!

I've made these several times since she won Next Food Network Star.  I like to use jumbo-sized muffin tins and pack them pretty tightly with potatoes, placing the potatoes around the sides of each cup as well as stacking them.  I also like mozzarella cheese better than Swiss.  I like very finely chopped red onion, and for the cream I just put a tablespoon into each cup.  I salt, pepper, onion and cheese them as I build them (not just on top.)  I also bake them longer to get them crunchy around the edges.  These potatoes are so good we could fight over them!!  Fabulous recipe!

This is a great white pizza sauce!  It made just the right amount for a cookie-sheet sized pizza (I used 1 Pillsbury refrigerated crust).  My pizza had chicken, bacon and fresh basil, along with shredded mozzarella and provolone cheese.  I loved the garlic in the sauce.  It came out nice and thick and flavorful.  I used slightly less Parmesan cheese.  Great eating on a cold snowy day in Virginia!  Thanks.

This was such a great recipe!  We really enjoyed dinner tonight.  I added salt and pepper to the chicken breasts (which were thin sliced) before the taco seasoning.  Sour cream really put these over the top.  A side dish of skillet corn and pinto beans with fresh red peppers accompanied this along with tortilla chips.  Thanks CoffeeB!
This was wonderful!  I used less chipotle peppers to make it kid-friendly.  This is a winning dish, very tasty and a huge hit at the table!  Yum!

This was a delicious chili.  Everyone loved it.  I used 1 can of beans, added a little sweet Italian sausage and just a 28 oz. can of stewed tomatoes (along with the 15 oz. can tomato sauce).  Served over Fritos with toppings of sharp cheddar cheese, sour cream and green onions.  Mini corn muffins to accompany.  Cest magnifique!

This is sooooooo good.  Simple and fresh.  I like to add a bit more olive oil (drizzle it right over the potatoes) and let the vegetables get a little crust on them in the skillet.  It's key to season well with salt and pepper.  Winning dish - we love it.

Very good, quick and simple. Next time I will dredge the steaks in seasoned flour before browning.  I made a half recipe.  It worked fine.  Only needed to cook 1 hour and was very tender.  I had to used canned mushrooms.  Thanks for a great, homey, stick-to-the-ribs recipe!
Delicious!  I added just a bit more orange juice to suit my taste.  I can't wait to try this during the summer and use a whole bottle to make a large bowl of sangria punch!

A good recipe, though I was a little disappointed in the flavor at first.  It's not your fault!  After tasting one when finished, I decided to drain the remaining sauce into a skillet and simmer it up to thicken it a bit.  I added some red pepper flakes, minced garlic, and another tablespoon of honey, to make it glaze better.  I poured that over the cooked shrimp, and all was well.
I think next time I will just cook these up in a skillet and save all the energy used to fire the oven to 450.  I think they will glaze up better in a skillet, too.  
Thanks for an inspirational recipe!

This is very good.  I used 4 packets of Splenda instead of sugar.  I also added 1 tablespoon of Dream Whip powder to add some fluffy dreaminess.
Thanks for the inspiration.
This is a delicious, easy recipe.  I used 1 tsp of Madras curry paste instead of curry powder, otherwise I followed the recipe exactly.  Very yummy!

A very good recipe that reminds me of a German hot potato salad my mom used to make.  I made a half batch and, I used sour cream instead of yogurt, and white vinegar instead of verjuice.  I also used only 1 tsp of olive oil (instead of walnut) in the dressing.   I forgot the Parmesan!
I will definitely make this again.

A very tasty rendition of chicken salad.  I bet this would be good made with immitation crab, also.
I used 1/4 of a green pepper since I had no red.  My feta was the creamy type, so it got mixed in a bit more than I wanted.  Next time I'll have the crumbly kind and I bet it will be even better.  I like the addition of dill!

Yummy, yummy, yummy.  I used Rose's Lime Juice like Julie B suggested.   I didn't even bother with the coconut on the glass rim because I just wanted to get to the drink.  Very nice, indeed.
Thank you.
This was very good, but I think I might cut back on the lime juice just a little.  The juice was a little too sweet and tart.  Or maybe I just need more rum and Sprite!  Very refreshing!
A delicious recipe.  I made a half recipe using 1 can of green beans, and halving everything else.  Very tasty.
I really like this.  Very refreshing.  I grated the gingerroot on my mircoplane grater to get the full amount of juice, and let it steep a half hour before squeezing it out.

Delicious cookies!  I had to add an extra half cup of flour.  That might be because I used neufchatel (lighter than cream cheese).  I made drop cookies since the dough was still very sticky and hard to roll into balls.  These will become a regular in my rotation!

This is a good and refreshing recipe.  I left out the oil.  It is not needed.  I used light sour cream.  I also used dried dill, about 1 teaspoon.  I used two packets of Splenda instead of sugar.  I will make this again for sure. Thank you for posting, Bellinda.
very good and easy too, you need a sweet tooth for these, my cinnamon-loving DS enjoyed this, thanks bmc!
my DH made this on Sunday during the football game, with some minor amount adjustments, and was enjoyed, thanks loof!

This makes a wonderful coffee, I used one heaping coffee scoop in my small a 4-cup coffee machine, I did not have any butter flavor extract only the rum and it was still wonderful, will keep on hand for a morning coffee, thanks Annacia!
this was made and thoroughly enjoyed by my DS, I used instant espresso coffee and topped the mugs off with mini marshmallows, thanks Booms!
this is wonderful, I plan on making this often in the summer months, thanks for sharing MsSally!
this was made by my DH and was thoroughly enjoyed, thanks Shelby!

these were great but way too much dill for out liking, I used 1 teaspoon dried and found it too strong, I added in 1 teaspoon garlic powder in with the flour mixture and increased the Cajun seasoning, will make again but with some adjusments, thanks Booms!

This is like a deluxe sloppy Joe, we like lots of spice so I added in 2 good teaspoons dried chili flakes and increased the garlic to 3 tablespoons, I cooked mine for more than the specified time, almost 1 hour and that really intensified the flavor, we loved this thanks for sharing Booms!

Delicious! I doubled the recipe and sauteed the garlic and mushrooms with a small onion in the butter, I didn't use the microwave at all,  I also added in about 1 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, this was very good, thanks for sharing bmc!
I made these without the kisses, but this definately needs more water for me the dough was a little too dry, however they turned out fine, thanks for sharing Dreamer!
this is heaven in a glass, the coconut cream really adds so much flavor and the perfect amount of sweetness, I made for my DH and he gave it two thumbs up, thanks for a great smoothie BK!
my DH made this and  hethoroughly enjoyed it, thanks Loof!

my lord this is so good! the only small change I made was I increased the espresso coffee only slightly, thanks for sharing this mersaydees this would make  a wonderful after dinner drink to serve to guests!

made this s couple of hours ago and boy what a difference chilling time makes, made as stated only I used seasoned salt, I'm looking forward to using this tomorrow, and I will make again using my garden tomatoes in the summer, this is wonderful thanks for sharing hon!
My DH really enjoyed this this, I did some amount adjustments and I'm going to try this again using lemon pudding, thanks for sharing Hokie!

this was good but the canned chopped mandarin oranges made this a little thin,  I used more than 1 teaspoon of filling for each cracker so I got nothing close to 48 next time I will squeeze out as much of the moisture as possible in the oranges and double the recipe, thanks Hokie!

delicious cookies! these baked out with the most perfect texture, I increased the vanilla to 2 teaspoons, these had an intense peanut butter flavor that really please my DS, he quickly scooped them up to take home with him, thanks for a great recipe hon!

this so delicious!  I grilled the salmon burgers between a two-sided grilling rack (the ones that have two sides and lock together) I added in about 1 teaspoon fresh minced garlic to  the salmon mixture and used seasoned salt, I used Atantic salmon fillets for this, make certain not to over process the fresh salmon, process until only coarsley chopped.... this made the most delicious dinner served on homemade rolls with the delicious mayo mixture YUMMMMM! thanks for sharing hon!

Delicious! I used butter in place of the oil and also added in some parmesan cheese and reduced the whipping cream down to 3/4 cup,  added in 2 teaspoons crushed red chili flakes, this made for a wonderful creamy tomato dish that was served with spaghetti, thanks for sharing hon!
very good! I used canned baby shrimp for this and added in 2 teaspoon fresh minced garlic and Tabasco in place of the cayenne, the longer this chills the better the flavor, thanks for sharing Brook!

well for a flourless cookie these are very good, I thought I had the right amount of quick-cooing oats but when I measured all I had in the bag was about 3-3/4 and that is what I used,  they still turned out great, I just used the baking chips and added in a little chopped nuts, thanks for sharing hon!
wonderful, I used Greek yogurt for this and reduced the dill amount to 2 teaspoons, I served this with  spicy taco burgers what a great combination, thanks for sharing Sharon!
what a great easy treat, I included these in  a take-home package for my peanut butter-loving DS and received many thank you's, so thank YOU Susan for a great treat!

this is delicious, I did a few amount adjustments and added in cayenne pepper and a large jalapeno pepper for heat, the flavor only improves with refrigeration time, so I made this a day ahead, thanks for sharing hon!

I have made cookies like these in the past so I knew these would be great this is the first time I have made them with white chocolate chips and will not be the last, this is a wonderful recipe and they were thoroughly enjoyed by all, thanks for sharing hon!
another winner here Booms, my DH loved this drink, thanks for sharing!

this was good but I felt it needs something else to boost the flavors together, needed more oil and I added in some garlic powder but still something was missing, I might make again with some other additions, thanks Syd!
Quick and easy, I used half milk and half and half fo a more creamy taste also added in some cayenne pepper, thanks for sharing Brooke my DH enjoyed this!
delicious, the only change I made was I added in a large clove of minced garlic and some Tabasco sauce, the sun-dried tomatoe really brings this dip to life, thanks for sharing Coffee!

these were awesome! I made 24 jalapeno peppers (very spicy jalapenos!) from my garden with 12 slices of thick sliced bacon cut in half, I used the neufchatel cheese, next time it will be flavored cream cheese, easy and so good and the plus to these is that you can prepare them earlier in the day to grill in the evening, thanks for sharing Karen, will make again!
these are great,  I only had 4 ripe bananas in my freezer so that is what I used,  I served them with homemade buttermilk syrup, thanks for sharing Syd!
delicious! with a few amount adjustments and the addition of freshly ground black pepper we thoroughly enjoyed this chicken, a recipe i will make again, thanks iewe!

great salad! I made a few amount adjustments and also added in some garlic powder to the yogurt/mayo mixture, I used a good helping of Tabasco sauce, chilled for a few hours this was thoroughly enjoyed, thanks for sharing loofie!

this was tastey but not sure if I liked the addition of the tomato paste, also if I were to make again I would use chicken broth in place of water, I used kalamata olives which worked fine and also added in 1 tablespoon fresh minced garlic to the onion, thanks for posting Syd!

delicious slaw and only gets better with refrigeration time, I did a few amount adjustments and add in 1 teaspoon garlic powder to the yogurt/mayo mixture, I used Greek yogurt for this, make certain to hand-squeeze out all the excess moisture in the shredded carrots or you will end up with a watery salad, thanks for sharing Kate, this was enjoyed by my family!
well I didn't make this but I did drink it we all gave it thumbs up, thanks for sharing another great drink recipe Booms!

I made this a few days back but somehow forgot to rate it, although the lemon was a little overpowering for our tastes I am still giving it 5-stars, I also added in whole garlic cloves sliced in half when blanching the veggies, thanks for sharing Syd!

a few changes to this great comfort meal, for extra fluffy eggs I added in 1/8 teaspoon of baking powder to the egg mixture and used 2 tablespoons whipping cream in place of the milk and lots of fresh ground black pepper added, thanks for sharing pups!
the flavor was great although even with patting the carrots dry with paper towels i found them to be a little watery after adding on the cream, all in all a nice recipe with good flavor, thanks Syd!
wonderful! this has all the flavors I love, I used garlic powder in place of the garlic salt, did a few other amount adjustmens, thanks for sharing Lynn this was thoroughly enjoyed by my family!

yummy cookes, I made the dough the night before, I baked them in my convection oven at 325 degrees for 8 minutes and they baked out perfect, I increased the vanilla to 2 teaspoons and used 1/2 teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg, these baked out on the crispy side just the way my DS likes them, thanks for sharing CoffeeB

we loved these mashed taters, the only change I made was I used whipping cream in place milk and used russet potatoes, skipped  directions 1-7 as I keep roasted garlic in my freezer to use in recipes, thanks for sharing mersaydees!

this cake is wonderful, I also added in apples to the cake batter as well as the topping, increased the vanilla to 2 teaspoons and used 1/8 teaspoon salt, this is wonderful served with vanilla ice cream, thanks for sharing  this great treat Dreamer!

this is simply fabulous, I also added in some fresh minced garlic and used Tabasco sauce in place of the hot pepper flakes, I ran out of shallots so I subbed minced green onion, thanks for sharing Booms, will make again soon!

I doubled the complete recipe and baked it in a larger casserole dish, I use half peaches and nectarines, also for a double recipe I used 1 tablespoon vanilla, for my sweet-tooth family the sugar amount neded to be increased slightly, this baked out wonderful and was thoroughly enjoyed, thanks Syd!

lovely flavor and colour, I used light rum, I definately will try this again using dark or spiced rum, the light rum all I had at the time, both DH and myself enjoyed this drink, thanks for sharing another great one Booms!

well I did a few changes to this recipe I used half mayo and sour cream and also added in 1 teaspoon garlic powder and some cayenne pepper to the cream mixture, I would strongly suggest to use only Roma (plum) tomatoes to avoid too much moisture from the tomatoes, also to brush the unbaked crust lightly with egg white to avoid a soggy crust,  we enjoyed the tonight, thanks Shelby!
this is a great way to use up wonton wrappers, I did some minor amount adjustments, this was a great treat that was thoroughly enjoyed, thanks Syd!

this was great, I like the addition of the Italian seasoning and parmesan cheese, for extra fluffy eggs I added in 1/8 teaspoon baking powder, I also added in fresh ground black pepper, thanks for sharing Kate!

very good, I add in 2 tablespoons fresh garlic when sauteeing and 2 teaspoons red chili flakes for heat, I omitted the cilantro and used butter in place of the margarine, next time I make this I would reduce the sour cream to half, I used fresh ground black pepper, I did not have any thin spaghetti so I used regular and that works out fine, thanks for sharing weekend cooker, my family enjoyed this!
great French Toast, I had to make this recipe three times to feed my DS and a friend for Saturday brunch, thanks for sharing this iewe it was thoroughly enjoyed!
Great drink not too heavy just a nice easy drink that we enjoyed, thanks Sarah!

I made this salad as stated using all ingredients although I did a few amount adjustments, I would probably try this with orange juice next time instead of the grapefruit, my fruit-loving DH really enjoyed this salad, thanks for sharing Kate!

well I did some changes to this, I did not have any lemon cake so I used white, I also added in 1 cup of thawed Cool Whip to the frosting to make it softer and creamier, I look forward to making this again with lemon cake, thanks for sharing Shelby, my DS and DH loved it!

This sauce is to die for, I have made other vodka sauces in the past nothing comes close to this one, I used frozen fresh basil that I store in my freeze from my summer's crop, I also increased the chili flakes way up and used bulk Italian sausage in place of the turkey sausage, use half of each crushed and drained diced tomatoes, I doubled the complete recipe and i think I really should have tripled it this is so good, what a great recipe I will repeat many times, thank you for sharing ChicagoRN!
great soup, I sauteed the onion with 2 tablespoon chopped garlic in butter firstly, I used half and half cream instead of skim milk, we enjoyed this thanks for sharing Brooke!

I couldn't be happier to have found this recipe - it's as amazing as everyone says! Mine turned out like a cross between ricotta and feta (my favorites!). Here's what I did: I soaked slivered blanched almonds for 21 hours, made the mixture in the food processor, then strained it in a strainer lined with a coffee filter (a great alternative to cheesecloth, since that can be hard to find). I only strained for 3 hours, and I'm guessing the full 12 hours would make the final product more crumbly and less ricotta-like (either way, I'd be happy). I put the mixture in two small ramekins sprayed with vegetable spray, baked for 10 minutes at 400, then 20 minutes at 350. This gave the cheese a nicely browned top that looked beautiful. I only had time to chill for 4 hours, then I turned them out and topped them with the olive oil and herbs. The presentation was gorgeous, and my dinner guests absolutely LOVED it.

I'm thinking of all kinds of ways to use this. To use the cheese in it's creamy form (unbaked), I would suggest using a clove of roasted garlic to avoid the raw flavor of garlic, and I'd also cut back the lemon juice just a bit.

 I cook and review a LOT but have *never* had success with cakes, until *NOW*. In fact, I've become rather too well known for my cake making disasters. Then, in a rash fit of optimism I said yes when DS asked for a home-made  " Cars Lightening Mac Queen Birthday Cake.. after all who can possibly say "No" to the " please please Mama" of the upturned  pleading face of a soon to be 4 year old? Thank You Thank You Thanks You Lynn for changing my Cake Baking Life forever!

This turned out really good! I simplified by using rotisserie chicken and adding 1 cup of chicken broth. This turned out really good! I made it healthy by using whole wheat crust, turkey bacon, reduced fat cheese and light ranch dressing mixed with basil. It was super easy and my whole family loved it. Thanks for posting!
This rice was easy to make and tasted great.  Thanks for posting!
Great recipe!  The fries actually came out crispy, which has seemed to be impossible to do with baking before finding this recipe.  I will definitely make again.  Thanks for posting!

Wow! These turned out great. I made a double recipe for my family of 4 and even my teenage son really liked them. I used green enchilada sauce instead of salsa (a bit less) and regular colby-jack cheese. I also needed to cook them a while longer to get them crisp. My husband was surprised that they were homemade. The tortillas were easy to roll after microwaving in the damp paper towels as directed. Thanks for posting. I'm sure I'll make again!

I used two cans of pork and beans (undrained) since I didn't have the other beans and baked for 45 minutes.  Turned out very well for being much lower in sugar than the regular beans that I make.  Nice side dish for the weight watchers plan.  Thanks for posting!
This is great soup and very easy to make.  We loved it and I can imagine making it with other small noodles or none at all.  Thanks for posting!

Wow!  These are the best!  They turned out perfect and I love the protein they provide.  I used to make some pancakes with cottage cheese run through the blender, but these are much easier. They even taste great eaten right out of your hand without any toppings.  I just bought some more greek yogurt so I can make them again.  Thanks for posting!
This was an easy meal and turned out great!  The flavors blended well.  I will definitely make again.  Thanks for posting!
This is the best creamy coleslaw ever! I used light mayo, tarragin vinegar and dried chives instead of the green onions and it tasted just like Houston's. Perfect!

At the grocery store yesterday they had packaged cucumbers that were going bad very cheaply.  So I bought a pack but needed something to do with them right away and where I could slice them as parts needed to be thrown out.  This was easy to make.  I used fat free mayo and splenda and doubled the recipe.  I found this soupier than I would have liked and just a little sweeter then I like.  That said, I'm not having any trouble eating them!  Thanks for a good very light one to try.

We loved these.  I did make one major substitution, which is that I used dried cranberries instead of cherries.  I loved the taste of these and did not think they had the weird splenda taste that often comes from baked goods that don't use any regular sugar.  I thought the texture of these was perfect and look forward to enjoying these often!  Thanks.

I can never get the outside to get crispy and was thrilled that it actually worked with this recipe.  Thanks for posting it!

This is fantastic sauce.  Much better than bottles, and not that hard to make.  The only thing I changed, was using chipotle chili powder for the regular.  Gave it a little added heat and smokiness.  Used this to baste bbq'd chicken, and also has a dipping sauce at the table.  Made for Spring 2008 PAC.

What a nice combo of flavors!  I used French Press coffee and couldn't find hazelnut extract at the store this morning, so used s/f hazelnut syrup and omitted the Splenda.  I added some steamed milk.  Great for my mid-morning break!
This is really easy and a simple presentation with a nice flavor.  The glaze is subtle, and lets the flavor of the salmon shine!  I had never used white balsamic before, but really liked it.
I agree with Sharon-the little bits of candied ginger really zinged this up!  The flavors all went together nicely!  Made for the Summer Salad and Berry Recipe Challenge.
Can't get much easier than this!  Very tasty, too.  Great appetizer or side dish.

If you are looking for a sweet bread, this isn't it, which is fine with me!  I like them not-too-sweet.  This is a dense bread, but also moist.  I subbed walnuts for the sunflower seeds, since someone seems to have used my sunflower seeds all up! 
I also left out the raisins.  (I know Sydney Mike will think this heretical of me, but I don't like them :) )  The bits of apricot are a nice addition.

This filled the kitchen with great aroma during the roasting and grinding process.  Nice flavor, with a little bite from the peppercorns and chilies.  I cut recipe in half-IT MAKES A LOT!  Looking forward to using it in cooking.  Going to try it as a rub on a pork tenderloin.  Will report back later!
UPDATE:  Used this as a rub on a pork tenderloin grilled on the rotisserie.  What a great flavor it gave the meat!  Needed nothing else!!!

This is a great marinade.  The flank steak turned out tender and flavorful.  I used the honey option, but I think it would be good with the maple syrup also.  I heated the leftover marinade to boiling and strained out the solids, and used it as a sauce for the meat.  Made for Camera-Less Chef #5 game.

This is tasty and I can see the possibilities of other combos.  Kind of like a calzone.  I used the prepared pizza crust, but would make my own next time.  It was a little hard to work with.  Too spongy?  I lightened this up a tad by using ground turkey, turkey bacon and reduced-fat cheddar.  Worked fine.  I think I will try an actual pizza type filling next time.

These were very easy and tasty!  I like the addition of cream cheese (I used reduced-fat).  I used sugar-free raspberry jam and Splenda (I only used 1/8 cup)  I skipped the powdered sugar.  These will be on my holiday list next year!
This is a great combo of flavors.  I used baby carrots.   I think I had the heat too high, since the sauce thickened up too fast and was lumpy, but tasty!

Ditto everything LonghornMama said!  Very easy and the molasses really adds to the flavor.  I have always used brown sugar, but this is MUCH better!  I am looking forward to trying it on French Toast!
UPDATE:  Tried this on French toast made with Anme's Recipe #250385, and it was delicious!

This is an excellent marinade.  I used it on boneless chicken breasts, but it would be great on pork, too!  Made as written, and marinated the chicken about 4 hours.  I also heated the marinade to a boil and used as a sauce on the chicken after cooking.

I agree that this doesn't taste as sweet as it sounds.  The flavors are balanced just right.  I used Smucker's Suger-free Caramel ice cream topping and sugar-free hazelnut syrup, so mine was guilt-free!  I also used "full-caf" dark roast coffee, made in a French press pot.  Thanks for sharing this treat!
Very nice flavors.  I used tilapia filets and cooked on Foreman grill.  The dry rub would be good on chicken, also, I think!
Not much I can add to the other great reviews here.  This is easy and very tasty.  I will try it with fresh oregano next time, and on the grill, as suggested by others.

Quite easy and tasty, but I think I would add some lime zest also, and puree the mojo ingredients in my mini-processor so that a little more of the jalapeno flavor would come through.  I cooked the chicken on the Foreman, but I think the bbq would be better so you get some smoke.  Will do that next time, and may try the mix on some salmon!  Thanks for sharing.

We love molasses cookies and to be able to have them almost fat-free is great.  And these are great.  Lots of ginger flavor.   They are somewhat crispy on the outside, and chewy in the center.  I had no problem getting them off the sheet.  I baked them 12 minutes.  Will be making these often!  Made for Fall 2008 PAC.

A nice balance of sweet and tart.  I used almonds in and on top, but will skip the ones on top next time, as they just fall off when slicing.  The almond extract gives this a nice flavor.  The bake time was a little long.  I took mine out after 55 minutes, but it would depend on your oven.  Mine may run hot.

Love the name!  These are moist (I used the buttermilk option) and they get enough sweetness from the carrots, but the allspice tended to overpower the other flavors.  I think I will try them again with the cinnamon and perhaps some nutmeg instead of the allspice.  Made for Fall 2008 PAC.

I liked the flavors of this very much, but mine turned out a little too al dente.  I will try it again and add a little more liquid or leave on burner longer.  I have to admit I was skeptical about equal amounts of liquid and rice, since I have always done the 2 to 1 ratio.  The rice turned out not gummy like mine sometimes does, so I will be trying this again, only cooked just a tad more.  I used cilantro.

This is very good.  The flavors are subtle and I like that it is not vinegary like some marinated vegies.  I also used olive oil.  Served by itself, but would be good on a bed of greens, or in a greek salad.  Made for Fall 2008 PAC.
This was just the right balance of flavors.  Nothing overpowering.  Went very well with broiled salmon.  I liked the addition of the carrot ribbons.  Made it fancier than plain couscous.

Loved the peanut butter and strawberry combination.  I used no-sugar-added nonfat yogurt and no-salt added peanut butter, so made this even healthier.  Consistency was perfect.  Great breakfast drink.

This is really tasty!  I didn't use the added sugar, and the onions caramelized fine!  Nice blend of flavors with the herbs and cheese.  I used the herbs listed.  Since we were having this for breakfast, I skipped the "salad" and served this with some fried potatoes and whole-wheat toast.

What a sauce!  I doubled the amounts because I used an oven-roasted loin instead of a tenderloin.  I also used some Calvados for the brandy, so it had a slight apple flavor to go with the mushrooms (I used a dried wild mushroom mix).  The sauce is very simple to make.  Thanks for another keeper, Boomette!
I loved the chewiness of these, and for being so low in fat, they are very moist.  I used dried cherries.  Will be making these again!

This is a delicious and easy pick-me-up drink.  I used a microwave milk frother, and added a little extra milk.  I saved some for foam for the top.  Nice flavors!  For the instant coffee, I used Medaglia D'oro Espresso Powder.  Thanks for posting this keeper.

This may be a good breakfast, according to previous reviews, but it is also a terrific light dinner!  I made mine after a hard day at work, and served with a toasted English Muffin.  Great and easy!  (I also got a bonus--a double yolk egg!)

I really liked the oatmeal itself, but didn't care for the protein powder/water topping.  Tasted like canned milk.  I will make this again, as it is a good way to use leftover pumpkin, but I will maybe stir the protein powder into the oatmeal and use low-fat milk on top.  I will also double the amounts, as suggested, as 1 serving was pretty small (for me!) :)

This hit the spot for breakfast on a cold, dreary day.  I had an added bonus of having some homemade cider made with apples and pears, with some ginger juice.  This needed no sweeteners at all.  I served mine with a splash of fat-free half and half for a special treat.  I don't have quick-cooking oats so just microwaved about a minute longer.
Another winner!  This has a great  flavor, with a light texture and crusty exterior.  Went great with homemade chicken soup.  I really liked the extra crunch from the pumpkin seeds.
This is a great and easy variation on plain rice.  I only used 1 medium onion (2 sounded like too much), and used pecan halves.  Went great with your Recipe #288933.

This is so easy and the results are so tasty!   I found some fresh baby shiitakes with a mellow flavor that complimented the leeks and salmon without overpowering, like some bigger shiitakes do.  The liquid mixture is perfect!  Thanks for a new way to enjoy salmon!
I grew up on buttered, parsleyed red potatoes but had never used lemon or chives.  Great additions.  Will be making them this way from now on!  Went great with some red snapper.

Delicious!  I made mine with regular coffee.  Loved the combination of orange, chocolate and coffee.  I made the full amount and drank it all!  I will make again, but cut sugar in half, as I prefer mine less sweet.
A great tasting muffin that is very light textured, more like a cupcake.  Loved the addition of the oats.

This certainly lives up to it's name!  Mice crunchy crust, and dense and soft on the inside.  Great bread to serve with soup!  I used sesame seeds.  I combined both methods.  I used the bread machine to do the kneading and finished by hand (rises and baking).  I made mine in a loaf pan.  Thanks for this keeper!

This was so easy to whip up and tasted great for my mid-morning coffee treat (I drink black coffee in the morning but on weekends I have some kind of "special" coffee later)  I used sugar-free Irish Cream coffee syrup and left out the sugar.  Nice combination of flavors.
This is really delicious!  I did not have curry leaves, but still great without them.  I am going to try it again, only with chicken thighs.  Thanks for this keeper!
This is really a good meatloaf!  Loved the cheesiness of it.  Will try  again and experiment with different flavored sauces.  And I will take your advice and make extra for freezing!
What a great bowl of oatmeal!  The oat bran makes it a bit more creamy than just rolled oats.  The flavors were great.  I used fat-free half and half on top, with a little butter.

Great flavors in these.  I found the batter to be a bit thick (which I thought odd, since others had said it was too thin) so I used another 1/2 cup of buttermilk.  Right combination of sweet/tart.  Served with maple syrup and honey, but will have to try the Cranberry Syrup next time!
Another winner, Pat!  Subtle flavors that don't overpower.  I used Jasmine rice.

This is old-fashioned comfort food.  We had this type of dish a lot when I was a kid (at least 100 years ago :)  )I used three types of pasta (I had remnants of boxes to use up)
The addition of worcestershire is a nice touch.  Thanks for the stroll down memory lane!

These are so easy to do, and taste great.  I made half as cloverleaf rolls and half as crescent rolls, and sprinkled poppy seeds and sesame seeds on some after I glazed them.  I got 14 rolls.  I have always shied away from making rolls, but with this recipe I will do it more often!
Great technique!  I used red wine and added some garlic powder and ground pepper.  I own the Kafka cookbook this originated in, but forgot I even had it.  Time to explore it again :)

I used canned pears, but looking forward to trying with a fresh pear during pear season. I also used vanilla yogurt, and only 1 tbls. of honey. I added some ground cardamom with the nutmeg, because I love pear and cardamom together.  Great smoothie!

This hit the spot on a cold, snowy day.  Tasted like a Milky Way bar.  I used sugar-free caramel and chocolate syrups, and fat-free half and half.  I frothed the syrups and cream a bit with a small whisk before pouring in the coffee.  Thanks for this keeper!

I did the baked in the oven option and used boneless, skinless chicken breasts.  They turned out very flavorful.  I was a bit concerned while cooking the sauce, because it smelled too vinegary, but it didn't taste too vinegary at all.  Nice balance of tart and sweet.  Looking forward to trying this on the grill when the weather warms up.  I am going to try some cayenne pepper instead of black pepper, also.

I love tandoori chicken and this is really good.  I prefer it grilled (I don't have a tandoori grill, though) but for being done in the oven, this really turned out nicely.  I am going to give this a try when the weather permits some outdoor cooking!  (I have to use up the BIG jar of tandoori paste I bought! :)  )

What a great way to start a cold, dreary morning (this is Spring? :( )  I used Hershey's Special Dark Cocoa, Splenda, and nonfat milk, but replaced some of the milk with fat-free half and half for richness.  This reminds me of a Mexican Chocolate product  I had back in the 1970's that a Mexican neighbor had.  It was a solid block of sugar/cocoa/spices that was broken up and dissolved in hot milk.  Made for Spring 2009 PAC.

This is really easy and tastes delicious!  I think the butter got left out of the ingredient list, though, so I cut olive oil to about 1/8 cup and added 1/4 cup unsalted butter.  I also left out the red pepper, since we were having this as a side with salmon, and not over pasta.  But will make it for pasta next time.  Would be a quick, fancy after-work meal!

Very easy and tasty, although we will take your suggestion and go with more seasoning next time (we like it spicy!)  Cooking time was spot on.  I used Recipe #96102 for the seasoning.  Made for Spring 2009 PAC.

This is so easy and SO tasty!  Love the sweetness of the onions with the bite of the Gruyere.  Cooking time was right on.  The only mistake I made was cutting the recipe in half.  Now no leftovers :(
Made for Spring 2009 PAC.

I also made this as a mix to have on hand to make by the cup.  I put everything except the water (including the vanilla extract) in the food processor and mixed to a fine powder (put the extract in while processor is running so it won't lump) and stored it in an airtight jar.  Great flavor.    I love the Special Dark cocoa.  I am going to keep this in the motorhome for making hot chocolate while camping.  Made for Spring 2009 PAC.  UPDATE:  I put a couple of spoonfuls in my coffee this morning for a great mocha!

This is delicious and turned out fork tender!  Loved the lemon flavor.  Cooking times were just right.  Took me longer to pound the chicken then to cook it :)  Served with your recipe #363280 and steamed broccoli.  Made for Spring 2009 PAC.
This was a quick, tasty lunch.  I used bacon and rye bread.  Made for Spring 2009 PAC.

I love cardamom, but had never thought of putting it in my oatmeal.  This is delicious!  The amount of cardamom is just right.  I made one change-instead of raisins, I used dried cranberries.  Drizzled with blackberry honey and used fat-free half and half for an extra treat.  Thanks for a great breakfast.  Made for Spring 2009 PAC.
Very flavorful mixture.  Great on steamed broccoli.  Going to try it on a steak also.  I like the bite the pepper gives it.  Made for Spring 2009 PAC.
These are very good, and an easy way to use up those leftovers.  I made mine to go with some eggs, for a "breakfast" dinner.  Made for Spring 2009 PAC.

Very easy to make and tasty, too!  Makes just enough for 2 large chicken breasts, which I baked in the oven.  I made as written this time, but will bump the "heat" a little next time.  The best part is it wasn't overly sweet like some store bought sauces.  Made for Spring 2009 PAC.

A very moist, flavorful snack cake.  I made a couple of changes:  Subbed Splenda for the granulated sugar, but kept the brown sugar (and adjusted baking time down as per Splenda website instructions) and used pecans instead of walnuts.  I was leery about the amount of cinnamon, but it turned out to be the perfect amount.  Served with a dollop of sugar-free Cool Whip.  I used Granny Smith apples.

These are delicious!  Love the cornmeal and ground flax seed in them.  I used the vanilla, also, which added a lot of flavor.  Beating the egg whites first made these nice and light!  I splurged and served with real maple syrup!  This is a really easy recipe, also!

Very good cup of coffee!  Like a maple nut candy bar.  I cut the amount of syrup in half to cut down on sugar, but added 1/8th teaspoon of maple flavor (Mapleine) to make up for the lost maple flavor.  Worked fine!
This is a very nice and flavorful way to dress up broccoli!  Loved the bite from the red pepper flakes!
I used the microwave method, and it is really quick and easy to do.  (My squash was quite large, so I had to do it in two batches.)

This really tastes wonderful, but my squash layer was a bit watery.  Not sure if I overcooked the squash or not.  I did drain and squeeze the spinach well.  I will be trying it again, though, since the flavor was so good.

I love the combination of juices in this.  The orange gave it a little extra sweetness.  I used Splenda.  I am going to try this as Syd suggested, also, with sparkling water.  Thanks for a nice refreshing drink!

These have a great texture and are not too sweet, with a subtle maple flavor.  I used fat-free, no sugar added vanilla yogurt and pecans instead of walnuts.  I like the added texture given by the whole-wheat flour.

Very tasty and just the right amount of heat and spices!  It IS a little labor intensive, so  will make it for special occasions.  I think it would be good with shrimp, as a previous reviewer made it, so will give that a try, too!

Another winner, Boomette!  I had never done salmon on skewers before, but will more often now!  The combination of shrimp, scallops and salmon was great, and the Greek flavors from the herbs was subtle but tasty.  I used a mix of yellow and orange peppers instead of green.  Great addition to our "skewer" party!

This is so easy and refreshing!  A great recipe for making in the RV.  I only made one pie, and the little store near where were staying only had raspberry-lemonade Crystal Light. I used 1/2 tub, but after I tasted the mixture, I added the rest of the tub, since it wasn't as tart as the regular lemonade.  I think this would work with some of the other flavors, also!  I also used sugar-free Cool Whip.  Thanks for a light dessert!
Very satisfying and a nice "dessert' drink on a hot day.  I used S/F raspberry and non-fat milk.  Looking forward to trying it with orange or lime jello.

This tasted great.  The coffee amount was fine for me and I like the vanilla flavor.  I also had a problem with the oatmeal sinking to the bottom of the glass.  I was expecting something thicker, so I might add 1/2 a banana next time to thicken it.  I used Splenda.

Delicious!  My market only had the medium shrimp this weekend, so I am looking forward to trying this again with the jumbos.  The mediums cooked too fast to get "grill marks" on them.  The sauce is great!  I also couldn't find any decent lemongrass stalks I wanted to spend the money on so I added about 2 tsp. of lemongrass paste I had in the 'fridge to the marinade.

This needs 10 stars!  The flavors in this really make your taste buds stand up and take notice.  It makes small servings (I used 4 oz. cups) but it is so rich and strong, you don't need much.  I only made 2 servings, but given that it is a tad labor intensive, I will make the full amount next time and store it for later use.  I also think this would be great served hot in the winter.  Made for Comfort Cafe Summer 2009.

I really enjoyed this.  The lavender flavor is subtle, and I might add more next time, since I love the flavor of it.  I made mine in a French press pot.  I used Splenda, with a couple of drops of vanilla extract, and fat-free half and half.  Made for a great mid-morning coffee break.  Made for Comfort Cafe Summer 2009 (Recipe of the Day)
A very tasty way to "fancy up" rice.  Went great with my grilled chicken.  Flavors were great and it added some color to the plate.

A perfect blend of spices.  I made just a half recipe.  Since I was doing them while we were out in the motorhome, and 'fridge space is at a premium, I put the cubed chicken in a Ziploc bag with the marinade overnight, and "skewered" them just before cooking on the portable grill.  Served with rice.  Will be making these again, for sure!

Great combination of flavors and textures.  Great way to get flax seed meal into the diet.  Not too sweet, which lets the banana and pumpkin flavors shine.  And low-fat to boot!  I will try it next time with some chopped walnuts.

Very moist and tasty bread.  I used the brown sugar, but subbed Splenda for the white sugar, and baked a little less time.  I also used the 1 cup whole wheat flour option, and used the wheat germ.  For nuts, I used pecans.  This is a bit high in fat, so won't be making it often (but I don't have zukes around that often, anyway :) )but as a treat this is a great recipe.

This had a great flavor (I used fresh sage) but mine turned out a little heavy, which may be due to having a hard time rolling the dough out into small enough rolls.  I will have to work on my gnocchi techniques :)   I served with a mushroom sauce.

Very easy way to grill a chicken (much easier and less work than my usual rotis method).  Cooking time was right on.  AThe meat was very moist.  I used Recipe #163831 for the rub.  Thanks, Nif, for another great recipe!

Delicious!  I used brown Basmati rice, which is a bit chewier, but the grains  still separate nicely.  I wanted a rice dish that had more flavor to it than plain white rice, but wouldn't detract from my meat dish.  This is it!  Easy recipe and the broth and pine nuts were just the right touch to go with the satays.  Made for Ramadan 2009 tag.

An excellent salad!  I have made a similar one, but not with goat cheese.  That really added a nice flavor.  I used Newman's Own Light Raspberry & Walnut dressing, which was perfect on this.  I am going to try MsSally's suggestion and add some grilled chicken next time.

Wow!  This really has some zip!  I used 1 chipotle with about a tablespoon of the adobe sauce, 1 garlic clove and the juice of the whole lime.  Served with some salsa and chips.  Very easy to put together.
Great potatoes!  I made half the recipe for 2 of us.  Loved the garlic and lemon combo.  Went well with salmon.  Would be a good breakfast potato dish also.  Made for Fall 2009 PAC.

Really refreshing, even on a cool Fall day.  I used dried lavender, but looking forward to trying this during the summer with fresh lavender from my garden.  I used Splenda instead of sugar.  Made for Fall 2009 PAC.

One of the tastiest pot roasts we have had in a long time.  The meat DOES melt in the gravy.  Very tender.  I added some frozen boiling onions and some mushrooms to the crock to cook along with the meat.   Served with roasted red potatoes and baby carrots, and steamed red cabbage.  Great Fall dinner.  Thanks, Janey!

One of the best banana muffins I have tried!  Not too sweet.  I used homemade apple butter.  These turned out moist and very flavorful.  I used the nuts option instead of blueberries.  Made for Fall 2009 My 3 Chefs game.

Very moist and tasty!  I love the texture the oats give them.  I used Splenda brown sugar blend (2 tbls + 2 tsps = 1/3 cup brown sugar)  Used a gala apple which added some extra sweetness to the muffins.  I think I will try this with all apple juice instead of the milk next time, for even more apple flavor.

I loved this and wish I had a piece of pumpkin pie to go with it, as suggested in the description :)  I really love the flavor of molasses so i might be tempted to add a bit more next time.  Made for Partying the Diabetic Way tag game.

This is delicious!  And very easy to make.  The subtle rosemary flavor is very nice.  Also very hearty for not having any meat or vegies other than mushrooms.  Great dinner with a loaf of bread and a small green salad.

Simple, basic mulled cider, but so good.  Just the right amount of spice and fruit and no added sugar!  Did mine in my crockpot on low for about 4 hours.  A nice warmer-upper on a wet Thanksgiving day!

This was the perfect side for the Thanksgiving turkey.  I made it early in the morning and put it in the refrigerator, and then baked it in the countertop convection oven just before dinner.  I made two changes.  I used ricotta for the cream cheese, and added some snipped chives.

A very hearty, filling soup.  I made it a bit healthier by cutting the amount of butter to 1/4 cup and used low-fat milk instead of half-and-half, and it was still plenty rich.  A nice change from our usual turkey-noodle soup.

Tastes like Christmas!  :)  I used a French Press pot and put a cinnamon stick in with the grounds while brewing for more cinnamon flavor, and put a fresh piece in the cup.  The cinnamon and peppermint are very good together.  Go easy on the peppermint extract, as it can be overpowering.  I used a microwave milk frother to "steam and froth" the milk.
Very easy to put together and makes a nice coating for  skinless breasts.  Nice flavor with the almonds and cheese.  I made an extra one to take to work for lunch.
This is a very nice way to dress up plain rice.  Lots of flavor and went well with roast chicken.  Other herb combinations would work well also, like poultry seasoning or Herbes de Provence.

These went together quickly, and are very tasty and chewy.  To make them more diabetic-friendly, I used Splenda for the brown sugar, and agave nectar with a few drops of maple flavoring for the maple syrup.  Worked great.
Made for Sweet Traditions Tag.

Nice, Christmasy flavor!  I just used my regular method of making coffee-French Press Pot-and went from there.  I don't have sweetened cocoa powder, so I used Hershey's baking cocoa and subbed Torani's Vanilla syrup for the vanilla extract to sweeten the coffee..  Recipe doesn't say what kind of mint extract, so I used peppermint, but may try it with spearmint also.

Excellent hummus! I made the Cumin variation, and added sesame oil for half of the olive oil. We like ours thicker, so cut the amount of water in half. (I actually doubled the whole recipe EXCEPT the water, since I was making it for a crowd-it doubled easily.) Served with baked pita chips.  Sprinkled with some paprika before serving.

Great warmer-upper on a very chilly day!  I didn't have the flavored coffee so used instant espresso powder, and hazelnut syrup (left out the brown sugar, since the syrup is sweet).  I love hazelnut flavor in my coffee, but had never added the cocoa before.  Will from now on!  :)

Great comfort food.  Like MarraMamba, Campbell's Tomato Rice was a favorite of mine growing up, and this reminded me of that.  I followed her advice and only used 2 cups of broth, as I like it thicker.  A quick easy dinner on a cold evening after a LONG day at work.  Thanks!
Easy to make and very satisfying!  I left out the vanilla and used Torani's Sugar-free Vanilla Syrup for the sweetener.  Made for Winter 2010 Comfort Cafe.

I wasn't sure about lemon and coffee together, but Annacia has never led me astray, so I tried it, and it is GOOD! I topped mine with a bit of whipped cream, since I used milk instead of creamer (didn't have any). Made for Winter 2010 Comfort Cafe game.
Very easy way to "fancy" up rice.  Flavors are subtle and color is nice.  Great side.

These were easy to make and tasted great.  I used 1/8 cup sugar but would cut that down a bit next time.  I also used fresh rosemary, chopped, since I have it growing year round :)  I liked the texture the cornmeal gives them.  Great with an herbed cheese spread I made.  Would be good with Romano cheese, too, I think.

This really works well, and much less expensive than the ceramic cleaner I usually use, and can never seem to find in the stores when I need it. I used orange oil instead of lemon because my herb and spice shop was out of lemon. Loved the smell it left in the kitchen, and NO vinegar smell either. My stove is older so it will never be completely mark free, and I had boiled something over. This took off much more than I expected it to!

Great cup of coffee, with nothing overpowering.  I used Sumatra, as suggested.  I made mine in a French Press pot, and steeped for about 5 minutes.  Served with milk and agave nectar.   Made for Winter 2010 Comfort Cafe game.
Simple to put together.  I keep most of these ingredients on hand anyway, so can make this up when I need it.  I used buckwheat flour for the barley flour.  Mad pancakes with it and they were great.

These are really tasty.  I used cheddar, but looking forward to trying other cheeses.  For half of the flour, I used Recipe #404288.  The dough was easy to roll out and cut.  Went very well with a bowl of soup.

This was a nice treat for breakfast, served with maple syrup.  I think it would be a great supper recipe, topped with creamed chicken or shrimp, also, since it is not too sweet.  I halved the recipe with no problem (used 3 smaller eggs) and also halved again the amount of butter.

Very rich tasting, and the cocoa was a nice addition.  It helps to crack the cardamom pods a bit before using, to get more flavor from the seeds.  Personally, I really like cardamom, so may use ground next time for more flavor.  A nice comforting cuppa on a cold, dreary afternoon.  Made for Winter 2010 Comfort Cafe game.

This is very easy to put together, since it uses already ground spices.  As stated by previous reviewer, the aroma is terrific.  I used it to coat boneless, skinless chicken breast, which I then baked.  Very tasty!  I think it would be good on pork chops, also.  Made for Winter 2010 Comfort Cafe Recipe of the Day.

Delicious!  I used thighs.  Sauce is really good with just the right amount of "heat".  I did miss-read the recipe though and added a CAN of coconut milk instead of a cup, but it turned out fine (and gave us extra sauce to put on rice).

Very tasty!  I made this for 2 servings, using  3 eggs.  I used white cheddar and an herbal no-salt seasoning blend, as well as the dried onion.  I baked it in a 5"x5"  baking dish for 30 minutes.  Ate half, and taking the other half for lunch!  Thanks for a keeper!
Easy, tasty way to dress up potatoes!  Loved the flavor of the caraway seed.  I halved the recipe and didn't bother peeling the potatoes.  They were great with a pork roast.  Thanks for this keeper!

Quick and easy comfort food dinner!  I subbed ground turkey (dark meat) for the ground beef and also upped the Worcestershire to 1 tsp.  Served with brown gravy and mashed potatoes.  Thanks for a nice, quick weeknight supper!
Very tasty and moist!  I took the suggestion of a previous reviewer and put most of the butter mixture under the skin.  Cooking time was right on.
This does taste like a peanut butter cup!  (I actually made this twice-once with peanut butter and once with almond butter.  Great both ways!)  Made for Winter 2010 Comfort Cafe game.

Excellent!  Made as written, except I got a good deal on chicken breast cutlets, which saved me the step of cutting the breasts in half.  Very easy and quick.  Served with pasta.  Certainly easier than the standard method.  I will be making these again.  Going to try with some tomato based pasta sauce also.  Made for TOP FAVORITES of 2009 COOKBOOKS TAG GAME.

The title says it all--"YUMMY"!  Flavors are very good.  I used it on a small steak.  I misread the the recipe and chopped my onion, but it still worked great as a steak topping.  Will be making this again, to try on a burger or fish!  Made for TOP FAVORITES of 2009 COOKBOOKS TAG GAME.

This is a bit labor intensive and packaged blanched, and slivered  almonds are readily available here.  But if I only need a few for decoration on desserts or garnish on vegies or salads (and don't want to buy a whole bag), I would use this, since I always have whole almonds around.

This is a quick, easy meal that tastes elegant.  I halved the recipe and made it for 1 serving (myself, for a light supper).  Served it on a split, toasted English muffin.  My mother used to make a sauce for salmon loaf that was very much like this (without the bacon).  Brought back memories.  Made for TOP FAVORITES of 2009 COOKBOOKS TAG GAME.

Great texture and flavor.  Loved the addition of the quinoa.  I am going to try flax seed next time.  I also added about 3 tbls. of vital gluten.  Was great with a bowl of soup!  Made for TOP FAVORITES of 2009 COOKBOOKS TAG GAME

Delicious!  I used salami, but am going to try it with ham or bacon also.  I think the cheeses could be varied too.   Great flavors and the sour cream is a nice touch.  Made for TOP FAVORITES of 2009 COOKBOOKS TAG GAME
Delicious!  I didn't add the sugar, because I find carrots to usually be sweet enough, and I doubled the nutmeg.  Very nice change from just steamed carrots.

Delicious potatoes.  I had to cook the potatoes in batches because my steamer is small, so next time I will just boil them like I usually do.  The amount of garlic was just right.  Made for TOP FAVORITES of 2009 COOKBOOKS TAG GAME

Very tasty and moist muffin (for being so low in fat!)  Plenty sweet enough for me (I used Agave Nectar).  I also added about 1/2 teaspoon more cinnamon and another 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg because I like to really taste those two in my muffins.  I used the optional pecans.  Made for TOP FAVORITES of 2009 COOKBOOKS TAG GAME

Delicious!  I used the spice recipes you "linked" in the ingredients list.  The only change I made was using thighs and wings instead of a whole chicken (I left the skin on and skipped the oil)  Wonderful aroma and tender, juicy chicken.
Very tasty blend of spices.  I used in your Recipe #369174, but I think this would be good on fish and on buttered carrots!
I loved the flavor of this rice and it is very easy to put together.   Very good side for roasted chicken.

Another great mac n' cheese from Lori!  This reminds me of the way my grandma used to make it.  I couldn't get my mom to make it with tomatoes because no one else liked it that way but me and grandpa, so grandma would make it when I stayed with them.  I love it!  This is a very rich and creamy dish, and the addition of the cayenne gives it a little snap! I only had 1 cup elbow mac on hand, so added 1 1/2 cup penne also.  I will be making this often!
Very tasty and fresh!  I will leave more of the seeds from the peppers in next time, since we like it hotter.  I also doubled the cilantro.  Simple to make.

I love French toast made with cinnamon or nutmeg and this did not disappoint!  I doubled the amount of milk and skipped the powdered sugar and served with maple syrup.  Great breakfast while we were out in the RV.  Made for Spring 2010 PAC.
