Instead I used canned green beans that I drained and did not have to keep them on the heat long to warm thru so that worked well with the sour cream. Great flavor and so easy and quick to make. Will be making this recipe again as soon as we find some good looking fresh green beans. Made and reviewed for PAC Spring 2013.

Have added this recipe to DH's favorite egg salad sandwich collection. Easy to make and I used real bacon bits that I guestemated for the amount of 6 bacon strips. Not far from the recipe I was taught for making egg salad so knew this would be a hit for us. Made and reviewed for PAC 2013.

We have always had beef stroganoff but sure did enjoy this chicken version. I used chicken tenderloins that I cut into bite size pieces, baby portabella mushrooms, chicken broth for the sherry, and sour cream. Also added some minced garlic and lemon pepper then served over kluski noodles. Easily could  be a full meal by adding some broccoli or spinach and very versatile with the seasonings. Made and reviewed for PAC Spring 2013.

Wonderful mashed potatoes! I used yukon gold potatoes with a bit more cream and butter. Also substituted green onion for a yellow onion for the milder flavor and added frozen corn. Creamy potatoes with a little texture from the corn, very good. Made and reviewed for PAC Spring 2013.

I used english cucumbers with olive oil and enjoyed a very good cucumber salad. The lemon and dill added fresh flavors. Another keeper from out team! Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest event 2014 - Cruisin Culinary Queens.

This definitely is delish! We used ground round, one large red onion, instead of the ketchup used 1/4 cup  tomato sauce, and all my herbs were dry. Served over linquine noodles and loved our supper.Thank you LifeIsGood for sharing! Made and reviewed for Culinary Quest 2014 - Cruisin' Culinary Queen.

DH bought me a new toaster/convection oven and I used that to make the toast. We had nice crunchy toast to add  our tomato topping to. Didnt find a piece of parmesan at the store to grate ourselves so I subbed an italian blend shredded cheese. I made the tomato mixture in the morning and refrigerated then took it out about 1/2 hour before we were ready to eat. This will be our go to recipe for bruschetta. Made and reviewed for the 2014 Culinary Quest - Cruisin' Culinary Queens.

These muffins are amazing! Anyone who enjoys chocolate needs to make these muffins. I used unsalted butter, vanilla extract and the toasted almonds. Didnt have expresso on hand but did have a dark roast that worked great. Definitely a keeper! Made and reviewed for the 2014 Culinary Quest - Cruisin' Culinary Queens.

A very good breakfast scramble that we enjoyed this morning. For the two of us I did halve the recipe and there was more then enough for two good size servings. Since peppers are not DH's favorites I used a larger red pepper, cooked the potato in the microwave, used a red onion and cherry tomatoes instead of a whole tomato. Great flavors, cheesey goodness, and everything you would want in one dish. Chocolatl thank you for sharing this recipe with us! Made and reviewed for the 2014 Culinary Quest - Cruisin' Culinary Queens.

I love soup  and this one was so good! Did use more carrots and celery, only 2 zucchini, and vegetable broth instead of water. Simmered on low for a couple hours then added small macaroni noodles right before serving. A hearty meal for me and will be a favorite soup to make this fall. Made and reviewed for the 2014 Culinary Quest - Family Picks.

I made alfredo sauce years ago but  used salted butter and it tasted like we were eating spoonfuls of salt. Wanted to give this recipe a try but used unsalted butter and it was very good.  Rich and delicious side dish to grilled chicken breast and broccoli. Made for the 2014 Culinary Quest - Family Picks.

I used tea bags instead of loose tea and did add a few lemon slices. Easy to make and a nice change from plain iced tea. Thank you for sharing! Made and reviewed for the 2014 Culinary Quest - Family Picks.

I made this for myself and only enough for two servings and it was pure comfort food. Enjoyed the apples along with the cabbage, used a red onion, and only one tablespoon of brown sugar since I like more tart. Paula I will so make this again! Made and reviewed for the 2014 Culinary Quest - Family PIcks.

Great fruit dip! I used strawberries, bananas that I kept in  chunky pieces, grapes, peaches, and nectarines. Cant wait to make this for a family get together! Made and reviewed for the 2014 Culinary Quest - Family Picks.

Wish I could give these pancakes more then five stars! I used Bisquick baking mix, frozen blueberries, and strawberry jelly. Lemon flavor is spot on for me and the berry topping put these pancakes over the edge. Will make these again! Made and reviewed for the 2014 Culinary Quest - Family Picks.

Making bread or biscuits is not an easy thing for me but this recipe worked out well. I used the food processor and couldnt find biscuit cutters so used a glass about that size. Loved the pepper flavor and how moist and fluffy the biscuits turned out. Made and reviewed for the 2014 Culinary Quest - Family Picks.

After reading the reviews and looking at the photos I decided to double the recipe. Tender beef and vege's in a  nice  gravy. I dont think DH would have liked the pearl onions so I chopped a medium size red onion and added  that. He loves  gravy so I did not thicken mine and served with mashed potatoes. Do want to give those pearl onions a try so will make it again! Made and reviewed for Culinary Quest - 2015.

This coffee is so good! Would be nice for a special celebration or maybe brunch. Added just the nutmeg to the coffee and enjoyed. Will be making this yummy coffee again! Made and reviewed for Culinary Quest 2015.

Great meal and loved it was one dish! I did double this recipe because we enjoy leftovers. Very flavorful and will make this again instead of my recipe.  :)  Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2015.

BBQ, bacon, and pork chops what more can be said!   :)  My DH  was in heaven! He did grill the chops and I didnt have fresh rosemary so I added a sprinkle or two  of dried to the bbq sauce. Made the six pork chops for two us so we could enjoy leftovers too. Charmie we will be making these again! Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest .

My DH loves deviled eggs and I like trying new recipes for him to taste. These eggs were a big hit with him and I also enjoyed one or two.   :) I used a package of real bacon bits that were chopped into small pieces instead of frying bacon. The honey mustard was a nice touch with the mayo, I used Hellman's mayo,  and sharp cheddar cheese added a little zing.  Next time might try dijon or a grainy mustard instead of the honey mustard. Congrats for winning the Football Pool breezermom!

A very nice change of pace from our typical sandwich spreads. Had a ham on rye sandwich and loved it! Cant wait to use it on burgers and anything else I can find. Will be making again breezermom thank you for posting. Made and reviewed for the For Your Consideration tag game.

We had some warm sunny days in November and this coffee was so enjoyed! Always have chocolate syrup in the fridge and will now be  keeping the ice cream in the freezer. Added the whipped cream and cinnamon, love cinnamon, and it added a nice hint of flavor. If you love iced coffee and chocolate definitely give this  a try! Made and reviewed for the Football Pool 2015-2016.

All I had been wanting was a basic soup with no bells and whistles and this one was terrific.  I used a frozen bag of the Steamer  broccoli, red onion, and did use a tad less basil. Also used my immersion blender and left the soup chunkier. Super easy to make, guilt free, and great tasting soup. Made and reviewed for the Football Pool 2015-2016.

The hubby loves floats/shakes so made this  as a surprise treat for him. Had a bit of trouble finding the fudge ripple ice cream but it was well worth the effort. We loved using Cherry Coke with the fudge ripple ice cream, reminded us of a chocolate covered cherry.    :) Definitely add the whipped cream and cherry to top. Made and reviewed for the For Your Consideration recipe tag game.

I very much enjoyed this soup! Used Great Northern beans, turkey bacon and the chicken that comes in the packet like tuna does. Didnt have the bacon grease so I added olive oil to saute the vegetables in. Instead of the cayenne pepper I added a pinch of red pepper flakes. Couldnt wait for the soup to get done as it smelled delicious and it tasted just as good! Light, simple, and flavorful soup I enjoyed for lunch. When finished dieting will make this again with real bacon. Thank you for sharing LIF! Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2016 - Azores required.

Terrific chicken and the pineapple salsa was great. I only added a pinch or two of red pepper flakes, took the seeds out of the jalapeno and used parsley instead of cilantro. Marinated the chicken for 8 hours and made salsa 1/2 hour before grilling chicken. Enjoyed a bite of chicken with every bite of salsa! Easy and quick supper to make on a hot humid day. Thank you for sharing! Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2016 - Bahamas.

Orange and pineapple are great flavor combinations and adding the yogurt makes this a creamy fresh tasting smoothie. I did not need to add the water with the juice from the pineapples. Easy and refreshing! Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2016 - Bahamas.

DD loves tropical flavored drinks so we made this for her using Malibu Rum. We had to take a sip or two to make sure it was just right, LOL, and it was! All it needed was a a little umbrella and ocean view. A fav for sure! Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2016 - Bahamas.

Couldnt find yellow sweet potatoes but wanted to try this recipe so I used yams and loved them. Used half and half instead of whipping cream and whipped everything together with my electric hand mixer. Put the potatoes back in a pot to heat thru before serving. If I ever spot yellow sweet potatoes will have to try them too. Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2016 - Bahamas.

Nice change from tuna with mayo! I had romaine salad mix on hand and diced up some green pepper to add instead of the jalapeno. The orange and lime brightened up the tuna and made this a refreshing salad I enjoyed for lunch. Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2016 - Bahamas.

Very good chicken! We used chicken breasts and bbq'ed on the gas grill. To go along with the lemon flavors already in the marinade I added lemon pepper instead of black and a couple shakes of celery seed, my all time favorite. Easy to put together and the chicken is great. Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2016 - Greece.

I wish I could give a higher star rating for this fantastic salad! This is very easy to put together but the flavors sure make you think it was much harder. Served after being in the refrigerator for about 1/2 hour with grilled chicken. Cant wait to make this again! Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2016 - Greece.

I used two packages of chicken tenderloins and bought an extra lemon or two, love lemon flavors. Marinated about 2 1/2 hours and cut the lemon wedges larger so they would stay on the skewers better. Hubby grilled until just beginning to get a char on the chicken then removed. These kabobs are simple, quick and very tasty! Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2017 - Turkey.

Just say stuffed cabbage and I am there! My aunt made stuffed cabbage as far back as I can remember and it was always served with mashed potatoes and cucumbers with sour cream. I didnt boil the cabbage leaves or use tooth picks so my cabbage rolls didnt look as nice as the photos shown. Used a cast iron dutch oven to cook them on the stove checking the pot every so often. The house smelled yummy and I couldnt wait for them to be ready. Very good cabbage rolls the only thing I would do different is season the meatball mixture a bit more. Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2017 - Austria

Wonderful mashed potatoes! I did mash mine by hand and liked the bit of tang from the creme fraiche. I forgot whole milk so I had to use skim but it didnt make a difference to the flavor. Served with cabbage rolls, cucumber salad and pumpernickel rolls. Cant ask for a better meal! Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2017 - Austria.

What an easy and great tasting potato salad. The fresh dill smelled amazing and added to the sour cream made a very welcome change from mayo based potato salads. I added the salt and pepper to the potatoes lightly then adjusted after adding the dressing. Served with Linky's tuna salad and sliced tomatoes. Thank you MamiJ for sharing! Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2017 - Austria.

Wonderful muffins! Not overly sweet so the flavor of the fresh berries can be enjoyed. I love cinnamon and nutmeg flavors so I used a bit less sugar for the topping. Enjoyed with a cup of tea for breakfast and for a late afternoon snack. Will definitely make these muffins again! Made and reviewed for the Culinary Quest 2017 - Wales.

What can I say? Just wonderful. The whole house was filled with the fragrance of the spices, the finished curry was yummy to say the least and indeed even better the next day. The garam masala I always use is of the "hot" kind and I was a little afraid that it would "kill" the rest of the spices. Not to worry, it went very well together. Was also worried that the curry would be too dry with just one can of chopped tomatoes as liquid. On the contrary, just enough sauce to mix with the rice. I should not worry so much.........it turned out perfect! This will certainly be made again. Thanks for posting.

I used 1/2 of a 12 oz. bag of frozen mixed brocolli, carrots, sugar snap peas, and water chestnuts.  These veggies went really well with the sauce.  Bf and I both thought the veggies got slightly overcooked though.  My sauce didn't thicken up either, and I even added 1tbsp cornstarch/1tbsp cold water.  I started off with 8 mins covered on med-high, 7 or so mins uncovered with the slurry mixed in.  When the veggies were getting overcooked, but sauce didn't thicken, I just gave up and served.  We had this with white rice.  Bf said "pretty good and pretty spicy".  I said "almost too spicy" and he said "no way!"  Personally this was just on the verge of being too sweet/too spicy for me.  We both did like this dish though, and bf's been looking forward to it since I showed him the recipe last night. :)  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.  Thanks for sharing Michelle!

Oh wow, wow, yummy, yummy, quick, flavorful, and did I mention yummy? I had to make a couple changes. I was only able to afford cooked tail-on, deveined frozen large shrimp (the 1lb bag was on sale). I decided to halve this recipe. While thawing the shrimp in a strainer, I snapped off the tails. I used 1/2 tsp paprika for approx 1/2 lb shrimp. I used 2 tsp jarred, minced garlic for the fresh. For the wine, I got one of those mini bottles of white wine (Sutter Home Chardonnay) and used 1/4 cup. I used a pinch of salt and a couple pinches black pepper. Instead of lemon wedges, I added 1 tsp of lemon juice along with the shrimp to the reduced wine mixture. I used the amt of olive oil called for and for the butter, I used the same amt called for, but used Smart Balance with Flaxsweed OIl spread. I also added 1tsp dried parsley flakes a few mins before the shrimp was removed from heat. I cooked the shrimp for several mins so it could steep in the sauce, even though they were already fully cooked. I'm really glad I made the full amt of "sauce". I served this atop recipe #256215 for a very quick and flavorful supper. I would definitely make this again! Bf seemed to enjoy it, also. I made this for Please Review My Recipe. Thanks for sharing, Bird! Shrimp Scampi is one of my all-time fave dishes, so this will be a happy addition to my faves cookbook.

Yay, a potato salad safe for my sensitive IBS!  I used 2 small and 1 medium Russet, which I peeled (I love potato peel, but it's safer for my IBS w/o it) and cut the potatoes into chunks and boiled.  I forgot I was going to halve the dressing ingredients, so I used a slotted spoon to serve b/c the full amt of dressing was too much for the lesser amt of potatoes.  Bf thought this was okay and gives it 3 stars.  I tnought it was a very unique potato salad; light and refreshing and tasty.  The flavor was unique.  I'm overriding bf's 3 stars to give this 5, lol.  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.  Thanks for sharing Maito!  I will make this again, even if it's just for myself. :)

Ohhhh how cool is this?  I have been wanting to try nutritional yeast for months now, and when I saw this recipe, I thought it would be a great way to try it for the first time.  I love all the seasonings here, and I love popcorn.  I opted to use chili powder instead of curry.  I don't have a way to make air-popped so I had to make my popcorn on the stove with a bit of canola oil.  I also didn't have olive oil flavored spray, but had I Can't Believe It's Not Butter Spray.  The nutritional yeast on this even smelled cheesy after I sprinkled it on the popcorn!  It tasted quite good with all the other seasonings and had a cheesy-ish flavor, too.  Definitely a keeper in my book.  Thanks so much for sharing, Sharon! :)  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.

WOW, first peanut butter cake I ever made.and CB is right, the frosting really makes this over the top amazing.  My bf didn't feel like trying this, so none of this is his opinion, lol.  I was going antsy waiting for this cake to cool.  It took 20 mins exactly in my oven.  I halved this recipe since it's just 2 of us and bf doesn't really like cake, no matter what kind it is, though I thought I'd have tempted him with peanut butter... ah well.  I love PB, and I used Jif Creamy.  For my dietary needs I replaced whole egg with Eggbeaters and the milk with Unsweetened Organic Soy Milk from Fresh & Easy Market brand, and used Smart Balance with Flaxseed Oil for the butter.  This was light and peanut-buttery rich.  I'm really glad I stayed up late to make this.  Hope this will be just as good after being refrigerated (since the whole thing is frosted).  I'm not a frosting fan, so I quartered the frosting ingredients and it was the perfect amount for a thin glaze over an 8x8 cake.  Tyvm for sharing this CB!  HokiesLady had made this and I'm recipenapping it for NZ/Aussie March Swap #14.  Hope the hosts don't mind, i know it's past midnight RZ time, but I'm going to try to sneak it in anyway. :D  ETA:  Btw, this cake tastes fantastic from the fridge, too!  I also sprinkled some chopped nuts over the frosting, yum! :)

Yummy!  I accidentally melted too much butter, so this was a bit moister than intended, but still tasty, crispy, and easy to make.  In place of the butter, I did use Smart Balance Light spread.  I used lots of pepper and just a little salt, also served this with some chopped green onions on top.  Mmm, thanks for sharing Syd.  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.

Bf and I both love coleslaw so we were excited to try this new twist.  I modified the recipe a bit by using half a 16oz package of coleslaw mix made of green cabbage and carrots (too bad no red cabbage though), used 2 slices of bacon, and got lazy and didn't chop my salted peanuts.  We have a profusion of mayo so I used 1/4 cup light mayo and halved the rest of the ingredients.  We were both disappointed by the coleslaw but it was still very tasty.  Thanks for sharing Shelby Jo! :)  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.

Quite yummy and don't know why I hadn't thought of this before.  All I had on hand was Quick-Cooking and Jif Creamy, so that's what I used.  I microwaved for 1 min 30 secs.  This was sticky, but flavorful.  I also added a little bit of Rice Dream Rice Milk.  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.  Thanks for sharing, Brooke. :)

Syd this was so, but bf had two complaints; marinate the chicken longer and more dressing!  I halved the recipe, made exactly as directed except I only had canola oil and I had marinated the chicken for almost 1 1/2 hours (apparently bf still wanted it marinated longer).  I grilled on my George Foreman.  I used a Parisian Salad blend from the produce department and added some extra carrots to it.  Very yummy, well-liked by both of us.  Thanks for sharing. :)  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.  I will make this again, for sure (with the bf's suggestions).

This is one of my fave flavor combos for smoothies; but I tend to forgo the ice and use frozen fruit.  I used the orange juice (added a bit more than a splash though), frozen unsweetened strawberries, banana slices that I had frozen while fresh.  This created a slushy cold smoothie that tasted great, even if it was a cold morning!  Thanks for sharing mersaydees; I will make this again.  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.

OMG!  So glad I found this recipe; actually I found more than one, but decided to try this one.  I was craving chocolate cake but did not want to bake a whole one or even a bunch of chocolate cupcakes.  I had never heard of this mug cake thing before.  For dietary reasons, I used 1/4 cup Eggbeaters for the egg and unsweetened applesauce for the oil, and Silk Unsweetened Soy Milk for the regular milk, following the rest of the recipe as directed.  I had to use a cereal bowl instead of a mug as I don't have large mugs.  Cereal bowl worked out great!  Cake smelled wonderful, only needed 3 mins cook time as directed,  It rose slightly but did not need to worry about overflow, though I had wax paper down.  I let cool for 5 mins.  I ate after 10 mins so cake was still warm.  This is very dense, spongy, but still delicious!  Normally I like a lighter textured cake, but this had just the right feeling of cake plus pudding or cake plus sauce or something that I enjoyed it a lot.  Surprisingly the bottom was moist like a sauce sort of.  Maybe the few choc chips I used sunk?  I was worried the shape of a cereal bowl would cause uneven cooking, but I didn't have a problem (it was a stoneware bowl from Corelle).  This mug cake is best eaten warm imo b/c I think it will toughen up if you let it cool off.  I did add about a tbsp of dairy-free semisweet choc chips.  I didn't have walnuts.  This ended up being a nice chocolate fix for me.  Thanks so much for sharing.  I will be making again for sure.  Oh, I have to add this cake is almost better for sharing with 2 people.  I feel stuffed and this cake wouldn't really save well for later.

Even though I was only cooking for 2, my pork chops were really thick, so I kept the amounts the same.  Followed this recipe to a T.  I used 1/2 tsp cayenne which was the perfect amount of heat for me.  First thing my bf said when he tasted this was, "Spicy."  Heh.  He said this was pretty good, but I enjoyed it a lot.  The sauce is excellent over white rice and the veggies are between tender-crisp and tender.  I am very glad you posted this recipe here, thanks!  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.

First time ever trying/cooking something like this.  I heard this was called Bubble and Squeak because of the sound it makes while cooking? Lol.  Not sure if mine quite did that, other than sizzle.  Okay so anyway I had about 2 1/2 cups worth of mashed veg (roughly mashed since the veg I had weren't mushy-tender, just tender and they didn't mash up well).  I halved the cumin and chili flakes (used crushed red pepper for the chili flakes).  Heated oil on med-high, mixed in seasonings, added veg, forgot to stir the veg in the oil just shook the pan a bit to distribute the oil in along bottom of pan, smashed veg down and checked them every few minutes.  Full cook time for mine was about 10 mins on med-high and a few extra on medium.  This was browned nicely on the one side.  I am glad I halved the spices, cuz this was spicy!  I like medium heat and halving the spices was perfect for my tastes.  My veg were some broccoli, a little celery, onion, and mostly potatoes and carrots.  Yes I did cook these ahead of time on purpose to try this recipe. :D  I used chicken bouillon and water to make a broth to cook the veg in, cooled, strained, refrigerated a day or so before making this.  Thank you for sharing, Noo, I was surprisingly pleased by this dish and will make again next time I have leftover veg.  Made for Please Review My Recipe Tag Game.

Syd, this one was another winner for me.  I used approx 1/2 lb of baby carrots which I sliced in half lengthwise (in fourths lengthwise if the baby carrot was very tick).  I halved the rest of the ingredients.  After this cooled off I took a bite, and oh wow, what an addictive way to munch carrots.  I can't wait to see how they turn out later but I don't doubt they'll be fantastic then too. :D  Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.  I'll be making thees again for sure.  Thanks for sharing, Syd!

This is a good sandwich. I made one for my husband and myself with just a few slices of sourdough instead of with a whole loaf. I did have to substitute smoked gouda for the swiss. I would make this again and in fact spoke with my SIL about making for my brothers birthday next month. Thanks Annacia - Hill Family

I made this and never told DH it was lowfat. He was talking about how good it was etc ... I finally had to tell him and he said in that case he would have another piece. I made a few changes just based on what I had on hand. I used 1/3 low fat philly cream cheese and 3 eggs instead of the egg beaters. The top did feel a bit funny when it came out of the oven but tasted fine. This recipe also made more then even a larger then normal crust. So I will whip a few little cheesecakes up later. Thanks for a great dessert.
This was great ... DH made it so it has to be fairly easy as well.  We will be having this again especially when we have a crowd for breakfast.

We enjoyed these with dinner. They had great flavor. I baked them for 45 min and then DH started the meat on the grill so in the intrest of having everything on the table at the same time I microwaved them. AHH I know but what else could I do. They were crisp enough though because of the baking. The only change I would make is toss the potates in half the butter and then sprinkle the seasoning on.
These were pretty good ... I had to add a little bit more flour as they kept tearing when folding. We served these with a peach compote and drizzled the syrup on top. Thanks for a good breakfast.
These made a great lunch for us. We used to go out for meatball sammies ... not anymore. Thanks
This was a tasty breakfast for the family this morning. I used frozen peaches so I didn't use ice cubes. I like a sweeter smoothie so after DH and DD took thiers I added a bit of peach syrup to mine.
This was a good lunch ... I left out the corn due to personal taste, added a bit of salsa and a bit more cheese. We also served with "Recipe#186675" because we always seem to have some on hand.

Mine turned out more like pancakes then pattycakes. My dough was also very wet and not rollable. I coated them with peach syrup and ate them for breakfast. The really great thing is that they hold together like a cake or cookie so my 15 month old could hold one in her hand and eat it. I will make these again because they tasted great.
We enjoyed these for breakfast this morning. They even held together good enough for a lunch snack with peanut butter and jelly - rolled up.
This was pretty good. I only used 1 banana as it tasted right and I didn't want to add the other banana and have it over power the drink. Thanks for a good smoothie everyone enjoyed this morning.

I love chicken cordon blue but I rarely make it because it is such a pain in the butt ... but not anymore! Thanks to this recipe I will be making it alot more often. This was not only easy but the taste was excellent. Thanks for making my life at dinner time just a bit easier.

This was good. I didn't have any green pepper so I added a bit of parsley for color. I also forgot to make it last night so made it this morning - it had to bake longer because of that I think. Anyway, this was a good breakfast.
What a great salad. This tasted like it came from a deli. I used my own olive mix and used spiral pasta instead of penne but other then that follwed the recipe to a T!!

These were good little cookies that were easy to whip up. I had chocolate frosting I wanted to use up so I frosted the cookies and pressed another one on top for a cookie sandwich. Thanks for a great snack.

This made for a great breakfast - it kind of tasted like french toast only better. I added 1 tsp of vanilla extract and had to add just a bit more baking mix to have a ball form up. Turned out I only needed one apple. I drizzled some of the sugar and cinnamon mix from the bottom of the bowl that held the apples over the top prior to baking. So good ... DH enjoyed it as well - said it wasn't too sweet. Thanks

I thought these tasted pretty good. I did the garlic and herb variation. I could have added more garlic to suit my tastes but others in the house don't like it nearly as much as I do. I like the idea that you could make these to bake later - I didn't do that but its great to have an option. Don't forget to add a bit of salt and pepper

I thought this was ok - kinda dry even though I added 1/2 cup applesauce instead of oil and added a half pint of peaches. DH and DD ate just as is with a bit of milk. I pour some hot peach syrup over the top.
I am always looking for ways to use whole wheat flour in lieu of ap. This is a great way to do just that. The only sub I made was to use Romano cheese instead of parm. Thanks for the good biscuits.
OMG - this is so delish. I will be making this alot. The only change I made was to add some cooked bacon - kind of a BLT. The leftovers were great too!

I am not sure what happened but these didn't turn out well for me at all. My dough was pretty wet to start with so I added an extra bit of flour. I ended up with 12 very buttery soggy muffins and that was after cooking for a bit longer and turning them out on a paper towel to soak up a bunch of the butter. I tasted the crust that was done and could tell these have great flavor I am just not sure what went wrong - we ended up throwing them out. I will try these again and update my review.

GREAT!! I amended it a bit to make it a one pot meal. I cooked and cubed up 3 chicken breasts, sauted 1/2 cup onion and 2 garlic cloves and used half mozzarella cheese. I knew I had french fried onion rings but didn't find them until it was too late - so no onion rings. Oh and I used a roasted red bell pepper - yummy!! I liked that the broccoli was soft and the celery a bit crunchy and oh the sauce. I think this would be great too with water chestnuts!! Thanks for a great dinner!

We thought this was pretty bland - spiced up it could be pretty good. It was super easy though. I baked it in a 11x7 but would recommend a 9X13 to thin it out just a bit. We topped this with a peach rum sauce and peaches.
This worked great - DH wanted to just get a new shower head but this saved it. I also used this on the sprayer in the kitchen. Thanks

This was a good down home dinner. It is also lower in fat then your traditional pot pie. I subbed celery for mushrooms and reduced the liquid just a bit. I also sneaky chefed the mashed potatoes with pureed zucchini and no one could see it under the pot pie sauce! Thanks for a good dinner. Update: Had this with rice today for leftovers - better then last night!!
This was a tasty little sandwich - I liked the addition red onion but used mayo instead of miracle whip and smoky cheddar instead of American.
MMMM ... I used regular yogurt and frozen peaches. So good.  This has endless possibilities - thanks

We also loves smoothies and this one doesn't disappoint. We had this just as written the first day except used frozen strawberries and agave nectar. Then the next day I didn't have enough strawberry yogurt so I used raspberry - good as well. Thanks
Yummy! I froze some of the pineapple so no ice cubes and used oj instead of water.  Very nice smoothie - thanks

This is a great way to spice up some cider. I used 4 cups cider and 4 cups fresh apple juice. I didn't have cinnamon but did have homemade cinnamon applesauce so I used that is lieu of the cinnamon and apple. The only thing I had to do when serving was to strain :) Thanks for a great drink we will make again
I like a sweet coffee so I upped the caramel and cream a bit but DH had just as listed. We both went back for seconds - Thanks

Great tuna salad. I added a bit of crushed garlic and ranch dressing mix - the dry stuff. I only eat tuna salad on toast but never thought of adding butter - mmmm. I didn't use lettuce but instead chips under the bread. Thanks for a tasty lunch

This is a great little idea and tasty at that. It does need to be left overnight Dh decided to whip this up the morning of and the eggs didn't quite set up and we had to cook it quite a bit longer. We will try this again and let it set overnight. We really liked this.
MMM good smoothie. The only change I made was to add a bit of flax oil.

I have always sprinkled cinnamon on top of my french toast but never thought of adding it to the batter. It was a great addition. I made two changes I used sprouted cinnamon raisin bread and I didn't have powdered sugar so I spread a thin layer of royal icing on top - mmmm good.
This was fairly tasty. I used homemade pie filling and used 1/4 cup dried cranberries and 1/4 cup raisins. I plan on trying it with frozen chopped cranberries. Thanks for a tasty dessert
I ended up using snowman shaped marshmellows and milk chocolate. They turned out cute and were not only tasty just to eat but great in hot chocolate and coffee.
We liked these - the kids were so so on them. I made as directed only cut the recipe in half. I agree with another reviewer not worth the extra calories.

We had this tonight and made as directed except we used a bit of old bay and white pepper. I didn't have onion powder so I left that out. I used San Joaquin Gold cheese which add a lot of flavor. We loved this and the kids ate without question. Thanks

We loved this! By the time I went to make this the spinach had gone bad so we had to leave that out and no raspberry vinegar so I used rice vinegar and fresh raspberries. We will defiantly have this again.

I had to make a few changes based to things I had on hand. I used Coppa and prosciutto instead of salami. I also used San Juan Parmesan cheese instead of fontina cheese. I didn't have milk so I added another egg and no bread so I used 1/2 cup bread crumbs. I also didn't have any green olives and I really wish that I would - next time I will make sure I have some as I think it would benefit from that flavor. I didn't have white wine vinegar so I used red wine garlic vinegar. Even with all these changes these were great. Thanks
The only substitute was the cheese, I had parmesan but no romano.  I baked them for 30 minutes at 325 and they came out tender and tasty.  Thanks.

I had to adjust this recipe for two people and one very large chicken breast.  I only made one half of the Essence and sprinkled the rest over everything while it simmered.  It was served over garlic noodles, DH's not fond of rice!  I also used mini-crimini mushrooms, yum.  It was quite spicy but wonderful.  I will make this again and again and even with the rice!

This is wonderful.  I didn't have any dijon, white wine vinegar or green onions so I substituted with 2T yellow mustard, 1T of cider vinegar and minced sweet onion.  The taste is fantastic.  Next time I'm at the store I'll pick up the real ingredients and make it again.  Thank you.
These were the best leftovers!  I used smoked paprika and added some chopped red pepper for color.  Will make this one again.  Thanks.
The pepper gave an interesting kick mixed with the honey.  My DH loved this.  Thanks for a great recipe.

I used this recipe for recipe #19305, spinach spoon bread.  I will never buy a box of jiffy mix again!  I did cut back the sugar to 2T but it still seemed too sweet so next time I'll use only 1T. Now I want to make some muffins!  Thanks

I had my doubts about this with no flour to bind it all together.  Made it as written and they were wonderful.  I did add one teaspoon of ground chia, (trying to use it up).  I stored them in the fridge, they lasted us about a week and  the flavor and texture seemed to improve.  Thanks for a tasty and healthy snack.
I really like this recipe. Had to use chicken broth and I added a medium chopped onion, out of habit I guess.  Thanks for a great healthy meal.
Great fish.  No fish stock but chicken stock worked just fine.  I used a mixture of red and green peppers which gave the sauce a beautiful reddish tint.  Thanks.

I halved the recipe as I was only cooking two chops.  Only sub was red wine vinegar in place of the balsamic vinegar which I did not have.  It's on my grocery list now as we love this recipe.  Next time I will make the full amount of marinade and cook it down so I have some leftover sauce to pour over the chops.  I'm going to try this with chicken.  Thanks for a great, easy recipe.  Ok I tried this on chicken and it's even better than on the pork if that's possible!  DH loved it.
What a wonderful and easy recipe.  I used the Montreal seasoning and mixed everything together to marinate before cooking.  This is a  great change.  thanks.

I'm impressed!  My DH doesn't really care for Asian but my kids loved it so I always had a bottle in the fridge and one in the pantry.  They have left home so I found myself with no hoisin, first time in 20 years.  I couldn't believe it!  I just made this up and it is fantastic.  I used black bean sauce, bead molasses and rice wine vinegar.  Without the peanut better for sweetness I added 1T brown sugar.  It was perfect.  Thank you.  Can't wait to spring this on my kids when they visit.
Another convert here!  This was simple and the results were amazing.  This will be my party plate from now on.  Thanks.

All I can say is wow!  I used vidalia onions, some roasted garlic that I needed to use up and omitted the salt.  DH is on a low salt diet so the parmesan really was sufficient.  Ths would be good with chopped tomatoes but the cherry tomatoes are prettier.  Thanks for a great recipe.
I marinated the steaks overnight and this did come out great.  The coffee is magical!  Thanks for a great marinade.
We really enjoyed this recipe.  I used a panko/breadcrumb mixture, and thyme, rosemary and chives for the flavors.  Thanks for an easy and quick dinner!
Wow!  I used some roasted garlic form the freezer and added shrimp.  I'm in love.  Thanks for an easy comfort meal.

I'm guilty of adding sliced vidalias and some left over mushrooms.  We really enjoyed the flavor, the soy sauce gave a unique taste.  The spinach I used was rather old and seemed tough so I will try this again using that baby spinach.  Thanks.

What a wonderful hummus!  I was so eager to make this that I used garbanzo beans instead of cannellini as that was what I had in the pantry.  My basil is thriving and I was looking for uses.  I'll make this again and freeze some for my DH who loves hummus.  Thank you for a great recipe.

This was wonderful.  I used sour cream as I didn't have yogurt and powdered garlic as my fresh was kind of old and I didn't want a bitter taste.  I also had trouble with the water ratio but it was nothing I couldn't fix!  I want to make small bread bowls for soup with this recipe.  I used roasted red and green which gave it beautiful color.  Thanks.
We really enjoyed these potatoes.  DH went back for seconds!  I used sweet onions which sweetened the dish, next time I'll use regular onions.  Thanks.

This reminds me of the patties my Mom used to make!  The green onions are a nice color addition.  I did not have regular Monterey Jack cheese but I did have hot pepper cheese.  Wow,  DH loved them.  Thanks for a versatile recipe.
Thank you for a great side dish.  My kitchen smelled wonderful and the dish tasted even better!

This was so easy!  Will agree with other reviews regarding the salt.  I did not add any as we are low salt and it was plenty salty!  the peppers were fantastic and gave the dish a unique flavor.  than you.
This turned out wonderful ribs!  For the first time I had no leftovers for breakfast.  Thanks.
We enjoyed this recipe.  I added sliced vidalia onions and used chicken bullion.  thank you

I used this marinade on a split cornish hen for dinner tonight and it was fantastic.  I marinated the hen in 1/2 of the marinade, reserving the rest for basting.  Will try this again on chicken pieces and use the glaze.  Thanks.
Quick and easy, just my style.  we enjoyed this.
I really enjoyed this recipe.  I had to make some additions, sliced peppers and mushrooms so they would not spoil.  The flavore blended beautifully and were better the next day.  Thank you.
We enjoyed this easy recipe.  With our low salt diet I forgot to add the sugar so it was quite salty for us but tasty none the less!  thanks

Picked some fresh sprouts just for this recipe, it well worth the effort!  I did omit the salt because I used beef bullion which was plenty salty.  Also added some sliced button mushrooms.  I cooked them uncovered and the liquid reduced beautifully giving the sprouts almost a glaze.  Thanks

This was a great way to have a low-fat mocha at home!  It tasted almost like the coffee shop varieties. A very rich treat...almost not sugary enough for me though. I used instant decaf coffee only because it's night time and I didn't have any ground decaf around. I read a review of this recipe and just had to make it pronto.  :)
I really enjoyed these, although they were a bit time consuming to make.  I added red pepper to mine. It was a great change of pace for dinner.  Thanks!
WHOA!  These are crazy good.  I took them to a Memorial Day gathering and we all enjoyed them a lot.  I only came home with about 5 bars left.  :)  These will become a favorite for us!
Really delicious, especially on a 90 degree day!  I had never made sweet tea before.  My kids seem to love it (I made a decaf version).

These are tasty muffins. I think the flavor of the black pepper is subtle, but then I love black pepper. I like muffins that are a little more moist, though, but these are good served with a comforting bowl of soup. I only had to bake mine for 25 minutes, but I might decrease that time to 20 and maybe that will help make them more moist. Made for Photo Swap! Thanks Bonnie!
Delicious and easy! I love finding great recipes for the crock pot and this is definitely one of them! I will make this again definitely.
Delish! These are the easiest apple dumplings I've ever made and they are equally delicious! I made exactly as stated and served warm with ice cream.
Quick and tasty! These are just wonderful and so easy to make. I made my own self-rising flour and it worked out well. I will be making these again.

This is a great combination! I never thought of putting kielbasa and pasta together, but this really works well. I thought it was just delicious and my family enjoyed it as well. It's a great use of kielbasa!

These are really good and a great way to have a light dessert. I believe they are only 1-2 Weight Watchers points when made into mini-muffins. These are very chocolaty and it's hard to believe they are light! I have also made these with a spice cake mix, pumpkin pie filling and some raisins. A great treat!

I knew this recipe would not disappoint me. I love chocolate and coffee and I know they are both great together. I made this for my DH and I and he really loved it and he is not a big chocolate lover.
Very good, easy and refreshing. This will be really good on a hot day!
What a wonderful dressing and so easy to make. I can't wait to make this when tomatoes are in season!

I think this could use more broth - it was too thick for us. It also could use a little more seasonings. I didn't think it was all that spicy. I used the cheese tortellini. I bet the mushroom kind would be wonderful, but I couldn't find that in my store. Good luck in the contest!

I loved these simple-to-make but oh-so-delicious biscuits! They can be addicting! I loved everything about them - the pecans, the gouda cheese and the kick from the cayenne pepper. I made these several times throughout the contest period so that is definitely a winner in my book! Good luck!

This is a 5-star recipe for me all the way! I've already made it several times during the contest period. It is a very tasty and filling breakfast. It is so simple to make and turns out great. The corn tortillas are a nice touch, I think, but I might like them better crunchy and sprinkled on top when serving. The gouda cheese made the eggs extra creamy. This has a nice little bite to it, but not too much for the morning. I didn't serve it with the optional garnishes because I prefer my eggs with no additional toppings. I think this is a versatile recipe to play around with; sausage or bacon would be nice substitutes for the ham. I bet this recipe does very well in the contest! Good luck, Chef, and thanks for a great recipe!

This recipe was OK for us. We are relatively new to sun-dried tomatoes until this contest, but I don't think we really cared for them in this dish. I couldn't really taste the gorgonzola cheese in this so I think it could be omitted. I did like the addition of pancetta, though, and the croutons. They both were a nice touch! Good luck!

This is definitely a 5-star recipe! I loved this sandwich. I am not a big fan of mustard, but I will eat it in small doses. The Gouda cheese melted perfectly after about 10 minutes in my oven and it went so well with all of the ingredients in this sandwich. This is now one of my favorite ways to prepare chicken! It is sooo good. The sauce is just amazing. I will be making this one often! Thanks for posting!
This is wonderful! A great combination and one I will make again. Thanks for sharing!

What a wonderful treat this makes! I love that it is only 2 points for Weight Watchers and that it is sooo good. I love to watch my calories and fat anytime possible so this is great! Thanks for sharing.

Rich, creamy, smooth and delicious! This recipe is exactly what you want in an alfredo sauce. Alfredo sauce is one of my favorite things to order and to make and this one is now my all-time favorite. This is a wonderfully versatile recipe: it's simple, one pot, flavorful. The ingredients should be in your pantry, so this can be a last minute decision. You can vary the spice intensity, or choose to vary the spices (I followed the directions exactly, so I can really rate the recipe as written). You can vary the texture, by how long you choose to simmer the chickpeas or by using a spoon to crush some. Best of all, once you know your own stovetop, so you know how much time you'll need for all the water to be absorbed), this recipe takes no real attention or effort. 

Oh, and the taste is wonderful -- even my son, not a great veggie eater, asked for seconds for this one.

Definitely a keeper ... and a recipe that I will use frequently.

BTW, if you want to save a little more money, but plan a little in advance ... soak dried chickpeas overnight instead of using canned.

But once assembled you can forget about it. The aroma as this is cooking had my teenage son almost drooling over the oven. Thanks for the recipe.

Loved this. I did add some extras though. I started by cooking some diced onion in beef broth(water with a half knorr beef cube), then added diced jalapeno and red pepper. I added the rice and added a little sesame oil in place of the bacon drippings. The green onions give this a wonderful flavour and colour.  I made this twice today. the second time I added frozen green peas, but I think corn would be good too. My teenage son ate the leftovers in a flash, declaring them excellent. This is easy to make and the amount of soy sauce is perfect. Thanks for the recipe
This was a very fast stew to put together. I doubled up on the veggies I liked and left out the turnip. Thanks for the recipe.
I made as written. This is an excellent soup and very easy to make. Thanks for the recipe.

This is wonderful. I did not feel like peeling apples so I grated them instead. I made as written otherwise. It is easy to make and has a wonderful tart flavour explosion when you bite into a cranberry. This was gone in one ight when I made it. Thanks for the recipe.

I made this with steak and then with pork the next day. My family went crazy for this. They loved it with both types of meat, but preferred the pork. It is easy to make and so very good. Thanks for this wonderful recipe.

My family loved these. I used only 
1 tsp of salt as suggested and they were perfect for saltiness. My family likes a sweeter bun so next time I will increase the sugar for our tastes but that is our personal preference.  I got 12 large buns from this and they stayed fresh into the next day.  Thanks for a great recipe.

My family really liked these. In anticipation of that and their hearty appetites, I made these in a large pan. I layered the potato, salt pepper, a little garlic powder and cheese and then repeated until I had used up all my potatoes. I did not have heavy cream so I just used skim milk. They  were so popular I made them again the next day. I think they would make a great presentation if made in the muffin tins. Thanks for the recipe.
I subbed applesauce for all of the oil and we all really enjoyed this loaf. It is easy to make and tastes great. Thanks for the recipe.

Very good and so easy to prepare. Sometimes we prefer a sweeter bread so on those occasions I am going to add a bit of sugar. I made this exactly as written and fresh out of the oven it has a wonderfully crispy crust and then softens as it cools. Thanks for the recipe.

My family really enjoyed this recipe. I did not want to run to the store so I subbed what I had on hand. I used "Recipe#2836" in place of the Italian dressing and mozzarella cheese not cheddar. My son saw me making these and once he tried them did not want to wait for them to come out of the oven. Thanks for the recipe.

Knowing my kids would enjoy this soup, I went ahead and doubled the recipe. I am glad I did because they loved it. I only had one can of evaporated milk, so I used skim milk for the rest. I also added a little extra cheese. I decided to puree the soup so skipped the thickening step. Thanks for the recipe.

I doubled the recipe so I did two layers of all the ingredients, except the butter. I kept it the same. i had something in the oven cooking already so I had to baked these at 350 for a longer period of time but they turned out great. They are easy and my family loved them. Thanks for the recipe.

This was very very good. I used a 19 oz can of tomatoes because that is what I had on hand and I did not add the fennel. My family really enjoyed this and it was quite easy to make too. Thanks for the recipe.

I used vanilla soy milk in this, so I skipped the vanilla and only used about 1 Tblsp of sugar as the milk has sugar in it. I think I could have added a little more sugar though as it was not quite sweet enough. This is easy to make and made a nice addition to out Sunday brunch. Thanks for the recipe.
I made this this morning and wow is it good. I left out the oil, salt and parsley. It is great by itself. It is also very easy to make. Thanks for the recipe
This was easy to make. I make the 'sauce' part in the morning so when it came time to cook the beans it was on the table fast. Thanks for the recipe.

A very easy soup to make. I added a couple of potatoes to make it even heartier. I used a combo of parsnips and carrots and forgot to add the parsley,lime,  and Worcestershire sauce. Thanks for the recipe.

Easy and not too sweet. I used apple and blueberries and let it cook until there was very little water left. We really liked the fruit in these so next time I would double the fruit. Thanks for the recipe.

I left out the raisins so my picky son would try these. I also subbed soy milk for the cream. My family loved these and I wonder how they would taste with fresh cranberries added. As another reviewer suggested, I used lemon juice in place of the water. Thanks for the recipe
These are great when you need a treat. I made these exactly as written. I gave these to my teenagers and even they liked them. They are easy to make too. Thanks for the recipe.

What a great flavour packed soup, I decided to leave out the chicken and added some julienne bamboo shoots, grated carrot, garlic and a little sesame oil. I used about 3 small lime leaves as mentioned in the forward to the recipe too. My daughter was diagnosed with bronchitis and she requested bowls of this soup while she was sick. Thanks for the recipe
My boys really liked this soup. Thanks for the recipe
I used soy milk in place of the regular milk. These are tasty muffins. Thanks for the recipe

This was great and so easy. I used only 1/4 tsp of cumin for personal preference and I was out of corn. I wanted these more like a wrap so I did not use the enchilada sauce either. I know I made quite a few changes but these were fantastic so I had to rate them. Thanks for the recipe.
This was an easy muffin to make and not too sweet. Thanks for the recipe.

I love smoothies because they are so easy to make and refreshing. It is 93 F here today and this really helped cool us down. I love the fact it is not too sweet either. I used fresh strawberries and banana and the rest of the berries were frozen.Thanks for the recipe.
My family really enjoyed this easy to put together recipe. Thanks for the recipe.
This great. I made as written except I added 1 extra pkg of Splenda. It is easy to make too. Thanks for the recipe.

I made some changes to this recipe to suit our tastes, but not enough to alter the recipe significantly I think. Regardless we love this soup. My 15 year old daughter asked me if I could make another potful right away she liked it so much. So I used 1 can of coconut milk, no oil, 1/2 Tblsp of dried ginger,  1 kaffir lime leaf and no zest or juice, and 1 tsp of red curry paste not cayenne and I forgot the cilantro and I left out the chicken. This soup tastes amazing and is almost exactly like a Thai soup we get in a local restaurant we love. This was so simple to make too. Thank you so much for this recipe.

My family loved this easy recipe. I tried to use what I had on hand, so I substituted sweet chili sauce for the apricot preserves and used honey mustard for the mustard. I did use my oven though. I baked the roast for two hours, then sliced it and put it back in the oven for another 30 minutes. Thanks for the recipe.

Well this was very easy to make (especially since I made the marinade and my husband BBQ'd), with amazing results. Comments around the table were that this was the best chicken ever, and exceptional chicken. The chicken was moist and extremely flavourful. Thanks for the recipe.

When I make a recipe that everyone not only eats, but argues over who gets the last one, I know that I have a winner. My entire family loved these. I did make a double batch of the pancake mixture but left everything else a single batch and I still have cinnamon filling leftover. The only thing I found was that I needed to wipe the pan between batches to keep the pancake looking 'pretty'. These are very easy to make with excellent results. Thanks for posting the recipe.
This was excellent. For my veggies, I used broccoli, carrots, peppers, mushrooms and onions. Thanks for the recipe
Simple and good. My kids loved them. Thanks for the recipe
This was very simple to make with very good results. Mine did not get glazed as it was gone almost as soon as it was out of the oven. Thanks for the recipe

I made this for supper tonight and we really liked it. I subbed swiss chard and kale for the spinach. It was easy to make and very filling. Love the Looneyspoon series cookbooks. Thanks for the recipe.
This was easy to make and my family enjoyed  it. Thanks for the recipe.
Excellent, fast and easy.  I used ground turkey instead of sausage.  My family loved it even the spaghetti expert, my daughter.

Oh yeah!  Wonderful bread!  A friend asked for some Jalapeno Cheese bread and I found this amazing recipe.  I showed it to my wife and she asked when I was going to make it - and she asked again, and again - so I did. I used green chiles since my wife is not a fan of hot peppers. 
I love this method.  I made a double batch and made this recipe and Zurie's Overnight No-Knead Bread since both share the same base recipe.  Now to make another for my friend.

I'm in love with this method and recipe.  It takes a minimum of effort for great bread several times a week.  I used weight instead of volume for better control (32.6 oz AP flour, 25.6 oz water, 0.49 oz active yeast, 0.88 oz kosher salt).  I also used whole wheat flour for 25% of the total flour by weight).
Excellent!  Fast, fun, easy and delicious!  I used bone-in chicken breasts and bone-in thighs.  Very tasty.
Yummy! Really good chicken made in one of my favorite convenience appliances: my crockpot. I did skip the red peppers, substituting sauteed onions.
Yummy! I used cream cheese instead of goat cheese, as it was what I had on hand, and skipped the peppers. The sauce really made this sandwich!
Great deviled eggs! Another variation to add to my collection.
Easy and fun way to dress up mashed potatoes. Yum!
Very good easy soup. I like my curry mild, so I used my own curry mix and adjusted the spices accordingly.
Another easy and fun way to dress up mashed potatoes! I canâ€™t get enough of this stuff!
Another great, easy way to make chicken! Yum! Thanks!
I made these for a snack for lunch tomorrow. The ingredients were things I already had on hand, and they went together easily.

A low fat onion soup! This is hearty enough to be dinner all by it's self and the only thing I would change at all is to add a bit less white pepper. It smells so good as the cooking time gets on. This is very easy to make and really fills the tummy with only 12% fat. Whats not to smile about! Made for Photo Tag.

DH insists that this recipe has to have 5 stars. He LOVES it! I would probably go with a 4 myself but as we can't assign halves it's getting full marks. You sure can't get any easier and it does taste very good. I personally found the sauce a bit to thin for my preference but that will be easily cured by adding less milk next time, and there WILL be a next time. I used no added salt and didn't find it needing a grain when tasted. I cut the recipe to use 2 breasts and still used the whole can of soup because I would just have thrown the extra out. This is a lovely recipe that I think everyone in the family will enjoy.

Yummmm. Quick and delicious. I used skim milk,1 tbsp of Splenda Brown Sugar and Dutch cocoa. I topped it with canned whipped cream and cinnamon only because DS was here and was feeling a bit down. He said that he would try it but didn't want much and then wanted more after tasting it. He said that it every bit as good as what you get at the pricy places and I have to agree. I might cut the vanilla back just a bit, to 3/4 tsp. Thanks Boomie this is wonderful!. Made for Photo Tag

I didn't have any mayo in the house so I used fat free sour cream. I love this, it isn't too sweet and really crunchy. It will make a ideal summer salad. (Shoot, I'm loving it in Feb too!). A perfect light and flavorful side to chicken or pork as well as along side a sandwich. I cut up baby carrots. Yummy

Since the recipe doesn't say what to do with the majority of the ingredients I cooked the floured and egged chicken in the skillet and removed it from the pan. Then I used the rest of the items (except the capers) to de-glaze the pan and to make a small amount of sauce. I used lime in place of the lemon and just squeezed the juice of it into the pan along with everything else. I did need to add a small bit of corn starch as I wanted the sauce thicker than what it was. The capers were used to top it off as garnish and it all turned out absolutely delicious!

Zippity Do Da! You really should be sitting somewhere when you have one of these. I cut the alcohol's in half and it still had a potent kick. I didn't have any fresh orange to zest so I added a bit of dried zest into the "coffee". Skipped the butter because I was going to use the whipped cream. Then sat back and enjoyed this Sippin' Coffee. The flavors blend very nicely indeed and I enjoyed it for dessert tonight. Made for Photo Tag.

Very nice quick meal. I used mushroom soup (because thats what I had) and added some frozen peas and some dried minced onion. I skipped adding any milk and just used the water in the tuna can which worked out just right. I not a fan of fish and cheese together so that was left off to. The result is very tasty and really hits the spot when cooking time is short. Thanks for posting. Made for Photo Tag

Wonderful recipe! I didn't gave the canned items so I used fresh mushrooms and tomato's. I used water in place of juice, no sugar or oil and a boneless-skinless chicken breast.The timing was dead on by I set the temp at 400 as I was only doing 1 breast. The flavor in this is full bodied , deep and very satisfying while being very healthy. A total winner for me.

Anything that DH literally scrapes the pot to make sure he gets it all is 5 stars in my book! It came out perfect and I omitted the sugar. It's very easy to make. Thanks very much for a stew that I'll use as my standard from now on.

How I wish I could give this 10 stars. It's absolutely to die for. I used fat free evaporated milk in place of the cream and still got a rich, creamy, frothy, deeply chocolate dream come true. I used Dutch cocoa and Splenda Brown Sugar and skipped the booze. For the ice I used 6 frozen coffee cubes (my trays make very small cubes). I don't need a crystal ball to know that this will be appearing many times over in my future. Bless you BK.

This is an excellent full bodied soup that is perfect for cold weather. I don't know why anyone would choose a canned soup when you can make one that is fresh and so much better tasting as easily as this. Hearty, healthy and delicious. This recipe has it all.

There is no way that something this low in fat and rich in flavor isn't getting 5 stars from me. I used Splenda Brown Sugar, Dutch cocoa and espresso powder. The addition of bittersweet chocolate (my fav) just clinches top marks. You feel like your being decadent while savoring each spoonful. Not a problem to make and more than worth the minimum effort. Thanks Boomie!

I loved the spices, coffee and the chocolate. I skipped the topping. There was something (I think it was the allspice) that resisted blending well into the coffee base. This left a grit in the bottom portion of the mug that I wasn't in love with. I believe that I'll try this again without the allspice and see if that was it. It's certainly worth another try. It's yummy and legal! Thanks for posting Sherrybeth.

I have to admit right off the top that I used 1/2 the whiskey and for me this still had a hard kick. However, it's wonderful! I used Jamison whiskey and enjoyed every drop. It's so pretty to watch the cream run down into the coffee mix and incorporate it's self. This would be amazing sipped by a fireside.

I marinated the chicken all day and I think that a bit of salt in the marinade would be a good idea. That said the lemon and oregano flavor is very nice. I used whole,bite size, Yukon Gold's that were perfectly roasted when the chicken came out of the oven.  I used one thigh and had a very nice dinner. Thanks Marra for a small sized meal. Made for Photo Tag.

WOW, add my 5 stars to the rest. loof, you have a winner. I used 1/2 an ounce of each liqueur to the cream (yes, I used real cream for a change because I thought I just had to here). It's smooth, rich and goes down way too easy! I think that this is a real ladies drink but I don't see anything wrong with that. It's a perfect blend.

This is GOOD! I used Irish Breakfast tea, mixed berries, pomegranet juice, plain fat free yogurt and a very little Splenda. I stopped the blender when there were still tiny bits of berries (my choice) and enjoyed a a delicious, healthy breakfast. Thank yo so much Jen for this keeper. Made fot Photo Tag

These are very unique wee treats. They are indeed yummy and I seriously suggest that you at least double the recipe and if you have kids your going to need more than that! They are a breeze to make up . I whizzed the banana and pb, cinnamon and vanilla in the food processor then stirred in the seeds.  I used Adams crunchy pb. You really need to leave them in the paper cups to serve because they will soften and start becoming gooey quickly. They aren't something that you can take outside to leisurely nibble on. Take just what you want at the time out of the freezer. They are SO yummy and easy that I might even suggest keeping some in the freezer on a regular basis.

I'm not in love with the typical tomato soup. The tomato flavor is the main one in this wonderful soup but it's fresh and clear. I loved each and every spoonful. I don't use the red lentils often and was very glad that I had some in the pantry. The seasoning is unusual for me but it really makes this a winner. It doesn't take long to make and is a marvelous lunch. I would recommend this as a first course to a North African meal also. Made of PAC, Spring 08.

What a treat. I made this with sugar free ice cream and no sugar added syrup to make it diabetic usable. The maple flavor comes through beautifully and it's thick but not too thick to use a straw. Congratulations to this young chef.

This is nothing short of fabulous. I used bittersweet chocolate, 1 tbsp of Splenda Brown Sugar and fat free evap milk. I didn't get the amount of froth I had expected so I dropped some whipped topping for the photo. The flavor this coffee delivers is superior to that expensive coffee house and you don't have to leave home. The next time I make this I'll make both servings and use a taller mug!

WOW, I lightened these quite a lot and they are still scrumptious.
I used egg white instead of whole egg, Splenda for the sugar, skim milk, heart healthy margarine for the butter and unsweetened applesauce (with 1/2 tsp of butter extract mixed in) for the shortening. They tried to rise to the top of the oven and they're  moist, really fluffy, mildly flavored with sweet spice and utterly wonderful!

This was a grand lunch today. So easy and yummy. I'm not a lover of creamed corn but DH loves it and I had some in the house. I thought that it might just work and it really did!. I used 1 cup of skim milk to keep it on the thicker side but that is just personal choice. There is lots of flavor and texture. Made for Photo Tag.

Lovely fluffy pancakes. I used 1 tbsp of Splenda, no sugar added syrup and skim milk and soured (with lemon) skim for the buttermilk. As dh was having breakfast with me I skipped the added fruit and just added some cinnamon because he doesn't want "chunks" of any kind in his pancakes. They are very flavorful, quick to make up and the recipe works beautifully. Made for Photo Tag.

Reds, I love this. I made 2 servings and squeezed 1/2 of a lemon into it and for my taste that was a good amount and the capers are a great touch. Aside from the extra lemon I followed the recipe and it worked very well. Easy to make and lots of flavor. I paired it with  lemon sauteed shrimp. Yummm!

You have made my dh a very happy man. He has pronounced it a 5 star recipe and has given me "permission" to make it often. You can't get much easier to make and with my uber picky man praising and scrapping the dish I'm pretty sure that anyone who enjoys tapioca will love this one. Thanks pup, this is something I think I'll be using a lot.

This is yummy! I used some mixes veggies (broccoli, yellow squash, snow peas and carrot) because I had them in the fridge. For the dressing I used a 50/50 mix of low fat mayo and fat free sour cream to trim the fat with Italian herb mix and used it lightly. Loved the addition of the mustard!. This is a great light lunch and will be a wonderful summer side for sandwich's and goodies off the grill. Thanks Gert. Made for Photo Tag

I'm very impressed with this. This simple to make recipe gave a lot fore flavor than I was really expecting. I skipped the butter and just softened the onion is some water to save on fat. I also left the pecans in big chunks so that DH could pick them out. He gave the rice 4 stars and thats really good considering that he usually refuses to eat anything with nuts in it. I made 2 servings and used more stock than ask for (about 2/3-3/4 c to 1/3 c of rice) and that gave me well cooked, fluffy and separate grains. Made for Photo Tag.

I used this on Pecan Chicken. It tastes very good and is lovely and smooth (I used skim milk). It's really a good multiple use recipe. I'm thinking of using it for the gravy in a chicken pot pie come next Fall. You sure can't get any easier. Thanks MsSally :D. Made for Photo Tag.

Mine baked on convection @ 375 for 20 mins and came out lovely. My real difference was that I grated a Gala apple and when grated it was much closer to 2 cups than one. Not having any imminent use for grated apple just put it all in the scones. That made them heavier but all of that apple and cinnamon is delish!. I used Splenda in place of sugar, 1/4 cup heart healthy margarine and 1/4 cup unsweetened applesauce for the butter, skim milk and just the egg white to trim back the fat. Apple, cinnamon and walnut, is there a better combination? YUM. Made for 1-2-3 Tag Game.

This is another grand dish from this Chef. I don't  buy the boxed mixes so I started with Basmati rice and in place of saffron (which I don't have on hand) I used 2 tsp's of Nasseh's Recipe #262189. It didn't take any longer to cook that the mix would have and the result was wonderful. The chicken breast I used was on the large size, that and 1/3 cup of rice gave me enough for 2 servings. Easy, quick and delicious, whats not to love!

Very nice oatmeal. I think that the cinnamon could be a lot stronger but thats just me. For the sugar I used Sugar Twin Brown and reduced the amount of raisins to 6 to trim back the sugars. I made a single serving using 1/4 cup of oats.  All in all quite tasty and will surely make it again.

I made this for DH and his rating was 5 stars. He says that he thought it was "very tasty" and really enjoyed the apple juice sauce.  The only thing I changed was the use No Yolk noodles because I couldn't find the spaetzle. This is easy to make and only takes one pan. Thanks loof for something that DH will eat and actually enjoy. Made for Photo Tag.

This is a great tasting, quick, salad that is also a color riot. I had it alone for lunch but this would be the perfect thing for a BBQ side. It is best after a good chilling and flavor mingling. Made for Photo Tag.

Marvelous tasting veggies that are quick and simple to make. The yellow and green peppers that I used made a colorful side to my salmon. Next time I make this I'll give the peppers a head start in the pan before adding the mushies.  The peppers were perfectly done while the mushrooms, while very tasty, were more cooked that I would have preferred. This is a keeper. Made for ZWT4.

I really tried to float the top layer but it just sank and mixed. No gorgeous layered presentation but it sure didn't hurt the taste any. This was a grand dessert and goes down way to easy! Simply delicious. Along with the Bailey's I used Vermeer Dutch Chocolate Cream Liqueur. Made for ZWT4.

This is a lovely and simple dessert. I did replace the honey with Splenda for diabetic reasons and I know that it would be even better with the honey. The yogurt was the perfect finish to a lemon chicken and rice dinner. Made for ZWT 4.

Well, you knew that I was going to fall completely in love with this. I made in the pot because I just couldn't wait for the 20 mins to do it the other way. The cinnamon stick was transfered from the pot to my cup (after rinsing,lol). The cloves are identifiable but not over strong at all. Thanks Engrossed for a lovely cup. Made for ZWT4.

Wowsers, potent, sweet and rich. This isn't a gulper by any means. I'll admit that didn't add the ice and blend (mainly because there wasn't enough room in the glass that I wanted to use) so I got more of a wallop than would be expected. Be sure to use your favorite Scotch here because your really going to taste it.  This is wonderful for an after dinner linger. Made for Photo Tag.

How can anything with cinnamon be bad? Made as directed for this mornings brekkie with one exception. I used Splenda for the sugar. I went for the double cinnamon sticks. One in the pot and one in the cup and it just kept getting better and better. The tea was Tetleys. Made for ZWT4.

I tried this recipe in order to try the Israeli couscous that I had purchased. This is the first time I have ever tried it and I'm glad that I chose this recipe because I loved the seasoning and lemon juice. I do need to say that I had to add an extra 1/2 cup of broth for the couscous to cook enough. Thanks Mikekey.
Pure Pleasure. I used skim milk, Cool Whip Light and white chocolate pudding (sugar and fat free). It's creamy, rich and uber delicious with no guilt at all. What more could you ask for? :D

Really excellent. I did the same as Sharon, made 1/2 and used the veggie option (Yves Ground Round Original) and softened the onion in water instead of oil then followed the recipe. It tastes great in a spoon from the pan and I used it in Recipe #307560 which was much enjoyed. It's a keeper!

Simply delicious! I used liquid fat free/no sugar added coffee creamer to make it richer without adding any fat in place of the Irish Cream. I have no way to froth milk so mine is naked *blush* but I enjoyed every sip. A sensational diabetic recipe. :D

Outstanding. I used strawberry syrup and Sprite Zero. Oh,magawd I swear that it's just like your 10 again only better because now you have boobs! I had to use no sugar added vanilla bean ice cream. Thanks Twiss for turning a summer afternoon into a trip back in time. :D

I made my sticks smaller that ask for because 4 ozs would just have given me 2 sticks and I wanted to feel like I had more. The flavor is really good with the garlic and pepper. My only suggestion is to NOT cut them as small as I did because when they are done they aren't at all brown and when they brown up some they are overcooked. Follow the recipe and you should be just fine, lol. I would also suggest a dipping sauce because fish sticks just seem to scream for it. I WILL be making these again but they will be larger next time. I use salmon a lot and a different way to do it is very welcome. Thanks Paula. Made for Photo Tag

Whats not to love about a chocolate shake? I need to use no sugar added ice cream and even though I have been asking the local store only wants to carry vanilla. SO, after adding the milk (skim) I put in 3 heaping tsps of cocoa powder and 2 heaping tsps of homemade hot chocolate mix made with Splenda to supply the sweetness that would have come from the syrup. With a good blending it all came together in a rich creamy and very chocolatey shake. :D

This is a perfect summer meal. I skipped the oil and added some lemon juice to the dressing (also skipped the French dressing by personal choice). This has a fresh and not heavy taste. I do love the mustard and pepper sauce in this. I used red pepper because I didn't have green. It all came together beautifully and was very much enjoyed tonight. Made for Photo Tag.

Oh this is SO good! Instead of using instant coffee I mixed the the other liquid ingredients and topped up the glass with strong cold brewed coffee. I used Cool Whip Free (still frozen) and splashed white Creme DeMenthe on top of that (didn't have green). Excellent :D

Nothing short of wonderful. I didn't add the sauce to the burgers because DH wants his food dead plain. I used the marvelous mayo mix on mine as a condiment with onion and tomato. I made buns to go with this burger using Recipe #187552 and they complimented each other well. It's raining again tonight so I had to cook the patties in the broiler but I don't think they suffered for it. They were moist and flavorful. I use salmon a lot and this will be back at our house beyond doubt. Thanks Boomie for a wonderful recipe.

I ask you, how can you go wrong with Fudge in any form? Another total winner from Kit. I used skim milk, sugar free diet pudding and sugar free ice cream. DH took a drink from the glass after I had the pix and wanted to know if I should really be having something this rich! Yes, it's THAT good! :D. It will thicken some as it sits. It's a wonderful dessert tonight :D. Thanks so much Kit.

Excellent! I'll be the very first to admit that 1/2 a cup of ground coffee to make one serving is too strong for me (even if it is an 18 oz serving). I used 2 tbsp of each coffee and proceeded with the recipe using caramel and hazelnut (no 1/2 and 12). As Sharon said it's not over sweet which I like. Also wonderful is the fact that it made sugar free by using sugar free caramel syrup in place of the ice cream topping. A complete winner :D.

What a great change of the daily pace. Total yumm factor here. I used cocoa powder in place of the chips only to trim the sugar. If this won't get the kids to eat their oatmeal trade them in because they are defective! *wink*. Thanks Mandy :D

It works for me. Creamy goodness with no sugar and so little fat that it's not worth mentioning. If you enjoy cold coffee this mocha is for you too. Pure deliciousness while walking in the light of staying on the diet. Bless you Coffee.

Very refreshing! I used unsweetened o.j. and sugar free ice cream. It's best when the ice cream has melted into the juice, then it really has the creamesicle taste. I froze just 1 cup of juice to make one serving and it took about an hour with stirring it every 15 mins to get good slush. The whole family will love this.
Excellent. I used fresh berries, did strain, and enjoyed very much indeed. *Note to self: must try with the suggested Amaretto :D

This will hit the spot on a summer afternoon. I don't believe that I've had peanut butter in a shake before but while this may be the first I don't think it will be the last! It's smooth and creamy and delicious. :D

Whats not to love about this? While I did back off on the amount of Kahlua by half, the coffee, chocolate and Kahlua combo is tops and it couldn't be any easier to make. It's summer atm but you wouldn't go wrong having this for a warmer when the temperatures dip low either.

Ok. I used a lot of soda in a pretty good sized glass but this is yummy. While sipping I was thinking that a vanilla vodka would be lovely here. It goes down very nicely and is simply the perfect summer drink. Made for Photo Tag.

Looks like I copied Boomie in that I used canned whipped cream and Kahlua. I very much enjoyed this it wasn't too strong with alcohol taste. I used Jamison's and I did add some Splenda. Thanks Jen :D. Made for Photo Tag

BK, this is simply grand! I used frozen mixed berried, 1/8 tsp of powdered ginger (it's what I had) and Splenda for the honey. That small bit of ginger adds a real brightness and zip. The berries. pear and ginger are a top notch trio. It's thick and just delicious. Thanks Kato for another winner :D
