I forgot to add the sesame seeds but I don't think it really mattered. I didn't see the suggestion to serve with chili oil so I didn't do that but I sure will next time. Thanks for sharing a great recipe. Made for ZWT 6.

Very nice recipe! I made it as the recipe stated using a korean red pepper in place of the chili powder. I loved the use of sesame oil in this. I omitted the sesame seed due to personal preference. This went very well with my Asian themed dinner tonight. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

This is a very good bread recipe. I followed the directions exactly as written. It made a rather small loaf but the aroma was great as it baked and the taste and texture are spot on. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.
This is a great quick bread recipe. It was easy to make and tasted wonderful. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.
I liked this! I added a little bit of vanilla and a teaspoon of sugar. It was very refreshing and so easy to make. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

Great fries! They looked and tasted wonderful. I don't know why I bother with frozen fries when these are such a cinch to make. I made homemade tartar sauce for dipping. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

We loved this recipe! I used ground pork. I liked the use of bean thread noodle. I'd never tried it that way before. It was easy to make, fried up nice, and tasted fantastic! Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.
This was a great drink! We really enjoyed the fresh pink grapefruit in this and will definitely make this again. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.
This was terrific! I made it as written using cheddar cheese and fresh grated nutmeg. We all loved it. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

I wish you all could smell this bread. I made the dough in the bread machine and baked it in a loaf pan. I skipped the orange rind and fennel. This made a perfect loaf of bread with great texture and wonderful taste! I'll put this in my tried and true file because I'm certain I'll make it often. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.
Great recipe! I loved the use of ginger. Very easy to make and it tasted so good. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

Great recipe! We love cucumbers and have them often. This was a little different so I thought I'd give it a try. I'm sure glad I did. I made it just as written, let it cool for the hour and put them on the table with our salad. The jar was nearly empty when it was time to serve dinner so I say "Perfect". Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

Excellent recipe! I chopped the thyme and rosemary as suggested and then followed the recipe. I only let it marinate for 30 minutes but it was enough to let the flavors come through perfectly. My chops were a little small so 10 minutes gave me more of a medium doneness but the meat was tender and juicy with a great taste. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

I loved this burger!!! The sauce was great and I really enjoyed the pita. I'd never had one before and I was pleasantly surprised at how good it tasted. I used black olives, tomato, lettuce and white onions. I served the burger with fries and cucumber slices. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

This is a great bread! I made the large loaf in the bread machine. It was very easy to make and looked and tasted so good. I served it with Greek Lamb Stew and it went perfect with it. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.
This is indeed a perfect cup of greek tea. I used chamomile and some super good honey that I found at a local store. Made for the Nectar of The Gods Challenge for the Mischief Makers ZWT 6.
We really enjoyed this method of making sweet potatoes. The flavors went well together and tasted great! Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

Wonderful, just wonderful! I made exactly as written except I didn't have the red onion so I used yellow ones. I used a spicy pork sausage that I bought from our local butcher. We like our sauce a little thicker so I added a Tbs. of cornstarch mixed with an equal amount of water. We all enjoyed our meal very much. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

I had some leftover peas and saw this recipe and decided to try it. I used 2 eggs and only 1/2 tsp. cumin. It tasted great and isn't weird at all. I had a toasted english muffin with it and loved every bite! Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.
We enjoyed this roasted vegetable dish very much! It was my first time for parsnips and I like them! The roasted garlic was wonderful in this. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.
I used chicken broth to make this wonderful mushroom recipe. This is so easy to make, tastes great, and looks very nice on the plate. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.
This is a great pie! We haven't had fresh peach pie in years and it really hit the spot. The custard and streusel are top of the line. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

Oh boy, is this great or what!!! I had to use frozen rhubarb but did get fresh strawberries. This is a perfect blend of both fruits with just the right amount of sugar. Thanks so much for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

Superb! I used a Granny Smith apple and regular sugar as that was what I had. I loved how quick and easy this was and how great it tasted. I plan on buying some Splenda and using this for a weight-loss dessert. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.
This is awesome! I made it as written but used garlic tabasco. All of the flavors blend nicely. I used it as dressing on a tossed green salad. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6.

Wonderful! This was so easy to put together and tasted sooo good. I used cherry tomatoes, red onion, minced garlic and my own oil and vinegar dressing. I let it chill for 4 hours before eating it. It was perfect!! Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2010. Congrats, FloridaNative!!!

Awesome!!! I loved the addition of fresh garlic and green onion. I've never put sugar in my blue cheese dressing and was afraid I'd ruin the great flavor I already had but then decided to add 1/4 tsp. so I could rate the recipe honestly. It really didn't make much difference with that tiny amount but I'm sure more would not have been better. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool Week 4 2010. Congrats on your win!!

This one got a huge WOW!! from my family. We all kept eating and smiling while totally enjoying this chili. It was very spicy with great flavor that really stood out. I simmered it for 3 1/2 hours and it was perfect. My meat-loving roomies made chili burgers and topped them with cheese and onions. I opted for just a bowl with cheese, onions, and avocado. This is definitely the winner for us! Made for Dining On A Dollar 2010.

This was a nice use of kidney beans. The sauce was pretty good but it was a little too vinegary for us. My jalapeno was kinda small and evidently not very hot because we didn't get the kick we were expecting. All in all, a very good recipe. Made for Dining On A Dollar 2010.

I followed this just as written using Rotel. I had trouble getting the rice to cook. It took 1 hour and 15 minutes. The taste was ok but it seemed like something was missing. I wonder if less rice would help as it didn't hold up well in the refrigerater. The rice soaked up all the broth. Made for Dining On A Dollar 2010.
I never remember to buy wine vinegar so when I saw this I got very excited. This is clearly a 5 star recipe. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2010.
Super easy and very tasty. Made for Football Pool 2010.

Very good muffins. I had to use frozen berries but I don't think it mattered. They were super easy to make and baked up beautifully! The taste was great and the texture perfect. Will definitely make again.

Wow!! This is comfort food at its best. My guys loved it. I made it early in the day so I could watch the football game at the bar. They devoured most of it before I got home. I'll certainly put this on my list of keepers. Thanks for sharing.

Great tasting sauce!! I used it for french fries tonight. Tomorrow I'll use it on a tossed salad. If I have any left I'll use it as a spread on a grilled hamburger. I'm so glad to get this recipe. I like how easy it is to make and how many ways it can be used. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2010.

Thanks for a great new way to use boneless, skinless chicken breasts. We loved the taste of the fresh tarragon in this. I used the oven and was pleasantly surprised at how tender and moist they turned out. Next time I'll try the grill.

I also used less olive oil as suggested by NorthwestGal. These were so easy to make and the taste was great! I served them with lamb burgers covered with melted goat cheese w/ proscuitto, fresh tomatoes and a little mayo on a bun. Congrats alligirl on your Super Bowl win.

This recipe rates much higher than the 5 stars allowed! It is the best tilapia recipe I've ever tried. The flavor is perfect as written and it was so easy to prepare. It's definitely a keeper. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC 2011.
This made for a great Sunday brunch. I made it as written and used the sour cream and salsa options. We really enjoyed this recipe. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC 2011.

This was very good. I used pork steaks instead of chops. I made it as written and added a couple of fresh mushrooms. I served it over rice with fresh asparagus on the side. The meat was very tender and the sauce was excellent. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC 2011.
What a nice treat! This was so good and very refreshing. I will be making this often. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7.
Wonderful!! I really enjoyed this recipe and loved how easy it was to make. My banana wasn't all that ripe but it still made for a great tasting beverage. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7.
I thoroughly enjoyed this beverage! So simple to make and so delicious. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7.

This was my favorite of all the recipes I tried! It was quick and easy. During the first 10 minutes of cooking I made and sauce and prepared the bread (I used bollilo). Then I turned the sausages and veggies and put the bread in the oven for the last 5 minutes of cooking. The cheese was perfectly melted, the bread was hot, and I was ready to assemble. I used hot sausage and the sriracha option. With the first bite, I was in sandwich heaven! Slightly messy, but oh, so tasty. Thanks for sharing. Made for RSC #16.

Very nice recipe! I used the larger biscuits because that's what I had. I made mine a little smaller than stated so I would get a thicker crust (my preference). I used jarred pizza sauce and added a few chopped olives. I will make this again but use half swiss and half mozzarella. Thanks for sharing. Made for RSC #16.

I made this as directed but omitted the topping. I loved the addition of onions and hot sauce. Thanks for the tip on heating the milk first. This would have been a 5 star recipe for me but it wasn't as creamy as I expected from the title. Thanks for sharing. Made for RSC #16.

I cut this in half for 2 servings. I followed it as written. I thought it had too much ricotta for the amount of tomato sauce. It tasted gritty and the sauce was pink. I think more sauce and less pasta would make for a better looking and tastier recipe. Thanks for sharing. Made for RSC #16.
I love this recipe! It is so garlicky and spicy that you just have to keep eating one after another. Thanks for sharing a real keeper. Made for ZWT7-Italy.

I bake yams in the oven often because I like them much better than regular potatoes. I never thought about putting brown sugar on them and was pleasantly surprised. Thanks for the tip on how to serve them. Great idea! Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Africa.
Very good salsa! I made it as written except I subbed cilantro for the parsley. I served it with taco chips and cold beer. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7.
I really liked this tea. I didn't use the full amount of sugar but followed everything else. I really liked the peppercorns. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Africa.
This is a wonderful bread recipe! I used the dough cycle and then baked it in the oven. It tastes great and the recipe was perfect as written. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7.

This was so good! I used dried mint and the flavor really didn't come through but since it was an option it doesn't matter. I plan on making this again with fresh mint as soon as I get some. Thanks for sharing your, cool, refreshing salad. Made for ZWT7- Africa.
This was very tasty but very HOT! I loved everything about it but next time I think I'll try jalapeno or less of the serrano. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Africa.
Oh, Wow!! I love spinach and peanut butter so this recipe had my name written all over it. It didn't disappoint. This is a true keeper for me! Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Africa.
I only had one can of beans so could only make half this recipe. It was HOT but very good. Next time I'll use less pepper. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Italy.

This was so good! I just happened to have an orange in the fridge when I saw this and had to try it. I loved it. I will definitely make this often. Thanks for Sharing. Made for ZWT7-South and Central America.

Thanks for posting a recipe that I can make at home instead of buying all those nasty little packets that are aways so salty. I made this as directed but used only half the salt. This came out perfect and I'll be using it often. Made for ZWT7-South and Central America.

I made just a single serving of this and was very happy with the results. It was my first time using Coco Lopez and I'm hooked! Thanks for sharing a recipe I'll use often. Made for ZWT7-South and Central America.
This is a very good seasoning. I only made half the recipe to start but next time I'll definitely make more. I used it to season some chicken that I grilled. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Italy.
This recipe is so easy to make and it tastes terrific! I used whole baby clams and jarred organic garlic. This is a true keeper. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Italy.
I made one of these for lunch today. It was excellent. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Africa.
Wow! This is so good. I used slices of Recipe#155369 for this. It turned out fab! Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Italy.
Fantastic recipe! This was so easy to make and it tasted great. I made it as written and really enjoyed the apple and brown sugar with the kraut. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Switzerland.

Great recipe! I didn't measure anything for this. I just put the mixed baby greens in a salad bowl and added a sprinkling of craisins, walnuts and cheese. I used blueberry-pomegranate vinaigrette for the dressing.
I enjoyed it very much. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Switzerland.

I loved this corn! I only cooked 2 ears and it came out perfect. I served it with sauteed prawns and a tossed salad for my dinner tonight. Yes, I ate both ears! Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.

Excellent recipe!! I used 10 large prawns to make this. I omitted the red pepper but used everything else. Great garlicky sauce with a nice amount of lemon. The sherry wine really set this apart from some other recipes I've tried. Thanks for sharing! Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.
Great mac salad! I made as written except I added more tuna. I like just the way it is and wouldn't change a thing. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.

This was a nice dressing for my salad of mixed baby greens, tomatoes, green onions, and salad shrimp. I garnished it with pickled beets and hard-boiled egg. thankd for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Switzerland.
I made a 6 inch pizza using a store bought shell. I made this as written and it was great! Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.

Great! I used a rye bread that I made for one of the challenges for the tour. I cut it rather thick, slathered it with mayo (I always do that), and proceeded with the recipe. I loved the tomatoes with the swiis cheese. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Switzerland.
Great recipe! I haven't had ovaltine in years so I just had to try this (the peppermint schnapps is a favorite). I was very happy with the results. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Switzerland.

I only made half of this recipe. I used Tillamook Extra Sharp cheese and the beer option. I really liked the potatoes and leeks in this. The flavor was awesome. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Switzerland.
Excellent! I made as written and used bone-in new york steaks that I cooked on the gas grill. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.

I ended up marinating these for 2 days. They turned out a perfect golden brown and the sauce was to die for! I left the wing tips on and I'm glad I did. They were nice and crispy. I'll be making these often. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.

I made this to go with Recipe#455166. It was a great side along with a tossed salad for a wonderful dinner. I used regular raisins because that's what I had. The coconut flavor wasn't as strong as I expected but I did know it was there. I loved the onions in this and the cashews provided a nice taste and crunchy texture. Definitely a keeper! Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.

I bought some Kona coffee beans at the store so just had to try this recipe. It is fantastic! I didn't use the cream and sugar but made it as written. The spices were awesome. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.

This is a great pasta salad. I used small shells for this and made it as written. I added a small amount of pickle juice and a little more mayo. Definitely a keeper!. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Switzerland.

I really enjoyed pineapple cooked this way. I used a Maui Gold pineapple. The grated ginger appears on the ingredient list twice and I couldn't figure out what should have been there so I used 1 Tblsp. of grated ginger and 2 tsp. of crystalized ginger. I broiled it 6 inches from the heat source for 5 minutes and it was perfect. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.

Excellent cup of coffee! I loved everything about this recipe even the coconut that wouldn't float. I wished I would have had some whipped cream but wasn't to be. Next time, and there will be one, I'll make sure I'm better prepared. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.
Excellent and so easy to make! I used mango, papaya, pineapple, kiwi, and strawberries for the fruit. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.

This was really good! I used diced tomatoes and fresh sauteed mushrooms. It was so easy to make and quick too. By the time my rice was done so was the goulash. I only used half the garlic powder and added tabasco to my portion. Definitely a keeper! Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.

I loved this recipe! The cabbage was sweet and tender and tasted so good. I cut it in wedges and roasted it for 25 minutes. I also skipped the vinegar and used a bit of butter. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Switzerland.

I used a mix of different colored baby potatoes for this. Also used thyme and steak seasoning.
This is a great way to make potatoes and the taste was very good. I really enjoyed this recipe. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Switzerland.

Just perfect! I made this as written and took it to a meeting to share. Everyone raved about how good it was and how much they loved the sugar-nutmeg dip. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT7-Pacific Islands.

Very nice meatloaf! I think my ground beef was a little too lean because it wasn't as moist as I like. The glaze was great! I didn't use a pie plate but shaped the loaf my usual way. It was very easy to make and sliced perfectly. Good luck in the contest.

The omelet was not spicy as the title inferred. I only made half of this and was glad I did because it was very hard to fold as it was. I would have never been able to do it with 6 eggs. The taste was good and I enjoyed it even if it wasn't as pretty as it could have been. Good luck in the contest.
The zucchini was great but we didn't care for the sauce. I really liked how easy this was to make. I'll definitely use this coating for frying zucchinni in the future. Good luck in the contest.

I cut this recipe in half and got 3 large burgers. I loved the aroma of the sauteeing veggies and had great hopes for this. I used bread crumbs, half mushrooms and red pepper, and refrigerated the mixture overnight. I had no problems shaping the patties and they cooked just fine. I didn't care for the sauce mainly because of the honey. I had the patty topped with sauce for lunch. I froze the other two. Good luck in the contest.
We didn't care for this slaw as much as I thought we would. The dressing was very bland even after chilling overnight. I'll stick with the mayo based dressings. Good luck in the contest.

We really enjoyed this sauce except for the carrots. I just couldn't get them to soften even after 2 hours of simmering. I made it exactly as written but added a bay leaf and a little more italian seasoning. I froze some for later. Good luck in the contest.

We enjoyed this meatloaf. I used homemade cornbread and enchilada sauce that I made earlier in the day. The cornbread was an interesting touch that we really liked. I used jalapeno because I didn't have poblano. I upped all the spices except the paprika and added a teaspoon of white pepper. I added the cheese to the meat mix instead of using it as a topping. I ended up with a tasty meatloaf that was easy to slice. The sauce didn't go over very well so I'll skip it next time. I had to bake it longer than stated, about 1 hour or so. Good luck in the contest.

Good job! This is so simple to make and tastes great. I added garlic but followed the rest as written. I served this over penne pasta with a salad and garlic bread. Very enjoyable meal. Thanks for the great idea. Good luck in the contest.

I made this mostly as written. I used beef bouillon, red bell peppers, and mushrooms. I used fresh garlic that I sauteed with the other veggies. It was very tasty and went well as a side with a grilled steak. Good luck in the contest.

I've been making something quite similar to this for years. Since yours had a few different ingredients I had to try it. I really liked the addition of wine and the spices. I served it with meatloaf and baked potatoes. It really tasted great together and I didn't need to glaze the meatloaf or put catsup on the table. Good luck in the contest.

We really loved this recipe! The salmon was seasoned perfectly and the pilaf was awesome. I didn't add the walnuts because I didn't have any. I really liked the orange in this because it went so well with the salmon. I know I'll be making this again. Good luck in the contest.

I made this exactly as written and wouldn't change a thing. This is comfort food at it's best. I served this as a side with meatloaf and green beans. I really liked the method of layering the macaroni and cheese. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC Fall 2011.
I love this!! So simple and so tasty! I'll be making this all winter. I used sugar-free cocoa mix and it works very well. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC Fall 2011.

Terrific! This is so much better than the store stuff. I made it as written and wouldn't change a thing. I used it for fresh crab and shrimp cocktails. We loved it. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2011.
Excellent recipe for cukes! I used homemade thai chili sauce for this and we really enjoyed this recipe. I will make this again. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC Fall 2011.
I made this for breakfast this morning. I made it as written except I used fresh mushrooms as I don't buy canned. Super tasting eggs! Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC Fall 2011.

I halved this recipe and used 2 boneless pork steaks. The coating was nice and crispy, had a great flavor, and the meat was nice and juicy. I served them with Recipe#451305 and Recipe#419896. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC Fall 2011.

Made these for lunch yesterday. I halved the recipe and made 4 little slider burgers. We topped them with lettuce and tomato. The cheese did keep the burgers moist and juicy and they had a great taste. I liked the fresh garlic (used a whole glove) in these. I pan sauteed them. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC Fall 2011.

I don't buy frozen meatballs so I used Recipe#380242 for this. I put the soup, gravy mix, bouillon, and water in the crockpot first and stirred it together. Then added my meatballs and let it cook on low for about 5 hours. I served them with mashed potatoes and green beans. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC Fall 2011.
Terrific guac! I halved this but made it exactly as written. It is perfect just the way it is. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC Fall 2011.
We really enjoyed this easy to make fish dish. I made it as written and wouldn't change a thing. I served it with Recipe#456678 and a dinner roll. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC Fall 2011.

This is an excellent recipe for soup! I made it this time as directed and we really enjoyed it. Next time I'll add some other veggies too. It's a good way to use up all those bits and pieces of veggies that I normally have in the freezer. Thanks for sharing. Made for PAC Fall 2011.

I made this with 1 ounce of bittersweet chocolate and 2% milk. I didn't need any sugar (or substitute)as the fat-free topping made it plenty sweet enough for me. I really enjoyed this simple to make tasty hot chocolate. Yep, I drank it all! Made for Football Pool 2011. Thanks for sharing!
I really enjoyed this egg salad. The use of dill put it over the top. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2011.
I made this as written but forgot the cheese. It was very good and thanks to the crock pot easy to make. I'll make it again. Thanks for sharing.
Wow!!! These were so good. I made them as written and wouldn't change a thing. Thanks for sharing.

I didn't precook the potatoes or use the cheese in this. Since I was baking a ham at the same time my oven temp was 325*. It took about one and a half hours to cook and the potatoes were perfect!Thanks for sharing.

This is how I learned to make hashbrowns at a restaurant without the onions and cheese, of course. That addition put these potatoes on a whole new level. I only used 1 potato,swiss cheese and adjusted the rest of the ingredients. I served it with ham and eggs for breakfast. Very delicious! Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2011.
Wonderful! I used black tea and Sweet Cream coffee creamer. I love the flavor from the 5-spice powder in this. I'll make this again. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2011.

Yummy! I used a frozen banana and an extra scoop of peanut butter to make this shake. I didn't have any extract but really didn't feel like it needed it. It was terrific! Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2011.
Excellent way to cook mushrooms. I made as written and loved 'em. Thanks for sharing. Made for Spring PAC 2012.

Great recipe! I goofed and put the onions in with the flour and potatoes but it didn't hurt it at all. I really loved the tangy taste of the buttermilk. It certainly didn't hurt to have a recipe that was so easy to make either. I'll definitely be making this one again. Thanks for sharing.
I used butter instead of oil for this but followed the rest as written. I love carrots so this was a great new way of preparing them. Thanks for sharing. Made for Spring PAC 2012.
I made 2 of these using silicone cups and the bread option. They turned out perfect and made a terrific breakfast. Thanks for sharing. Made for Spring PAC 2012.
We really enjoyed these pancakes. Great taste and texture. I also made only half the recipe. Thanks for sharing. Made for Spring PAC 2012.

I made this using baby shrimp and a bit of imitation krab. I left out the peas as I'm not a big fan of them but made it as written otherwise. Very tasty indeed! Thanks for sharing. Made for Spring PAC 2012.

I made this using the cinnamon- allspice option. I cut the carrots into thin rounds and baked on a foil lined baking sheet. The timing was right on and the carrots were delicious! Thanks for sharing. Made for Variety is the Spice of Life event.
This was a great salad. I loved the corn with all the other great veggies. The dressing worked well with the salad and had a terrific taste. Thanks for sharing. Good luck in the contest.

This is the best method of poaching eggs that I've ever tried. They were perfectly cooked in 4 minutes. I used the steamer basket of my rice cooker to drain the eggs and served them on a slice of whole wheat toast. Made for ZWT 8- France.
I made this using Swai fillets. Excellent way to cook fish. The sauce was fabulous. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8-Spain/Portugal.
I loved this easy to make sandwich. The green olives really made it special. I used rye bread. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8-Spain/Portugal.
What a nice way to jazz up plain rice with very little work and just a few ingredients. We enjoyed this rice and will make it again. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8-Spain/Portugal.

I have to agree with the others. This is the only way to cook perfect srambled eggs. I liked the addition of cream and cheese. Definitely put it over the top. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8- France.
Wonderful, creamy, cheesy goodness! I made this as written using gruyere cheese. We loved this and will make often. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8- France.
Great biscuits with lovely orange flavor! I made it as written and they were delicious. I served them with bacon and scrambled eggs for breakfast. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8- France.
I used cooked salad shrimp for this. I cut the recipe down to serve 2. We loved the avocado puree. Thanks for sharing. Made fpr ZWT 8- Spain/Portugal.

I skipped the pre-cooking and just grilled 2 ears of corn. I mixed a little cayenne into the paprika and mixed it into half a stick of butter. I didn't bother chilling the butter, just lathered it on the corn and sprinkled a bit of Pensey's Arizona Dreaming. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8- Spain/Portugal.
This is a terrific sauce for burgers! I used medium salsa for this and topped my grilled burger with it and a slice of cheddar cheese. Yummy. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT8- Spain/Portugal.

Outstanding! We loved everything about this recipe. All of the flavors worked well together and the gravy was great. It was very easy to make too. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT8- Australia/New Zealand.

Great new way to make potatoes. I didn't have the cheese but I didn't miss it. I served these with recipe#483082 #483082. I made just 4 potatoes for the two of us and it was just right. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT8- Australia/New Zealand.

I used one slice of monterey jack and one slice cheddar (I love cheese) for this. I didn't do the tortilla chip option but did everything else as written. This is one great sandwich. The addition of guacamole put it over the top in my opinion. Will make again. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
Great potato salad. We really enjoyed the cilantro and spicy brown mustard in this. I added some sweet pickle relish but otherwise made as directed. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
We really enjoyed this tasty grilled corn on the cob. The chili-lime butter was great. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWt 8.
This is going to be my new recipe for mexican rice. I also used diced tomatoes. We enjoyed this very much. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.

This is soooo good! It's a huge burger but oh, so tasty. I cooked the bacon in the microwave while the burgers were grilling. Then fried the eggs kind of over easy. I really liked the beets on it. I'll definitely make this again. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.

I made this for the gluten free challenge (Australia 2012). I used chicken breasts and gluten free soy sauce. I marinated it overnight then grilled on the gas barbie. Delicious, tender and great flavors. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8- Australia/New Zealand.
I was making tacos and didn't have any seasoning packets so used this. It was so much better and super easy to make. Will use often. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
I was craving a BLT and found this wonderful Tex Mex version and had to try it. I used regular bacon and Texas toast. I loved the avocado in this. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
Delicious! I loved the honey and lime on these. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
I really liked this. I used banana and raisins in mine and drizzled with some honey. I know I'll be making this often so I can try some of the other fruits. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
So easy to make and so good. I made as written using baby red potatoes. Will definitely make again. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWt 8.
Perfect summer breakfast! I cut the recipe in half and served it with sourdough toast. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
I made this as directed using the coffee creamer. We enjoyed it very much. I plan on making this again around the holidays to share with friends. Thanks for sharing a great recipe. Made for ZWt 8.
Wow! I love a good gin gimlet and the cucumber in this put it over the top. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
Excellent recipe! I made it exactly as written. It was easy to make, looked fabulous and tasted great. Definitely a keeper. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
I used microwave popcorn and cut way back on the spices and omitted the salt. It was very good. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.

I only made one ear of corn as I had another recipe to try at the same time. My son and I each had a half ear of each and had fun comparing the two recipes. We really liked all the different spices on this one and the use of the foil made it so easy. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
I made these on my griddle. I made half with garlic powder and half with curry powder. I liked both ways but the curry was outstanding. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
My new love is corn on the grill. I made this as written and we loved it. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
I only made half the recipe for the 2 of us. It went very well with your chicken recipe (482144) and garlic rice. We thoroughly enjoyed this fine meal. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.

I used bone-in thighs and mild curry powder to make this delightful chicken dish. We enjoyed it very much and will make it again. I served it with your raita recipe and garlic rice. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
This is a great rice recipe. We loved the nuts and garlic flavor. I served it with chicken and raita. Will definitely make again. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
This was very nice. I made it as written and enjoyed it a lot. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
Other than the constant stirring time this was easy enough to make and tasted great. I used whole milk and chocolate chips. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
Terrific scrambled eggs! I used parsley, tarragon and chives. They had such a creamy texture and the flavor of the fresh herbs really stood out. Great breakfast. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.
Loved 'em! I used corn tortillas and yellow onions. The sauce was wonderful and we really enjoyed our meal. I served these with rice and black beans. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.

I had to use canned peaches and regular milk to make this but it turned out great. Oh, my yogurt was Australian instead of Greek. I chilled the peaches first and then put everything in the blender including the Bailey's. We loved it. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 8.

I made half of this recipe because there's only 2 of us. Since we don't care for roasted peppers I used regular red bell pepper. The pickles I used were called Wickles and they are spicy and sweet. They worked really well in this salad, just enough of a bite to let you know there's something just a little different in there. The dressing was perfect just as written. I plan on making this often. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2012.
Very nice! I used the potato water option because that's how I remember my Mom making mashed taters. Thanks for the walk down memory lane. Made for Football Pool 2012.
I made this without the salt. I mixed it in flour and fried the chicken. The spices went well together and gave it a nice flavor. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2012.
I used gin and pink grapefruit juice to make this great drink. The triple sec was a nice touch. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2012.

I made this wonderful corn dish to go with tonights dinner. I also used ritz crackers as that was what I had. We really enjoyed it and will make again. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2012.
This is really good! I made it as written and it was just right. Thanks for sharing. Made for Football Pool 2012.

This was very nice. I used about 10 oz spinach. I wilted about half of the spinach with the shallot mixture before adding the pasta and was glad I had as I kept throwing bits of orzo out of the skillet, trying to stir it & wilt the rest of the spinach. Next time I may use some of the oil from the tomatoes to saute the veg. to add some additional flavor. Also, I tried this cold the next day and it was pretty bland so I definitely recommend serving this warm. Thanks for the recipe and good luck in the contest!

This was delicious! I couldn't find French rolls so just used bakery whole wheat buns; otherwise made to the recipe. I ate it open-face instead of closing it together. Thanks for the recipe and good luck in the contest!

This was very good. I also used skinless bone-in thighs and used crimini mushrooms. Because tomatoes are not in season yet I used a 15 oz can, drained, for a half recipe. This was very easy and tasty and the chicken was super tender after the long braise. I thought the sauce could use a little more seasoning but that is probably just personal taste. Thanks for the recipe!

Simple, delicious, and very filling - what more can I say? :) I couldn't find cans of chili, just individual microwavable serving containers, but those were perfect for making one serving at a time. I agree with a previous reviewer that taco meat or homemade chili would also be great in this. Thanks for the great dinner - I'm stuffed!

Delicious! I had enough chocolate mixture to make two s'mores. The second one, I added some marshmallow fluff to make it more s'moreish - and moreish! Yum yum yum! Will definitely be made again. Thanks and good luck in the contest!

This is definitely a brownie that requires a milk chaser - and from someone that doesn't drink much milk, that's saying something! LOL Very rich and chocolaty and the peanut butter topping is like p.b. fudge. The batter seemed a little thin to me so I added an extra 2 Tbsp of flour (I used all-purpose because I didn't have any whole wheat). Used an 8x8 pan and they were perfect after 25 minutes. Thanks for the awesome recipe and good luck in the contest!

This was good, but needs some tweaking for my taste. I prefer dark meat chicken so would use thighs instead of breasts and am not a big fan of swiss; I used provolone this time but it needs something stronger. The baked casserole was extremely soupy so I think I would cut the soup in half and leave out the water. I served with Recipe #275036 and it made a nice combination. Thanks for the recipe!

Yum! I used a purple bell pepper that a co-worker grew, red onion, blue corn tortilla chips, and skipped the celery. It was a very pretty combo of purple and green - I almost hated to mess it up with dressing! lol Used homemade Recipe #131467 and homemade Recipe #66591 (only used about 1 tsp taco seasoning and mixed it into a 1/4 cup ranch). Went awesome with Recipe #323775 for dinner. Thanks for the recipe!

This was really good! I made a couple slight changes, in the spirit of the Dining on a $ Contest, to save $$ and use things I had on hand. I had 1/2 a portobello mushroom so used that instead of the bell pepper, salami instead of pepperoni, and Monterey jack cheese instead of mozzarella. I had some homemade Italian dressing mix on hand so used that and didn't use the whole can of olives (seemed like too much to me). Thanks so much for the recipe - I will definitely make it again!
I was afraid this would be a little strong for my tastes as I don't drink gin very often but it was lovely and refreshing. Thanks for the recipe! [Made for 1.2.3 Hits]

This was a wonderful use for a pie crust besides pie! I was trying to use up items in my fridge (a single pie crust being one) so made 1/2 the recipe and used cheddar-jack cheese and instead of pepperoni, used my favorite pizza toppings, black olives and banana peppers. I had trouble with the assembly but it was totally operator error as I misread the directions and cut my single crust into 8 wedges, but I made it work and next time will do it correctly LOL Thanks so much for the recipe! [Made for 1.2.3 Hits]

Wow! This was not a combo I would've ever thought of before but it made an awesome sandwich! I used Jonagold apple (one of my favorite eating apples) and American cheese with Trader Joe's preservative-free raisin bread. Thank you so much for the recipe! [Made for 1.2.3 Hits]

Very nice! My blender doesn't do well with ice so I just served this over ice instead of blending. I did cut back on the lime after reading other reviews (1/2 oz) and added another ounce of pineapple juice (needed to use it up). It was perfect this way. Thanks for the recipe!

Sooooooo good and dangerous (I'm in danger of eating them all right now!) I used a Jonagold apple and dark brown sugar. I agree with other reviews that the dough was a little, well, "doughy" on the bottom and there also seemed to be a lot of sauce (delicious though it is). Next time (and there WILL be a next time!) I will try with half the amount of sauce. Thanks for the recipe!

These are fabulous! I made them for dinner tonight with your recipe #167241 and it was a great combo. The meatballs were super tender and flavorful. The only change I made was using red bell pepper not green. I think the breadcrumbs could be cut back to 1 cup without a problem. Thanks for the recipe!

This was a very interesting recipe. I made a 1/4 recipe but found it too cocoa heavy and added an extra Tbsp of sugar; I may also add more cinnamon (but I'll try it again as-is first). I have always preferred my cinnamon toast with peanut butter instead of butter so I tried this both ways; I also liked this better with the peanut butter. I will probably stick with regular cinnamon sugar in the future but was glad to try this variation. Thanks for sharing!

This was very tasty and super easy. I didn't change the ingredients (except to leave out the cilantro) but made a change to the cooking method. I have a different couscous with dried fruit recipe and followed the cooking method for that: bring the water to a boil with the orange zest, bouillon, sugar, currants and butter, stir in the couscous, cover, remove from the heat to sit for 6 minutes. Fluff and add the remaining ingredients. I used veg. Better Than Bouillon and next time will reduce the amount as it is stronger than your average bouillon - after tasting, I ended up adding some melted apricot marmalade to offset the bouillon flavor. Thanks for the recipe!

I thought this was very nice. I halved it but used the full amount of paprika (it's my favorite spice). Contrary to the previous reviewer, I actually thought this was a little too juicy saucy, at least for my taste. Rather than serving over rice, I served with recipe #361380 along side.  Thanks for the recipe!
I made this with light cream cheese and peach preserves. Delicious on a turkey sandwich or alone on graham crackers. Thanks for the recipe!

This is an excellent dressing. I just whisked it together rather than dirty my blender. I used it right after making it and it was great so will be looking forward to trying it again after it has chilled :) Thanks for the recipe! -May 1, 2009. Update: Just wanted to add that this is also good with lemon juice! :)

Very tasty! I used red and yellow tomatoes, red bell pepper, and kalamata olives; didn't change a thing except to mix it up the same way JackieOhNo did. Made this for Father's day dinner and it was enjoyed by all (mom thought it was a little vinegary but I thought it was perfect). Thanks for the recipe!

This is really really good! I cut it down to one serving and it was a _huge_ serving! I used organic linguine, heirloom tomatoes, crimini mushrooms and kalamata olives. I was a little short on mushrooms (1 oz shy) and probably used more tomato since I used smaller ones and had to guess what made up a medium-size tomato. I happened to have everything on hand for this which made it super quick and easy. Thanks for the recipe!
This was lovely! I don't think I've ever had blueberries on a salad but they were great. I used olive oil to make it healthier and regular balsamic. Thanks for the recipe!

This was really good. I followed the recipe to a T. The topping was kind-of overtaken by the bubbling up of the fruit so it wasn't as attractive as a standard crisp but it still tasted great. Thanks for the recipe!

I don't think I've ever made a recipe as quickly after finding it as I did this one - and I was not disappointed! This was an excellent sandwich! I had to improvise just a bit to use what I had (yellow cheddar & slices of small tomatoes not large ones). I used spicy globe basil that I grew from seed :) I will be doing this one again for sure! Thanks for the recipe!

I hate to contradict everyone else but I guess I'm just really picky when it comes to sloppy joes. These were way too soupy for my taste, and seemed to be missing something that I couldn't put my finger on. I cooked them uncovered and added about 15 minutes to the cook time to get rid of some extra liquid, as well as adding extra mustard, chili powder, sugar, and some vinegar. Sorry they didn't suit me but I'm glad I tried the recipe. Thanks!

I love Raisinets so just had to try this - sooo yummy! I used semi-sweet instead of milk and had a little over 9 oz raisins. I used my cookie scoop to dish these out which made them even easier. Thanks for posting this superior alternative to purchased Raisinets!
Excellent quesadilla! I used some leftover spaghetti sauce and Monterey jack cheese. I didn't try freezing, just ate it for dinner right after making. Thanks so much for the recipe!
Yummy! I left off the chicken and used homemade pesto and naan bread instead of pita. Otherwise didn't change anything (except my pepper was diced not sliced). Thanks for the recipe!

So so so so good! I halved the recipe and will still be enjoying this for a while :) This would be great on biscuits, toast, muffins, just about any bread product you can think of - I had it on a bagel today. Thanks so much for the recipe!

I used yellow cornmeal (what I had) and 2 Tbsp. sugar. My log was 8.5" long and I got just 20 slices at 1/4" thick. I think the rosemary I had (borrowed from my mom) was a little old so I threw it in a spice grinder; it isn't really detectable so I will add some more next time (unless I buy newer rosemary beforehand). Served with herb chevre which was a nice combo. Alone, I think these could use less sugar but when paired with goat cheese, the sweetness is good as made. Thanks for posting! [Made for PRMR Holiday Special]

This was very good. It needed a lot more salt for my taste, though. I used 2 lb each of thighs and legs, and skinned them before adding to the crockpot. The only thing I changed was to leave out the celery. I did on low for 6 hours and it was falling off the bone. Served with Recipe #216995. Thanks for posting! [Made for PRMR Holiday Special]

This is very good. I had just 12 oz shrimp so reduced accordingly. I used recipe #63812 (made into dressing) and left out the celery. I also did not have lemon pepper so just left it and the salt out (the dressing had enough). Used medium shell pasta instead of angel hair. Next time I might add some diced bell pepper in place of the celery. This was very tasty for lunch today. Thanks for posting!

This is lovely! It tastes much like some dark chocolate-raspberry candy bars I've had - yummy! I used Schokinag Triple Choc. European-style drinking chocolate which uses milk and makes a 6 oz serving. I only used 1/2 oz of Chambord, which was the perfect amount for my taste.  Thanks so much sharing!

This is excellent! I love the tartness from the cherries. I used the white meat from one of those already roasted chickens from the supermarket. The only change I made was to leave out the celery. This is great right after making it so I'm sure it will be even better after melding together. Thanks so much for the recipe!

This is very tasty! I did everything per the recipe except for using red instead of white onion and adding a little extra vinegar. I'd never noticed it before but I found the Crazy Jane's salt at our regular grocery. Next time I would use even a little more vinegar and maybe a little less sugar (I tend to prefer tart dressings over sweet). Thanks for sharing!
These are very nice! I really liked the tang from the cream cheese. I didn't really taste the lemon zest, though. I used extra large eggs. Thanks for posting your creation and good luck!

These are very tasty! I didn't really taste the lemon zest. The recipe didn't say how to use the jalapeno so since it was optional, I left it out. I used a very spicy homemade whole grain mustard and extra large eggs. I really liked the cheddar with the rest of the flavors. Thanks for posting your creation and good luck!

I made this yesterday and thought it was wonderful; when I came back to review it I realized I totally forgot the lemon zest! So I made it again today and I think it's even better with the lemon zest. The only thing I had to change was that I was a little short on apricot preserves the second time so used orange marmalade to make up the difference (probably only a couple tsp). I didn't measure the cinnamon - just used what looked good, which was probably close to 1 tsp. I had this over chocolate ice cream and it was lovely! Thanks for posting and good luck!

These were very tasty! I used what I had on hand which was tomato & basil tuna, light mayo, club crackers, and no celery. Maybe the club crackers have more surface area, or I loaded them up more but I only had about 15 melts (which were my dinner tonight :) ) Thanks for posting!
Just the right amount of tart and sweet. No problems with it not staying combined (though I might have drunk it before it had a chance lol) Thanks for posting!

Lovely! And tasty! I used Recipe #174297 (with double the sugar) for the sour mix. I didn't have Sprite so used Mt. Dew which made the color more minty but the orangeness of the Dew went perfect with the orangeness of the curacao. Perfect for the unusually warm weather we're having today! Thanks so much sharing!

I made these for Easter today and everyone liked them a lot. I had been given a dozen *extra large* eggs so used those but used Recipe #64854 to cook them (adding a few extra minutes because of the size). I used Hellmans mayo (only 3/4 cup) and only 1/2 tsp salt (one person still thought they were too salty, but I thought they were fine). One person commented they were like egg salad in deviled egg form. I love dill pickle relish so loved that addition. Thanks for sharing your grandmother's recipe!

Excellent, excellent burger! I used Kettle brand bbq chips and skipped the salt as I figured the chips would provide enough salt (which they did). I don't have a grill so cooked in a skillet. Served with Recipe #380632 on the side. Thanks so much for the recipe! [Made for Spring Pick A Chef 2010]

I make a lot of homemade dressings and this one was very different from any others I've made in the past. I wasn't sure about it on first taste, but it really grew on me! It is quite tart, but I love tart dressings. Like the previous reviewer, I did not get 3/4 cup - I had about 3/8 cup, but that was perfect for my needs. Thanks for sharing your recipe!

I don't know if mine still qualified as a Vampire's Kiss since I used cranberry vodka instead of raspberry (it was what I had) but it was still delish! I did add an extra ounce of cranberry juice (by accident, but I'm kinda glad I did). Very lovely drink! Thanks very much for sharing!

Too cute! And tasty! I'm a big fan of The Muppets, so I just had to make this for myself :) Though Elmo's not my favorite, I enjoyed eating him! LOL I had everything on hand for this except pepperoni so cut a couple slices of hard salami into 8 smaller circles, which worked perfectly. If I had kids I'm sure they'd love this as much as I did :) Thanks so much for sharing!

While at the store this week, I got a chunk of "Five Counties Cheese" which is layers of Derby, Red Leicester, Cheshire, Double Gloucester, & Cheddar so I thought this would be the perfect way to use it. I used wild chives and red onion (what I had) and no bacon (though I would have done if I'd had some!) Used lightly toasted wheat bread for one and will have the rest (on untoasted bread) for lunch tomorrow. Thanks so much for sharing!

I grew up not liking sloppy joes (which is what I would call this barbecue mixture) until I realized that what I didn't like was the commercial brand SJ mix (Manwich). As a result I tend to be pretty picky about sloppy joe recipes, but I really liked this one a lot. I cooked the onion with the beef and used dark brown sugar but otherwise made as directed. When it came to filling the biscuits, though, I only used about half the mixture (and will freeze the rest for another time). I also used jack cheese because it was what I had on hand. I liked these a lot and will definitely make again! Thanks for sharing!

I love eggs done over-easy but don't make them at home (ever), so this recipe gave me the opportunity to practice :) I really enjoyed the addition of dill and will use it again for scrambled eggs as well! I only made two eggs since I was having toast with it also. Thanks for sharing!

This was very tasty! I used light cream cheese and added chives and bacon.  Yum yum! Like another reviewer, I spread the cheese on both pieces of bread so it held the extras better. Thanks for sharing :)
This was perfect! I didn't have any English muffins so used one of those thin sandwich buns they sell now-a-days. Used Monterey jack cheese as it was what I had on hand. Thanks for posting!
This is lovely - perfect for the Indian Summer kind of day we are having today. I used a little over 1 oz cranberry vodka (what I had on hand). Thanks for sharing!
This was a nice quick lunch. I used pickled jalapeno for the chiles and parsley instead of cilantro. Would be good with other cheeses. Thanks for sharing!

This was very good. I only used one jalapeno (and it was a pretty mild one) as I was afraid using two for the small amount of meat would be a waste. I might try pickled jalapeno next time for more heat. The orange flavor came through nicely though. I marinated about 16 hours or so (overnight). It did take a bit longer than 25 minutes to complete cooking - about 20-25 minutes more in my oven. I took out at a little over 155°, letting it coast up to 160° out of the oven. Juicy and tender - delish! Thanks for sharing :)

Mmmmmmm what yummy little treats these are! I used Neufchatel and finely shredded cheddar so it would mix in really well.  I only used one jalapeno and Frank's hot sauce. I had a little extra filling (I was afraid to fill them TOO full) and just ate it cold with crackers and it was still tasty. I think I might make these again in a couple weeks for Christmas. Thanks for sharing!

Mmmmmm these are dangerous - I'm liable to eat the whole pan at once! I used a few more chocolate chips (and used Ghirardelli semi-sweet). They are a bit soft if you don't put them in the fridge, but I find that to be the case with most sweets with similar ingredients to these so wasn't surprised that was the case here also. Next time I might try using less butter and more chocolate (maybe 1 cup chips and 2 Tbsp butter). Thanks for sharing your aunt's recipe!

I needed something for our Post-Holidays Holiday Potluck at work and this fit the bill perfectly. I made 1.5 times the recipe (which was a ton!) and used pre-cooked bacon (2.3 oz pkg) and pre-shredded lettuce (10 oz) to save time. The only change I made was to cut back the mayo just a little bit (used 1 cup instead of 1 1/8 cup). Many of my co-workers told me how good it was. Thanks for helping me preserve my standing among them as a great cook! :) - Jan 6, 2010. UPDATE: I made this again for this year's potluck and only made one recipe (instead of 1.5) and it was plenty. I again used pre-cooked bacon (8 slices) and an 8 oz pkg of lettuce. I still cut back the mayo a Tbsp or two. The only thing I did different this time was using homemade bbq sauce - recipe #159145. Got rave reviews again! Thanks again for sharing! :)

Mmmmmmmm! I made these gluten-free for a work friend with celiac and after tasting, I'm going to have to make more tomorrow (regular this time) for two more work friends that are not celiac :) They are so tasty! I used salted butter (didn't have any unsalted) and did not change anything else. I ended up with 25 cookies and baked them for 14 minutes. Thanks for sharing FN! - Dec 18, 2010. Update: I just finished making a double batch of these with regular flour - I must have made them slightly larger this time as I ended up with only 44. I baked for 15 minutes this time. They are just as yummy with regular flour as with gluten-free! Thanks again FN!

Woooo, this has quite a kick to it! Next time I might cut back on the hot sauce by a couple Tbsp, not that the heat level kept me from eating it this time, I just didn't eat as much as I might have otherwise (which, now that I think about it, might not be such a bad thing!) I didn't have quite enough mozzarella so used jack cheese to make up the difference. I also left out the butter when I discovered I was out of butter! I used homemade blue cheese dressing, recipe #415739 and instead of canned chicken I used the equivalent weight of shredded white meat from a supermarket roasted chicken. This is delish! Thanks for sharing!

Mmmmmmm yummy! The only corn I had was frozen in "butter sauce" so I cooked enough of that for my dinner and added the cream cheese and pepper called for here. Will be making the rest of that bag of corn this way too! Thanks for the recipe!

What's not to love about this? :) I used semi-sweet chips and sourdough bread. I think this would also be great with raisin bread. And maybe a dab of peanut butter! Mmmmmm... Thanks for sharing Boomette!

Very nice cheese sarnie! I used thick-cut sourdough bread, extra sharp cheddar and homemade rhubarb chutney (recipe #300651, which I had in the freezer). Because my loaf of bread was quite large, I added an extra 1/2 oz of cheese (left quantities of everything else the same except for skipping the salt). I made in my non-stick skillet with a little butter on the outside to promote browning ;) I did accidentally forget about the chutney until I had the sandwich in the skillet so waited until it was done, opened it up, and mixed the chutney in with the melted cheese. As others said, it was a little messy, but totally worth it! Thanks for sharing FT :)

Mmmmmmmmm! This is going in my favorite drinks file! Love the orange with the cola - never would have thought of the combo. I used Coca-Cola and triple sec. It would be easy to get very drunk, very fast drinking these LOL they go down so smooth :) Thanks for sharing EmmyDuckie!

Tasty! I only had 1 lb of (26-30 ct) shrimp so cut everything back, though rather than trying to figure out 2/3 tsp for the spices, I used 3/4 tsp. The only thing I changed was parsley instead of cilantro. Served over Greek rice (recipe #36346). Thanks for sharing Tink! :)

These are very tasty! As previously mentioned, I also found them a little crumbly, but in my experience that tends to be the case with this kind of cookie bar. Maybe using a little more shortening would help that? I reduced the sugar in the filling to 1/2 cup (was the perfect sweetness for my taste), otherwise made no changes. Thanks for sharing!

Excellent! I cut this down to two 1/4 lb burgers. For BBQ sauce, I used homemade (#159145) though my conversion may have been a little off as I think there was just a bit too much sauce, making the mixture a little too soft - they wanted to fall apart a bit when I flipped them. Otherwise, this was excellent! I thought they might need more sauce on top after cooking but they were plenty flavorful without any extra. I used sliced cheddar as it was what I had on hand. Served with nothing more than pickles on top (I can't have a burger with out pickles!) Thanks so much for sharing!

Delicious! I had super thick (about 1 inch) chops so they took a lot longer than I expected to cook through, but it all worked out fine :) The only change I made was Monterey jack instead of cheddar. I also added a tiny bit of water right after adding the beans and salsa as I was afraid it was going to burn. Once the chops started to release their juices, then I had a little too much liquid, but I just turned up the heat a tiny bit (which I did also to get the chops done as they were taking so long) and the liquid thickened up. This was a great easy one pan dinner. Thanks for sharing!

Different and nice! I halved the recipe and used just chicken thighs, cooking the chicken the day before I needed it. I left the juices in the fridge overnight so I could easily remove the fat from the top when I finished it the next day. The only thing I changed was dried instead of fresh basil (about 1 tsp) and I cooked the sauce for 45 min. to thicken before adding the chicken for another 15 min. to just heat it through (I didn't want the chicken to get overcooked). Next time I would cook the sauce for at least 60 min. before adding the chicken as the sauce was still too thin for my taste. Oh, I also didn't have swiss cheese so used marbled cheddar. This was good with baked beans on the side. With the last of the leftovers, I ended up making a quesadilla and I think I liked it even better than as a sandwich. Thanks for sharing and good luck in the contest!

So good! I used a 16.3 oz, 8 ct pkg of biscuits (Grands) because I tried making a pizza crust with a regular-size biscuit I had leftover from another recipe and the largest I could get it was about 4 inches (the Grands themselves were still not quite 6 inches). I halved the sausage and onion (and skipped the oil as the sausage didn't need extra oil) and still had *plenty* for those 8 Grands biscuit crusts. I didn't have any fresh basil so used about 1/2-1 tsp dried. I didn't measure the sauce or cheese, just used what looked good. For the cheese, I used what I had on hand, which was a mozzarella-provolone mix on some and a 4-cheese Mexican blend for the rest. I only baked the crusts about 6-7 minutes before adding the toppings and they were done just right for my taste. These are super easy (I cooked the sausage a couple days ago) and tasty - the biscuit makes a yummy crust. Thanks for sharing and good luck in the contest!

This was good but didn't blow me away - it seemed to be missing something for my taste. When reheating the leftovers I added some sour cream and that seemed to help a bit.
I couldn't get hot Italian sausage except in links in a huge package so used mild (which I could get uncased in a 1 lb pkg) and added 1/4 tsp of crushed red pepper while browning the meat (in addition to the 1/4 tsp added later). The only change I made to the recipe as written (besides what I just mentioned) was to use 8 oz instead of 6 oz of the sausage (due to the pkg size - the other half went to another recipe). If I were to make it again, I might use cream cheese instead of ricotta for the slight tang it would add. Thanks for sharing your creation and good luck in the contest!

Delish! I am somewhat ashamed to admit that I used "American Air Bread" for my sandwich, but it was all I had (it was whole wheat though at least!) To add a little structure to it, I toasted the bread first. Used Black Forest ham and spicy brown mustard. Excellent with the pickle and olive accompaniments. Thanks for sharing!

Awesome!! I used I Can't Believe It's Not Butter (Light) spread. I bought Rice Krispies for another recipe and since I hardly ever eat cereal for breakfast I was trying to think of other ways to use it up. I didn't want to make a full 13x9 pan of Krispie treats since I know I'd eat them all within a few days but if I make these I can more easily spread that out over a few weeks (or months!) Thanks Greeny! :)

You weren't kidding about the amazing smell! I put this on this morning before leaving for most of the day and when I got home I could smell it before I even got to my apartment door - and even better, as I soon discovered, the taste is just as great as the smell! I was surprised by how much of a kick there was from the red pepper flakes (yum!) I made exactly to the recipe, cooking for just under 8 hours. I didn't have any crusty rolls or giardiniera, so served on toasted bread with provolone, banana peppers, and pickled onions. Love it! Thanks for sharing!

Mmmmm this is great stuff! I don't eat at McDonald's (it doesn't like me) so don't have any basis of comparison but I love mustards of all kinds and this is a good one! I halved the recipe and since I only had light corn syrup on hand, I replaced about 1/2-3/4 tsp of it with molasses to get more of a dark corn syrup vibe (I added a drizzle of molasses to the measuring spoon then topped it off with the corn syrup). For the yellow mustard I used Plochman's since it was what I had on hand (I like it better than French's). This was a quick, easy, and tasty mustard so I'm sure I'll be making it again! Thanks for sharing!

These were very tasty! Ashamedly, I like my green beans a little softer than most people and since the fresh beans at the store didn't look that great, I used frozen. As a result, I changed the cooking method slightly. I sauteed the frozen beans in a little oil in a non-stick skillet for 5 minutes then added the butter and onion, cooked until beans were browned slightly then added the paprika and sour cream. This worked so well, I will probably make them this way next time (and there will be a next time!) Thanks for sharing Karen E! :)

This is an awesome dip! I was looking for a way to use up some whipped cream cheese when I found this and being an Ohioan through and through I love me some buckeyes so had to try this!
I cut the recipe in half but only used about 1/2 cup sugar. I also used skim milk instead of 1/2-n-1/2 (it was what I had on hand) and didn't need anywhere near the amt of nutella listed. The nutella with the p.b. mix is a great combo. Thanks for sharing your fab recipe!
P.S. I can't imagine ever throwing away buckeyes - I'd have eaten them anyway! LOL :)
So simple and yet so delicious! Combines three of my favorite things :) Thanks for sharing!

This was delicious! I had whole leaf spinach so threw it in the food processor with some of the broth then put it all in the saucepan with the cheese and heated through. I did not add anything except a little fresh cracked black pepper. Thanks for the recipe!

This is very tasty - kind-of Greek-Italian fusion! I halved the recipe and used leftover deli roasted chicken (white meat only), orange bell pepper, and just a tiny bit more spinach (I had about 6 oz from a 16 oz bag of frozen spinach and wanted to use it up). I also used more cheese, but that's something I almost always do, being a serious cheese lover! Baked the half recipe in an 8x8 (2 qt) dish. Thanks for sharing! [Made for Adopt A Tag 2010/2011]

Fabulous! I did not have any plain vanilla ice cream - was debating between caramel cookie crunch gelato or salty caramel gelato. Decided to go with the cookie crunch and it was awesome with the bananas and caramel sauce. Thanks for an awesome and simple dessert!

These are awesome! Instead of dirtying another dish to melt the butter, I put the cakepan with the unmelted butter in the oven while it heated then removed once the butter was a puddle. I used basil and a 12 oz can of biscuits (couldn't find a 10 oz can). I started to roll the biscuit pieces in the herbs but it wasn't sticking very well so I just gave up and left the rest alone (which you can see in the picture LOL). These were fantastic with recipe #402990 for lunch today. Thanks for sharing!

Mmmm I loved this! Made for a great change from my usual go-to, maple syrup. I had some leftover homemade pancakes in the freezer so to make one serving I cut this way down to 1 1/2 Tbsp honey, 1 Tbsp butter, 1/16 tsp cinnamon. Instead of the stovetop I just heated in the microwave for 25 seconds, stirred to melt the butter and combine and then when the pancakes were ready, reheated the syrup for about 10 seconds. Used local honey produced just a couple miles up the road. Thanks for sharing!

After making some other things, I had just three slices of bacon leftover and this recipe intrigued me. I used maraschino cherries instead of glace because I had them on hand. I rolled up the edges of the foil to make a little lip which kept the bacon fat from running everywhere - one of the smarter things I've done recently LOL The cherry and bacon were an unusual and interesting combination. I would like to try again with something just slightly less sugary than the cherries - maybe pineapple, dried fig, or dates. Thanks for sharing!
Delicious! I used whole wheat bread with American and cheddar as they were what I had on hand. Definitely used the Dijon too! Thanks for sharing!
Very nice and refreshing cocktail! Will be great for summer :) I wasn't sure if a "measure" was the same as an ounce, but that's what I used. Thanks for sharing Noo!

So wonderful! I used mostly 70% chocolate but didn't have quite enough so added some 49% to make up the difference. I did use the rum but skipped the white chocolate. Used pecans and instead of glace cherries I used sweetened dried cherries. I could have gotten a hold of digestives but instead I used some shortbread cookies I had on hand that someone had given me. Love these so so much! Thanks for sharing!
This was nice, though a little plain. I added a dash of salt and some fresh black pepper which helped. Went nice with recipe #450605. Thanks for sharing!

So good! I only made one so used a 6 oz custard cup. Used the hash browns and had hoped they would get brown on the bottom but that may be my use of glass instead of metal for a baking dish. Regardless, this was delicious! I used pre-cooked bacon (2 slices) and that made it super easy! Forgot the cheese until after taking a picture but did add a sprinkle of jack cheese before scarfing LOL Thanks for sharing!

This is a very nice sauce and I look forward to finding various ways to use it! :) I halved the recipe, using an 8 oz can sauce, only 1/4 cup sugar, and 2 Tbsp vinegar (instead of 1 1/2 T). Otherwise made as directed. Thanks for sharing!

Really good! I made the mustard-caper topper. I only had two chicken breasts but they were *ginormous* so I ended up making the full recipe (and cutting them in half to serve!) Because the breasts were so large they took much longer to cook through, about 23-25 minutes on medium heat. I made the topper exactly as directed except instead of Dijon I used a German mustard called Loewensenf that is very similar to Dijon. Next time I will rinse the capers as they added a lot more saltiness than I expected. I cooked the sauce for 2 minutes extra to get it really nice and thick. Thanks for sharing!

Perfect! I needed pre-cooked bacon for two different recipes so did 5 strips - 3 with pepper and 2 plain. At 17 minutes I took them out but wanted them a bit crispier so put back for 2 more minutes and it was just what I needed. Thanks for sharing!

This was very tasty! I had a 6 oz container of Greek yogurt instead of 7 oz but I followed the recipe as listed and it came out fine with the slightly less yogurt. Served on top of Recipe #484263. Thanks for sharing!

Rich and delicious! I used 2% milk, 60% dark chocolate (Ghirardelli), and 4 1/2 tsp raw sugar. Also did not have apple pie spice so used the kitchen dictionary conversion (1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp nutmeg, 1/8 tsp cardamom). I didn't have any whipped cream or cinnamon stick so left those out but didn't miss them :) Thanks so much for sharing Anna!
I love peaches with cottage cheese so this was a no-brainer for me. I didn't have a parfait glass so used a martini glass :) Thanks for sharing!
Delicious quickie dessert. I used Triple Sec for the orange liqueur. Instead of whipped cream, I served the berries over some raspberry frozen yogurt, which was fabulous. Thanks for sharing!
Very quick, tasty, and easy lunch for a cold winter day. Thanks!

The sauce is absolutely delicious though I did have some minor problems (probably my own errors though and not the fault of the recipe). I had two huge chicken breasts (the equivalent of three "normal" size) so adjusted ingredients to 2 slices bacon, 2 jalapenos, 2 garlic, 3/4 cup broth, 3 oz cream cheese (Neufchatel), 3/4 cup cheddar (extra sharp). I left out the cilantro. I had to cook the chicken an extra 5-10 minutes to get it cooked through, even after pounding it even. Later, when I added the jalapenos to the pan, it was like having a pan of "Mexican jumping beans" LOL They had been frozen (from a friend's garden) so were fairly wet - when the water got hot, they flew out of the pan! They also almost smoked me out of the kitchen - the fumes from the hot chiles made me cough terribly. Anyway, even with the problems I had, the end result was super delish! Thanks for sharing!

I used boneless thighs, only because they were so much cheaper than wings. Roasted for 30 min, turned, and only did for 15 minutes more before adding the drizzle and going another 10 minutes. I may have had too much lemon juice as the drizzle was pretty thin and didn't stick as well as I think it needed too, but the final chicken was still delicious. Thanks for sharing!

Tasty! I cut this down to 3 servings, using 2 oz sharp cheddar. I don't care for sweet relish so used dill relish. Also used light mayo. I added just a dash of kosher salt but it probably didn't need it as it was just slightly too salty. Served on lightly toasted thin sandwich buns. Thanks for sharing! [Made for Spring 2013 Pick A Chef]

This is awesome! I made another microwave brownie last week that was very similar but I like this one a little better. The coffee and vanilla really added something that was missing from the other one. The best part is that I LOVE warm brownies right from the oven so this way I can have a warm brownie right from the microwave whenever I want (which is more often than I really should! LOL) I used an extra dark cocoa from Penzeys. My microwave took the full 75 seconds. Thanks for sharing! [Made for Spring 2013 Pick A Chef]

Yummmm! I went with a classic combo of cherries (1/2 cup dried) and chocolate (3/4 cup semisweet chips). Since cherries and almond are also a classic combo, I used the almond extract option. My only issue was bake time - after 25min they were still gooey in the middle. I had to add another 5min to get to done. Otherwise, these are simple and delicious! Thanks for sharing! [Made for Variety is the Spice of Life 2013]

I made a simple Mexican variation which was delicious - sweet and slightly spicy. I browned three links of fresh chorizo (casing removed) and added 1/2 can of green chiles (had them left from another recipe). Used a combination of cheeses: jalapeno jack, "regular" jack, and sharp cheddar. Reduced the butter to 2 oz (4 Tbsp) which was plenty. Thanks for sharing! [Made for Variety is the Spice of Life 2013]

This was good and easy. I was afraid there was too much batter for my mug so I used a bowl. Added a couple crushed mini Butterfinger candy bars (and another on top for garnish!) Might add some vanilla next time as it seemed to be lacking something for my taste and am thinking that might be what it needs. Thanks for sharing! [Made for Variety is the Spice of Life 2013]

The peanut sauce was the definite highlight of this recipe - it was sooooooo yummy! The chicken was good by itself too, but I'm not convinced the seasoning in the coating paired with the sauce. I didn't have any rosemary so left it out. Next time I will also leave out the thyme - I like thyme but the flavor of it was incongruous with the peanut sauce. (I also used garlic powder instead of garlic salt.) The technique for the chicken was great (love the way the coating snap crackle popped LOL), but I only baked for 15 minutes which was plenty of time to cook the chicken and get the coating crispy - 30 minutes would have been way too long. I used 2lbs. of chicken tenders and the amounts of everything else were perfect for that quantity. Thanks for the recipe and good luck in the contest! ~August 22, 2008 UPDATE: I had to come back to say that I have made just the peanut dipping sauce many times but instead of a dipping sauce, I use it as a sauce for buckwheat noodles (with about half the water). Love it! My favorite peanut sauce I've had to date. Thanks again!
I felt very Dutch as I ate breakfast this morning! LOL I used softened butter and Tijgervlokken (milk chocolate and vanilla shards), which had been sent to me from the Netherlands ;) Thanks KD :D
This is delicious - love it! I used whole wheat instead of rye but otherwise made as listed. Thanks for sharing!

I LOVE peanut butter on toast so grilled pb&j sandwiches are a definite hit with me! I used strawberry-lime preserves which are a bit tart but the grilling/heating mellowed the tartness and made an awesome combo with the peanut butter. Thanks!

Delicious! Though a little mayo heavy for my taste. Next time I make this (and there will be a next time!) I will do more sour cream and less mayo (maybe 3/4 & 1/4 not 1/2 and 1/2; oh and I used low fat of both). I used homemade refrigerator pickles (and the juice from them) that were made with dill & mustard seeds, peppercorns, and fresh garlic, onion & serrano chiles. I used a couple extra tsp of pickle juice and added some fresh black pepper. Otherwise followed the recipe. Awesome dip for potato chips. Thanks for sharing!

I subbed orange pepper for the green and used vegetable broth. Otherwise followed the recipe but threw it in the blender once it was done cooking as I prefer a smoother tomato soup. Served with garlic toast, it made for a rather tasty dinner. Thanks for sharing!

These are awesome. I shared them with a couple co-workers and then had to share the recipe too :) Made exactly per the recipe (was a little scared of the full tsp of cayenne but it's perfect!); stored in the same bag I mixed them in. Thanks for sharing! [Made for Spring Pick-A-Chef 2014]
Mmmmmmm lovely! Thank you for sharing! [Made for Spring 2014 PAC]

YUM. These are tasty. I made the Mexican version but instead of dissolving the coffee in water, I just added it to the batter straight from the jar. I used half special dark cocoa and half regular cocoa. I did have to bake for longer, about 5 minutes. Thanks for sharing!

A wonderful breakfast. Quick, easy and satisfying with a good cup of tea or coffee. I eat this at least evey other week. I have a small addiction to marmite :-) Very good with any type of bread I like white, whole wheat and especially rye.

This was soooooo yummy. DH was worried but he loved it too. I used a whole 1lb box of macaroni but didn't change the soup amount. I may have added a bit more milk tho.
