I used 6 of the open mushrooms (they were nice and plump). I used all the cheese. The sauce/glaze sank nicely into the cheese topping, and later I added the rest of the sauce as well. Baking time given was spot-on. DH and I each had 3 of these, and he thought the flavour was stunning. I made this to go with your Peanut Butter Chicken (plus some fresh veggies and a salad). A great meal on a cold night! Thanks!!

Made for ZWT 7. Wow, we love an exotic combo of flavours! I used considerably more chicken pieces than 1 lb even if we are only 2. Yes, there are leftovers: will be eaten or frozen! I used a can of coconut milk, less than stipulated in the ingredients, but it seemed enough to me, it's about 420 g. Instead of shop curry powder I used masala (basically a mild curry) which I buy in Cape Town from a Malay spice shop. Added some dried, flaked chilli (did not have the powder). I also simplified the directions, by adding the chicken, potatoes and carrots all at once in a large pot. Made brown basmati rice to go with it. Lovely, awalde, thanks! (Sorry no photo -- this afternoon both my cameras' batteries went flat, no kidding! They're loading at the moment!)

Made for ZWT7. I admit that I, myself, could have done better with this EXCELLENT recipe. I had pork leg slices, which I had to use -- not ideal. I "stewed" them a while in part of the marinade (they were tender after being left in the marinade quite long because I had to go out). I used less meat than stipulated, and made a little less pan sauce, as we were only 2 to dinner. The sauce was tangy, really very nice! I do not know "dehydrated chives", so used chopped spring onions. It's midwinter here, so no fresh basil! Whatever -- a very nice recipe, and I think it can also be adapted to taste, such as adding hot pepper. Thanks, Random Rachel!

Made for ZWT7. Very nicely flavoured dish! I used 4 chicken breasts (which I had to use up). The sauce was enough for them. I did add a little brown sugar, but I am almost certain that our cartons of juice have less sugar than their USA equivalent. Once you have the ingredients at hand, it's an easy recipe. I made brown basmati and fresh vegs to go with it.

Made for ZWT 7. I looked at this recipe, and thought, "this kite ain't gonna fly ..." But this kite DID fly!! The surprise was to fry the onions, which of course made all the difference. I fried them in butter. I confess, I did not use "small onions", merely sliced 2 medium onions and fried them. I added a pinch of sugar (have a DH who hates anything too acidic -- yikes from me). This Salat would be ideal, maybe the recipe multiplied, with outside-grilled meats.

Made and reviewed for DINING ON A DOLLAR. This was hard for me! Nothing much wrong, but the recipe seemed a bit contrived. Because this is a contest, I followed the recipe exactly. But I did feel as if the spices, onion and grated zucchini should first have been fried together, and then added to the beaten eggs. That might have been a great flavour infusion. We did not mind the veggies going in raw, but it did seem like an afterthought, rather than integrated with the omelet. I used a lovely spicy tomato salsa, which added a kick. Although I followed instruction #4 I could see the omelet was not going to cook successfully on top, and finished it under my oven grill. However, no photo, as I broke the omelet when after folding it and manoevring it out of the pan, sorry! Good luck with the contest!

It's long since I made this simple starter, so had to check again on ingredients! Very nice recipe! I am sorry about a less than good photo, but I battled with the photos -- under kitchen lights, as it became dark early due to heavy clouds.

Deb, this was SO great, in two ways: time was short and this is a quick recipe -- and I was short of fresh veggies for dinner. But I had lovely ripe tomatoes, the cheeses, the herbs, gorgeous fresh garlic -- and phyllo which needed using up pretty quickly as I'd kept it in the fridge too long already. I hate posting a picture, because NO photo will come close to French Tart's, but I also feel I want to show you how nicely it came out!! Apart from the phyllo (no time to make pastry, and no ready-made at hand) I added 1 beaten egg to the flavoured cheeses. This firmed up the bottom beautifully. I'd hoped that with only 2 eaters I could save half the pie for today -- but DH left only slightly more than a slice in the plate!! The flavours were wonderful! This was a perfect side dish with a roast chicken, potatoes, and a salad. Thanks for a winner, with that gorgeous French-style simplicity I love. Please edit your photos so that FT's is again the default!!

Great fritters! We especially liked the addition of the mint. The fritters are light and fresh, probably due to the absence of flour in the batter. They have to be fried carefully, as they can break up. Mine had a very nice yellow colour, not due to cheese, but to the orangey yolks of the free-range eggs! This made a great side dish with roast chicken (and 2 salads). Thank you, HokiesMom!

I LOVE risotto and this one is delicious! I did leave out the mushrooms but did not change anything else. This dish deserves the extra time and effort required while cooking it. The petite peas are the finishing touch for me. This is a keeper. Thank you for choosing me in the Help a Camera-less Chef Game #5.

I made this as posted, broiling and throwing it in the crockpot on low before I left for work. The house smelled fantastic when I got home, and the roast was tender and moist. I did thicken the gravy a little more than the recipe directed and served it over the meat and leftover RECIPE #264944. Thanks for sharing PugGrannie. Made and enjoyed for PAC Spring '09.

I am not a vegetarian and I love my burger-filled tacos, but I also love garbonzos. I just made half the recipe and I enjoyed them so much, it won't be long before I use the other half package of taco seasoning and try the taco salad version. Thanks for posting a keeper *Lena*. Made and enjoyed for PAC Spring '09 .

I made 1 potato as directed on my George Forman grill (we had a snow storm today) Instead of garlic salt I used smoked paprika, so it tasted like BBQ chips. Very good and easy too. Thanks Hokie, I will be making these on the grill if summer ever gets here! :lol: Made and enjoyed for PAC Spring '09.

This is a wonderful OAMC recipe for a single diner. I did make extra gravy and divided in 3 portions.To make 18 I patted the meat evenly  in a 9X9 pan, cut into 3" squares, then cut them each in half, and rolled into meatballs. Perfectly portioned! I made 3 portions  (6 meatballs each) of the finished recipe and froze 2 portions. I ate 3 meatballs with mashed potatoes and yummy gravy for dinner.  Two days later, I had a quick meal when I got home from work: reheated the last 3 meatballs and gravy with a dab of sour cream mixed in, boiled some noodles, and heated some green beans. I'm looking forward to using the other 2-meal portions I have in the freezer. Hokie, this recipe is true comfort food. Made and enjoyed for PAC Spring '09.

I made this on Saturday and planned to freeze half, but DARN, I ate it all by yesterday! Except for using parsley flakes because I didn't have fresh, I followed the recipe and it is so simple to make. My mom made a simpler version (just half-beef-half-chicken broth, potatoes, rice and dried minced onion). It warms the soul. I'm going to try this again using Arborio rice, but already I wish I could give 10 stars. Thank you so much for posting and I'm honored to be the first to review it.

I used homemade stock I had in the freezer and this was very fast and easy to put together. Very tasty and definitely will be made often. Makes a great starter for any oriental meal. Made for Unrated Asian Recipe Tag Game.

I've never roasted green beans before, but this won't be my last time. These were excellent! Served with Recipe #379195 and Recipe #340851 this was a wonderful combo. Made for Unrated Asian Recipe Tag Game.
Made 1/2 the recipe as a side dish with Recipe #379195. They fried up nice and brown and the flavor was delicious! Made for Unrated Asian Recipe Tag Game.
This made a perfect side-dish with Recipe #367839. Quick and delicious as promised. Thanks for a great recipe Dreamer! Made for Unrated Asian Recipe Tag.
I never had a luncheonette hot dog growing up. Now that I see what I was missing, this will be my only hot dog in the future.  What a treat! Thanks for posting DiLo. Made for Fall 2009 PAC.

I used 2 bone-in chicken breast halves in place of a whole chicken and cooked in my 1 1/2 qt. crock. This was wonderful to come home to. The chicken was tender and juicy and the potatoes were perfectly seasoned. I used the leftover chicken breast in Recipe #324833 . I love these recipes that give me 2 delicious meals! Thanks for posting Ashley. Made for Fall 2009 PAC.
Great potato salad Debb! I loved the dill flavor and it was perfect served as a side for Recipe #340393. I will definitely be making this again. Made for Fall 2009 PAC.
These were excellent served with blueberry syrup. Now that I have this recipe I will be having pancakes at home more often. Thanks for posting a keeper Debb! Made for Fall 2009 PAC.
I love this! Peach is my favorite fruit, and the almond exctract was a sweet note. I will me enjoying this again. Thanks Debb! Made for Fall 2009 PAC.
This makes tender ribs and brushed with Sweet Baby Ray's sauce and baked for 20 minutes makes great ribs. Thanks for posting Ashley! Made for Fall 2009 PAC.
This was a great side with a simple meatloaf dinner. I always love buttered noodles but the croutons make thos extra special. Thanks for posting Gayla. Made for PAC Spring 2010.

I used wide Amish noodles and they cooked up so well in the parsley-butter sauce. These were scrumptious with Recipe #413336 and Recipe #77943 . Thanks for sharing a super recipe Sharon, Made for PAC Spring 2010.
I made 1/2 the recipe as posted to serve with Recipe #395659 and I enjoyed it very much. What a great combo. Thanks for posting mersaydees. Made for PAC Spring 2010.

What a great lo-cal treat! I used Cherry Jell-O and a carton of Lite Cherry Cheesecake flavored yogurt. So easy to make and can be changed with different flavors, I'll definitely be making this again. Thanks for posting Heathersmilez. made for PAC Spring 2010.

I made half the recipe and cooked 2 patties in my GF Grill. Served with thin sliced onion and pickle, my favorite toppings. I will be making these again. Tastes great! Thanks for sharing Stacie. Made for PAC Spring 2010.

LOVE White Castles and this is a great copycat recipe. Easy to make and easy to eat! Thanks for posting Random Chef, I didn't have to venture out in the cold to satisfy my "crave". Made for PAC Spring 2010.

These are fantastic and very healthy mashed potatoes. My BIL and his 14 yo grandson both had 2nd helpings and I had no leftovers. I did add 1 TBS. dry minced onions to the potatoes as I boiled them for a little extra flavor (no added calories!) Thanks for posting a winner Lori!

I made 1 corn cob with butter, garlic powder, paprika, dried parsley, dill weed and salt and pepper. Wrapped in foil and baked as directed. Great side with a cube steak and fries for dinner. Thanks for posting Jubes! made for I recommend Tag Game.

i saved a portion of the beef from last night's meatloaf and made 1 burger for myself for lunch today. I used green onion and a dash of garlic powder and did not change the rest of ingredients. Cooked in the GF Grill and served with a slice of Vidalia onion and pickle chips. This made a juicy and tender burger. Thanks for posting Chocolatl! Made for 1-2-3 Hits Tag Game.

Such a tasty way to cook peas! Quick and easy to prepare. Served with Recipe #233734 and mashed potatoes. I love pine nuts but never use them for everyday recipes. That will teach me! Thanks for sharing smellyvegetarian. Made for 1-2-3 Hits Tag Game,

I still have the pasta machine my Mom bought me. It does it all, mixes and extrudes and it takes me longer to clean it than to make the noodles. I made half the recipe and had some chicken stock in the freezer. Made a wonderful pot of homemade chicken noodle soup!! Thanks for sharing Pink Diamond. Made for Newest Zaar Tag.

This was easy with the pat-in-the-pan crust, and I used sugar-free raspberry jam. I had to try a piece as soon as it was cool enough and it was delicious. Thanks for posting Starrynews. Made for the Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.
Great and easy casserole, made as posted. Served with Recipe #425677 and rich beefy gravy. I will be making this again! Thanks for posting Deantini. Made for the Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

I made half the recipe, as posted. Next time I will make the full recipe and freeze for OAMC as this was delicious and fairly easy to make. Thanks for posting ingrid. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.
Excellent and simple side dish served with Recipe #325218. Added  Recipe #216380 to the finished dish. I will be making this often. Thanks for posting littlemafia. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

This made a great "breakfast for lunch" meal served with Recipe #173794 for a side dish. What a wonderful combination! Fluffy eggs and savory muffins -definitely a keeper combo! Dill is one of my favorite herbs. Thanks for posting jewe, Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

Great golden brown French toast! I've never added flour to the eggs before and this batter was a plus! I spread mine with blackberry preserves and it tasted heavenly. Thanks for sharing this recipe, it's a keeper Melissa. Made for Swizzle Chicks for ZWT6.
I served these potatoes with Recipe #427202 and they went together so well. I like potatoes with bacon! Thanks for posting France. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6,

I used baby peas and found this unusual combination to be a nice surprise! I loved the spice combo too. I added an English muffin and a cup of Recipe #233108 to take the chill off the morning. Thanks Nasseh, Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

I subbed a large skinless chicken breast half for the thighs (personal preference) and followed the instructions. Needed the hour to cook the chicken. It was tender and tasty! Served with Recipe #359156 for a side dish. Great combination. Thanks for posting Michele. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.
I love fresh green beans and this was an easy and quick way to make them! Served with Recipe #289194 made a great meal. Thanks for sharing Lynn. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

As a confirmed dill nut I use it in soup, spaghetti sauce, pasta salad, tuna salad, egg salad, potato salad, ETC.... Now I love it on fried eggs too! LOL! I prefer "basted" eggs and fried a sliced potato with them and had a wonderful breakfast this morning. Thanks for sharing littlemafia. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

Mmmmm! THE Friday night supper of my childhood ~ a great mac and cheese! True comfort food! I went a little lighter on the salt and added a few extra grinds of pepper. Thanks for sharing Sharon. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

I just lot my review so this will be shorter. Made as posted and even better than the local Greek restaurant by me. I will be making this again. Thanks for posting Syd. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

I reduced this to 2 servings. This was my "lesson" since I never made couscous before. I'm glad I chose your recipe Rita. It was so easy. I used beef broth and butter and left it plain and simple to test it out. I liked it and feel I'm ready to try a little fancier now. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

Made as posted with a little less garlic than specified. The meat was very tender and I served the sauce over wide noodles. Loved the addition of spices. I will be making this again for sure! Thanks for posting Chocolatl. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

if you grew up with your mom making these eggs for you, they continue to be comfort food when you grow up (even into your 60's LOL). This is an easy breakfast and needs to be enjoyed often! Thanks for posting Nif! Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

Roasted with herbes de provence and found this was so easy to make. The gravy was delicious served over buttered noodles. I have another breast half to serve chilled tomorrow with Recipe #227732. I love these two-fer meals that only require cooking once! Thanks for posting Scoutie! Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6.

Made 4 servings, this was good. I used 3 tablespoons Splenda and it worked out well. It's much better than the commercial flavored tea available. Thanks for posting Rachel. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6 ZINGO.

I made 1 serving for breakfast. I had just about 1 cup leftover Recipe #383719 that was just enough for me. Topped with Recipe #391832 and a a nice cuppa Lady Jane tea! I love this combo and will definitely make it again. Thanks for posting SarahBeth. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6 Family Picks.

I made these with homemede white bread and found if sliced very thin it dries faster. It is fresher and better than store bought but if I am in a hurry and not preplanned I will use store bought. Thanks for sharing Rachel. Made for Zwizzle Chicks for ZWT6 Family Picks.

I quartered the recipe as posted using Recipe #39350 and Splenda in place of sugar, and served it on Recipe #226443 for a light and tasty lunch. Thanks for posting kittycatmom. Made for When It's Hot Tag Game.

I wasn't real sure about this but doggone it, it worked! I was afraid of smashing an egg when I tried to poke it, but that didn't happen either. I followed the recipe and instructions and put 2 eggs in the ziploc with a dash of salt for the fridge for tomorrow, We'll see what happens, but I have been happy so far! Thanks for sharing some great tips Monstr, Made for When It's Hot Tag Game.

I split a sourdough English muffin, piled on the filling (including a dash of marjoram) and used muenster cheese, closed the muffin and quickly heated in the George Foreman grill. Loved the flavor and enjoyed this for my evening snack! Thanks for posting Kitty and thanks to Boomie's review which prompted me to make this! Made for I Recommend Tag,

Made half the recipe and made as posted. This is so refreshing! I love watermelon and the lime juice is the perfect touch. The 1 tablespoon sugar was just the right amount. Thanks for sharing Nif. Made for Choose Your Event Party.

Made half the recipe as posted. This is an easy and delicious side dish. I used frozen baby peas and added just to heat at the end of cooking so they stayed a little crunchy. Thanks for posting Sid. Made for I Recommend Tag Game.
Made as posted but used mayo instead of Miracle Whip. Served with a few pickle slices for  great lunch. Thanks for posting iewe. Made for I Recommend Tag.

Made these super easy potatoes to go with Mini Skillet Meatloaves #400651 on a hot and humid 90°  day and did not heat the house up! YAY! No pan to wash either! YAY again! I made as posted but added a sprinkle of onion powder for seasoning. Thanks for postng bmcnichol. Made for I Recommend Tag Game.

I followed the recipe using 1 lb ground turkey and 1/2 lb ground beef to lower fat content and cooked in electric skillet at 400°. I loved the tangy sauce and had 2 for dinner tonight and have 4 to wrap and store in the freezer for 2 more quick meals! Thanks for posting Crafty Lady. Made for I Recommend Tag Game.

I made half the recipe with 2 eggs & 1 egg white, and used honey mustard and fresh dill, and served with rye toast and a wedge of cantalope. I loved the texture and the flavor combination! Thanks for posting Boomie! Made for I Recommend Tag.

This is a great soup. made as posted for 4 servings but skipped the Maggi Sauce (never used it and checked on line - The sodium count is 1480 gr per tablespoon and lots of chemical ingredients - too scary for me personally. Another reviewer mentioned a smoky taste so I added a bit of snoked paprika. This had a full "earthy" taste which I loved. Thanks for posting Julie. Made for I Recommend Tag.

Made as posted using Instant sugar free Cafe Vienna mix for instant coffee and only 1 packet of Splenda. The added protein rounded out my daily nutrition. The "cheesecake" caught my eye and I'm so glad I made and enjoyed this. Thanks for posting Annacia, you win the golden coffee cup award! Made for I Recommend Tag.

I made 1/4 recipe in my 1 1/2 qt crock! 2 packets sugar free cocoa mix, 2 c water, 1/4 c hershey syrup, 1 Tbl PB, and a dash of vanilla. Reduced calories and sugar by half! Yummy treat and warmed me up on a chilly fall morning. Thanks for a keeper Annacia. Made for Diabetic Tailgate Party.

Made this today and enjoyed on a chilly rainy afternoon. My only changes, I left out texas pete (I don't do hot) and salt (I limit sodium). In place of water I added 1 1/2 c of V8 juice. This smelled so good all day while it cooked and tasted even better! I will put half in the freezer for another chilly day. Thanks for posting a keeper SB. Made for your win in Football Pool 2010 Week 4.

Made as posted except omitted hot sauce. This is quick and easy. I love rice in tomato soup and the chicken broth and celery were a nice addition. Excellent served with a grilled cheese sandwich. Thanks for sharing loof. Made for your win in Football Pool 2010 Week 6.

I made half the recipe as posted except I checked my spice drawer and found I'm out of thyme so I subbed a dash of marjoram. I also used low-sodium chicken stock for broth. Great tasting and easy to put together, the carrots and corn giving substance and flavor. Thanks for posting Sarah. Made for Crockpot and Rice Cooker Game.

Such an easy and delicious recipe. I used diet ginger ale as I never have regular pop in the house. I also did not have brown gravy mix in the house but I had pork gravy mix so I used it instead. The beef was very tender and the gravy was rich. Sometimes these little accidental subs turn out VERY good! Served with mashed potatoes to spoon the gravy over. YUM! Thanks for posting a keeper weekend cooker. Made for I Recommend Tag.

On this cool rainy morning I cut the recipe down to 2 servings, served in a large mug just for myself! YUM! I used Splenda for the sugar and this made a creamy, chocolaty treat! Thanks for posting Julie. Made for Recipe Swap #46.

Made with thick slices of homemade bread as posted. Great combination of flavors! Grilled in my George Foreman grill for a total of 5 minutes. Quick and tasty! Thanks for posting SB6. Made for your Football Pool 2010 - week 11.

I made 2 servings in my 1 1/2 qt crockpot. I cooked the rice in pineapple juice/water. Used an 8 oz can pineapple and it wasn't too much. When cooled, I topped with Cool Whip, cinnamon, and chopped pecans and it was creamy and thick. Thanks for posting Doug. Made for your win in Football Pool Week 10 - 2010.
Made these as posted and I am lucky enough to have a spaetzle maker. An easy to make side dish with some leftover pot roast and gravy! Thanks for posting awalde. Made for Newest Zaar Tag.

I love deviled eggs. I boiled 1 extra egg for the yolk and ate the extra white empty. I like to really "stuff" em! I used dill weed and followed the recipe otherwise. These were perfect! Thanks for posting breezermom. Made for Everyday is a Holiday. Great PARTY food!

Made half the recipe in my 1 1/2 qt crock, used 1 can cream of chicken, 4 oz can chunk chicken breast, added 8 oz can peas and carrots, 5 count can buttermilk biscuits. Very easy comfort food. Thanks for posting breezermom. Made for your win in Football Pool Week 15.

This was easy to make and I used baking toffee chips sprinkled on top. Very sweet, so I tried to limit my portion, but there was plenty for others. Thanks for sharing Alligirl. Made for yuor win in Football Pool Week 14.

Made as posted with Mock Chicken Stock Recipe #359988 from my freezer and very low in fat and sodium. I came home from shopping today chilled to the bone. This goes together quickly and in less than an hour I was eating and enjoying this! Thanks for posting breezer. Made for Newest Zaar Tag (Winter).
Very easy recipe. I made half in a 6X9 loaf pan using sugar free maple syrup and Mexican cinnamon chocolate. Great flavor, Thanks for posting loof. Made for RECIPE SWAP #48 - January.
Wonderful and easy recipe! Made as posted and I was very pleased with the crunchy topping. Thanks for posting gailanng. Made for RECIPE SWAP #48.

Made exactly as posted and this is the BEST pumpkin bread I've ever had! I loved the addition of marmaladee to the bread and the orange cream cheese spread would have kicked it up to 10 stars if I could. Thanks for sharing this keeper Breezermom! Made for Everyday Is A Holiday February 2011.
This is a nice easy recipe. I added a touch of dill to the dumplings and they were terrific! thanks for posting Kalice . Made for Zaar Cookbook Tag.

I had roasted garlic instant mashed potatoes and mad them per this recipe with my meatloaf. They were better if only because they were so easy to make and they did taste better too. Thanks for posting mailbelle. Made for Zaar Cookbook Tag.
I made half the recipe, used 1/2 c 2% milk, frozen strawberries, and skipped the ice. This was very tasty. I love it! Thanks for posting Alli. Made for your Football Pool 2010 - SUPERBOWL win.
I made half the recipe to go with simple oven baked chicken breast. Easy and tasty! Thanks for sharing alligirl. Made for Everyday Is A Holiday.

So easy to make heavenly muffins! Great for breakfast, lunch, or snack! Made as posted and stashed half in the freezer to have on hand as needed. I have a feeling they won't be in there too long, YUM! Thanks for posting Deb. Made for Pick A Chef Spring 2011.
Super easy and very tasty! Great sandwiches for lunch. Thanks for sharing Jean. Made for Pick A Chef Spring 2011.

Love pasta! This was so rich and decadent! Not something I would eat everyday but makes a meal into a special occassion. I had to sub Parmesan cheese. Thanks for sharing Bonnie. Made for Pick A Chef Spring 2011.

This is the opposite steps of my Mom's Best Ribs. I figured I would try it and by golly it works real well. The house smelled like Sunday did when I was growing up. I used Mom's homemade BBQ sauce too. Your dad and my mom were smiling down on us today! Thanks so much for sharing Britta, and I would recommend your method to newbie chefs just starting out. Made for Pick A Chef Spring 2011.

I used 1 cooked chicken breast and half the remaining ingredients, slicing the celery with my mandoline. I loved the addition of honey and served it on bakery deli-rye. Thanks for posting Jean. Made for Pick A Chef Spring 2011.
Cut down to 1 serving as posted for a tasty splurge! Thanks for the sweet treat RyGuy. Made for Pick A Chef Spring 2011.

What a wonderful recipe this is!  I really wasn't expecting much but wanted to give it a try to see if it was something my grandkids would eat even though I'm not a lasagna lover.  I halved the recipe but used only 1/2 lb hamburger.  Also used 2 cups water and 2 chicken bouillon cubes in place of the broth.  It was extremely thick so I added a cup or so more water.  This is SO good and I'm SO impressed!  I know my grandkids will be crazy about it.

This is one of those recipes I almost wish I had never discovered because I love it too, too much!  It is SO GOOD!!!!!  I don't have a large enough coffee mug so I used one of my straight-sided soup bowls, which worked well.  Then the 2nd time I made it, I experimented by mixing the dry ingredients in a separate bowl, then adding it all to the wet ingredients and that worked well also.  I really like that it doesn't require egg.  Hey,  I'm thinking Christmas gifts, folks...

I really like this quick and simple recipe.  I added some dry onion flakes to the water, plus more salt.  Used whole wheat macaroni and did have to cook it an additional 5 minutes.  Also used non-dairy creamer powder mixed with water for the cream.  Will definitely make this again.  Thanks for sharing!

Like Andi, I also decided to try this recipe after seeing it's low rating and I'm so glad I did. I followed the recipe exactly and used regular soy sauce. After marinating the thighs for 3 hours, I then cooked as directed, although after 35 min. it wasn't quite done so I left it in the oven another 10 min. We absolute loved the dark, crispy and oh-so-tasty (and not excessively salty) skin. And the meat itself was moist, tender and delicious. Perfect!
I'm very impressed with this lovely recipe and wouldn't change a thing. Thanks, Silver. I'll be making this often.
Can't really understand what all the 5 star reviews are about. I used fresh potatoes and followed the recipe and thought this was ok but I honestly would prefer plain mashed potatoes.

Decided to try this recipe since it didn't call for ketchup and all kinds of sugar and I'm so glad I did.  It's good but (thankfully) not sweet like so many sloppy joe recipes.  Since I was also testing this recipe to see if my grandkids would like it, I didn't add the green pepper but will if I'm only making it for myself.  I cooked it uncovered and it was just right after 15 minutes, not too sloppy at all.
This was a simple and good crock pot recipe.  It was a little bland, but I will make it again and maybe play with some spices.

There is a local restaurant that makes the most wonderful fresh fruit martini's.  This recipe tastes exactly like their Lemon Drop Martini, which is my favorite.  Thank you so much for this delicious drink.
These were dee-lish!  Very Sex and the City!
This was good for a WW dinner.  I was torn between 3 and 4 stars but because of the simplicity of the recipe, I gave it 4 stars.  I don't like mushrooms so I left them out.
I was disappointed with this soup.  It was really thin and bland tasting.  At the last minute I added more cheese to give it more flavor.   I am not sure how many points this added.
We found this to be pretty ordinary.  It was good, but my carrots were not done, so I had to cook it longer.  Thank you for posting, but I don't think I will be making this again.
These were good but I thought they were a little dry.  They are like a dense coffee cake.
This baked Ziti is sooo good!  A big hit in our family and easy to make.

Usually, when a recipe calls for Cream of Mushroom soup, I substitute Cream of Chicken soup because I hate mushrooms.  I did not do thst with this recipe, and I am so glad.  This was sooo good!  I think it was probalby the Golden Mushroom soup that gave it such a rich flavor.  I will definately make this one again.

This is delicious and very easy to make.  I love the cooking with spices until most of the liquid is gone, and then putting on the barbecue sauce. This makes the chicken so much better. Made for Kittencal tagathon 2008.
This is good and easy to make. I followed the ingredients. Made for BT 2008.

This is a tasty and good side dish to make instead of potatoes or rice.  I followed ingredients in recipe except for jalapenos, used green chilis, no mushrooms, used all medium cheddar cheese. Made for Newest Tag 2008

The RSC list of ingredients includes some strong flavors and colors, and this dish does a pretty good job of accenting and balancing several of the more exotic ones.  We had it for lunch; it could be breakfast alongside a couple of eggs. The men of the house gobbled it down while the ladies were indifferent.  If I do it again, I'll boil the potatoes less, since they have plenty of cooking time in the skillet.  Made and reviewed for RSC #11.

Any chef who likes to bake, and especially one who likes the herbal and the cheesy kinds of bread, will not be able to resist this recipe.  The process is a delight, the aroma from the oven a treat, and the product is delicious.  There are some problems, however.  The spiral trapped air and created large voids in the slice, especially at the top, and the spinach looks more like cooked vegetables than herbal decoration.  Great possibilities but needs some refinement.

We thought this a bit contived to fit in RSC 11 and now believe it should be three recipes.   In any case, all three are delicious and won me over on a fork.  Toppings 1 and 3 resemble fondue.  Topping 2 is entirely different, a thin clear sauce, calling for a different presentation.  I wouldn't serve the three together unless I was hosting a party.
Wonderful!  I sliced and bruised the garlic instead of mincing it, for the sake of appearance mostly.  This is easy, delicious, and distinctive.  Made for Market Tag March 2008.

Marvelous, and could be better with practice.  We used the oven since the bar-b-q is put up for the winter, and perhaps should have cooked them a little longer -- but the family ate them and asked for more.

You'd have to appreciate shrimp to understand the pleasure of finding a plump, firm one with your tongue that your eye had missed in the bed of cheese.  This is a delicious and hearty meal.  We used a sweet red sauce left over from another Zaar experience, and our kids wished we had used our usual basil-centered marinara, but it was very fine nevertheless.  Made for OZ/NZ swap March 2008.

Something we've wanted to do for a while, and did not disappoint.  These are delicious!  A few comments:  be sure to keep the dough cold until it goes in the cooker or they'll be hollow.  Also, an inch is too thick; roll to half an inch.  We made some round ones as instructed and then got the result we really expected by cutting the dough in 1x2" strips with a floured knife.  Great! Made for Pick A Chef Spring 2008.
This is a good and easy potato dish to a make for dinner. The ingredients go well together. I followed the ingredients per recipe.  Made for photo tag.,

We made this with beef and had to cook it under the broiler because our grill was out of propane.  Dumped the extra marinade with its veggies on top midway through broiling. Came out great!  My DH has a fond place in his heart for "schaschlik" served at Faschings Fests in Germany in the seventies, and this is the very thing.  Thank you!  Made for Let's Get Skewered, May 2008.
This is very good marinade. I followed ingredients per recipe except we used chicken tenders and we ran out of sherry so added some white wine.  Made for Please Review My Recipe.

This is very very good.  It is very creamy and extremely chocolatey.  1 scoop of this gelato is just the right amt.  The biscotti added a nice touch.  I do not care for anise but you couldn't taste the anise in the gelato.  I followed all the ingredients per recipe except for the Frangelico, we substituted Hazlenut syrup.  It worked great. Made for ZWT4 Cookin Cats.

Way cool, we can make our own pita bread!  The whole process was fun and rewarding, and the result was a pleasant surprise.  DH used K.A. "white whole wheat" flour throughout and added a little wheat gluten, but otherwise followed the directions exactly.  The only difficulty was the wide spacing of our oven rack; it would have been nice to have a screen of some sort to cook them on. Still, they puffed up into the traditional pockets and came out looking great.  We made this as an ingredient for another recipe being made for ZWT4.

This is a wonderful base for a fruit salad.  We used cantaloupe, watermelon, bananas, apricots, kiwi fruit, pineapple, strawberries, green grapes.  My DD accidentally threw out the juice off the apricots so I used a cup of tamarind juice left over from last nights fruit salad recipe. I put the vanilla in but no sugar.  It was not necessary.  Made for ZWT4.

This makes a delicious wonderful panini.  I used artesian garlic bread.  I used cream cheese because I didn't have any goat cheese.  I followed the rest of ingredients per recipe.  The sauce reduced very well and is a really great sauce.  We will be making these again. Made for ZWT4 for the Cookin Cats.
This are very tasty and easy to make.  I followed the ingredients per recipe.  I used Canadian Whiskey.  Made for ZWT4 for the Cookin Cats

This is a very good recipe.  Anythign involving chicken breasts, marsala wine and mushrooms just has to be good.  I followed ingredients per recipe including using marsala wine. I used a combo of Baby Bella  and crimini mushrooms.  Made for ZWT4 for the Cookin Cats.
This is a delicious chicken marinade.  I planned on making his during round 3 but didn't get it in.  We had friends and all loved this, Made for ZWT4 for the Cookin Cats
This is a very good marinade.  I followed the ingredients per recipe except no cayenne pepper.  Made for ZWT4 for Cookin Cats

This is a very good guacamole.  I followed ingredients per recipe except I didn't have tomatoes or jalapeno so I used my homemade salsa which has both.  I love the lime juice instead of lemon juice.
Made for ZWT4 for the Cookin Cats.

This is so easy and so delicious.  We made this and recipe#73103 last night for a wonderful barbecue loved by all my family. We followed ingredients per recipe except we ran out of olive oil and had to use canola oil. Made for ZWT4 for the Cookin Cats.

These are tasty, remarkably uniform and attractive large cookies, suitable for a buffet spread. We followed ingredients per recipe, except that we accidentally made one batch without brown sugar; that made them thicker and softer but still delicious.  Thank you for translating and updating these wonderful old recipes! We made these for ZWT4 for the Cookin' Cats.

This made a plain old chuck steak into a juicy and rich treat. We used extra brown sugar in place of honey but otherwise followed the recipe exactly, and it was terrific. Made to post in the July grilling photo challenge.

This is a very good beef and broccoli recipe.  I followed the ingredients per recipe.  The only change I would make is to add the green onions at the last minute so they are just fresh looking.  Made for PRMR 2008.

Simple and great! We did leave out the green onions just because DH used them up and didn't get more... and when there is cheese to add to potatoes, LL puts more on top. Bacon and sour cream, yum! No leftovers. Made for the new Kid Friendly thread.
This was so easy and quick to make. The chicken is very moist and tasty.  I followed the ingredients per recipe.  My DH barbecued this on the grill. Made for Beverage Tag.

This is a good take-off on a classic sandwich.  I didn't have a pizza crust or the time to make a yeast one so I used a flour tortilla.  I put a little oil on it and put it under broiler until browned on each side.  Then I followed ingredients per recipe except for I only had mozz cheese.  The mayonnaise mixture is a little like a pesto.  I cut up my tomatoes.  I put the pizza in the oven until cheese was melted for about 10-15 minutes @300 degrees F.  Made for 1,2,3 Hit wonders.
This is a great way to make a different kind of corn on the cob.  I wasn't sure what herbs to use so I used 1/2 basil and 1/2 oregano.  We added extra garlic.  This was made for Az/NZ swap#19.

This is a very good and easy to make dinner.  I followed the recipe except for the green onons, we were out of them.   My Dh cooked this on the barbecue.  My DS and DD just loved this.  Made for PRMR.
Super easy, absolutely delicious and one of the prettiest dishes we have had the pleasure to photograph. Very rich.  Made for PRMR August 2008.

This is great.   My DS even made the recipe and got it ready for my Dh to cook when he got home from work. My DS followed the ingredients per recipe.  We had run out of fresh ginger but everything else the same.
 Unfortunately my DS was hungry late last night and ate the meat that DH was going to take a picture of.  Mde for swap #19

So good!  Light and fluffy batter compliments the mild chili flavor, and its warm color is appetizing on the plate.  We found most of the chilis in the can already broken, but improvised and it came out fine. Technique is a little intimidating to a newcomer, but in fact it was not hard to do, and well worth a try. Made for PRMR Aug. 2008.
We served this with meat loaf, broccoli and watermelon on the back deck for a relaxed and hearty dinner.  Very good comfort food and easy to do.  Made for Holiday Tag Aug 2008.

We liked this marzetti.  It is easy to make.  We are really enjoying bell peppers as an ingredient.  I  used regular tomato sauce. I followed all the ingredients but I am sure I added some extra cheese.  Made for PRMR 2008.
This is very good.  It is also easy to put together. I followed the ingredients per recipe except for the walnuts, personal taste. Made for PRMR.

Four solid stars for an easy, tasty, hearty beef stew whose only shortcoming is a flavor accent we often experience in crockpot cooking; I'd like to try it again using the oven and shorter cooking times.  (No rating whatever, good or bad, on the dumplings since we couldn't find fresh suet in our area and DH's attempted substitution just didn't work.)  Made for PRMR, Nov. 2008.
A bright spot on our table tonight in both color and flavor!  Sweet on first taste, then a little spicy afterward.  Made for Photo Tag Nov 2008.
Simple and delicious!  We made this from frozen cut beans and served it with our Thanksgiving dinner.  Easily done even amid the chaos of turkey day in a small kitchen!  Thanks, Lainey!

This is absolutely delicious.  My DS and I made this to go with our Dinner and we loved it.  Followed all the ingredients per recipe.  Just the right sweetness and great tartness.  Made for Holiday Tag.

This is a good easy casserole.  This is my first time making homemade macaroni and cheese so I don't really know how it is supposed to taste.  My family felt that this is a little bland.  Made for PRMR.

This is a good and very easy steak recipe.  I followed all ingredients except the charbroil seasoning, it is not available here.  I looked it up to see what was in it and added that.  Made for Holiday Tag.

This is a great, easy, and quick lunch.  My children and I used to make these all the time when they were little.  We made these for lunch today while being home from no school.  It really brought back memories.  I did't have add celery from personal taste.  I did'nt have any lemon pepper so just used regular pepper.  We used provolone and cheddar cheese.  Made for 1,2,3 Hit wonders.

We had to substitute fresh crisp-fried bacon and toast our own chopped almonds, but otherwise followed instructions exactly. The beans were delicious and a little different from what we usually make, and easy to do, too.  Made for Holiday Tag.
This warm, sweet spiced cider just hit the spot for my DH and his head cold -- the steamy flavors came through!  The rest of us liked it, too. Made for AU/NZ swap Dec. 2008.

While we had doubts about all the chunky bell pepper and tomato while making this, we loved the final product!  One of us suggested less thyme, but still eagerly wolfed it down. We usually use very plain chips with our guac, but the hearty flavors in this will stand up to the spicy ones, too.   Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders, Jan. 2009.
Nice and easy, and also rich and delicious!  A little reminiscent of chicken Marsala.  We served it alongside Recipe#292368.  Made for PRMR, Jan. 09.
I found this marvelous skinny little asparagus and cooked it into this rice for a great companion piece to Recipe#321656.  Easy to do and great flavor!  Made for PRMR, Jan. 09.
Only complaint is that the pan was too small!  These are a fudgy, flavorful treat.  Made for Market Tag, Jan. 09.

This is really a marinade recipe, and it's good! garlic, lime, and herbs shine through into the finished taco, which we served on flour Gorditas.  Although this is billed as "summertime" fare and for outdoor grilling, we used the broiler in January with great results.  Made for Market Tag, Jan 09.

"Stir until just blended" and our cast iron skillet gave these a more rustic texture and appearance than some others we've tried, but the flavor was great, and the texture light and fluffy.  Two to three pancakes satisfied most appetites, so this is a great recipe for a houseful.  We scaled it to three eggs, fed four people, and put half the batter in the fridge for tomorrow.  Made for the Potluck Game, Jan. 09.

Something between a quiche, a strata, and a tamale pie, this dish is fairly mild but distinctly Mexican in accent, and its appearance is colorful and festive.  We made it in a 13x9" glass pan and it came out right on time.  It's a pleasure to eat!  Made for PRMR, Jan. 09.

This went away very quickly! The best part is the aroma of the chorizo cooking -- maybe it was just the variety we bought, but it smelled almost floral. Too spicy for one of us, but that's more for the rest of us. Made for PRMR in January 2009.

We eat a lot of quesadillas here, mostly the plain cheese and tortilla kind with sour cream and salsa, and this variation with meat and corn was a big hit. Olive oil is a natural match and a nice flavor accent. We made this exactly to the recipe then embellished it further with celantro, homemade salsa, extra cheese, and jalapeno slices to taste.  Very nice!   Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders, Jan 2009.
Been searching for a good pot sticker sauce recipe like our local restaurant.  This sauce comes very close.  We added twice the sugar to get the flavor we wanted.  Made for AZ swap#25.

What a luscious salad!  The dressing alone is awesome and the combination of pecans and blue cheese topped it off. In spite of the featured appearance of the wedge, I think I'd go ahead and shred the lettuce next time; the flavors would be the same and it would be easier to eat.  (Also, I added black olives to mine and might suggest hardboiled egg which would make it almost a Cobb salad.)  It did seem to me to be about enough toppings for four wedges, needing only a little extra cheese to double the listed number of servings; your mileage may vary.  In summary: Really nice salad with room for personalization!  Made for AZ/NZ tag Feb. 2009.

Easy and indulgent, this came out tender and saucy and wonderful.  We couldn't get dried mushrooms, so we used fresh Crimini ones, cut in pieces and steeped in boiling water as suggested for the dried ones.  This seems to have worked.  Ooh, fabulous, TDF!

As our grill was put away for the winter, we used the broiler.  It came out great!  We thought we caught a hint of lemon or lime, but there's none in it.  We used a scattering of red pepper flakes instead of a whole chili, giving the whole dish a bit of zip and some flecks of color. Made for Gimme 5, February 2009.

Although there were jokes about "special (fry) sauce" when this was going into the oven, it really is pretty special coming out, and our crew wolfed this down enthusiastically.  It's tough to photograph; you can't see the meat in the sauce!  But that is the best part anyway.  Made for PRMR, Feb. 2009.

We served this with Recipe#241877 and completely enjoyed both together!  Using oil to cling the breading was a new idea to me, but it worked and produced a crispy crust. I prepared this in a well-seasoned cast-iron skillet which made it darker than non-stick coating would have.  Rich, moist inside, and delicious!  made for PRMR, Feb. 09.

DH made this and made a dialect translation mistake: he used corn meal instead of corn starch for "corn flour."  As a result, our cookies have a whole-grain texture that wasn't intended but also isn't half bad! So they feel healthful but this is a guilty pleasure: it's clearly not a low-fat or low-sugar recipe. Regardless, the cookies are tender and sinfully delicious! If they're this good done wrong, we'll have to try them again to see what they could be.  Made for PRMR, Feb. 2009.

We actually compromised the healthy feature slightly with plain white flour tortillas.  The recipe and techniques remain solid and produced a tasty, satisfying dinner with low fat and modest effort.  Made for PRMR, Feb 09.
After discovering panini's on the ZWT I try every recipe I come upon and this is a great one.  Delicious and easy to make.  I used fresh basil and ciabatta bread. Made for PRMR.
Flavor of this casserole was right on delicious. Made this w/o the onion rings for DD preference. Made for Gimme5.

Hearty, easy casserole that comes out something like a cross between lasagne and ravioli.  Great tasting and filling at the time, and reheats nicely for lunch the next day!  We cut back on the onion (personal preference) and added sliced pepperoni on top, just under the cheese.  Made for PRMR, March 2009.
We're used to thinking of oatmeal cookies being thick and soft; these are different, thin and crisp and quite sweet. That didn't keep the teenagers away! We'll definitely make these again.

Family reviews on this came out positive but lukewarm: everyone liked it, nobody raved about it.  We blame the crockpot rather than the seasonings -- the balance of sweet and sour was just right -- and would probably suggest shortening the cooking time for the beef itself. I followed the recipe exactly except for using carrot chunks instead of baby carrots.   Made for Zaar Stars, March 2009.
Easy, quick, and sweet, indulgently sweet.  I'd like to try doing this with from-scratch dough, too, but when we made this batch we were glad it was so simple.

Easy, quick, appetizing, and delicious! We served this as a bright-colored side to sticky chicken over rice, spooning on the extra liquid to flavor the rice.  In this way we served it to seven, but any one of us could have finished it off alone. Made for OZ/NZ swap, April 09.

This is a meaty sloppy joe, not much sauce, but great BBQ-style flavor.  We didn't have any celery, but one of us doesn't usually like it anyway. Otherwise, made as instructed; it went together quickly and came out terrific. Great treat to take out to the patio on a spring evening!  Thanks!  Made for OZ/NZ swap, April 09.

If you like garlic, you'll love this!  We made it in two pans, not having one pan big enough, and made the sauce in one.  Your choice: crispy or moist; both are delicious.  Super simple to do and delightfully different from what we would usually do with these ingredients.  I worried about the amount of oil/fat, but if kept hot, nearly all of it pours off.  Made for Zaar World Tour 5.

You could just sit and look at this beautiful slab of salmon and get great enjoyment, but the flavor is terrific as well. We would put on the glaze a little thicker in future, but that's our own fault; it looked like a lot before broiling. Made for ZWT5 and served with Recipe#367789.

We loved this!  By habit we went a little heavy on the fresh ginger, so no surprise that it was the first accent when the first bite hits the tongue.  After that the citrus and mustard come through in balance and the salmon was about perfect, both moist and flaky with a thin translucent glaze.  We grilled it on a little broiler rack on the gas barbecue, and found it stuck by the skin and impossible to turn so finished it off, rack and all, under the oven broiler, which worked well.  Made for Zaar World Tour 5.

I agree with the previous reviewer that the sauce made this dish; although I left some burger exposed for the photo, it was actually served completely smothered and accompanied by Recipe#249021 and roasted garlic.  DS22 remarked that the sauce would be even better on a steak.  Made for ZWT5.

Revised!  We made these recently with yams because we couldn't find sweet potatoes. Today we found them and tried again, with much more satisfying results. Yams are sweeter but didn't bake to the nice fragile crispness.  The flavoring was terrific both ways, and the notes of cayenne and smoky paprika gave them a bit of a zip that hangs around after the fries are gone. Well worth the effort for the adventure alone. Made by LL's DH for ZWT5.

Very easy to make and wonderful on the table!  The mustard and honey play off against one another and the preserves give it an unusual and delightful texture. We used boneless thighs, since that was what was on hand, and it worked well except for being in smaller pieces.  Made for ZWT5.

Just a classic deviled egg! Ingredients are all "to taste," meaning that with a little practice, this will be your own. We garnished them with paprika, served them alongside Jerk Chicken and enjoyed them. Made for Zaar World Tour 5.

Especially for such humble-looking fare, this is amazingly good!  Because of a mixup on what should be done before and after cooking, we left out most of the salt, and didn't miss it; the garlic salt, chipotle cube, and hot sauce gave it flavor aplenty, without being unreasonably hot. Very satisfying; you can see why it's a regional tradition.  Made for Zaar World Tour 5.

Really simple, bread at its most basic, just right for the table, and delicious.  I made three baguettes out of this and sprinkled poppy seed on one, sesame seed on another.  Made for Zaar World Tour 5.

Sinfully rich, just delightfully excessive with the bacon, onions, and gouda cheese.  We made a lot to have leftovers and there may not be any come morning. A great companion to our dinner of grilled Jerk pork.  Made for Zaar World Tour 5.
Just the right crispness and full of peanut butter. A perfect peanut butter cookie.  Made for ZWT5 for Zingo.

Enjoyed this a lot.  Our pork came to us as thick chops, and because one of us had to leave, we cooked one chop with the rub in a cast-iron skillet to get it done sooner -- that one was the best.  The rest were roasted as instructed.  Both ways, delicious; the pan fried one was juicier. Raves for the onions and peppers!  Made for Zaar World Tour 5.

After seeing Magpie's picture I want to try this with asparagus!  DH is also intrigued with using some of the dried hot Mexican peppers in place of the sweet red one. This time, though, I made it exactly to the recipe and it came out great.  It was just one piece of a terrific ZWT supper, but DD16 commented that it was the rice that tied it all together, because it went so well with each other item on the plate.  Made for Zaar World Tour 5.

My husband insists he invented this years ago as a starving student.  It's easy, quick, cheap, and classy all at once, and don't tell anybody, but it's good for you, too. I love summer squash and this is a very good way to make it.  We used shaved Parmesan+Romano cheese, which melted into a nice blanket on the squash. Made for Zaar World Tour 5.
Citrusy, crisp drink.  I used gold rum instead of white and orange juice (instead of cointreau).  Made for July Comfort Cafe.

We had no idea what Gazpacho should look like or taste like, and ours looks a little green because we used a green pepper in place of the orange one.  Aside from all that, this stuff is good!  Spicy because of the jalapeno, but all the flavors are present and make themselves known, with the ginger and celantro giving it a twist and the honey lending sweetness.  Made for Comfort Cafe, July 09.

Simple and classic.  We had only dried herbs, but that worked; they reconstituted somewhat while baking, and the garlic was fresh in any case. What Mom used to do with margarine and garlic salt is so much better with real stuff!  Made for Zaar Stars, July 2009.

This was really good and enjoyed by all, except that one didn't care for the strong ginger flavor.  The sauce thickened more than expected and very quickly, so I would suggest half the cornstarch next time.  Luxurious in appearance and flavor, this was an excellent supper and whatever nit-picking I may do is lost in the excellence of the whole plate.
Just peachy, creamie, easy to make.  Made for breakfast for my DD and I.  The taste of honey was just a little too intense for us.  Made for Beverage Tag.

Delicious Potatoes.  I added extra cheese in the middle of the layer of potatoes.  We love cheesey potatoes.  We didn't have a shallot so added extra garlic.  Didn't add the red pepper flakes because of personal preference.  Made for Gimme 5.
Good Chicken.  Enjoyed the rub and the barbecue sauce.  I used paprika instead of red pepper because of personal preference.  Made for PRMR.
I really love this potato salad! It's way different from what I usually make, but every bit as good or better, and has a nice chunky texture and great blend of flavors. Made for Beverage Tag.

I don't drink coffee so I gave this to my DH, who does.  He normally takes his coffee strong and black, but added cream and sugar to this version as suggested. The aroma of the lavender brewing is better than the flavor in the coffee, but sweetened and with a few drops of good vanilla, it's quite pleasant and leaves an herbal, slightly astringent-feeling aftertaste that lasts for quite a while.   Made for Comfort Cafe.

We did reduce the rosemary, and we served it over homemade egg noodles.  Both sweet and savory, it has a great aroma and nice gravy. Bring a fork, for the pork and carrots, and a soupspoon, for the slippery noodles and sauce!  Made for Comfort Cafe, July 2009.
Easy and pretty to make.  I thought this needed more berries so I added extra.  I used sugar instead of honey, personal preference.  Made for summer Comfort cafe.
I made this for 1.  It has a nice rich flavor. I only baked it for 10 minutes and my sauce was very thick.  Mde for the Summer Comfort Cafe.

This was a really elegant and fancy dinner for us.  We loved it.  I did add more garlic and salt and pepper to the sauce. I doubled the recipe for sauce because we love sauce.  We substituted green beans for the asparagus and snow peas.  Made for Summer Comfort Cafe.
I could not get the coffee to mix in.  It was still in little pcs after stirring for a long time.  It tastes okay with coffee crunches in it.  Made for summer comfort cafe.
Delicious, wonderful flavors.  I used a little more garlic than called for, love garlic.  Made for Potluck tag.
These are very good.  I made these and marinated a couple of days before we could get them cooked.  I did put them on skewers with onions and peppers. Made for PRMR.

Oh, but this is good!  This is one of those things that could be described as "comfort food with a gourmet touch," as it's pleasantly indulgent with treats like shrimp and pesto. We used firm, dark Crimini mushrooms and they fit in beautifully. Made with pleasure for PRMR.

We used this to marinade our steak for our campout. We mixed it up ahead of time so the steak marinated for 3 days before we cooked it over an open campfire and ate it outdoors. We used a cabernet for the wine. Made for AZ recipe swap.

We made this with chicken thighs for easier serving, flexibility to add cayenne only to one pan, and all dark meat. That reduced the cooking time by a third, but otherwise worked just fine.  Since we brined it longer than we planned, we were worried about it being too salty, but it wasn't; the beer flavor was fairly noticeable, however. Moist, savory, and delicious, we all enjoyed it.  Made for PRMR.

I have always wanted to make twice baked potatoes for the freezer and this is a good and relatively easy recipe.  I was given 2 bags of regular Idaho potatoes so I used them instead of buying thin-skinned potatoes.  Other than that I followed the recipe except made part of the potatoes w/o green onions because of DD dislike of onions.  I will definitely make these again.  Great OAMC food.  Made for PAC Fall 2009.

We may not have done this perfect justice, because life got busy and the meat stayed in the marinade two days!  However, the final result was wonderful saucy chunks of beef with vegetables and gravy. We served it over curly noodles with garlic green beens, and enjoyed every bite.  The pearl onions are a special treat!  Made for PRMR, Sept. 09.

We like quesadillas in general and we all declared this one "nummy."  (The two photos posted over my name are the work of DD16 and DH, respectively.) The recipe didn't say what to do with the bacon but we mixed it in with the chicken and it seemed to belong. Made for PAC, Fall 2009.
Tasty and delicious. My DH picked out this to make when we were picking recipes this month.  We all loved them.  Made for OZ swap OCT 2009.
These made a good snack while waiting  for our dinner to finish cooking.  I used crescent roll dough instead of biscuit dough.  The topping is very good.  Made for AZ swap 11/09

We used baby carrots, because that was on hand, and left them whole as in the package.  We also used reconstituted dried basil.  We agree with other reviewers that more garlic is a good thing, but these carrots were easy and delicious and may become a regular side.  Made for Aus/NZ swap, Nov. 2009.

An essential Thanksgiving ingredient for us.  We always make my mother's recipe for cornbread dressing.  This was a very fun and different type of cornbread.I had never used white corn, buttermilk, and actual corn in my cornbread. Also I loved making it in my cast iron skillet. It did not disappoint.
This is a much more dense and heavy  cornbread than we are used to.  Ours was a little underdone in the center so others should check carefully to make sure it is done.  Thank you for a fun experience, breezermom.  Made for Holiday PRMR.

These reminded me of the great baked potatoes at Red Lobster.  I always wondered how they did them. We did add the salt. We had these with steak and broccoli and my DD said what a great dinner!!!! Made for PARTY Dec 2009.

Beautiful, Easy and Delicious.  We made this for our Christmas Eve Dinner with some rustic garlic french bread.  We used half four cheese tortellini and half pesto tortellini.  We had to use dried basil the store was out of fresh.  Made for PRMR.
This made a wonderful breakfast combined with toast.  One of my favorite childhood breakfasts.  We made this for 4.  It was enjoyed by all. Made for the Comfort Cafe 01/10

This is awesome, and if you don't like it, I don't want to cook for you. We ended up marinating 24 hours, which didn't seem to hurt it; and those who can handle the heat applied Dragonfly Red Sweet Chili Sauce. Fantastic! Made for Please Review My Recipe.
Sweet, crisp bacon that you eat like a chip.  We laid it on spinach leaves for a photo, and discovered that the two together were a great compliment to one another. Thank you, Breezermom!

This is a great, easy meal that everyone with a family to feed needs to have in the mix.  I do suggest a real oven-baked potato for quality, but ours was cooked in a crock pot and they can also be nuked for convenience.  Taco stuffing in a potato is a pleasant surprise to those who haven't tried it and comfort food for those familiar with it. We have been doing something similar for years, calling it "Irish tacos."  Kids love them, and they can be done salad-bar style with varied toppings so picky eaters can build their own.  Made for Top Favorites of 2009.
Delicious, quick, and easy.  We loved this.  This marinade has all the right ingredients.  Made for Top Recipes of 2009 prize.
Delicious and wonderful.  I cut this in half making sandwiches for 2 meals for me. I used small salad shrimp.  I loved it.  Made for Top Favorites of 2009

Something different and unusual for us.  We substituted shells for elbows. We felt that the barbeque sauce seemeed to take over a little more than we liked. Next time we would use less.  Made For Top Favorites.
This is a very different taste for us.  Only thing it needed is a little salt and pepper. Made for a prize for Top Favorites of 2009.

With the bacon, garlic, and green pepper, this is very reminiscent of the stuffed bell peppers we've enjoyed for years. It's not your standard Italian spaghetti sauce!  We used fresh Crimini mushrooms, and our Provolone came sliced, but otherwise followed the recipe exactly and it came out terrific. We did bake it as instructed, but I think it would have been good if the sauce had been simply served over the spaghetti, too.  Made as a prize in Top Favorites of 2009.

We made ours with roasted garlic; while the potatoes were boiling, the garlic was wrapped in foil in the oven. Ours were even richer than the recipe because we were a bit short on potatoes; I think they could be described as, uh, decadent. Made for a prize for Top Favorites of 2009.

It took a couple of tries to get the temperature right in the skillet, and what worked best wasn't as hot as I expected. Once that was solved, we turned out delicious and perfectly golden cutlets one after another with ease. Made for Please Review My Recipe.

We made this with chopped chicken breast instead of ground turkey, and part of our bell peppers were green. The dish is beautiful and delicious, both fun and messy to eat. If you like a savory blended stir-fry with lots of sauce, you'll love this; if you're an elegant and fastidious eater you might want to shred the lettuce and serve it over a bed of rice. Made for Top Favorites of 2009.

An easy, quick snack when kids arrived hungry from school events looking for a late supper. Very good stuff -- the kids commented that it was flavorful without being harshly garlicky.  Made for Top Favorites of 2009.

This is delicious and -- ahem -- probably fattening. That said, my only question would be about draining off the fat, since gravy is all about the flavor from the drippings. This is usually a breakfast item but tonight was a ten o'clock supper as the younger generation arrived home from various points of the compass.   The biscuit was just for the photo; we mostly ate it with Recipe#389232, a marriage made in heaven.  Both made for Top Favorites of 2009.
Really simple and surprisingly good.  We made it with our own homemade salsa and scooped it with chips.  Made as a prize for Top Favorites of 2009 cookbook game.

Awesome! Just the color alone is fantastic; since it took more bell pepper than called for, we cut in a red one and that made it even more flamboyant.  We had to use the broiler as our grill isn't out for the season yet, but they came out perfect and delicious. We don't do seafood at home all that often but this was fun and not difficult and the flavor was amazing. Made for Top Favorites of 2009 Cookbook game.

We rubbed this on a whole chicken with a little olive oil drizzle and baked it for an hour and a quarter at 350. The result was a splendid golden-brown centerpiece that was as tasty as it was beautiful.   Made as a prize for Top Favorites of 2009.

French toast is one of my favorite breakfast foods and this is the best French toast recipe that I have tried. The flavor is exceptional all on its own without the usual extras that we  have on french toast.  Bk thank you for a great recipe.  This was made for a prize for Top Favorites of 2009.
My husband wolfed these down.  The beans and onions could have been served separately but the combination was terrific, and beautiful in the dish to boot.  Made for PAC.

Great sausage gravy!  Although I made a couple of biscuits to pose the picture, we served this with garlic mashed potatoes for a comfort-food supper.  Not for the weak of arteries!  ... but delicious and homestyle good. Made for PAC.

Classic chilimac with a twist of taco; good to eat and filling, would be better with more taco and less mac.  Leftovers will make an easily reheatable lunch for a couple of days.  Made for Pick A Chef.
Quick and Easy for dinner.  That is great for our family.  I substituted cottage cheese for ricotta, personal choice. Made for Spring PAC 2010.

These are really great, a little messy, sticky, salty, spicy, and just generally good.  We have a couple of other recipes for sticky wings and these will be added to the list.  We did cut the hot sauce and pepper flakes in half because one of us can't take the heat.  Made for Pick A Chef.

This was easy as advertised, though a bit messy in the breading process.  Please read the directions thoroughly before starting, as my first attempt was delicious but not photogenic because I didn't follow directions well.  We loved the finished product and it was gone in minutes.  Made for Zaar World Tour.
Great cucumber salad with a distinct oriental flavor.  Made for ZWT6 for the Voracious Vagabonds.
Simple, tasty, filling; we served it with Recipe#425238, using dried Spaetzle noodles from a German specialty store.  Made for Zaar World Tour 6, the Voracious Vagabonds.

Sweet, spicy, savory all at once! A matter of taste, but I suspect many people will be happier with less pepper in the glaze.  Made for Zaar World Tour 6, the Voracious Vagabonds.

Just sweet and delicious.  The conversation between the apricots and the mustard is one to enjoy.  Made for Zaar World Tour 6 on behalf of the Voracious Vagabonds -- but really just because it looked good!  and it was!

Don't know why people think this odd... it's hearty, filling, and easy to do. The fried egg on top is the missing piece that ties it together.  Made for Zaar World Tour 6 on behalf of the Voracious Vagabonds.
This is a great combination.  I cut this in half and used basil as my italian seasoning.  Made for ZWT6 for the Voracious Vagabonds

This made a wonderful Sunday night dinner for us.  My DH used chicken for our protein.  He made the recipe with the spicey ingredients in a separate pan to  be added to those who like the heat.  Made for PRMR.

Very easy to prepare.  We love potatoes in any form.  Made for Aus/NZ swap Oct. 2010.
Very easy to make and tastes delicious.  Greek yogurt is what we had on hand.  Made for Aus/NZ swap.

My DH made this for a quick and easy dinner tonight.  He made recipe#274204 to go with it.  Made for Aus/NZ swap.

This made a great lunch for my DD and I today.  I added extra mozzarella over the cottage cheese layer.  We both had seconds.  Made for PRMR.
This was a big hit with my DD for our lunch today.  I marinated it about 3 hours while I was gone.  We will be making this again.  Made for PRMR.

These made a wonderful and unusual lunch for my DD and I today.  I substituted ketchup for the tomato paste also.  I loved makiing the little buns.  Mine got really crisp so next time I will cook them for less time in the oven.   Made for PRMR.
This is a great cookie.  I used brown sugar in place of muscovado.  I also appreciate all the info from other reviewers.  It was really helpful.  Made for PRMR.

When I tagged this recipe I didn't read the amts of ingredients close enough.   I don't really care much for italian seasoning and this has a lot of it.  I honestly shouldn't have tagged it knowing my preferences.    This  is just a personal taste issue.   Made for PRMR.
These meatballs were loved by DD & DS who don't normally like meatballs.  I used teriyaki sauce and didn't add the chilis.   Made for PRMR.

Delicious Valentine's day breakfast!!!   We had to sub ham for the bacon but was so good.  We used green onions.  Made for 2010 favorites!!!
This is an easy and tasty soup to make.  I made mine with carrots, broccoli, cauliflower, onions, garlic, and zucchini.  Made for 2010 Favorites.

Very good, a great side for any Mediterranean feast, very festive and colorful -- and yet a little less than expected. For all that, very enjoyable and will be seen on our table again. Made for 2010 Favorites.

This made two dozen light-textured, sweet oatmeal cookies.  Better than most cookies this healthful, and healthier than most this good; but be honest when you count them!  It's really easy to eat three or four without a second thought. Would have put raisins in them but didn't have any on hand.

Completely enjoyed these, both making them and eating them. These went over great for bunko tonight.   I cut down the mustard to 1 T because we aren't big fans.  I didn't use the onions because of peoples preferences.   I have never added pickly relish before but it was a great addition.   Made for 2010 Favorites.

Just delicious!!!  This is the best pot sticker sauce I have ever had and now I have the recipe.  We had this with some delicious pot stickers my daughter made for her anniversary dinner.  Made for PAC Spring 2011

We used fresh thyme from the back yard and wished we'd used less. Also, I'd suggest adding salt only at the end, with the cornstarch thickener, for less shrinkage of the meat.  Overall, we enjoyed this very much except that it looked better going into the crockpot than coming out. Made for PAC.
This is a great way to increase veges in meals and to put some cinnamon in my diet.   The sauce ingredients really compliment the flavor of the carrots.   Made for spring PAC 2011.

I made this for a work potluck.  I work with lot of health conscious people who do like desserts.  I really think they are going to like this,  It is so easy and tastes delicious.  Made for PAC Spring 2011.

One of the best things to come out of my crock pot in months! Rich savory flavor, tender enough to shred with a fork.  We served it over rice with a few stir-fried veggies for color.  We like sesame a lot, so we used what the recipe called for and loved it.  Made for PAC.

This was made, sampled, photographed and reviewed by the selfless, sacrificing DH because the dummy who tagged it is diabetic and WW and can't touch stuff like this. These made a wonderful night time snack.   Ours are little round puffy cookies.  Only after making the majority of them did we discover that my DH left out the milk so the last batch has milk in it.   Made for PAC.

Barbecue is a figure of speech here; the cup of barbecue sauce (we used baby Ray's) is as close as it gets to a grill. Made for 2010 Favorites game.
This was enjoyed by all.  We used bread and butter pickles and juice because we were out of dills.   We only used onions on the side because of DD taste preferences.  Made for Az/NZ swap.

We all loved this tuna casserole. This morning we were fighting over who got to take the leftovers for lunch today. Loved these potatoes.  We have never found a potato recipe we didn't like .  Made for PRMR.
This was good and easy for a nighttime snack.   Made for PRMR.

Good and easy recipe to make from scratch. It is nice to know I can just whip this up. I hadn't tried spam since I was a kid.  Made for ZWT7.
Tasty, Enjoyable, and new take on swiss steak.  We all thought this was delicious.  made for ZWT7.
This made a great dinner that wasn't too hard to make for my son who is now on the dinner and dish rotation.  Both DD and DS love A-1 sauce so that made this recipe extra special.  Made for PRMR.

Delicious and Fun.  This was going to be a joint project for DD and me, but she couldn't wait.  She was too excited to make these. Added sticks to make them cookie pops. Great seasoniing mix. I used it on chicken breasts. I cooked them under the broiler 5 minutes per side.  They were delicious with this rub. Very good and fresh light tasting sauce.  More sauce than usual with Chicken Parmagiana.  Definitely need to make pasta with this recipe.  Made for I Recommend tag.

This made a wonderful lunch for my son and I. Great recipe and delicious ingredients.  Made for PAC Fall 2011.
Easy and quick for very hungry people.  Made for PAC Fall 2011

Decadent tasting and Delicious. My family loves enchiladas made with sour cream and the cream cheese was a wonderful addition.  The spiciness was just right.  Made for Fall PAC 2011.

My son was over the moon for this stuff over the weekend.  I also enjoyed sipping it though it was a bit sweet for me.  This would be a fabulous popsicle as well!  Yummy!  Thanks for the great recipe.  Made for ZWT5, Storybook Challenge.

These were so delicious!!  To be honest, only about half of them made it to the firm/set stage.. I devoured the other half  with wet or semi-wet chocolate.  Added a few peanuts also, sooooo good! I used Grey Poupon whole grain mustard instead of Guldens and did not have dill, but I think I still got the wonderful essence of the dip.  Great with Recipe #295738!

This sandwich was great!  I wasn't sure if I would like the cream cheese pineapple combo, but it was very good together, especially with the honey mustard.  Very refreshing, reminded me of summer!  Thanks for a great dinner!
