Thanks for posting, made for ZWT4.

Delicious! Couldn't really taste the coffee in it, so maybe I'll try a strong 1 1/3 cup of regular coffee or even some espresso crystals next time. A nice breakfast or brunch treat. Thank you for posting!
These were good. I'm always looking for breakfast recipes that break up the monotony of the old stand-bys. The Caribbean touch to these is definitely nice! Thank you for posting, swissms.
Simple good memories with this. Thanks for sharing!

I really like raspberry and chocolate together, but somehow this didn't work. I'm not exactly sure why. The raspberry filling was somewhat tart, and the chocolate ganache was too semi-sweet. 3 out of 5 family members didn't care for it, which is very rare for any type of cake in my household.  I will say though, on the second day, it was more popular.
In the ingredient list, pecans are noted, but the instructions don't say where to use them. Obviously, from the ingredient grouping, they should go with the raspberry cream. But, since the instructions never mentioned, I completely forgot to use them. Also, instructions mention vanilla in the raspberry cream, and it is not in the ingredient list.

Great cake. I'm usually very wary about trying a new carrot cake, because we have a family favorite recipe, and I hadn't found another recipe to compare..until this one! I liked that there are just tons of carrots. When you slice in to the cake, it is pretty obvious it is a carrot cake. My family devoured this cake in embarrassingly quick time. I did not put the pecans on the top, because I felt that the cake already had plenty of pecans and more might be over-doing it. There is an instructional error in steps 5 and 11. Both of those steps say to add vanilla, but there is no vanilla in this recipe...it should read brandy extract.

I liked the taste. I think they needed more milk. They were very thick for pancakes, and didn't spread on the griddle. WHen I flipped then, I had to squish them down. And of course, that made them not so light and fluffy! I added some milk to the remaining batter, and the second batch cooked much more like what I am used to for a pancake.

It was hard to find a main dish recipe in RSC#11 that wasn't loaded with fat or sugar, so I was happy to see this recipe entered. Unfortuntely, I didn't like these at all. Nor did DH or my youngest daughter who eats most everything.  For me, I found the shallots were overpowering because they were essentially uncooked.

Great recipe. I used 1 1/2 times the pecan mixture for 6 cutlets and barely had enough. But, had more than enough raspberry sauce. I used only a drizzle of raspberry sauce so as to not drown the cutlets in sweetness, and that was perfect.

I love a good biscotti, and this one has the potential to be outstanding. I'm having one of these right now with my morning coffee, and they taste just a tad too sweet for my taste first thing in the morning, so I may reduce the sugar a little next time. I also found that the baking time was too little....at least for my oven. A few technical notes: The directions don't mention where to add the almond extract, so I almost forgot. Also, just about every biscotti recipe I've tried before, suggests turning the biscotti on their sides for the second bake. I did that for this recipe as well. I actually baked the original 20 minutes (which could have used another 5), then 10 minutes on each side of the cut biscotti.

I liked these.  They remind me quite of bit of Matrimonials.  When they first came out of the oven, the honey aroma was prominent and I was a little worried that the honey would overpower the bars. But as they cooled, the flavors blended nicely.

*Made for PAC Spring 2008*  This was our first experience with bread soup -- made a SUPER soup supper !  I followed the recipe as closely as possible, we ultimately ended with soup the consistency of applesauce. The bread I used was a few slices of left-over beer bread (maybe more dense than I should have?), plus a slice of ciabatta bread - all dried a tad in the toaster oven.  I added NO S&P seasoning, and could not believe that the 15 flakes of red pepper added so much flavor !  The sausage I added was cryopacked skinless Polish Kielbasa - turkey/pork. I also added about 1/2 can of water to the canned broths.  The taste was wonderful !  Spicy without being obnoxious, and extremely full flavored -- and MOST filling.  I am glad to have had this experience, - would have to VERY carefully chose guests for whom to prepare this- wish I had known when we had the "Gourmet Group" ! This is what is great about Zaar -- exposes us to taste sensations we may have never otherwise tried.  Thanks, Maito, I hope we did were able to successfully demonstrate your your lovely recipe.

*PAC Spring2008*  DH and I had this for lunch -- made 1/2 recipe.  I used vegetable broth, white wine, and 1 Tbsp. brandy - and we had a small glass of white wine, just to celebrate Thursday.  I used the European chopper on the marinated artichoke hearts, and the submersion blender after it simmered.  It was a nice rich flavor, but we decided that the spoonsful with sour cream added a tad of taste.  Will likely add a few Tbsp. of cream to the pot next time.  Thanks for posting, Maito

We have been preparing tilapia (our fave fish) with this method for years.  I did not know Progresso made panko, as we have always used it in a bag.  It makes a lovely, light breading and is a versatile coating for many sauteed dishes.  Thanks for adding to my knowledge bank, RecipeJunkie !!

The garden zucchini are still producing, and this was a major surprise for dinner !  I used an entire egg instead of whites, and roasted just about 12 minutes total.  DH was so delighted finding another use of panko !  Will be serving as long as the zukes hold out -- then will try eggplant!  Thanks, JimnLyss, for posting.

thanks for posting, iewe

Needed to get dinner on quickly, so added some nice, crisp celery stalks and onion quarters, to the potatoes and carrots, and put the skin-on/bone-in thighs on top.  Could have baked a tad longer but was "done" in stated time.  A VERY tasty and easy combo !  Thanks, QB

4/08 Had some fingerling potatoes, baby carrots, and GIGANTIC bone/skinless breasts - "sort of" cut back for 2 servings, but cut chicken breasts in half.  Nice flavor -- easy prep. I also used dijon mustard and added some honey.  Thanks, QueenBee, for posting.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #39*
A lovely dish -- and so pretty !  Sorry DH did not get to take a photo !  Prepared 1/2 recipe exactly according to directions.  I, too, used skin-on/bone-in thighs -- such superior flavor !  I'm not sure of the "10 min prep" time -- but any effort was worth it.  I truly love to have the meat falling off the bones, but these were very large thighs -- done, but not to that extent. The flavor was delicate but definite !  Thanks, floWer, for posting such an elegant chicken dish.  This will be done for company.

On a whim, bought a pound of bacon (off the slab) from a local "sausage" maker (who supplies the Polish Embassy in D.C.!)  Searched for something equal to the task-- and prepared 3 sandwiches for DH and me tonight !  (Was TOO much !) -- Very tasty, had gotten hi-qual cheddar, and finished in the George F.  A really nice combo.  Thanks, Ashbow.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #40*
"twas a hot and sticky afternoon after a few cool days, and Oh, Dear -- WHAT to have for dinner ! Made according to recipe, and grilled on good old George F. -- served with roasted red pepper soup and left over potato salad. So much BK's high standards !!  Thanks for posting !

*Made a s a "nap" for Australia/NZ Swap #40*
Only made the cake, as there is just 2 of us and combining the glaze and strawberries would not have held up for the 3-4 days it will take us to eat it !  A lovely light sponge, baked in my smaller bundt pan and served with vanilla Ice cream or whipped cream, with a friend's GORGEOUS strawberries !  Will be lovely for a few days !  Thanks, Gerry -- will be prepared for any fruit topping !

Prepared 1/2 recipe last night -- with all ingredients except salsa (had none) -- and used dried cilantro for fresh.  Very yummy !  Went well with saffron rice and sauteed scallops.  This will be a great side for many dishes.  Probably good cold, as well.  Thanks for posting, SarasotaCook.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #41*
This was tasty, but not quite up to expectations.  The usually moist and tender frozen sl/bl chicken breasts, were not very moist.  The spices were very good, different from the standard -- and it was just wet instead of saucy.  I will make again and "tweak" a tad.  Thanks for posting, Paula.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #42*
An enthusiastic 5* for French Tart's "Cheddar Gorgeous! Cheese and Onion Bread and Butter Pudding" 301346 ! Prepared 1/2 recipe for DH and me for lunch, with garden tomato slices. Have lots of red, ripe, juicy tomatoes from the garden !  Used 10 Romas, seeded and chopped, and HUGE stuffed Manzanilla green olives with Kalamatas.  Thought the 2 tsp. of brine not "wet" enough, so added 2 tsp. light olive oil.  Was a very tasty salad with sauteed, breaded tilapia - almost a salsa.  DO NOT add salt !  A little fresh ground pepper is good.  Thanks for posting, AuntWoofie.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #44*  Only substitution was for small shell pasta -- didn't add garlic, which would be good.  Made a nice change from tomato sauce or the usual alternative-- oil and butter.  Tripled the recipe, and have a side for later this week.  Thanks Loula -- enjoyed it.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap # 45*  This was a quick, easy and tasty veggie side.  The garden squash were all gone, but they looked fresh at the super.  Served with salmon fillets and yellow rice, made a healthy and colorful dinner.  Thanks for posting, morgangeiser.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #45*   This was surely easy to put together -- however required significantly more than 5 slices of French bread.  I also added some of the liquid from the mandarin oranges to the egg mixture.  I melted Cross and Blackwell's orange marmalade, and spooned it over each serving.  Made a tasty breakfast treat for DH amd me on a day with no morning schedules !!  Will do this again when the DGK are here.  Thanks for posting, Julie.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #47*  Serving the last of turkey soup, was a perfect side !  Did the breadstick version, and coated with the herb mix and a tad of crushed garlic.  Very tasty -- and a sure keeper.  Thanks for posting, Crafty Lady.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #47*  This was a truly tasty dinner and DH and I enjoyed it -- only drawback was the need for 2 saute pans plus a saucepan to boil the gnocchi !  Was one of those "trash the kitchen" preps, which I will do for DDs and families, but not just for us.  Great combo of flavors.  Thanks for posting.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap  #49* --AHHHH -- what fun !!  A new culinary experience for me !  We have had a spaetzle maker in a drawer for years -- don't recall EVER using it !  Since we were having a rotisserie chicken tonight, thought I could use my prep time for this.  Batter/dough made up quickly and easily, made jut according to the recipe.  Added some melted butter and pepper when serving, but needed some additional salt.  Makes a LOT !!  We ate a significant amount and have a bowl of noodles to use as a pasta later.  Thanks, awalde, for sharing for a fun dinner !!

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap # 49*  Followed directions and used brown sugar and balsamic vinegar.  A REALLY tasty accompaniment to our pork tenderloin -- just the right zip !  Thanks for posting, mumma !

Prepared 1 tube of biscuits to serve with chicken noodle soup.  Had been interested in a "monkey bread" for some time.  Tasted really good -- baked in loaf pan -- but needed 10 minutes additional baking time.  Will do again soon !  Thanks for posting.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #50*  OH -- YUMMM!  have recently discovered the unique flavor of Meyer lemons -- here in the mid-Atlantic, with a dozen lemons found at Costco.  Ordered a 5# box from Cal. to prepare this (and a few other) recipes. Made JUST according to the posted recipe, and served tonight on a mixed green salad. TRULY tasty -- now will make a double batch to keep for this week !  Only change was 1 tsp Half&Half for the mayo.  Thanks so much, Cookgirl-- lemons will be costing me so much more-- but also more enjoyable !!

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #52*  VERY yummy, Boomette ! I had a carton of Greek Lemon Yogurt, which I thought would be tasty, and added cinnamon chips to the batter , instead of the topping.  The batter was VERY stiff, and I was concerned it wouldn't rise.  I baked 25 minutes at 350* and had 12 beautiful, light muffins !  DH said be sure to keep this recipe.  Thanks for posting.

*Made for Australia/NZ swap #54*  SOO fast and easy !  Had steaks and zukes on the grill, so MY part of dinner was done in 10 minutes -- DH didn't take much longer out on the patio !  This would make a tasty side to ANY meal !  Thanks for posting !

Put everything together as listed, then GRILLED in a hole-y basket on the grill, while a pork tenderloin cooked !  The zucchini are producing at full blast, so made that the largest proportion of the veggies.  Everything carmelized nicely, and DH and I ate the ENTIRE thing -- which I was planning to have leftovers.  Didn't miss the cheese at all.  Thanks for posting a nice combo of spices as well -- most I had fresh grown.

YUMM !  Having a banner crop of zukes and tomatoes -- even a few onions from the garden.   Zukes are larger than "small', so used 2, quartered length-wise and sliced, and 2 seeded slicer tomatoes and 3 romas.  Placed on grill rack for 15 mins., then on shelf while salmon fillets cooked for about 5 min.  The olives really impart a tasty addition -- will be doing this many times this summer.  Thanks for posting, Lynn.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #55*  I should have realized from the ingredients that this would be very mild.  I prepared this according to directions with the exception of subbing artisan Taco cheese blend for cheddar.  Not too flavorful the first night, but made a large quantity for 2.  Tonight. I took 1/2 of the leftovers and added 3 Tbsp. melted butter with 2 tsp. crushed garlic and 1/2 T. seasoned salt, and covered with shredded extra sharp cheddar, and warmed in a 350* oven for 20 minutes.  MUCH more flavor !  Will add same to the last for another night.  Thanks for posting, Mersaydees.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap # 57*.  Went together so fast, it beat my roasted veggies out of the oven !   I thought just a tad salty (and I am a salt freak), but DH thought it was just right.  It was amazing how quickly all that soupy sauce came together in a creamy way.  The DGKs will enjoy this the next time in.  Thanks for posting, LIG !

Just perfect !  We eat tilapia frequently, and DH usually uses a panko breading and flavored peppers.  The few fish I truly enjoy, I love best with just some butter and oil, salt, pepper, lemon juice and maybe chives.  This was so good, I ate the entire loin - unusual for me !  I will be using this a lot from now on !  Thanks for posting -- thanks, Paula, for your attention-attracting review !

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #58*  twas a chilly, damp night -- just right for a warm pot of stew and biscuits !  I followed the recipe except for adding additional potato and broth.  It took a little longer than I expected for the potatoes to soften, but the aroma made up for it !  All the flavors melded nicely, and I DID have enough for another meal.  Thanks for posting, morgaingeiser.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #59*  SEE-LISH !! I usually roast pork tenderloin, but this stovetom method is very quick and moist !  I dipped the slices in milk before dredging the slices in the crumb mixture, hoping to keep more of the crust on the pork.  I also used a fairly good sized onion, 'cause we like it that way.  DH was fixing carmelized apples while I tended my pot, and all ended up together !  Thanks for a lovely meal, Lynn !!

This was really good !  Had bone-in thighs which got well done in 90 minutes.  Used crushed garlic and sea salt, and just 1 russet for the 2 of us.  There was plenty of liquid for the full baking time, and saved some for leftovers another night.  Thanks for posting, Marie !

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap # 59*  Sweet potatoes cooked in record time and onions caramelized when ready to serve.  This is a new delicious method for us, since we mostly bake.  A great Winter-time dish.  Thanks for posting, Pat.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #60*  A new experience for us, who are broccoli lovers -- usually steamed with lemon !  This made an excellent, crispy side to a saucy chicken and rice dish.  We will be repeating this frequently !  Thanks for posting, Crafty Lady !

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #60*  This was REALLY good !  I always use Israeli couscous -- pearl type - and chicken broth.  Served with Barramundi fish fillets (yum -- had fresh when we visited Australia) - and you never notice  a chicken taste.  Went together in quick time, and looked very appealing with the red pepper.  Thanks for posting, Boomette.

Made as listed.  Had to interrupt cooking after 4 hours -- got invited out !!  Resumed crockpot coking next day, and noticed for "stew", all juices thin and watery.  Added 1/4 cup cornstarch dissolved in juices and let it cook on high for another hour.  Very tasty, but did need salt at the table.  Thanks for sharing.

*Made for Australia/NZ swap #62*  We love roasted veggies, and we love lemon !  I had baby carrots on hand, and used those -- only additionally sprinkling with salt, pepper, and dried rosemary -- what I had.  Roasted at 350* for 45 min. the 400* for 30 min.  Nice to squeeze the garlic cloves, but the onions burned some -- think I would add more oil next time.  Very flavorful side with sauteed tilapia loins.   Thanks for posting,  katew.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #63*  I made this according to directions, using thin chicken tenders and Greek yogurt -- which is usually creamier than regular.  It was done in about 10 minutes, but the coating entirely slipped off when I turned them over.  Mild taste, but I did salt and pepper lightly.  I do bake chicken frequently and will try this coating next time in the oven.  Thanks for posting, Kathy.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #64* This was really good ! I used shredded Bistro Mexican cheese and fresh rosemary, baked for 1 hour at 350* earlier (in danger of loosing power) - and left in warming drawer for almost 1 hour. They were really creamy and perfectly seasoned. Will definitely be a repeater ! Thanks for posting, Noo !
I learned a trick from an earlier sliced potato recipe -- left the slices in a bowl with 1 bottle of beer (any kind) - for 1/2 hour or more. Have no idea of the chemical reaction -- but any time I have done this, the potatoes are always creamy and tasty. My slices were very thin -- from large-slice side of box grater, so no question of them being done in 1 hour.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #65*  YUMMM-- comfort food and happy memories all rolled into one !  Was my absolute favorite lunch when I could walk home in elementary school !  Mom put fresh horseradish on, but the onion was new.  I only made one each, for DH and me, -- good thing -- I could have eaten another whole one !  So good !  Thanks for posting, Crafty Lady !!

Had saved this as alternative for Swap #62, and was very glad I did !!  Just did 2 skinless/boneless breasts for DH and me, and wish I had done more so that there would be another meal !!  Easy to put together, so will make this again soon.  Thanks, Chef Buggsy Mate !!

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #67*  Made half the recipe with tilapia fillets.  Lovey lemony flavor with just the right touch of capers.  We eat fish frequently, so this will be served as most often prepared.  Thanks for posting, Kathy.

*Made for Australia/NZ swap #68*  Just LOVE steamed veggies !  used all recipe ingredients, (except cilantro gel), but was dealing with broiling fragile crab cakes, so steamed for 15 minutes and skipped the saute this time.  Loaded everything in the steamer, so there wasn't much crunch (this time).  lovely fresh taste and best of all, enough for another meal !  Thanks for posting, my original A/NZ swap partner !

THOUGHT I was making this for A?NZ swap #72 !! OLD brain ! It was STILL wonderful, the only sub I made was for 1/2 28oz. can of crushed tomatoes for the diced tomatoes ! Had a lovely afternoon putting it all together !!

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #60* VERY yummy and perfect for a day which started at 12 degrees. Only left out the chile, and had no fresh basil, so used dry. Got a late start this time, but will will be ready earlier next time -- likely next week ! Thanks for sharing, BK !

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #73*  YUMMY !!!  I almost always squeeze some fresh lemon on veggies, but had never done on potatoes -- how delicious !!  I THOUGHT I had prepared enough for 2 meals, but DH and I just kept working on the bowl til they were GONE !!  No chervil -- subbed chives.  Thanks for posting, Tisme.  Will be a staple from now on !

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #75*  Wonderful and easy side !  I rarely peel potatoes,  and just cut then into chunks.  The lemon zest on top, with a squeeze of juice before mixing, gave a nice pop.  Will be saving this one for company !  Thanks for posting, Julie.
Made 1/2 recipe with 1 can of rolls.  Super easy and VERY tasty !  DH says this is a keeper -- great for breakfast !  Would not change a thing !  Thanks for posting !

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #76*  Prepared 1/2 recipe (still TONS !) - using Amish egg noodles, bacon, and ementhal.  I think pancetta would be more flavorful.  Was nice and cheesy, but a tad dry.  Will "soup" up the left-overs for another night.  Nice different way for "mac&cheese".  Thanks for posting Lynn.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #77*   A SURE inner !  We eat fish frequently, most often tilapia loins (Costco) -- and adding very little since we enjoy the flavor of the fish.   A little butter, lemon, dill -- and we are happy.  AMAZING how much the capers added -- had not given them a thought !  pan fried, served with steamed Jasmine rice, and fresh broccoli from the garden.  Thanks for posting, Jan.

*Made for Australia/NZ Swap #77*  This was SUPER yummy !!  Prepared with 1 pound of shrimp and 1/2 sauce ingredients.  DH and I almost polished it off -- just a tad left for somebody's lunch.  Very different without any tomato, but the paprika fools the eye with color.  I had leftover soft jasmine rice, which soaked up the sauce nicely.  Wish I had made the whole recipe !  Thanks for posting, Lynn !

*Made for Australia/NZ swap #79*  GOOD stuff, Connie !!  We have been having VERY un-August weather, so while it was cool, I made some soup !  DH groaned with the first bite --"UMM--this is GOOD "!  Made according to recipe, with lots of garden rosemary -- and used my stick blender rather than food processor.  Lovely, creamy. tasty soup !  Thanks for posting !
It was great.  I realized that I forgot the garlic so after the marinade was on the fish, I sprinkled with garlic powder.  I baked it until the top browned at 350.  Thanks!

These were great!  I had to use corn oil, dried parsley, bottled minced garlic, only 10 oz. container of fresh mushrooms, and I used an ordinary skillet  and they were still good.  I would imagine they would be even better with fresh crushed garlic.  My DH commented on how good he thought the mushrooms were before I even got to ask!  I will make these again!

This was good on the BBQ- I marinated it this morning but had to use a regular onion and dried cilantro.  I also used regular (not fat free) Italian dressing.  I would imagine fresh cilantro making this really great but it was very good even without it.  I my up the hot sauce next time.  Thank you!
I was looking for an easy recipe for Thanksgiving and this fit the bill. Very good!  Thanks

yum, yum! Both of my children loved this recipe! It has some of our favorite foods! Mushroom and Parmesan Fresh Tortellini with sundried tomatoes and even fresh basil....we gobbled it up and I will definitely make it again. Next time I will make sure to have a block of fresh Parmesan to grate over the top. I did add more spice and thinned the broth just a little. Thanks!
Easy, delicious and popular with everyone in my house! An all ages side dish. I think next time I will serve these with omelets. They were so good! Thank you for this recipe!
Delicious and so easy!! I added some chili peppers to my marinade and used a London Broil that I had purchased at the market on sale. It was great! Thank you!

Yum, yum. Made this for ZWT 4 for my daughter and her 4 friends. They almost ate them all up before I could get a picture but luckily I salvaged one right out of my daughters hand! Thank you for the yummy recipe!
This is such a wonderful recipe. Easy yet full of flavor. It's awesome and I made it exactly to the recipe! I needs nothing added.

Oh, this was delightful. I would recommend adding in the directions how to melt the chocolate for beginners and I would also remind slow people like myself to let the espresso cool before pouring it over the ice cream (yes, I KNEW better...)
It was JUST what I was in the mood for, decadent but easy. Thanks for this wonderful recipe. (I will now whip the melted one up in the blender for a snack tomorrow, ha, ha)

Oh, this is a good one! Would be great as a special drink for a romantic evening or even a romantic morning! It's fruit, yet a bit of tartness and of course bubbles always make a drink special!
I could not find my sieve or any cheesecloths so I couldn't strain the strawberry mix but I like the layered look anyway. Thanks Boomette for a delicious and refreshing drink!

This was delicious! I grilled the fish on a bed of rosemary sprigs and also add some fresh thyme springs which gave the fish a wonderful flavor! I also sprinkled the top with dried thyme and rosemary in addition to the oregano. It was wonderful! ZWT4 recipe.

This was delicious and super easy to make. I love the refreshing citrus blend! A perfect summer treat! I couldn't really taste the basil flavor but what the heck? It was delicious anyway. Make for ZWT4.

This was great but I ended up adding half and half as the gin AND vodka made it a bit strong for an AFTER dinner drink. I used dark Creme de Cacao, hence the caramel color. It's always great to try something new!
Thank you. ZWT4

A decadent drink that is delightfully sweet. A perfect replacement for dessert after dinner! I loved the combination of flavors! And I REFUSE to think of how many calories....no, no. Thank you so much for this yummy recipe! ZWT4

I LOVE this salad! Sweet, nutty, fruity, delightful! Of course I can never completely follow the directions and sort of made a mix with the mango, peppers, etc. But it  is just divine! The only change I made to the ingredients was to add a few bits of jalapeno pepper (we like spicy at our house.)

Delightful! Thank you for this yummy cocktail recipe my dear friend! It's sooo good I think I'll go have another! I did, and I made it with rum this time! That was delicious too! It's not too sweet and that is what makes it so refreshing!zwt4

Honestly, this was an extremely tasty ice cream but it was a bit rich and I too felt that less heavy cream would have helped on that end. We love the goodies in ice cream so I'd suggest added a few more cherries as well. It WAS decadent though I can't deny. ZWT4
Boomette I hope you don't mind that I replaced the vodka in this drink with Rum...It's just like the title...an Island Girl Drink! I LOVE IT!!! Thank you!
Simple and yummy! Another great way to drink Cranberry juice....ha, ha, ha...I mean RUM! made for zwt4 in Canada.
My entire family loved this recipe. I was happy that there was plenty of sauce to go around as well! Delicious! I made this exactly to the recipe. Canada in ZWT4.

What a delightful way and super flavorful way to prepare a reasonably priced steak! Not one bite was left! Even my 10 year devoured this! Made for ZWT4 while visiting Central/South America

We love salmon any way it comes but this was a delightful and super easy way to prepare it! I add a squeeze of lemon and some cracked red pepper and grilled it on a charcoal fire. I would have liked a spicy cream sauce for it but it was lovely just as it was!
ZWT4 Canada.

This was another GREAT black bean salad! I used fresh corn and added fresh cilantro and some hot green chili's. Followed NcMysteryShopper's cue and splashed some Lizano on as well! Just delightful! Thanks! ZWT4.

This was absolutely one of the best burgers I've ever had!! Just wonderful! Used all the ingredients listed and used oaxaca cheese. Added some avocado slices! I grilled the burgers and they were moist and extremely flavorful! Thank you for posting this recipe! ZWT4 for the Babes!

I was pleasantly surprised at the delightful fragrance of this rice. The combination of lemon and garlic were perfect! It was the perfect accompaniment to our spicy South American dinner tonight! ZWT4 Babes.

Yep, I agree with everyone else! this was a TRUE winner. Thank you so much! I added some cinnamon, cardamom and nutmeg to the mix and we absolutely LOVED it. I also used coconut rum. ZWT4 with the Babes in Africa.

I am working late tonight so I made a pot of coffee and decided to use it for ZWT4 recipes. (I've had two others already that were very sweet so I am leaving the sugar out and only adding 2% milk to make it a little lighter). I used hazelnut coffee which goes well with the creme de cocoa! Thank you for this great recipe.

I'm so glad I chose this recipe. It seems that it might possible be a LITTLE less calories than some of the others. I have to admit that I left the mozzarella cheese out because solely because I had so much fat in the rest of my meal (Mediterranean Pork Chops) that it would have been overkill. I know it would have been awesome with it though. ZWT4

I LOVE okra and tomatoes and I thrilled to see this recipe. My grandmother used to make this all the time and I'd forgotten about it! Thank you from the bottom of my heart for posting this recipe! Made while travelling through Africa with the Babes. ZWT4

YUM! I made this because of my teammate in  ZWT4 Boomette's review for favorite tour recipes! She's right! It's absolutely wonderful and I am enjoying it immensely right this very moment! Sorry I didn't take a picture because it just isn't pretty without the whipping cream and I left that part off in an attempt to save calories.

So glad I finally tried this recipe! I've had my eye on it for a while. 
Honestly, I was going to make Veal Scallopini tonight but I didn't have any plain breadcrumbs and only had rye bread. I used the rye bread for this and the caraway seeds added a unique and great flavor. Sorry to steer away from such a traditional recipe but I wanted to use the veal and I'm glad I made this!! It was easy and delicious. I served this with another recipe I'd had my eye on back when we were touring thru Germany in ZWT4 - "Recipe #179708"

This was very similar to a dish that I make regularly but use cheese tortellini. The sauce I chose to use was a Spicy Tomato and Basil and honestly, this was just wonderful not to mention quick and super easy! Thanks for sharing this recipe! ZWT4 Zingo

This was perfect for my smoked oysters! (I saw Wildflour's review and picture and I just HAD to have some!)
Loved the spiciness and the lime was the perfect addition. Super quick and simple and I agree with others, WAY better than the store bought stuff in the bottle. ZWT4
Great recipe! Quick, easy and perfectly seasoned. Thank you so much! Love that sesame oil flavor and the bits of ginger! ZWT4 Family picks while travelling with the Babes.

This is a WONDERFUL recipe! Love guacamole and this is the perfect amount of each ingredient! I served this onto a piece of seared tuna and it was delicious! Thank you so much. Made for ZWT4 while travelling around with my Babes.

This was a perfect lunch for me today. I cooked the tuna last night for dinner and had it with an avocado salsa. Today the tuna was ready for the salad (the last of the sweet lettuce from the garden) so I just threw the rest of it together and thoroughly enjoyed the flavors! LOVE  wasabi coated Tuna and if you ever get a chance make some wasabi mashed potatoes to go with it. They are absolutely the BEST combination!! (Emmy you will love them!) Just got batteries for my camera this afternoon so I am sorry I couldn't take a picture of this :(,  it was beautiful! But I will definitely make it again and I promise I'll snap a shot for you when I do... Made for one of our Babes in Zaarland, Emmy herself! during ZWT4 Family Picks.

Yum!, we love authentic flavors at my house and this recipe has a very spicy and authentic blended flavor.
My daughter works in a health food store and proudly brought home a bag of beautiful red lentils and I had just picked some apples a few days back  so this was THE recipe that called out to me and I'm super glad! Made during ZWT4.

This was great but I did add double the fruit as I thought the guests at the party would like it a little sweeter. But what a GREAT summer drink! I ended up making 5 more batches of this before the evening was up because it was soooo popular at my friend's birthday party!!! Thanks V!!!

These were absolutely delicious! I prepared them exactly as directed except I grilled them on the barbecue over a very low heat. The orange was not too overpowering and it went perfectly with the fresh rosemary! Perfect!

These were so delicious! My son's comment was "these are really great wings mom and you should definitely make these again!"
Don't worry....I WILL!! Not only were they very tasty but they were so easy to make! I will add a little chili sauce next time as we love spicy food! Thanks France for a wonderful recipe!
I loved this tropical and delightful summer drink! It was nice and strong (which was just what I needed tonight)! Thank you dear Boomette for the perfect drink!

This was a perfect drink for me because it was not too sweet...I'm loving the refreshing flavor of the Absolute Pear Vodka! Thanks for another great beverage recipe Boomette! I did drink this without ice by the way....
Fairly easy, super healthy and yummy recipe! I did go with regular macaroni because it's what I had on hand, but whole wheat pasta would make it that much healthier.

Oh, yummy! I followed the recipe exactly as written except with regular part-skim mozzarella, and it really is so very good and also so very diet friendly. Next time I might splurge just a bit by using regular or just reduced fat ricotta instead of fat free because I think it would lend a little more flavor when there is some room for a few extra calories. Fresh ground pepper on top also adds a nice touch. Thank you for sharing such a yummy winner!

What a really great recipe this is! I went with regular cheese (sharp cheddar and used a little less to keep the flavor but save on calories) and a little less salsa but otherwise followed this as written, and I loved the flavor so much! It was very much like Mexican food but without the usual guilt. It was also very quick and simple, as well as being quite healthful, especially paired with some brown rice. Now, here are my beefs. The recipe itself could be slightly more detailed. There are a few things (salt, carrots, vegetable oil) that aren't mentioned in the ingredients but are in the instructions. There's no mention of adding the broccoli to the skillet (I added it with the red pepper and carrots - I used 2 carrots) and cooked them for a while before adding the ginger, green onions, onions and red pepper [which is also not mentioned] - I didn't want those more delicate items to burn). My other complaints are due to my (our) personal tastes. I could have used more ginger! I couldn't really taste it in here, but I think it comes out a little bit the second time around (if you have leftovers). Also, I could use a LOT more spice. LOTS MORE. It was a little bland, especially because I wasn't sure how much salt I should add. Finally, the sauce could have been thicker (though I'm pretty sure this was my fault/preference because it did thicken up a good bit, just not as much as I would've liked). Whew, that was a lot. This is a really solid base of a recipe. The broccoli absorbs the sauce well and it is delicious, but it could be a bit bolder. Thanks so much Debbwl!

Perfect!

This was good but a little too salty. I used Tamari to reduce the salt even and lightly sprinkled the fish with sea salt. I followed the time as listed and felt the fish was a little dry. Will make again reducing salt and cooking time. Thanks for sharing this recipe!
Great way to make kale!

This was so yummy! I reduced the sweetener to 1/2 c agave syrup. It was plenty sweet enough and added a smoothness to the recipe. I will be using this one again! Maybe adding some mango or papaya along with the pineapple. Thanks Lynn!
The mushrooms came out a little anemic with the microwave process. They did have a good flavor. The texture and lack of color was a little off-putting though.

This was such a pleasant surprise!
I mixed it all up in the crock pot insert the evening before and just popped it into the base this morning. Great blend of flavors and something a little different for a change. I will make this again. Thanks for sharing :)

Wonderful bread diner524! I got 3 nice sized loaves. The dough rose beautifully in about 1 hr 15 minutes and was very easy to work with. I only had to bake it about 25 minutes until it was quite browned and sounded hollow when tapped. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT4
Very good! I really liked this simple spin on plain canned corn and will make it again :) Made for ZWT4
We enjoyed this rub on chicken as well. I was a little leary of the sugar but it omplimented the spices nicely and was not too sweet. Thank You for sharing. Made for ZWT4

An almond lover's dream! Creamy gelato packed with fresh berries and crunchy cookies in every bite. I mixed in the cookies and berries to the finished gelato by hand as mine initially froze into a very soft set. I too found that microwaving my almond paste made it easier to mix with the sugar. This was my first time making gelato/ ice cream with half and half vs all heavy cream and was pleased with the texture and creaminess. Well done Cafe' ZMAKK Gypsies! Made for ZWT4.

Delicious!  It tastes like you put a ton of effort this dish, when in fact it is a snap to prep!  I almost always have the ingredients on hand for this and will be making it again. I used fresh dill, basil, and oregano from my herb garden. I thought the Dill/Ricotta mixture was brilliant! 
The only tiny change I might make is to add a little galic and/or garlic salt. I would also like to try the addition of crab meat which another reviewer mentioned. Thanks so much for sharing this recipe. P.S-. DH also gave you 2 thumbs up ! Made for Zingo ZWT4

Well I may not be a "man" but I sure did love your quiche! Packed full of flavor in every bite, I especially loved the broccoli slaw. I cooked my chicken and then refrigerated it while I prepped the rest. Before adding the chicken back to the mixture, I cut it up even smaller as this was easier after cooking and chilling. This is the first time I have tried Laughing Cow cheese and it delicious. I do have to admit I found the recipe to be a bit labor intensive due to the prep, but well worth it. Well done chef, you should be proud.

Wow! I have to thank reviewer RbdCbn for mentioning this recipe. Creamy and Dreamy! Use a good vanilla as the flavor really shines through. My only suggestion? I would double the recipe next time :) Thanks for sharing. *Made for Spring PAC 2009*

Oh my goodness this bread is so crusty and chewy! I know DS and I will fight for the end pieces. I am truly in bread heaven.
I too used only 3 portions of cheese and jalapenos and thought that was plenty. I have a feeling we will be having this often. It is far better than the bakery bread I have been buying at an outrageous price. Thanks so much for sharing, this is a real keeper! *Made for Spring PAC 2009*

I am so pleased with this recipe! I actually had a bunch of leftover cooked rice so I measured out 3 cups, added the diced tomatoes with chilies and microwaved until hot. Then I proceeded with your directions. I love it. This will be a great weeknight side dish. Made for ZWT 5.

We really enjoyed this soup. I cut it down to serve 4 and still used the entire 28 ounce can of tomatoes and 3 cups of water. I upped the garlic and salt a little and cooked for about 6 hours on mostly high. In the end even with using less lentils, the soup was quite thick- just how we like it. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT5.

Yum! Delicious shortbread cookies. They are so buttery and delicate. I'm glad the recipe only makes a 9 in square pan- LOL
I cut them immediately after removing from the oven and maybe I should have waited a while as they came apart a little. Also I used a glass baking pan and they did stick so maybe a metal pan is key. The taste was great though and I would try them again. Made for ZWT5.

Truly delicious! Made as directed for day 1, day 2 thickened the juices and made more of a beef and gravy mixture, and tonight I am making a pot pie out of the remaining beef and "gravy".  Very good and highly recommended. Made for ZWT5.

These are so good! I couldn't stop eating them warm, but they really are better after cooling. The recipe is very easy and made with ingredients I most always have on hand. I upped the cinnamom to 1/2 tsp- Delish!Thanks for sharing FN- Made for ZWT5

Oh my goodness- Divine! I do have a few comments though. The taste was thru the roof- easily 10 stars, but my omelette made as directed got way more browned than I normally would like. After beating the egg whites to stiff peaks and folding in the yolk mixture I could not pour the mixture into my pan but rather spread it in. I used 1 tbsp of butter as I didn't see it in the directions and I thought that was a pretty standard amount. I used medium low-medium heat and had to cover the pan as the bottom was cooking so fast and the top not yet done. I couldn't spread the mascarpone mixture because the top was so delicate but rather plopped it on in small spoonfuls. I too added a bit more cheddar and have to say that despite what I feel was overcooked probably one of the best tasting omelettes I have ever eaten. I will perfect this technique for my needs and make again very soon. Thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT5 Omelette Challenge. eta: I made this again and while it still was very brown, the flavor was as spectacular as the first time I made it! I forgot to mention in original post that I did in fact use all optional ingredients even though I went very light on the sage. I added a star as I craved this omelette for 2 days after originally trying it. So delicious!

Fabulous Burgers! I loved the filling combo and may even up the horseradish next time. The blue cheese gave it just the right tang. I also fried up a few slices of bacon that was delicious added to the burger. Made for Family Picks ZWT5.

Easy and delicious. If you can resist temptation and save them in a airtight container, they are even moister and more delicious the next day. I also like them warm out of the oven with strawberry jam. Thanks for sharing the recipe.

This recipe could really be made with any fruit you have on hand but the kiwi and strawberries are so bright and pretty. I whipped my marshmallow creme a bit before folding in because straight out of the jar it was pretty stiff. I used a 9 inch graham crust that was a little too big, but no matter I just piled on the fruit. This would be an easy and beautiful dessert to bring to a summer gathering. I love Susie's idea about using the individual tart shells. I may try that next time. Made for Fall PAC 2009

Tink this recipe is FABULOUS! I made the rice the night before so it would be nice and cold. I really appreciated the ease of preparing this as time is tight on weeknights. I served the rice as a side to recipe #397044 but I could easily eat this as a main dish- YUM! Thanks for posting Sissy- We loved it!! Bren

Great side dish. Easy to put together and a good option for something a little different on abusy week night. O loved the cream cheese garlic combo. I may add a little salt and pepper next time. Thanks for sharing. *Made for PAC Spring 2010*
We enjoyed these for lunch today. I did bake the potatoes in the oven because we like the skins crispy. Creamy and filling, thanks for sharing. Made for ZWT 6 German/ Benelux region.

This was a hit served on recipe #423193 along side recipe #425532 for lunch yesterday. My DS and his GF slathered the rolls with your butter and mentioned several times how good it was. There wasn't any left but I bet this would be AWESOME melted over hot veggies- for some reason carrots come to mind. I used fresh rosemary from my herb garden and jarred minced garlic. This is definitely a recipe I will double or even quadruple in the future. I bet you could freeze it too. Made for Scandinavian region of ZWT 6.

Absolutely delicious! I loved the simple yet enhancing seasonings in this dish. I used sea salt and a generous amount of cracked pink and black peppercorns. I was out of aleppo flakes so I used ancho chili powder. I served this over nutty brown rice for a late lunch/early dinner. Just wonderful, thank you for sharing the recipe. Made for the NA-ME region of ZWT6. eta: DS made hoagies with the leftovers.

Fabulous! I had a 32 ounce container of plain Greek Yogurt so I was probably a bit shy on the yogurt amount. I keep my KA freezer bowl out in the deep freeze so this literally went from start to finish  in under 20 minutes. Served with a drizzle of honey to compliment the tang of the yogurt and a light sprinkle of lemon zest. So good! Made for Greece-ZWT6

These are really quite good and something out of the ordinary. I didn't know what to expect with only 2 eggs as wet ingredients, but the finished texture is soft and chewy. I wonder if the beaten egg whites are what made the bars light and chewy? The graham crumbs add another layer of sweetness, almost honey like. This reminds me of something I would have found on my Grandma's cupboard. She always had simple yet tasty treats when we came to visit. I would make these again and not change a thing. After I added the mixture to the pan (it will be crumbly), I lightly patted the crumbs down with the bottom of a measuring cup to even the mixture out. I preferred these cooled and plain vs served with ice cream. Made for ZWT6- ZINGO!

These are delicious! My mixture was a bit moister than I had anticipated even using just 3/4 cup homemade buttermilk, but that didn't affect the final product. I patted it into a circle on a parchment lined cookie sheet and wasn't able to cut into triangles due to the moist mixture. I baked the scones about 15 minutes and then cut them, moved them apart a little bit and then baked another 6-7 minutes. It worked out just fine. I loved the added sweetness from the powdered sugar tops and my white chips were deliciously melted due to the extra baking time I added. What a forgiving recipe! I will definitely make these again. Thanks for posting. Made for Family Picks, ZWT 6

Just the way DH likes his meatloaf. I liked the hint of worcestershire sauce and would add a little more next time. DH won't eat onions so I used a little granulated onion powder- don't tell him :)  Made for Family Picks ZWT6.

I thought this was just okay. The marinade was really good (I let it soak for 3 1/2 hours) but after I fried it in the bacon grease, it lost a lot of that flavor. But anything topped with bacon and cheese is good. It was worth a shot but I think it's more calories than it's worth eating. Sorry!

These cookies were really good and I got a lot of compliments on them. Instead of leaving them as balls before I baked them, I flattened them slightly with the bottom of a glass for a more uniform shape. I found that if I baked them for 12 minutes, they got a little bit overcooked so I cut the time back to 10 minutes and they were perfect. I stored them in the fridge overnight and I think I liked them better the next day. I also liked them better when I added the cream cheese icing (I used Recipe #297863 instead of the suggested frosting) because they really tasted like Red Velvet Cake. The only problem I had with the recipe is that the hand mixer and this batter DID NOT get along well. After I added the cake mix, it got really thick and the mixer went haywire and I wound up with bright red batter spattered all over my kitchen. It looked like a scene out of Psycho and was very difficult to clean up. I would suggest using a stand mixer or mixing it by hand to avoid the giant mess.

This was a great meal that got good reviews across the boards from my family and friends that tried it. We added both broccoli and zucchini to the packets and seasoned the chicken with some Seasoned Salt before throwing them on the grill. I had to cook them a little longer than written (about 7-10 more minutes) but I used larger chicken breasts so I expected it. I completely forgot to add the mozzarella when I served it, but everyone was so busy eating that I don't think it mattered! I will definitely be making these again and adding some of the other veggies that were suggested by other reviewers. Thanks for posting!

Oh wow, this dish was so good!  I made it as instructed but followed Leggy Peggy's suggestion to add the salsa while it was cooking.  I also used 3 large zucchini that I cut into quarters to fit into my pan.  Halfway through cooking I tasted the "broth" and wound up adding more ginger and honey and it couldn't have been more delicious!  My husband raved and raved the entire way through dinner about how good it was.  Thank you for posting!  It is going into our weekly rotation file.

I love you for posting this!  I've used it the past 3 years since I received a GE roaster oven for Christmas, and I've always had a perfect bird.  I can't believe I haven't taken the time to give it the 5 star rating that it deserves!  I brine my bird with Recipe #101391 (with garlic cloves and fresh rosemary added) the night before, and follow your recipe exactly (with stuffing), and it is great.  I have always added about an inch of chicken broth to the bottom of the pan because I was afraid of the bird drying out, and I've never had a problem.  I've also never had a problem with the skin browning.  love that it frees up my oven so I can make other items.  Thank you again for posting!  I don't know what I would do without this recipe!

Mmmm..this was delicious.A very simple dish that produced such great flavours.I did have to substitute the sake for dry sherry (sorry) and I used green tea.We served it very simply with some steamed rice.A really classy dish,that we thoroughly enjoyed.Thanks so much Maito.

Oh my goodness!! Is it right that something that takes about 2 minutes to throw together should taste SO good?! Well let me assure you that it does!! Indecently easy to make and even more so to eat.Don't change a thing-it's delicious.Thanks Bird and Buddha,this is a real keeper!!!
What a wonderfully simple idea,that is so effective.It's a real no mess,no fuss,tasty way of eating mushrooms,and I LOVE it.Thank you Kate.

What a wonderfully simple recipe!! This was very well received as a lunch snack today,by my two children (aged 3 and 1),and I loved them too!! So quick and easy to whip up.I recommend that you do break the noodles up quite small (mine weren't!!) and also watch out for the sweetcorn when you fry them.I had a couple launch themselves out of the pan at me!!
We served ours with some chilli sauce to dip into (we like Linghams).A winner in our house-thanks for posting.Made for Zaartag.

I made this for my children's dinner tonight.I don't do shop bought sauce,and as I always have some homemade sauce in the freezer,I used that.I chopped up the chicken into very small pieces and also added some chopped courgette.If I'd had it,I would have also thrown in some mushroom.The children enjoyed it,and plates were cleaned.A very quick and simple dinner,thats easily adapted to the contents of your fridge.Thank you.

This was so easy and deliciously different.My potatoes were quite small,so just halved them,but next time I would definately quarter them,for the extra surface area.I used Maille French mustard,which gave the potatoes a wonderful flavour.
Thanks for a great recipe.

Applause,applause,applause!! This is a super little recipe,that really couldn't be simpler.I used chicken breast for mine,added a good splosh of tabasco to the marinade,and let it sit in the fridge for about 6 hours.The result was moist,sweet,spicy and quite delicious.
A real hit in this house,we'll be making this again.

Oh my-these are just GREAT!! I had these for lunch today on some toasted homemade ciabatta...absolutely fabulous! I halved some of my mushrooms as they were a little on the large side,and I also used bacon rather than turkey bacon.Such a quick and easy recipe,that is so flavoursome.A BIG hit with me.Thanks Sydney Mike.Made for ZaarTag.

What a fantastically decadent way to start the day!! We had this for a late breakfast this morning,and we LOVED it!! Even my little 22 month old daughter was tucking in with gusto.
I cooked the potatoes last night,and left them to cool,then first thing this morning, I prepared everything up to the oven stage.When we were ready,i just popped it into the oven to finish off.My brie was extremely ripe and pungent,maybe a bit too much for a first meal of the day,next time I think I might use a younger one.I might also throw in some quartered mushrooms and maybe sub bacon for the ham (I just love bacon and brie together).
A lovely recipe,that we all very much enjoyed.This will definately be found on my breakfast table again.Thanks Laffer.

Absolutely delicious!! Really lovely flavour and perfect amount of heat (I used the full quota of chilli).A minimum amount of effort results in a good,hearty and very tasty meal.This one goes in the keeper file,thanks Appley Dapply.Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

This was absolutely gorgeous!! I'm so impressed that so few and such simple ingredients can produce something that's full of flavour and low in fat therefore being healthier.I added a bit more hot sauce to mine (I like it zingy) and I had to up the heat to get my sauce to thicken and reduce.The sauce was sweet and spicy without any one flavour being too strong,the chicken was moist and delicious.I should imagine that if you stripped the chicken and mixed it with the sauce it would be great in a sandwich.A real triumph,thank you SO much for posting.An absolute winner!!
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

A really simple and really tasty salad.I just love things like this,and this is no exception.In fact I like it even more as it's low fat.
The crunch and sweetness of the apple and carrot are absolutely perfect,and just the right amount of mayo to bind it together and not swamp it.
This is one that I will definately make again..Thanks Dreamer!
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

I also used fresh cauli in mine,and cooked on the stovetop.I also used some skimmed milk mixed with cream rather than all cream.This was a lovely soup with lovely flavour,that was easy to put together.What more can you ask for?!
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.
SO very simple,SO very yummy.Munchie heaven!!

A very easy and delicious potato dish.I prepared mine all in advance,and just popped it into the oven when I was ready.
A lovely dish,that went down well with everybody.Thanks.
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

Cabbage is so under-rated,which is such a shame as it's a great vegetable.This recipe shows how verstile is.
The flavours were lovely and complimented each other perfectly.Everybody enjoyed this,including the children.
Thanks Loof.
Made for PhotoTag.

This was wonderfully simple to put together,and made a lovely weeknight supper.
I used a mix of Monterey Jack and Cheddar,which tasted great,and my tortillas were chilli and jalapeno flavoured.The sauce was lovely,creamy and delicious.This was a great meal as it was,but as said my another review,would also be great if you added shredded chicken to the tortilla mix.
We loved it Mersaydees!!

I made mine using homemade meatballs,and my beloved Jack Daniels,cooking on top of the stove.It really couldn't have been easier or tastier-they are delicious!!Absolutely no need to change a thing about this recipe,it's spot on!
I will definately be making this again!!
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

Whats not to like about champagne.orange and cranberry juice?Absolutely nothing!!This is a delicious twist on the classic Mimosa (or Bucks Fizz,as we call in here in England!),and we really enjoyed it.Perfect for a celebratory brunch!
Made for ZaarTag.

I marinated my chops overnight,and they came out tender and tasty.My only change would be to reduce the amount of hoisin sauce slightly (I use Amoy,and it's very thick and rich!) and I felt that it didn't quite let the other flavours shine through as well as they should have.A lovely,easy and tasty recipe.Thanks WiGal.
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

I was intrigued by this recipe,having never seen anything like it before.Mine took about another 20 minutes to cook than stated,and to be honest I thought that I had managed to mess it up (although with such simple and straightforward instructions I couldn't figure out how!).When it did finally emerge,it smelled delicious!!
As I have never had anything like this before,I don't have any frame of reference,but I think its lovely and the children have been enjoying it too.
Thanks Breezermom.

There really is something so comforting about gooey,melted cheese!!A deliciously easy sandwich,that hits the spot!
Thanks BakinBaby.
Made for ZaarTag.

Ingenious!! What a great and super easy potato dish!! I have just recently brought some Old Bay back from the US,and now it's definately going to go to good use!
We loved it Jackie..another winner!!
Made for 1-2-3- Hit Wonders.

My DH is an expert on things 'sausage roll-ish' and I wasn't convinced that this was going to get his seal of approval.Happily I couldn't have been more wrong!He thought they were great,as did my two little ones (who are not into this sort of thing ordinarily).The filling is light and tasty,and makes a real change to the usual denseness of your average sausage roll.
A very simple,and exceptionally tasty twist on an old classic.
Another winner from you Bluemoon.
Made for ZaarTag.

I used fresh broccoli and garlic,and breadcrumbs rather than Ritz cracker.The whole thing was really simple to produce and the end result was quite delicious..great textures and flavours.Definately a keeper!
Made for ZaarTag.

So easy,so garlicky,so crunchy,so yummy..so go and make it!!
I used chicken breasts cut into large pieces,and did everything else as written.It really couldn't be any easier.Whats more,all of the ingredients are things that you would normally find in the house (well mine anyway!),making it a great standby meal.
Another winner Miss Kit!!
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

This is a great little recipe!!
I cut my chicken into goujons,as I was entertaining my Dh's footie friends,so cut down the cooking time considerably.
They came out perfectly....crisp and crunchy on the outside,and beautifully moist on the inside.They disappeared swiftly,to say the least.My DH,who LOVES this kind of food,didn't even want to dip it into anything,as he said it tasted so good...and that's unheard of!!
Thumbs up for you BakinBaby,I'm keeping this little gem!!

I cooked mine in the oven,as using the bbq is not an option here at the moment.It worked really well.The potatoes were full of flavour,and very enjoyable.
A really easy recipe,and what's more there's no messy pan to wash up afterwards.Thanks for sharing.Made for PRMR.

What's not to love about this dish!! I love breaded mushrooms,and this certainly made a change from deep frying them,with the added bonus of a lovely buttery taste.I used homemade crumbs straight out of the freezer,and they adhered beautifully to the mushrooms,with just a few escaping when I turned them in the pan.A triumph!!Made for PRMR.

I had something very similar to this on my bar snack menu years ago.This was just gorgeous-DH hasn't stopped going on about it yet,and he ate it nearly 24 hours ago!!This was really simple to knock up and tastes just fab! I made some dijon mayo and spread it on lightly toasted homemade rustic baguette.
I recommend it-thanks Appleydapply for sharing.
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

A really tasty and easy recipe.I just loved it!! It really did 'dress' up the broccoli,without spoiling it.I shall be making this often.Thanks Dreamer,for a fab recipe!
Made for ZaarTag.

This is a good example of the fact that you don't need alot of fancy ingredients and hours slaving over a hot stove to produce something that is satisfying and flavoursome.
Delicious!!

Simple,tasty and easier than easy!! We used spaghetti for ours and a very generous pinch of pepper..it was delicious.A wonderful recipe for when the cupboards are bare!!Thanks Dreamer.Made for PhotoTag.

My DH absolutely loves a burger,and will soon complain if it's not up to scratch..within a couple of bites he was singing its' praises and has raved about it ever since!! I think that means its a winner!!Thanks for posting.
Made for PRMR.
Delicious little marinade.I used sherry and chicken breasts to make mine.After grilling,I sliced up the chicken and served it with stirfried vegetables and noodles..mmm!!

Sensational!This was so easy and tasted just wonderful,they were devoured in minutes!! A really great recipe,that I'm definately going to be using again and again..Thanks BakinBaby.
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

I just love potato gratins,and this one was no exception.It was creamy,garlicky,rich and delicious.I did have to pop it into the microwave just to finish it off for a few minutes,as the potatoes were not quite soft enough,but that's no great problem.
We had this as part of our Christmas lunch,and it was fabulous.Thanks Diner!
Made for 1-2-3-4 Hit Wonders.

A lovely recipe for using up leftovers,especially good for this time of year!! I used a combination of roasted parsnips and potatoes,and threw some mushrooms in too.It was a really tasty late breakfast dish that we enjoyed very much.Thanks BlueMoon,for another easy and delicious recipe.

Well...what can I say.DH finished his plateful,declared that I had really surpassed myself (and I make good scramble!) and that the eggs were superb!Not only that,my 2 year old kept demanding more! I think that you can say that this was a resounding success.This is the way that it will be done from here on in.Thanks Puppity for such a simple and fabulous recipe.
Made for 1-2-3-4 Hit Wonders.

A really delicious twist on the classis Waldorf Salad.I used a good cheddar in mine,but am going to try it with blue cheese next time,as I think that would be great too.I had to sub blanched peanuts for walnuts,as I had run out,but it gave a really good texture and crunch to the salad,which we really enjoyed.
A really tasty and simple salad,that we will enjoy again.Thanks BlueMoon.

What's not to like about this sauce? It's economical,super speedy and most importantly it tastes good.
We enjoyed it with some bucatini pasta.A great standby for when time is short,and a great one for the children!!
Thanks Lainey.Made for 1-2-3 Hits.

I used low fat natural yogurt rather than buttermilk (needed using up!),and homemade seasoned breadcrumbs.Also,rather than butter,I drizzled the chicken with cooking olive oil.I baked mine for just over an hour,and the result was moist,tender and crispy chicken,which we just loved.I shall be doing this again,WiGal,so thank you!!

Not very addictive then!!These are absolutely wonderful little treats that are compulsive eating!!
I knew that I would love these,and so doubled the recipe-nowhere near enough if you ask me..so be prepared to multiply this recipe by a lot!!
A fabulous recipe..thanks so much for sharing it BlueMoon.Made for 1-2-3 Hits.

This is a great lunch snack!! I made it as written,and we really enjoyed it.
A  simple and delicious recipe,that can be whippped up with little effort.Perfect for days when time is short,and you need something tasty to eat.
Thanks BlueMoon.

I have to admit that I adapted this slightly.Firstly,I don't have a crockpot,and secondly I used chicken breast,as my husband (much to my annoyance!!) still struggles with meat on the bone.Thirdly,I used finely diced onion instead of onion soup mix.
I realise that these changes were quite significant,but I just HAD to try this recipe.
I cooked my chicken in the oven,covered,on a low heat for about an hour,then removed the cover for another 30 minutes,turning the heat up.
The result was one fantastic chicken dish..deserving more than a five star rating.The flavour of this was amazing...the sweetness of the sauce being balanced perfectly with the spiciness of it.The chicken was tender and juicy,and just melted in the mouth.
I served this with some pilaf rice,and it was just delicious.DH absolutely loved it,and declared it could be made again!
Thanks WeekendCooker,this is a real winner!!
Made for ZaarStars.

I cut this recipe in half,as it was way too big for us.I didn't bother to peel my potatoes,as I was using my trusty potato ricer,and the skins come off when you squish them,making life really easy!!
This was a really delicious recipe,and we enjoyed it.My mixture was a little on the sloppy side,but it didn't matter,it still got devoured.
Thanks Jess.
Made for ZaarStars.

Since I am a Brit,and have no clue as to what a flat iron steak is,I used some good old rump.
The rub was an absolute cinch to throw together,and I rubbed it over my meat and left it for well over an hour.
The results were amazing,we just loved it.It had just the right balance of hot and sweet,and tasted divine.It really breathed life into what would have been a boring lump of meat.
Thanks BakinBaby,I shall be stashing this little gem away for furure use!!
Made for Newest Zaar.

These potatoes have really great flavour,the herbs and the balsamic vinegar work so well in this dish.
I,like Boomette,would have prefered them to crisp up a bit.I cooked them for over an hour,and turned the heat up considerably towards the end of cooking.
I also recommend that you turn them regularly to prevent them from sticking.
We did enjoy these potatoes,and will be making them again..so thanks for sharing WickedCook.
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

These really are very tasty,but like the others,mine never got crispy (something that is quite difficut to achieve owing to the sugars in the potato).I cut mine into fat fries,and also sprinkled them with some cumin (something that I highly recommend!!).I also lined my tray with silicone paper,as nothing sticks it it,no matter what!!
The fries were lovely,and made a nice change from regular potato fries.
Thanks Sharon.Made for ZaarStars.

This was a real treat for lunch today.Instead of bagels (you can't get a decent one here!) I used my recipe #348192#348192,and lightly toasted them.Instead of whizzing my cheese in the processor,I put it into the microwave for 10 seconds to soften it,and then mashed it and mixed it with the mayo (less washing up!).
The whole thing was just delicious..soft sweet onions,the richness of the Stilton all married together with the beef so beautifully.
Another triumph BlueMoon..many thanks.
Made for 1-2-3 Hits.

If you are expecting just another breaded chicken recipe,then you are wrong!!
The blend of herbs and spices in the breadcrumb mixture deliver fantastic flavour,the crumb itself is deliciously crunchy,while the chicken is tender and succulent in the middle....all leaving you desperate to get that fork back into your mouth again with the next mouthful.
DH gave this top marks,something he NEVER does..this really is a winner,and so easy to whip up too!!
Hokies,you're a marvel..thank you for sharing this little gem!!
Made for 1-2-3 Hits

A very simple and quick dish that is full of flavour.
I used rump steak (sirloin is just much too expensive) and left out the tomato.
The soft tenderness of the beef against the sweet crunch of the snow peas was just wonderful,a taste and texture sensation!.I should imagine that this would also be good with broccoli too.
A lovely dish,that I will definately be cooking again...thanks Loof.
