I used dried chickpeas and soaked them overnight before cooking them -- they turn out firmer than canned chickpeas, and the texture went really nice with the rice.  I plan on making another batch this week to keep in the fridge --  30 seconds or so in the microwave and I'll have a quick and tasty snack.  I'm going to add more of the spices to mine, but since DH and DS don't like things too spicy, the amount in the recipe was perfect for them.

Everyone in the family here loves bacon, and what a treat to find a recipe we can use for a snack.  I made it twice -- the first time I covered the bacon slices generously with the brown sugar mixture, but they came out of the oven a little burnt.  So I made them again, this time brushing any excess sugar off the bacon slices and they didn't burn at all.  Both times I did have a problem getting the slices as crispy as I would have liked, but the taste was terrific nonetheless.  And the applewood bacon was a flavor I had never tried before. Two of us finished the entire batch in one sitting; it was that good.  Thanks for posting.

Mmm -- so easy and so delicious.  We loved the sauce, and especially the wonderful taste of the toasted sesame seeds.  I used fresh, pre-packaged and pre-washed spinach from the produce section of our store, so it was super-quick to get this on the table.  The only change I would make is to perhaps stir-fry the spinach, or remove the excess water from boiling by putting it in a tea towel and pressing on it.  I found that by squeezing the spinach, it lost a lot of visual appeal as the spinach was all clumped together, but the taste is a 5-star for sure.

This was really good.  I added a tablespoon of tahini and omitted the parsley because I didn't have any.  I made it in about 10 minutes and ate it at room temperature the first time.  It's good at room temp as well as cold.  I dipped raw vegetables and whole wheat pita bread in it.  I will be making this often.  Thanks for the recipe!

This is a great, healthy recipe!  It was easy, too.  We used the Italian diced tomatoes.  I also added a little parmesan cheese on top of mine.  The only thing that I will change next time is to maybe mix the ground beef throughout or something.  It got kind of squished like a strange patty in the bottom of the crock pot, but it still tasted good.  I just had to break it up as I was mixing it.  Thanks for the recipe!
This was easy and good.  We used half of the oil just to cut the fat a little and it turned out perfect.  Thanks for the recipe.
We really liked these. They make a really tasty side dish. I would recommend cutting them quite thin to get more of the seasoning flavor.  They are even good with ketchup.

I cooked in chicken stock, baked  my bacon, (I do a whole lb. at a time so we always have it for recipes, and BLTs)  so I used Olive oil for mushroom and onion.  I served for Canadian Thanksgiving.  Great recipe.  All the flavors. work well together    Thanks for the posting.

I served this for Canadian Thanksgiving.  I made just as posted except I tossed the squash in a little melted butter & a wee bit of Maple Syrup.  I also added chopped fresh sage to the topping.  Really yummy.  Thanks for the posting.
i had this at an Ontario Zaarfest. it is todie for.   Superb!
I had this at Country  Lady's Appy Party!  Wow,yummy!
These are divine.  i had them at an Ontario Zaar fete and they are munchelicious.
i have not made these, but my friend and fellow Zaar made them for an Ontario Zaar function.   They were beyond delicious.  Super!!!!!
These were good, my kids enjoyed them. Didn't have quite as much flavor as I expected but they were good nonetheless. Served with Bourbon Chicken #45809

This was really good. My DH even went back for seconds (he doesn't like broccoli!). The kids weren't the biggest fans, but what do they know! The only thing I did different was double the sauce so I could mix the broccoli in with it in the pan. I used vegan sour cream and added just a touch of nutritional yeast for a bit of a cheesy flavor. Definitely a keeper, especially for a dinner without the kids! Served with recipe #90485. Thanks mliss!

The adults in the house really enjoyed this. The kids were iffy about it but did eat it all (who cares what they think right!). I left out the olives and cheese but made everything else according to the directions. Will definitely be making it again. Thanks Karen Elizabeth (I'm Karin Elizabeth too).

I swear I've reviewed this before, but apparently not. I used premade (but fresh) patties from the grocery store out of laziness, and doubled the sauce for 8 burgers. Added about two tsps of organic broth base instead of the bouillon and it was perfect. Thanks for yet another five star Kitten!

This was good, very meaty. We aren't vegan or vegetarian, but have been trying to find some healthier and less processed substitutes for some meats, and this is a winner. We put it in the food processor to substitute as ground beef as another reviewer suggested. Next time I think I will change the spices up too, to make it more meatball-like instead of pepperoni-like. Thanks so much AJO!

I thought this was good, as did one of my kids...the other two weren't so fond. I used the amount of soy sauce listed, but i think it could've used more, so I guess this is definitely a to each his own recipe! Sauce was great, and it was an easy lunch.

This was really good! Kids all loved it, DH loved it. Takes some time and effort, but is perfect for those days when I feel like doing a ton of prep work (which there are a lot of!). Thanks so much blue.

Yummy! I'm a lazy non-vegetarian so in lieu of the veggie stock powder and water I used boiling chicken broth. I can't find dried currants anywhere (looked in three states!), so I had to omit those as well, which bummed me out because I love currants! Tasted it hot and it was yummy, but I did prefer it on the side of lukewarm to cool. Thanks again Karen E, from your fellow Karin E!

Wow this was the BEST couscous I've ever had. The hummus absolutely makes the dish too. The only thing I did differently was omit the rocket after I discovered a dead grasshopper in the middle of my bunch (EWWW). I'll add it next time though, assuming no more insects are present lol. Thanks so much! Served with recipe #335368.

I made this with the asian sauce (I'm allergic to milk but would LOVE to try the cheese sauce), and altered the method slightly. Instead of steaming the veggies I braised the cauliflower first (8-10 min)  in about a quarter cup of chicken broth, then added the rest of the veggies, covered my pan, and let braise/steam in what little of the broth was left for another five minutes or so. Then I just added the sauce to the veggies to cook for a few. It was absolutely delicious...I ate it all off my plate before I touched one of my favorite entrees (recipe #45809)! Thanks KatieL, will be making often!
I don't eat pork but my family inhaled these so I think that means they're good. Thanks Grumpy!

This was really delicious despite the fact that I inadvertently butchered it. I didn't read the directions before I started making it (at least not far enough through), so I couldn't puree the sauce because I cracked my blender. Couldn't find curry leaves anywhere so I left them out, and the "soy" yogurt we have here (milk allergy) has milk in it so I left that out as well. This is the first of Gordon's recipes I've tried...Must find more! Thanks for posting Noo!

My hubby is the tomato soup eater in the house. He took one bite and said "Oh Wow!" and this man never wows anything. Was super easy to make, used margarine and soy milk instead of the dairy stuff. Thanks (as usual) Kitten!

These are great! I've always wanted to try some dark chocolate brownies but could never find a recipe that looked right. Only thing I changed was to use nonstick spray and cocoa powder in the pan. Thanks Bev!

This was very good and crispy, but not garlicky enough for me, and I used the full 4 tsp of garlic powder. Maybe I just love too much garlic lol. We'll still make it again though, because the chicken came out very crispy and juicy. Thanks as usual Kitten!
Did this for my 7 year old today, worked like a charm. Thanks so much!

Used an eye of round roast (about 3.5 lbs), doubled the sauce, and cooked for about 8 hours. It was super flavorful and tender, easy to shred. When my husband took his first bite he said "OH yeah"...And he's not generally the most complimentary person! Served on recipe #183081 (which is the best bun recipe ever). Thanks JacquelynLee!

This was quick and easy, kids loved it. Instead of doing the crock pot I simmered it over medium heat on the stove. I didn't taste it, the three of them ate it all (they only weigh 110 lbs combined!) so it must have been really good. Thanks so much for a kid pleaser! I am a Marine wife, and when he's gone some nights it just seems like so much work to come up with dinners that make everyone happy!

I only soaked the okra for about 30 minutes as some other reviewers did. Instead of sauteing them on the stove, I layered it into a casserole dish as okra, spices, and onions, dotted it with butter, then baked it at 400 degrees for about 25 minutes, stirring at the last five minutes (all of the burners on my stove were taken up). Anyway, there wasn't any left from the DH and kids, I didn't even get to taste, so I guess it was pretty good! Thanks Alskann!
These are great, I did them the old fashioned way by hand. Next time will take everyone else's advice and divide the dough into four bowls instead of six. Thanks!
I don't actually know what adobo is supposed to taste like (I needed it to make refried beans), but this is really good, so five stars regardless!
Doubled the batch, DH ate the whole thing, so I guess they're pretty tasty!
So so good. I could have easily gotten 8-10" servings from it though. They ended up pretty thick and nearly 12" just making five. Will be regularly making again though for flatbread pizzas!
I have never heard of Cane's, but if this isn't their dipping sauce it should be. Super super good, used homemade ketchup and served with recipe #89503.
Simple and tasty! My 10 year old made it tonight for his turn to make dinner. We left the cheese off because I'm allergic to milk, but it was still great.
I marinated first in the mix then followed the directions exactly. Kids and DH scarfed it down. Thanks!

Delicious!  I don't know why I never thought of using potatoes in replacement for beans in chili.  My son doesn't like beans, so I don't make chili that often even though everyone else in my family loves chili.  This was a hit with my family!  Thank you for sharing your recipe!

These are so good, yet so healthy!  Instead of making loafs, I made 40 mini muffins and had to cook them for about 25 minutes. (I started at 15 minutes and ended up having to bake them 10 more minutes.  Maybe because they are so dense?) They are great to just grab for a quick snack.

So moist and so delicious!!  I reduced the recipe to make 3 loaves (I only had 4 banana's), which resulted in two 9X5 loaves.  I also used low fat sour cream and egg beaters for the eggs.  I don't think the substitutions made one bit of difference.  You would never know that this was low fat!  The recipe was so easy.  This is probably the best banana bread I have tried!  This will be my go-to recipe from now on.  Thank you for sharing!

I see this exact recipe two other times, but kept thinking I'm not sure of the mixture of spices......After the third time of viewing the recipe (YOURS!), I decided to give it a try.  I am so glad I did.  I was so easy to throw together with ingredients I already hand on hand, so no revisions were necessary.  This end results was a mix of sweet and spicy and a very moist pork tenderloin.  This is a recipe I will be repeating for sure!

I made Kittencal's Perfect Pesto for this recipe and used your suggested chicken and cheese ravioli.  I added  chicken breasts which I cut into bite sized pieces and pan-fried before adding the sauce ingredients.  The sauce is delicious and I greatly appreciate you posting this recipe.  Very creative and the flavor is fantastic.  Thank you for posting your creation!
These are great!  I followed the recipe and came out with a wonderful crispy chicken tender.  They are much better than chicken tenders from a restaurant.  Thank you for posting.

This was easy to make and the meat was VERY tender.  I ended using top sirloin which I pounded out to about 1/2 thickness.  My BF and coworker enjoyed this tasty dish.  Thanks for posting this recipe.

I make muffins all the time, but this is the first time my BF came home and the first thing he said was how good these muffins were (I sent them to work with him).  The strawbutter is fantastic.  I will definitely make this recipe again.  Thank you for a winner!

This is buttery and melt in your mouth cornbread!!.  I made a mistake and handed my BF a can of creamed corn instead of corn kernels which I used in this cornbread, but it still turned out to be a tender sweet cornbread.  I doubled the recipe and used the full two cups of sugar.  I loved this corn bread.  This will definitely will go into my permanent recipe books!

I loved this recipe.  I prepped the flour, nut coating and pounded the chicken the night before I baked.  It was easy to put together the next night.  I would make more nut/cornflake crust next time.  This was a delicious chicken dish.  It is so unique, but something that everyone would love.  How innovative!  I will be making this again and have saved this recipe to my permanent recipe book.  Thank you for this wonderful recipe.

These are the BEST cookies.  I have tried so many chocolate chip cookies from Zaar.  Cookies that use pudding mixes, cookies that include an extra something, but I couldn't find the "perfect chocolate chip cookie".  These are the perfect chocolate chip cookies.  All this time the recipe was on the bag!  I will definitely be using these as my go to chocolate chip cookie recipe.

I just dropped a note on your website regarding these biscuits.  VERY GOOD!  These are easy to make and very delicious.  I took your advice which you posted on your website regarding the garlic powder option.  I took that option by adding 1 tsp of garlic powder to a doubled recipe (1/2 tsp for a regular recipe).  Kitten you are the best!

I really liked this recipe, but had to change the stuffing to seasoned breadcrumbs (so I omitted the water).  Next time I will follow the recipe, but the breadcrumbs worked out perfectly.  I loved the cheese in these tuna cakes.  Thank you for posting this great recipe.

Wow!  This is so decadent, yet easy to make.  I have had trouble with my cakes falling, but this cake didn't.  I baked this cake in 3 round cake pans dusted with cocoa powder after I greased them.  I used a cream cheese frosting.  Chef-V's photo is beautiful and I am so glad to have found this recipe.  Thank you.

I loved these!  They were quick to make, but such a great use of refrigerated biscuits.  Really a perfect recipe.  I definitely will be making these again. I made a double batch and am very pleased that I did!  Thank you Crafty Lady 13!

This is delicious and easy to make.  I doubled the recipe and took it to work.  Everyone is raving about how delicious it is.  Thank you for this great recipe.  I know that I will be using this recipe again.
Perfect!  This is a great recipe which I made for chicken which we grilled.  Great flavor.  I haven't had time to make many new dishes lately because of time constraints, but this was AMAZING!!
Great recipe, used butter and garlic club crackers. Thanks, will make this again.
Made this to go with burgers yesterday, very good, left out the green pepper but added 2 hard boiled eggs.  Thanks will make again.
Thanks for the easy recipe, it was very good.

AMAZING!!  This was my first taste of grits and it won't be my last, I'm sold!  Don't have easy access to real grits in Seattle (though I hear Bob's Red Mill has a White Corn Grits sold somewhere in this city).  I had to buy "quick" grits (not instant!), and it was still phenomenal.  The shrimp was fabulous with the grits and would be great on their own too.  Thanks for posting breezermom!

Yep, 5 stars for Peaches and Cream!  So simple, but the taste is sophisticated.  I both made and ate this in about 5 minutes.  You might think of it as "deconstructed peach Ice cream" and that makes it so much more than just fruit with milk!  Thanks Cookgirl!  Made for Cuinary Quest 2014
So simple and fabulous!  I tossed the tomatoes and avocado with the dressing.  I plated the salad then topped with cojita chesese.  Great stuff!  Thanks Starrynews!!

So easy and soo good!  What a great appetizer for entertaining!  Tastes great and lovely presentation!  I added proscuitto.  It was a great addition.  Thanks for posting Starry!  I'll certainly make again!
Yum!!!  The shrimp was great, the sauce made it out of this world!!  Quick, easy and tasty!  Thanks Nancy!

What is not to love?  Fresh tomatoes from the garden, good balsamic soooo summer and so good.  The tomatoes on their own are great, I added a bit of basil and some mozzarella to make it a bigger meal.  Thanks for posting Lavender Lynn!  Made for Culinary Quest 2014
Really like how this cuts the sweetness of the Amaretto.  Really liked it.  Thanks for posting allgirl!  Made for Culinary Quest 2014

Yep, these are really tasty!  I made just a half batch for 2 of us, it was easy to convert.  Served with huckleberry compote and maple syrup.  Thanks for posting!  Made for Culinary Quest 2014 PNW region.

Really liked this!  I was a bit heavy handed on the honey, and wish I hadn't been, my dressing was a tad too sweet, but like I said, used a touch more than the recipe called for, so my own fault.  The colors are beautiful and the flavor is lovely!  Thanks for posting.  Made for Culinary Quest 2014, PNW Region.
Nothing left to say except I agree it was awesome!!  Thanks for posting!  Made for Culinary Quest, 2014 PNW Region.
2 of 3 of us liked this!  We used a french press with 4 Tbs coffee, 12 oz of water and one large fresh lavender.  Thanks for posting a fun recipe.  Made for Culinary Quest 2014, PNW Region.
I liked this a lot, the spice needs a minute to absorb into the coffee.  I will certainly make again! thanks for posting.  Made for Culinary Quest, PNW Region.
Simple, tasty and fabulous.  The best part is that you have all the ingredients already in your fridge and pantry!  Thanks for posting!  Made for Culinary Quest 2014, PNW Region.

So wonderful and cooked in under 10 minutes.  I used the pork gyoza from TJs.  My only critique is I would double the recipe.  I made for 2 of us and we would have like more, maybe double the liquid and keep the gyoza the same.  Thanks so much for posting Sofie!  Made for Culinary Quest FP, 2014.
Love this!!  So easy and great tasting.  Thanks for posting!  Made for Culinary Quest 2014, FP.

These were really yummy.  I used left over baked potatoes, which made it really quick as they didn't have to cool.  I cooked them a little longer and got a great crust on them.  I added a little bit of sour cream.  Thanks for posting lazyme.  Made for Culinary Quest 2014, FP.
Great!  Simple, quick and tasty.  I did double the sauce and that worked well.  Thanks for posting!!  Stacy G. for Toasted Tourists, CQ 2015, Switzerland.

These are perfect!  I coarse chopped the pineapple and because I have a sweet tooth I added a little vanilla glaze to half the batch.    Thanks for posting these are my new go to muffin treat!  Made for Culinary Quest 2015.
Loved this.  Had more than one! Thanks for posting! Made for Culinary Quest 2015.

I really enjoyed this versatile soup.  I think next time I will add the chicken to the top of the soup when serving.  So easy to customize this recipe with additions when serving.  Thanks for posting!  Made for Culinary Quest 2015.

Loved this.  The pineapple is fabulous and this recipe is so easy to customize in flavor and quantity!  Thanks for posting!  I'll be making this again.  Made for Culinary Quest 2015, Toasted Tourists.

So good.  Easy to adjust the heat level.  I made a half batch and should have made a whole batch!  Thanks for posting.  This will be a new staple in my house.  Thanks for posting.  Made for Culinary Quest 2015.

This recipe was terrific! I was looking for a banana pancake recipe that actually had bananas in it, not just on it! I halved the recipe which worked out well. Batter was a bit thick so I added a splash more milk. We had a buffet of toppings: cherries, bananas, nuts, coconut, butter and syrup! We'll be making again! Thanks for posting! (Stacy G made for CQ 2016)

Mia! Thanks for posting this yummy refreshing dessert, perfect on a hot summer night. Couldn't be much easier to make and the cointreau at the bottom of the glass was a nice surprise after eating the oranges and coconut!! (Stacy G made for CQ 2016)
Very good dressing to accompany my Asian Chicken Salad! Thanks for Posting. Made for Culinary Quest 2016, Japan. (Stacy G)

This was one of the best things I've eaten all summer. Who would have thought about canned artichoke hearts?! It was a first for me, but won't be my last. I made recipe as written and it was phenomenal. Perfect on a summer night. The dressing is terrific and could easily be used on many things other than salad. Thanks for posting S-a-T!! Stacy G made for CQ 2016 Greece
This tzatziki was terrific! My first time making it! I used my serrated peeler to just shred the cucumber. A super easy taste of Greece. Stacy G for CQ 2016 Greece.
These were terrific! I served with tzatziki. I used panko and good parmesan. Will absolutely make again. Thanks for posting LLynn! Stacy G made for CQ 2016 Greece

So I thought this was going to be a just okay take on yogurt parfait...I was wrong. It was a FABULOUS take on a yogurt parfait. Never expected the dates to be soooo tasty. Really loved this and will make again (with more dates)! Thanks P. Nan! Stacy G, made for CQ 2017, Turkey.

Loved these so much made them two days in a row, the second time for company. I made exactly as written, though I found middle eastern alleppo pepper for the second batch. (not sure it made a difference). I would err on the side of more spice, don't skimp. Will be making again! Thanks for posting Jackie! Made for Turkish Dinner Challenge, CQ 2017.

This was simple and refreshing. I was nervous about the jalapeno, but didn't need to be, it added to the flavor but not too much heat. Had this dish with food that was rich. The acid of the dish was perfect to cut through the fat of the rest of the meal. It was great. Thanks for posting Dreamer.

These were really really good! I did add some nutmeg to my breadcrumbs. I think thyme or other herbs can easily be added too! I used panko which worked well. I think the pan needs to be pretty hot, mine took a while to really get heated so I doubled the time it took to cook. I also added more butter as the cooking went on as the pan dried out, just to keep the panko browning. At first, I didn't get why the onion was needed, but it definitely added to the flavor. After plating the mushroom I scraped all the onion and brown bits out of the pan onto the mushrooms. Absolutely will make these again! Thanks for posting Lynn! Stacy G for CQ 2017, Austria.
Great summer salad. Even better the next day! thanks for posting breezermom! Stacy G made for CQ 2017, Turkey.

This chicken was part of one of the best meals I've ever cooked! It was terrific and easy and the spices were great! I think it is critical to ensure the the lemon is squeezed over the top of the chicken before serving! The bright lemon was perfect with the spices. Will be making this many times in the future! Thanks for posting LifeisGood!

This great salad was part of one of the best meals I've ever made! It was a great accompaniment to Indian Spiced Roast Chicken on a hot hot summer night. I was skeptical about the combo of mango and tomatoes and I shouldn't have been. It was terrific along with the red onion. The spices were spot on, I'm not a mint fan, but I think I could have added a bit more! Thanks for posting L. Lynn!! Stacy G for CQ 2017, Himalayas.
These were just terrific and they aren't over sugared. Quick, easy and tasty. Exactly what a goo muffin should be! Thanks for posting BK! Stacy G, Culinary Quest 2017, Wales.

This is a beautiful rice. I love the color and the look of the mustard seeds sprinkled throughout. I served with Butter Chicken and then had the rice by itself the next day. It was really really good. I think this recipe can be a beautiful accompaniment or stand on it's own. Thanks for posting momaphet!!! Stacy G made for Culinary Quest 2017, Himalayas

I really liked your grandmas peas! I thought the celery should be cut quite small, and I think I as wrong, the celery just got lost. I guess I'm not sold on the cream. The peas and tarragon and butter was enough for me! Either way it's really really good and actually was great as leftovers too. Thanks for posting BK! Stacy G for Culinary Quest 2017, Wales.
Terrific sandwich! Thanks for posting Dreamer! Made for CQ 2017, Scandinavia.
This was a terrific meatloaf! thanks for posting breezermom!! Made for CQ 2017, Scandinavia!

I originally saw this in the Rachel Ray magazine and the original recipe didn't state the water in the ingredients list, but in the text so the first glass was horrible.  After reading it here I realised I had missed the water so added it and it tasted much better, however it was very seedy from the kiwis and it still was very tart.  No one I served it to could (or maybe didn't want to) finish even a small glass.
Phenomenal, reminds me of something from IHOP, I will definitely be making again!
These were amazing!  The whole pan was gone by the end of day 2.  =)
This was delicious!  I loved that it made a whole pan, so lasted for several meals.  Thanks for sharing this, I will definitely make it again.

Totally yummy comfort food. I halved the recipe for the two of us and it was perfect. I followed the recipe as directed except for adding some chopped green pepper for personal choice whenever eating fried potatoes. It is now safely stowed away in the to be made often catagory. Thanks so much for the post.

The flavor of this dish is outstanding but I had to modify the directions in order for it to be edible.  I realized that it was impossible to use uncooked rice and have it cooked completely in 10 minutes, plus the amount of liquid to rice was way out of whack so cut the rice to one cup and increased the chicken broth to 2 cups and increased the cooking time to 25 minutes and it was great. This was using white rice. If I had been using brown would have had to increase cooking time to 45 minutes.  All in all this is a great and easy recipe to prepare and it will tolerate other veggies as I was out of broccoli so ended up using peas and carrots.

This is an excellent hot chocolate..  We were simply blown out of the water at the wonderful taste of this mix.  It is far superior to any store bought mix I have tried and that includes the sugared ones. I believe the pudding gives it that boost to make it so special but it is a keeper and have gave it out to several people already.  Thanks SO much for posting this recipe

This is an excellent tasting, easy to prepare recipe that we have fallen in love with.  I used frozen green beans and I did cook a bit longer than crisp tender stage as that is how we like our beans and I also added some garlic to the mix, approx 1/4 ts of garlic powder to the dish based solely on our presonnal tastes. Totally enjoyed and on regular rotation from now on.  Thanks so much for posting.
I love versatility and this recipe surely has it in spades !!! I used bacon and sausage and leftover vegies including beans with a lovely result.
Fabulous and versatile meal and quick to prepare - made for ZWT 4 - thanks for posting.
Mighty quick to make and yummy - I did use brown sugar - fabulous to put on porridge or muesli - made for ZWT 4.

This was unusual but very good. i served it on  wholegrain rice and adorned it with some spinach leaves and tiny diced cucumber - so all in all this is a great high protein meal for our mainly vegeatarian family - thanks Marra for posting.
I love pesto so this was a successful pizza  combo for me - I added some artichokes as well so all round it was very yummy.

Great cookie but I am annoyed with myself that I ran out of oats and had to use about  a cup of muesli so my cookie was not as authentic as it should have been - yummy just the same!!! Made for ZWT family picks.[I am taking some of these to Singapore in my case to share with DD who is meeting me there ]

My cookies look just like the photo posted !! That's a first for me - they are golden and taste gorgeous. I baked them for 15 - 18 mins very successfully and they just could not be easier to do - made about 16 mid sized cookies  but would not serve 60 as recipe indicated but I think that is just a typo. I added an extra egg as my dough was incredibly stiff but I am cooking in mid winter here in Arctic conditions with no heating due to renos so under normal conditions 1 egg would totally suffice - thank you to Sydney Mike.
This made me one big and fabulous cake - perfect for after school ! Ioved the large amount of nuts in it and used pecans as they were in the pantry .Thanks Sarah for a great afternoon tea keeper .

Fabulous mid week meal ! I used tomato soup as any type of cheese soup is non existent here and I used blue organic corn chips so my meal was colourful, that's for sure. Even the 'I don't eat meat' DD enjoyed this meal .
Fabulous marinade for skinless chicken fillets !! I then baked mine in the marinade and they were so good. Paprika gives them such a lovely colour. Many thanks.

I have made this for dinner and the verdict from my early sampling is that it is great. I used green lentils and used mushrooms instead of carrots and vegetable stock - when I serve it I may top it with pesto - thanks for a great dinner for tonight TraceyMae

This was enjoyed by all the family. I did not put in the enchilada sauce as I do not know if that product even exists here but did drizzle sweet chilli sauce over the serves. This was a great mid week meal and the children loved it !!!!
Fabulous crumble and so so easy to do. I added berries to my apple and it was delicious. This is now the only way to make a crumble topping in this house - i love it !!

Mine didn't look like the photo but was super moist with crunch on top and a dark coffee colour and flavour - I am taking the last bit to work for my buddies there to try as I loved it - thanks so much !!

Made for ZWT 5 - I  had a glut of limes given to me by a friend so this recipe was a  perfect start to using them. My herbs came from my own garden and I used a combination of chives, oregano and a little coriander .I used whole grain rice and  this side dish had wonderful, piquant flavours and everyone loved it.

I added a couple of other standard salad ingredients to this - tomato and avocado- but the peanuts just made it !! I left out the raisins and added extra peanuts - just a delicious salad !! Thank you - made for ZWT 5 !!!

This soup is to die for !! DS said it was a 'cracker' soup - high praise indeed !! I altered not one thing when making this but offered sweet chili sauce swirled on top to the eaters. It is such a beautiful colour and makes a generous amount - thanks KE so much for this fabulous meal.
Great flavours and textures but i found the thin batter a bit tricky to deal with - I am always a bit challenged with the flipping !!! Made for ZWT 5.
Fabulous salad and my avocado was just perfect and ready to use so this was such a timely recipe.My only addition was diced cucumber - made for ZWT 5.

Just had a quick sample of this straight out of the oven - so delicious, a bit brownie like in texture. I, too, added some rolled oats and had to add some capuccino chips to the choc chips to get my 3/4 cup.  Yum and thanks - made for ZWT 5.
I made this for 1 for brekky this morning - used goat's fetta and fresh thyme from my garden, served on spinach too . Totally enjoyable .
This has made a beautiful and generous cake - perfect texture too. I used vanilla instead of rum. My oven runs a little cold so this needed 45 minutes but the result is perfect. made for ZWT 5.

This recipe surprised me as there is no flour but nontheless I got a yummy result just like a energy bar but not in a bar shape. I used dates and a mix of almonds and walnuts with great success - made for ZWT 5.

I had to use apples for this but crumbles are pretty versatile and this one was great ! The apple worked  well with the crumble ingredients and adding the juice to the dry ingredients was a new take for me and I had a fabulous result.

These may be the best muffins I have ever made - light and fluffy but not falling apart. I had to sub pear for the blueberries as it is mid winter here . I did reduce the sugar a little and used vanilla paste instead of liquid vanilla with a totally gorgeous result - in fact I greedily ate two straight out of the oven !!!

As delicious as I thought it would be - my sort of comfort food !! I added some diced zucchini but made no other changes. Made for tonight's dinner but I could not help myself and had it for lunch - so yummy !

This was thoroughly enjoyable and a great way to eat a healthy array of vegies. I halved the recipe and pureed it and served it sprinkled with smoky paprika and chopped parsley - great colour and great taste !!

I made this as a slice in a 6x10 ceramic dish .The cake is soft and almost creamy in texture and totally addictive. I used both lemon and tangelo rind and juice and I have had to hide it so I don't eat the lot !!

This worked well for me and was served as a side to rack of veal . It was easy to do and giving the potatoes a good go in the microwave first guarantees they will be done perfectly - nothing worse than serving underdone taties and then having to wait ages while they go back in the oven so I was well pleased with this result.

I set out with great trepidation here and had great success. Our packet mixes seem to be smaller here -  mine was 340 grams -  so reduced pumpkin accordingly with a very good result.Moist, dense, lovely colour too and  not a hint of pumpkin flavour so good for unsuspecting kids !! They will be in the lunch boxes this week !

I have just done the condensed milk in the crock pot so far with great success. I cooked on high and next time will do on low as it cooked faster than recipe stated .You do have to keep an eye on it though .Tastes yummy and may be gone before it sees the inside of a pie crust !!!!
I served this with little hot rolls and it was great! I added a splash of sweet chilli sauce and used lime juice instead of lemon . This is a great new way for me to eat lentils so thanks .

I left this on low all day and had a great meal tonight. I had no ground beef so used ground pork instead, also added leftover diced zucchini. This is a great chunky soup - a total meal in a bowl. I served it with grated cheese piled on top - my favourite type of meal - comfort food. Made for Holiday Tag.

If there is such a thing as poetic licence with recipes then i took it tonight and FT I hope you don't mind !! I unthawed fruit only to find it was peaches and apple. I added some strawberries and my jumble crumble was done and sooooo delicious. This was the first time I had done a crumble without oats and we just loved it.
Great result, thanks Loula ! I used banana yoghurt and added a chopped banana - I will freeze half and the rest will be great in the school lunches. Very versatile and so easy to do !!
This is a wonderful salad and dressing, I used iceberg lettuce and  the only thing I had to leave out was the parsley as I had none. It was such a healthy dinner - made for Holiday Tag.
Just loved this -the crumble topping is addictive !! I used frozen cranberries and fresh apples - made a wonderful combo - made for Holiday Tag.

My DD and friends have just eaten this as an evening pre party 'special'. I made individual serves in a large muffin  tray. Very, very tasty ! No changes made to the recipe with a perfect result .This is definitely something to be enjoyed at any time of day, not just brekky !!

I had a terrific result with this recipe. I used a mix of pasta and brown rice as I ran out of bow ties. I also had to use bocconcini cheese as we do not get Velveeta in Australia - it worked well and was creamy and very tasty. Made for Holiday Tag.

These worked well for me. I sprinkled the tops with dukkah so they looked nice and served them with warm with dips and soup. They did not look as perfect as your photos, Loula. Mine were more rustic with the texture of damper.
Way more than 5 stars !!! I took oven option - nothing could be easier, all the ingredients are things I have on hand. I couldn't stop eating it and that was BEFORE dinner !!!

This is such a refreshing drink and versatile too. There are a lot of variations that would work well here. I halved the recipe and used a combination of lemon, orange and grapefruit and it is wonderful. I enjoyed it  before it was chilled and will try it tomorrow topped with soda water after gym.
This is very easy to do and made a very enjoyable midweek meal. I used ham instead of salami and also diced two tomatoes into it - very tasty indeed.

5 stars, even more !! I have made this to take to a Cup Day thing tomorrow and I cannot stop tasting it. I used leftover mashed sweet potato adding the cumin and coriander to it and used 1 great big green pepper as I had no red. Mine is mixed all together and will not be served in the layers but will still have the cheese on top and fresh coriander from the garden. I can't thank you enough Karen for this !!

This was great to whip up and great to eat. I used baby silverbeet leaves out if my garden instead of spinach but I really doubt if there is much of a difference. I used fresh herbs too . The instructions for preparing the bulgar worked perfectly. I served this as a side to Asian flavoured sausages to DD and friends before they headed off to a party.Made for Everyday is a Holiday.

This cake worked so well for me. I was terrified not to grease the tin but I had no problems there at all. My rhubarb cooked well and the resulting dessert is delish - will have more with cream tonight !!
This was FABULOUS !! My tortellini was veal, my herbs were fresh and my walnuts were mixed with a few cashews and the meal was so great - many thanks !

This worked out very well. I used my own frozen pumpkin as we cannot get it in a can here in Australia. I made this as one big cake and dropped in a handful of diced dates  instead of flax - I have not seen that here either . I will freeze half of the cake. This is a very impressive recipe due to the lack of fats .

This was fabulous . We don't have the butterscotch pudding here so  I chose to use chocolate which worked really well and gave great colour to the dessert. It was incredibly easy to do and I would like to try next time with pears and choc pudding. Made for Everyday is a Holiday.
Just delicious and addictive - I used butter and oil and loads of herbs straight from my garden but just one onion. It smelled great cooking and was really easy to do.

Although this was meant for dinner we sampled it for lunch and it was fabulous - I dropped in a handful of diced silverbeet as I have so much growing just now and I put in everything to use it up. My pasta was a wide variety - great for the sauce to cling too. So all round fabulous !! Made for Everyday is a Holiday.
This was gorgeous - I served it on top of a Ceasar salad instead of a poached egg - just delicious and the chives were homegrown, I might add !!!

This worked fabulously well. I used  bran flakes instead of cornflakes and used dates instead of cherries and my slice is moist and chewy and addictive. I doubled the recipe to fit a big slice pan and now better be careful that I don't eat the lot !! Made and loved for Sweet Traditions Tag game.

This made a lovely dessert . I had to cook mine lots longerand that is I think due to my choice of fruits. I used a mango and it was so juicy that it affected cooking time - but it tasted just great. I will try with berries next time. I love the fact that the variations are endless so Loula -thank you so much.
This was a lovely 'holiday' punch and so easy to do for our Xmas lunch. I halved the alchohol though !!

I am reviewing just the pie filling and it is so yummy. As per other reviews I made my paste using 1/2 cup cream not the water. It is an incredibly easy recipe and depending how you make it - not like me with cream - it is not too unhealthy. I dropped choc chips into it at the end and left out the butter but used lots of vanilla. You could use a liqueur instead for an adults only dessert.I loved this pie filling and I so love how easy it is to make - thanks Lori - made for Everday is a Holiday.

10 stars Karen !! This for me is, when served with cream, a to die for dessert !!! I made mine with berry , apple and plum. The ease of whipping it up is outstanding. I doubled the fruit and dobbed all the dough on top - just DELICIOUS.

For me and DD this was 10 stars . My white dip looks pink as I used sweet chili sauce instead of crushed pepper. I used 1/cup milk and 1/2 cup cream cheese as I did not want to wait for the soupiness to firm up and it was a HUGE success. Made for EveryDay is a Holiday.
Just delicious - perfect as a side to our pasta. I am sure it will be just as good tomorrow cold too. We loved this !!
Absolutely divine - 5 stars plus. I added a handful of grated chocolate instead of nuts. Made for Everyday is a Holiday.
Great for the lunch boxes and so quick to do !! Made for Everyday is a Holiday.
Gorgeous and easy ! I used tomatoes from the garden and some herbs. Served with gnocchi and cheese. Thanks for lovely dinner.
This made a generous amount with a nice crispy top and incredibly easy to do. Pretty addictive too once you cut it. Made for Every day is a Holiday.
I folded apple and peach  through the batter and made this in a loaf pan. I just loved the addition of cloves. We had it buttered and it will be great for the school lunches.
DD and DS gave this a high 5 !! I decreased the fluid and served this over pasta so it is a versatile recipe for sure. Easy and quick, so what's not to love.

Breezer - sorry but I had to use apricots - got to the store and not a cherry in sight !! So I snipped dried apricots through the batter and they went fabulously with the oats - this is a great slice, does not last long though, no one can keep away !! I did not do the choc drizzle. Made for Everyday is a Holiday .
Excellent and easy - I did the rosemary version plus other mixed herbs from the garden. made for Everyday is a Holiday.

Lovely sauce, Boomie. Perfect for me with the glut of tomatoes in the back yard. For that reason I had to add a zucchini too, hope you don't mind. Served sauce with macaroni noodles and it was a great meal, full of fresh flavour.

I, too, doubled the recipe and it was a huge success. I just loved it  and had it for brunch !! I used a combination of diced pear and apple which worked well. Very easy to make too. We don't have Bisquick here so used plain flour and baking powder. Made for Everyday is a Holiday.

Five stars - more if possible !!! My only addition was some diced mushrooms. This was fabulous soup and pretty straightforward  to make, what's more the children loved it.Made for Everyday is a Holiday.
I doubled this, left the skin on the apples and left out the butter. Swirled vanilla yoghurt through to serve and it was delicious. Made for Potluck Tag Game.
I am a slabber too - I cut all my slabs, left the room and the dog ate the cheese !!!!!! So I re cut the slabs and served DS up this fantastic recipe. He raved so thanks FT !!

Wonderful, rich, easy to do - what a fabulous recipe ! I added some thyme and a finely diced green pepper that needed to be used and served this as a side to beef chipolatas to teenagers. Made for Everyday is a Holiday.
Just too delicious for words - every ingredient that goes into that first small bowl I adore. I kept to the recipe and the result is glorious !!
Wonderful sauce  and easy to do ! I kept to the recipe only adding a handful of grated carrot . I served this with fettuccini, topped with basil. Thanks, Tis.

We had this last night and it was fabulous - I used a purchased base and made the topping with one sub . I used a handful of rocket instead of bell pepper. I loved the addition of the mozzarella balls - I had little ones and diced them - I haven't seen a big one here I don't recall. Will try making the base next time when I am not in a rush.

Fabulous - I made my own pastry and picked the spinach fresh from the garden - we all loved the result ! I fried a red onion as we don't have french fried onions here. It was an easy recipe and delicious. Made foe Everyday is a Holiday.

This was marvellous and so quick and simple. I used bacon instead of ham and eggs. Made enough for 2 good serves for DD and I and we ate it in front of Master Chef - perfect TV dinner !! Thanks Pat !!

Wonderful dinner, thanks Boomie ! I served this warm as it is close to winter here and not really salad weather. I did as another reviewer did and used sun dried tomatoes instead of bell pepper  and the spinach came out of my garden. Made for the Pool Party tag game.

Marvellous sauce - served with couscous. I added a handful of mixed herbs straight from the garden. I used a couple of spring onions instead of a plain one, so easy to do as well. Made foe Everyday is a Holiday tag.
Nothing can go wrong here so this is a wonderful standby using pantry staples. I was even luck enough to have a fresh lime in my fruit bowl!! Served on salad greens and delicious.

This is a rich and excellent dish. My sausage was pork and fennel and is wonderful in this dish. I had no broccoli so used 3 green peppers fresh from the garden as a sub but one that I don't think altered the dish at all.Made for ZWT 6.

This is moist and sticky and so easy to do . i made mine in a round pan and used 1 cup of diced dates as i had no raisins. the spices make it a lovely colour and it smelled so great cooking ! made for ZWT 6.
Totally delicious - this is an old favourite and easy to make. I also added some cooked diced bacon to the sauce - so yummy - made for ZWT 6.
Quick, faultless and delish ! I mixed my feta through and so skipped the grill bit. Discovered the olive jar empty so dropped in a weeny handful of bacon - such a great quick meal. Made for ZWT 6.

I adored this and served it warm with cream. I made it like a slice and served it in squares. The couscous sort of gives the same texture you find in tapioca pudding. It really was a fabulous dessert. I only used 3 eggs as that was all I had in the fridge. Made for the Couscous Challenge ZWT6.
Great dinner !! I used lemons straight of my tree and pre breaded chicken fillets and served it with couscous - all delicious and so easy !!!
What a great and quick Sunday nights dinner. 20 minutes was a perfect cooking time for me and I served the eggs on a bed of lettuce and avocado - just delicious ! Made for ZWT 6.
Divine - served with rice - just the right amount of everything ! I used mango jam as I had no apricot and skinless fillets .Dinner was ready in a flash with this lovely recipe made for ZWT 6.

I made my scone as one like a scone loaf or damper and then cut it in wedges. My glaze is very yellow as I was too heavy handed with the butter but of course tastes delicious. I used lemons from my tree. This really needs no butter or jam on it - I loved it, great to serve with tea. Made for Family Picks ZWT6.
I adore oats so this was perfect for me - I left out the sugar and threw in a handful of bran too. I mad a big batch so I have some to microwave tomorrow.

I made one big gratin and it is gorgeous. I diced my potatoes and left skin on. Also I doubled the amount of mustard and used skim milk.. I just had a sample before heading off to the gym and it is soooo tasty.
Sticky and delicious, gone in 24 hours !!
Great winter's meal - I subbed tomato passata for the half and half to make it healthier for me - just a personal preference, also I doubled the carrots. Made for Everyday is a Holiday.
Creamy and delicious - I swirled strawberry yoghurt through mine.
Very nice potato casserole - I served this with some Asian flavoured sausages and I served in a sort of scoop as I found it difficult to slice. Tasty indeed.

DS pronounced this one of my best efforts yet !!! I served it with softly whipped cream instead of the sauce. I pureed my own pumpkin and used diced white bread - truly delicious. I cooked mine on high for 3 hours and it was puffy and fabulous when done.
Totally delish and so quick to do. I used raw sugar as that was all I had and lemons from my tree. I can't wait to do this again !! Thank you Pat !
Yummy - crusty on top , gooey beneath. I used raw sugar in mine and doubled the recipe.Made for Everyday is a Holiday.

Wonderful result for me here ! Really it  makes several breakfasts in one hit so very convenient. I mixed diced cooked pear through it and it all baked up well together.So now for brekky I take my serve , heat in the m/wave and add yoghurt and breakfast is done - just perfect !
Just delightful  - I made double, in fact, as written. Thanks Boomie.
This was easy to and made a yummy dinner. I halved the recipe and added some parsley from the garden. It rose up puffy and golden. Made for Everyday is a Holiday.

This made me very happy after gym. i put apple and pear into mine and served with vanilla yoghurt. I left out the oil and drizzled the honey over the top. It makes a generous amount and I will be able to microwave another couple of serves - very enjoyable so thanks Connie.
Great and easy mid week meal, made a generous amount too. I folded macaroni through it and everyone was happy.

Anything this fresh is 5 stars - all the rocket in my salad came from my garden - I just adore that slight peppery smell and taste. I added a little tomato and broccoli and served the salad with chicken.
As was expected this was divine, pure comfort food !
Great bar and easy to do. I used peanuts in mine. Quite an addictive slice - be warned !!
Five full stars of yumminess. As I made this for a vegan I left out the real chocolate but the coffee/choc flavour was marvellous regardless.
Can I give 10 stars - I wish I could !! This made an enormous amount of addicitive and to die for brownies. I got a text from DD " brownies are magnifique" - that says it ALL !!!!
Fabulous and easy and versatile too. I added some mushrooms and  even the children raved !!!

I was not quite sure what to expect and I got a nice dish that could be also a dessert. I diced my apples tine and left the skin on. This was great served with vanilla yoghurt and would be good to try with different fruits like berries or plums!

This is a lovely quick mid week meal. I used black sliced olives and threw in some home grown rocket. I forgot the red pepper - it is still sitting diced up in the fridge - I am so cross with myself !!!
Quick and  easy with a perfect result - a foolproof recipe, Pat, so thanks !!

I made this fabulous recipe and suddenly had to feed extra guests so 5 plus stars for the versatility here of this recipe as I swirled sour cream through it and served it on noodles and rapidly it became a creamy pasta sauce - I hope that is OK Loula as my BF has TWO BIG serves !!

This made a generous and delicious dish. I used all the spinach which turns the dish a bit of an "urky" colour but urkiness aside it tasted fabulous. My spinach was fresh from the garden.I can see how this could be so versatile and you could sub lentils or even add the chicken to the simmer. You could wait til it really thickens and it could be a dip with hot bread. My leftovers will go on top of gnocchi.
I loved this recipe and had a perfect result. I made it in a large dish so no "gooey" problems arose. It vanished fast too !!

Fabulous sauce - tasty and easy ! You could almost make this in your sleep - in fact I nearly did as I am so jet lagged !!! I served this over hokkien noodles and stir fried broccoli and we had a simple and healthy and very enjoyable dinner.
Crumble is my fave dessert so I could not resist this one. I left my apples unpeeled and also added some diced apricots and the flour I used was "normal". Delicious result !

I made this as a bar cookie and it worked really well. My mixture was a bit too dry and crumbly so I had to increase the butter. Good to have a different way of using up those black bananas. Made for Everyday is a Holiday.
Lovely light summer meal - I subbed baby cos lettuce and doubled the avocado - really enjoyable.
So yummy and so easy to do. I used light ricotta and apricot filling. They look so pretty when they are done too.

I just did the chicken part of this recipe to put in a warm salad and it was marvellous. Picky DD ate the lot - 2 serves in fact !! I let the chicken 'sit' overnight and we enjoyed the great flavours.
Fabulous and fast to make - fast to eat too. I had no choc chips so added some cocoa with a terrific result.  Next time I need to double this recipe !!

This was a delightful microwave fruit frittata. I diced 3 small apples with peel on, used 2 eggs and threw in some sultanas, cinnamon and a tiny amount of sugar. The time given was spot on for my microwave. This little dish is perfect for any meal or any time of day. I had some for dessert and the rest will be brekky.
Nice sharp dressing, fabulous on my spinach and rocket. Made for ZWT 7.

I love the versatility of this recipe and today made this as a slice using sultanas and banana. Having recently moved house my muffin tray was unlocatable sadly. Anything with open ended options is 5 star to me.
Fabulous as expected. I used mostly oats and only a little coconut due to personal preference and a mix of raspberry and crabapple jelly. Addictively delicious !!! made for Everyday is a Holiday.

We loved having breakfast for dinner !! This is a marvellous and easy dish. I finely diced potatoes as hash browns are hard to find here. Along with the bacon I added some finely chopped camembert cheese for a more dinnertime flavour. We all had 2 serves !!

I made this at lunchtime, went back to work and found most of it MISSING when I got home. That means 5 stars !! DD and DS both had big serves prior to heading of to their jobs as swim coaches. I used bacon, added frozen peas and tomatoes. It was a fabulous success - luckily I doubled the recipe !!

I made these to take to my mum's and they are delish plus plus !! I just cut rounds of the dough log after it had been in the fridge and shaped them into little rounds. I also put in some chocky chips that melted through out the dough . They are pretty  yummy !!
Easy to do, delicious to eat. I omitted the frosting and my marmalade was mandarin ! A moist and gorgeous cake, no doubt about it.

Fabulous cake, truly fast to make too. My cocoa box only had dregs left so I had to make up the amount with some coffee powder so my cake was really a mocha express. I added a handful of choc chips due to lack of coca powder. All round success though, very yummy !!

Just a divine breakfast !! I used blueberries and tinned peaches and served brown sugar aside so one could choose how much or how little sweetness was needed. I trickled toasted muesli around the edges. Made for Everyday is a Holiday tag.
Absolute 5 star quiche ! I put the filling into a phyllo pastry case as I had phyllo in the fridge. My spinach was fresh and my cheese was cheddar. We all loved it so much.

We just do not get fresh cranberries here so I subbed blueberries and made this yummy dessert. I made one end with gluten free bread. As the blueberries are so sweet I had no need for the maple syrup.

I had to do these as Blueberry Passion Muffins and they were magnif !! I served them warm for breakfast and everyone was passionate about them, moist enough not to need butter. I used apple juice instead of blood orange juice. Will do the strawberry version next weekend !
Delicious cake and very easy to do. I did drizzle with icing which probably made it an unhealthier version but looked pretty !

I used this topping on a family pizza using loads of diced up fresh tomatoes. A friend over for dinner said he would have paid good money if he could have ordered it in a cafe - high praise indeed. Nothing can ever be made for one in this household - too many combine harvesters lurking !!!
Incredibly delicious and addictive !!! I omitted the nuts and used sultanas as I had no raisins. These were devoured when I took them to a family gathering.
Cold bacon, cold pan and no extra oil worked really well for me - bacon was delicious , no sticking whatsoever. I used a very old trusty non stick pot.

I used home grown silverbeet for this and also rice vermicelli instead of wheat pasta due to children with intolerances. It was a great success and very flavourful - I did not even have to add salt and pepper. Sliced ham went into it instead of bacon and also I scattered in a few mushies - all together a great dinner with some lunch leftovers.

Perfect and totally delicious - moist and not too sweet ! I doubled recipe and made a round cake. I used lemon yoghurt instead of sour cream and grated a tiny bit of lime rind into batter. Fabulous recipe  !!
This was fabulous and everyone raved. I used salami as I had no ham or bacon. This made a generous amount and 4 people ate well. DS took recipe printout home even !!
I used this recipe and made muffins today. I halved the quantities and it worked very well, cooked in 25 - 30 minutes. I really enjoyed the peanuts in this - took good ole banana bread up a notch !!

Great salad ! I stirred through a little bit of rocket and this made a lovely meal on a hot summer's night. DD especially loved the addition of mustard in the dressing. Made for Everyday is a Holiday tag.
Simple and easy meal - perfect for a hot night. Everyone loved it and it does not heat up the kitchen - or the chef  !!
I made this with raspberries and it was delicious. I did not do the sauce as the dessert is wicked enough on its own. I halved the sugar and we all ate far too much of it !
Great result - many thanks - love the toasted tip and also went with that !!
Great shake and perfect recipe for DD who has just had 4 wisdom teeth out !!

Great pudding either alone or with fruit. I put apple puree on the top of mine. So easy to do and recipe makes a decent amount too.Leftovers will make delicious breakfast. Sorry that the pic looks like mashed potato !!
Divine and delicious !! So easy to do as well. I can see this becoming a staple as it is so quick to whip up and I always have lemons from my trees waiting to be used !!

I halved this recipe and it worked out so well. I used a green pepper that I picked freshly from the garden. It was very warm from the sun !! People never tire of mashed potato in this house and everyone loved this dish with the extras thrown in.

Great meal !! I had not heard of chili beef soup before so used some stock and some passata as a sub. My tomatoes and green pepper came from the garden. A handful of Mexican blend cheese  on top made a fabulous meal enjoyed by all !!

Wow - this is just so delicious.I used whole chicken breasts and put everything straight into the baking dish. They were cooked to perfection in 30 minutes and the sauce is fabulous. We don't get buffalo wing sauce here and I have no idea what it tastes like to added some maple flavoured seed mustard to the sauce ingredients - I have had a pre dinner sample but will put this chicken along side a green salad for dinner tonight.

I made this as a slab cake and it worked really well.It was easy to do in the food processor too.  I reduced the sugar a little and we all loved it. It made a large, nice, moist cake and I frosted it with a cream cheese style frosting.

This could not have been easier. I used frozen blueberries and for once the batter was not too purple from their colour. It vanished so fast, I could not believe it . Both DD's just raved about this cake !!

Really delicious midweek meal and so fast to make. I used ground chicken as I had no beef and it was really great and I used low fat cottage cheese instead of yoghurt. I left the skin on the potatoes. Three of us ate it and we all loved it - healthy too .
I made a mistake and put the apples on top of the bread and not vice versa but it tasted great anyway . Very easy to do and it vanished fast.

This both looked and tasted great, also smelled wonderful. I subbed silverbeet for the broccoli. I picked it fresh from the garden along with the green pepper and basil so it was very much a "home grown" meal. I made 1/2 the recipe and we all enjoyed it for an early dinner.

No yuca to be seen in Melbourne but lots of sweet potato !! And these fries were fantastic, just delicious, just the best !!! I have seen these prepared in bags at the supermarket but never bought them as I prefer to cook from scratch. I made two batches tonight and we shared them between three, served with sweet chili mayo. Thank you for introducing me to a very addictive and very yummy snack.
Bestever ! The jam made these so moist but not wet. I used red currant jam but any berry jam would work wonderfully with the chocolate. Made for Everyday is a Holiday.
Good winter pudding and really easy to do. Mine was apple and peach and everyone enjoyed it.

It was certainly yummy but took about 50 mins to cook and much stirring. Without the stirring it would have "caught" on the bottom of the pot. Luckily DD was wanting to eat it so much that she was happy to do the stirring and it was worth it in the end !!
What a delicious breakfast, great way to start any day. I put mango on mine and used my own home constructed muesli. Made for ZWT 8.
Great little tapas dish, tasty and easy to do midweek. Very versatile as would go well with pasta or noodles. We just used a toothpick and had a couple each . Made for ZWT8.

Fantastic soup and most ingredients are pantry staples. I used a mix of brown and wild rice and my coriander was fresh from the garden. I did not quite have a whole cup of tomato so added a slurp of tomato paste. We all loved this and the leftovers can be stretched a bit further today by adding a bit more stock. Made for ZWT8.
Best ever !! I have just made these for the DD's x 2 for Sunday late breakfast and they ate the lot with lemon and sugar. They had a perfect fluffy consistency. Made for ZWT8.

I have just made this now - I used skim milk and had to use cornstarch combined with custard powder as I doubled the recipe and was really low on cornflour and we all like our custard thick in this family. I added some actual vanilla seeds so it has that pretty flecked look. Made and enjoyed with fruit salad for ZWT8.
I made this as one big baked pancake full of diced green apples and chopped banana. I too ended up with a custard like texture which  was delicious and not overly sweet. made for ZWT8.
Could only be 5 star - easy recipe and fantastic all day eating - not just for brekky !! I used Costco frozen blueberries as it is winter here. Made for ZWT8.

This is like dream come true comfort food !! I diced up my own potatoes into tiny pieces as we cannot get frozen hash browns here and my sausages were gluten free. Too yummy for words !! Made for ZWT8.
This is a quick and delicious little sauce that livened up our stir fried vegies tonight. I used Kikkoman soy as I have never heard of Braggs. made for ZWT 8.
Classic and delicious dessert - I used plums - a mix of red ones and yellow fleshed ones, frozen from the summer. Made for ZWT8.
This is just fabulous !!! Unbelievably easy to do and so marvellous and enjoyable to eat - best ever - 10 stars !!
I served the "room temperature" version topped with organic black currant jam and it was truly delicious .

I hope it did not matter that I did not let it sit overnight but just gave it a couple of hours over lunchtime !! We loved it and the texture of the cake was soft and velvety. We ate it warm with custard.

Great flavoursome soup, nice and healthy too ! I used 2 trimmed pork steaks instead of sirloin and diced all my vegies up pretty small. I did leave out the tomatoes as I had none in the house but the soup worked out well and we all enjoyed it greatly. The recipe makes a big batch so we also have lunch for tomorrow now which is a great help.

I made this in a slice pan and cut it into squares. It was delicious and incredibly easy to make. I used real eggs and the spinach was out of my vegie garden. We all so enjoyed this and I am sure the leftovers will be great cold tomorrow for lunch.

I used small non red potatoes for this and it was a delicious and easy recipe. The potato slices were crispy and cooked quickly. People were eating them from the baking tray - always a sign of a winner !!
This was a fabulous and so easy to do. I added additional vegies which included a green pepper, some tiny sliced potatoes, a big handful of curly kale and tom thumb tomatoes . Loved it all !!

We loved the cake even though I did not make the pineapple butter. It was great both plain and with ordinary butter. I made it with coconut cream and it was wonderful and moist and I will certainly make this again. I cut back on the desiccated coconut  - just a personal preference. Made for Everyday is a Holiday.

What a delicious sprinkle and a delight to have on hand for baking purposes. It has made the kitchen smell great just putting all the ingredients together. I look forward to putting it on my porridge !!
I used lots of leftover vegies in this plus an extra potato and it worked out well - great mid week meal, very filling and enjoyable. Loved the cheese on top too.

I have not cooked a lot of red meat in my slow cooker so this was a great learning curve for me. I  thought it came together well after cooking on low for 7 hours. I enjoyed eating the vegies but also quite liked the meat even though I do not often eat red meat. It was not falling apart and this was what I was aiming for but this might be to do with error on my part.
Fabulous cake, easy to do, cuts beautifully. I halved the sugar in the cake and in the syrup. My cake isn't floating so it all worked out perfectly.
Refreshing and lovely. I passed on the almonds but added extra honey. Great lunch today.

This is absolutely ingenious! I had to cook my egg for a little over 1 minute but it turned out light and fluffy, just like the real thing.  I let the hot toasted muffin melt the cheese instead of cooking it with the egg and ham, but otherwise didn't stray from the recipe.  Thanks for a great idea!

This was a really simple but tasty appetizer/side dish.  I used a nice Stilton and the flavors all complimented each other very well.  I served these with Recipe #359556 (the sauce was fantastic on the mushrooms!) but would advise against using white "stuffing" mushrooms - they gave off a lot of liquid when cooking and just didn't hold much filling.  Next time I'll try portobellos.  For those who aren't sure, Gas Mark 6 is equal to 400F.  Thanks for posting!

Wow these are good!  Of course, everything from ATK is usually good.  These bars turn out wonderfully chewy with a moderate peanut-buttery taste.  They freeze well too - I cut them into squares and froze them two at a time in the little snack size ziplocs.  Every morning I would pop a bag out of the freezer and take it to work for breakfast.  What a treat!  Thanks for sharing this great recipe!

Wow, this was really good!  I wasn't sure if it would have enough flavor and was afraid it might be a little dry because there's no oil, but it was loaded with flavor and wasn't dry at all.  I used a sweeter, less salty soy sauce (Aloha Brand - my favorite) and used mirin rather than sugar.  I also halved the lime juice, but only because I don't like things too acidic.  Cold leftovers were just as good the next day.  This is such a tasty, healthy dish!  Thanks for posting!

WOW is this GOOD!!!  The nutella flavor really comes through (and as an added bonus it flavors the milk just like those commercial kiddie cereals! LOL)  I highly recommend using sesame seeds for a great toasted flavor.  This stuff is so addicting I can't stop eating it...  Thanks for posting!!

I love dal.  This has a nice warmth and subtle flavours.  The coriander (cilantro) really brings it alive.  I had it for lunch the next day, with rice, and the flavours were improved (IMO).  I'd like to make this with chana dal next time as my chickpeas  didn't break down as much as I'd prefer.  Thanks for the recipe. Made for Aussie Forum Swap #18.

The spice paste blend is what attracted me to this recipe and it didn't disappoint.  (I'm using the left over paste to marinate a lamb fillet.)   Chickpeas are also a favourite so this  salad was always going to appeal. It was so quick to make and I loved it.  The recipe didn't specify how to prepare the zucchinis so I made long ribbons. I too served it warmish (I was impatient) as a side to some grilled lamb loin chops.  I've got left overs today for lunch.  My only thing is that I would say that it serves 2 as a main or 4 as a side.  Made for Aussie: Make My Recipe, Ed #5.

A great meal.  I used the crock pot method and served with noodles & sour cream. It is richly flavoured and easy to prepare.  I, however, wouldn't say that it was distinctly German in flavour.  I will make it again but I will be increasing the caraway seeds (and bruising them) as I found the flavour of 1 teaspoon of these got totally lost in the dish.  Made for Aussie Recipe Swap #19.

This is the best pasta dish I have ever cooked! I made it for my weekly Pasta Wednesday dinner night with friends and they all thought I had bought dinner this week because it was that good! The pumpkin taste isn't too strong so if you want it more pumpkiny I would add a little more. I had some pumpkin haters at dinner and they were very surprised when I told them what was in the sauce. 

I scaled the recipe up to serve 10 but I don't think that caused any problems with the ingredient amounts. Only 7 people ended up eating and there was just enough with none left for seconds. I would recommend increasing the recipe a little depending on how many people you plan to serve...especially because it is so good and everyone will want second helpings. 

I did make a few adjustments, I added about twice as much pepper and I also allowed my sauce to simmer for about 12 minutes after adding the cream and cheese mixture. I think this brought out the flavors in the sauce a little more. 

Thanks so much for a recipe I will surely be making again!

I made and enjoyed this recipe for lunch today. I did not de-seed the cucumbers as I really enjoy the seeds. The taste of the salad was good, but there was too much of the yogurt dressing for the amount of vegetables I had. I even used a large cucumber and 3 medium tomatoes. Next time I think I would half the amount of dressing. The fresh cilantro and parsley added a great flavor though. Made for Potluck tag.

I made these for a dinner party with ribs. They tasted pretty good but mine took almost double the cooking time and weren't ready in time. I did enjoy the taste of both the potatoes together and will try that again. Thank you!

Delicious! I made this for a family dinner as an appetizer and had planned to take a picture but it was gone before I could get even one piece for a shot! I followed French Tart's suggestions and used phylo dough (her pictures looked so yummy I knew I had to try it like that) and added the red onions, which I would highly recommend. Also I wish I had made more of the seasoning mixture because I felt it could have added some more oomph. Made for PRMR Tag.
Delicious! I loved all of the veggies in this. Thanks for a great summer recipe!

Yumm! We loved this. I did use only one leek because they were really expensive at my grocery store and it still was delicious. Next time I will wait until the leeks go on sale and use all three. Thank you for the recipe. Made for PRMR tag.
Loved this. Green beans are my favorite so I am always looking for different ways to prepare them. This was quick easy and delicious. I chilled mine a little before serving. Made for Potluck tag.
Very good soup, it was quite spicy though so next time I would cut the  red pepper in half. Also I would add in some garlic as other chefs have recommended.
Delicious sandwich! We really loved this and will make it again. We used cheddar cheese but thought it may also be good with swiss. Thank you for the recipe! Made for Holiday Tag.
Easy and perfect for 2. I used Almond extract and used 4 muffin tins as my pan. Great treat without the leftover guilt. Made for PRMR.
Great recipe! I marinated for 24 hours and it was so juicy and flavorful. I served this with Recipe #264767, #264767 as a steak salad. Fantastic! Made for PRMR tag.

Great biscuits. Dense and flavorful. The pepper was a bit strong for my taste and I did feel they were much better with butter or cream cheese than alone. Mine browned beautifully on the middle rack in the time stated. I used canola oil but another kind may add a different flavor dimension. Also, I filled by muffin tins (greased, no paper) to the top and didn't have any overflow just a slight rise and they came out without sticking at all. Made for Potluck tag.
Good sammie! Next time I think I would leave the apples off though and serve them on the side. Made for Holiday tag.

I'm sorry Alli but this just wasn't as good as we hoped. I used lump crabmeat from Whole Foods and the quality was pretty good, but it just needed something else to us. I did add some Panko bread crumbs on the top and served with lemon wedges. I think next time I would add some garlic and onions to the crab mix and a little more hot sauce. Also I would do a butter cracker topping and some parmesan cheese on top. Thank you very much for giving us something new to try!

This was delicious! I took the suggestion and used Pasta Sauce #1 which is delicious and just perfect for this recipe. I put sweet onions and bacon on mine for toppings and used fresh shredded mozzarella, not the stuff out of the bag that tastes like paper. This made for a seriously good Pizzadilla. I made one and it was plenty for my BF and I to share. I will definitely be making this again. Thanks!

Yummy goodness here! It made a perfect loaf that was so moist and had perfect texture on the inside and had a thicker exterior crust to hold it all together. I did have to cook mine about 55 minutes in order for it to be fully done. Made for Holiday tag. Thank you!

This was pretty good. It was a lot more shrimp sauce than catfish though and that kind of drowned the taste a little. We liked the shrimp sauce, it was just a little more than I expected. Also, I was hoping there would be a stronger cajun flavor. I did add some extra cajun seasoning on top before putting it in the oven but we thought it could have used even more. Thank you for giving us something new to try!
This is so delicious. I will make again and again. I did add approx. 1/2 tbsp. more balsamic to make it a bit more like a dressing. It was really good. Thank you! Made for Holiday Tag.

I really loved this. Although I do have to say I made a lot of changes out of necessity. I didn't have a whole chicken only chicken tenderloin pieces that were obviously already skinned and deboned. Also, I had to run out while it was cooking so I couldn't do the basting. So to compensate I took my tenderloins and dipped them in the mixture before putting them in a baking dish. I baked for 30 mins and then poured the rest of the sauce over the top and allowed it to cook for another 15 minutes. I really loved the smell and the flavor. My BF who isn't a big sweet fan said that it wasn't his favorite, but that is just his tastes. I would love to try this again as you have it written. Thanks Annacia!

Yumm so good! This soup had a ton of flavor. I used chicken strips and baked them with a little butter and season-all salt i the oven and then shredded. I also added an additional can of chicken broth and a splash more milk because we wanted it to  last longer and we had a high broth to filling ratio ;) Thanks SarahBeth! Made for Potluck Tag.
We really enjoyed this recipe and will definitely be making it again. My fish was a little freezer burnt and you couldn't even tell! Thank you!
Sorry this just wasn't for me. I think it is the buttermilk, maybe with regular or cream next time. Thank you though!

So yummy. I am not a rice fan (I'd rather keep the calories for something else ;) ) but this was really really good! I did use an entire 14.5 oz can chicken broth and then used only 1/2 cup of the water. I served this with Recipe #10422 #10422. Thank you.

This was soooo good! It doesn't take too long, I started as soon as I got home from work and it was ready by dinner at 8:30. I used canned chopped black olives that had been drained and they were perfect. I also mixed this up in my KitchenAid making it extra easy. We just had this with pasta but next time I would make some sort of tapanade or sun-dried tomato spread to put on it. I will definitely be making this again. Thank you! Made for PRMR tag.

This was very good. I halved the recipe and it was the perfect amount for two. I did saute all of the veggies in the pan first but I can't say that I noticed any difference in taste than when I just roast them. Thank you.

We thought these were great! This was my first try at crab cakes and they came out very well. As Lori Mama said mine too needed some more breadcrumbs to hold together. I did halve the recipe to make for two. Served with deviled eggs as a starter and coleslaw as a side dish. I was planning on poached pears for dessert but we got too full! Thanks again. Made for Potluck Tag.

This was my first attempt at deviled eggs. I love deviled eggs, but I can't say that these were as good as others I have had. I halved the recipe and I thought that they were way too mustard-y and my BF thought that they were way too mayonnaise-y. Either way there wasn't quite enough egg yolk for the mixture. I would use jumbo eggs next time. Thanks for giving me a great recipe to try for my first deviled eggs! Made for Holiday Tag.
This was quite good. We liked the dressing but thought maybe there was something missing, I think next time I might do half mayo and half sour cream. Thank you for the recipe.

YUM! I hope you don't mind me rating this as I did make one major change. I used homemade caramel sauce rather than melting down caramels and adding cream. I then rolled them in chopped cashews mixed with the salt to give the salted flavor. SO GOOD! Next time I would probably just make them this way again because I usually have the caramel on hand but I would add the salt to the caramel itself so it blends in better rather than two the nuts. Great easy dessert. Thank you!

We very much enjoyed this. The onion and the apple definitely are a great complement to the pork. Next time I would season the pork with pepper and garlic salt. I would also add some sherry when the pork is on the stove top because I think it adds great flavor to sauteed pork. The fresh sage really took this over the edge. Made for PRMR. Thank you!

The taste of these was pretty good, but they just didn't really work out for me. I made a half recipe and the chocolate was so thick I only really had enough to coat 5 cookies.
