Told DS to bake it at 350 degrees for 40 minutes (was gone walking with my grandbaby) but now think it should have baked at a higher temperature so it would have browned more like in mersaydees' picture.  Maybe 375 for 40 minutes?  I did use all the oil and should NOT have but just forgot to reduce it. Thanks Wish I Could Cook for sharing. Made for Theirs, Yours, & Mine tag.

Wonderful tasting bread! Mine did fall and think perhaps I put the oil in at the wrong time. I did add my cheese later, but apparently not at the right time as you cannot see it but you can certainly taste it. Thanks SarahBeth for sharing. Made for Everyday.

Calling all chocolate lovers!  Here is a wonderful and easy dessert for just two!    My better half is already asking when am I going to make this again.  LOL!   I have a huge mug- holds 12 ounces-I just measured it-and this recipe fits that size.  I made as posted.    And the clean up  is easy too!

The aroma alone is TDF!  Delicious and easy too.  Love finding ways to use my leftovers-in this case turkey and kielbasa.    I used half the bread crumb mixture. Subbed in black eye peas for the white beans-1 can. Tonight, I also made a salad and Recipe#361967.  Thanks wicked cook 46 for sharing another great recipe. Made for Everyday is a Holiday.

Delicious!  I used 2 cups of chopped onion, 6 cups of chunky cabbage, 1 tablespoon hot sauce, and 1/2 teaspoon of black pepper.   I served over brown rice with Recipe#200595 and Recipe#43990.    Thanks Boomie for sharing.  Made for Theirs, Yours, & Mine game.
Very good and healthy salad!  I used iceberg and omitted the cuke-you gotta make your DH happy you know.   Made for Theirs, Yours, & Mine game.  Thank you Starrynews for sharing.

Love the texture, appearance, the ease factor, and handy ingredients-yes, even the quinoa. I had toasted mine as suggested. Next time I will reduce the curry powder by a third. I had frozen peas so put them in the last 2 minutes of simmering. Thank you for sharing Debbwl. Made for Everyday Is a Holiday.
Pretty please try these!  A refreshing delicious combination of flavors plus easy and attractive.  Thank you Debbwl for sharing a winner.
Very good!  Love its versatility! Easy peasy to make.  Used leftover turkey so this gave it a new "look".  Thanks CoffeeB for a keeper.

Perfectly delicious! You and your DDs have come up with another winner!  Love the flaxseed addition. I put in 12 ounces of strawberry yogurt or two small ones.  Thanks Deantini for posting. Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders.

Delish!  I bought a one pound container of ground pork and used the entire package with the same ingredients listed here and forgot to put in the bell pepper.  Froze the rest of chipotle peppers in individual dixie cups lined with plastic wrap-hate wasting them and usually you only use one or two.  Thank you Boomie for another great recipe!  Made for PRMR Holiday game.

Loved the crustiness, taste, and technique! Definitely delicious! Moist tender, easy prep. Caramelized nicely. And appreciate that I always have these ingredients on hand. Thank you for sharing.
Perfect medley of favorite ingredients! A definite repeater.

Fish was moist, topping was tasty but did not brown up as much as we prefer. Think it needs more olive oil/ butter in topping maybe doubled. I did not have olive oil spray so perhaps that would solve browning problem. Love the onion with lemon wine sauce-unique and delicious. We think this is much better than an Arizona fish fry. Wish ingredients were listed in same order as directions. Thank you for sharing.
Awesome! Love technique and showcases asparagus! Thank you for sharing.
Very tasty! Simple, not spicy, attractive. Omitted the olive oil for first step. Otherwise made as posted. Thank you for sharing.
Excellent! Easy. Although garlic bits did burn. Appreciate prep being done earlier. Served with grilled chicken, roasted carrots, salad and tiramisu. Thank you for posting.
Enjoyed this! Made as posted. We like lemon in savory dishes so all enjoyed and you can definitely taste the lemon.   Appreciate that I always have these ingredients on hand.  Thank you for sharing.
Always have roasted my squash shell side down but this works better and faster --less dry. Thanks for post.

We loved this! Our kind of food. Love packet cooking.  Assembled earlier in day. Served with grilled Italian sausage and roasted butternut squash and for dessert chocolate lava cakes. Did reduce sesame oil but otherwise made as posted. Thank you for post.
Great spin on baked potato! Big hit with dh! Made cheesy cauliflower casserole so baked along with that. Appreciate the simplicity. Thank you for a repeater.

Made as posted and it is easy to make. Did refrigerate dough overnight. Love the technique and need a convenient bread but found it too salty. I did mix flour and salt thoroughly before adding. I subbed in 1 1/2 cups whole wheat  but doubt that that would affect saltiness. We like bread for sandwiches. Think this would better with soup. Thank you for posting.

What a treat! Love sweet potatoes seasoned this way. Used black beans instead of kidney. And for some odd reason grocery did not have a red chile pepper so used jalapeño and that was too mild in heat. Would not change a thing. Roasted the sweet potatoes, made salsa, and guacamole earlier in day then assembled. For the two of us, this made three lunches.  Made for my Spring PAC 2014 baby.

This cake was beautifully light and fluffy. I agree with Kat's Mom about cutting the cold butter into the streusel topping rather than softening it and then mixing it in. Other than that, I was very pleased so thank you for a keeper! Made for PAC Spring 2009.
This is a divine chocolate sauce, really smooth and chocolatey! Next time I want to try it with white chocolate! Made for Went to the Market tag game.

This recipe has a lot of potential. The yogurt has quite a neutral flavour so to make it more flavourful I would increase the garlic. I would also add bell peppers to give the dish some colour. I'll definately be making this again with a few variations on ingredients. Thanks for a lovely recipe! Made for Went to the Market tag game.

These are different from store-bought refrigerator squares that I have had but these are very good! We didn't have rum so used bourbon which worked beautifully. My only change would be to increase the syrup or add a little sugar, although I imagine using really good quality dark chocolate would produce a less bitter taste. Thanks for a lovely recipe! Made for Please Review My Recipe game.
We loved this pasta! It was easy to make and tasted really good. Next time I'll experiment with adding various fresh herbs to the sauce. A really great recipe- thanks! Made for Newest Zaar tag.

This soup was easy to prepare and delicious! We really enjoyed it and will definitely be making it again. I added a little garlic powder and following on from other reviews, doubled the creamed corn but kept the regular corn as is. Thanks for a keeper! Made for Please Review My Recipe tag game.

We loved this coffee. The white chocolate is not overly sweet. I would have liked to try it with the liqueur but it's unfortunately not available here- I can imagine that making it to die for! Thanks for a lovely treat! Made for Went to the Market tag game.

If you're looking for healthy and refreshing, this is it! I had never frozen a banana before and a potato masher would only go through partially frozen bananas, but if you catch them just before they are done freezing, it's ideal. I think next time I'll try adding chocolate sauce swirls, just to negate the fact that it's healthy! Made for Zaar's Newest Tag.
Thank you for a lovely after-work treat. I added a little demerara sugar and it was perfect! Next time, I'm trying this with white chocolate! Made for 123 Hit Wonders.
Absolutely delicious! This was a gorgeous snack which I served with toast. Definately going to be making this again. Thanks Nasseh for a super recipe!

For a low fat dish, these were excellent- hardly tasted low fat! We really enjoyed them with chicken. It's definitely worth boiling the potatoes in the broth- it produces a lovely flavour. Thanks very much for a keeper! Made for Please Review My Recipe.

WOW! I absolutely loved this- the flavour was just what I expected. I also used low fat cheese and it worked beautifully. Definitely one to make again, and again, and again. Thanks for a keeper kitty! Made for 123 Hit Wonders.

An absolute 5 star recipe. I used low fat cottage cheese, carrot, cucumber, cherry tomatoes and red bell pepper. The cherry tomatoes gave a lovely sweet flavour. I will be making this a lot over the summer- this would be particularly great with a barbecue or quiche. I didn't find it too liquidy at all. Thanks for a definite keeper!
I used this to make Recipe#373571 and the flavours worked really well together. I cut back the mustard a little to adjust to our tastes. A really lovely vinaigrette- thanks for posting!

We really enjoyed this rice salad- the flavours blended beautifully. I left out the tabasco and celery but other than that, made as written. The rice ended up being about 7/8 of a cup raw, so I used 1 3/4 cups of water. I used Recipe#373598 which worked really nicely. Thanks for a lovely side dish!

This tasted really good and was very much enjoyed. My banana may have been a little too ripe- it was just turning brown and the shake seemed just a little too sweet. I'm sure this was the fault of my ingredients though, not the recipe! Thanks for a lovely treat!

A really good soup with a lovely blend of flavours. The coriander is the perfect herb for this dish. Next time though I would sub out one of the sweet potatoes and change it for a regular potato- although I love sweet potatoes, I found this just a little on the sweet side. Just personal taste! Thanks for a lovely recipe that we'll definitely be making again!

This fab little recipe surprised me. I must admit I didn't expect it to taste good, but it did! I used peach green tea and vanilla ice cream. I think this would be absolutely divine with plain iced tea and peach or raspberry sorbet. I'm very glad to have broadened my horizons from my usual iced coffee! Thanks for a winner!

So easy and so delicious! I had never heard of this simple combination but it works so well! I liked this with Ruffles style chips but I imagine it would work really well with stronger flavoured chips also. Thanks for a super snack!

We loved this salad. I couldn't add avocado as the ones I bought hadn't ripened yet, but I certainly will add them next time! The dressing had the perfect proportion of lemon and oil so it was flavourful but not heavy or oily. I also loved the addition of the cheese- I've never added cheese to a salad like this before! Thanks for a definite keeper!

This is easily worth 5 stars. The flavours are full but not heavy- the tomato and basil blends beautifully with the vinaigrette. Already planning to make it again! I did make one change- I left out the red onion as I find the flavour too strong. Thanks for a recipe I'll make over and over!

A very soothing drink. I used manuka honey, hoping to cure a sore throat at the same time! I also found that when I woke up during the night, it seemed easier to fall back asleep. Thanks for a lovely treat!

We really enjoyed this. The fresh herb flavours really stood out. My bf found the garlic a bit strong but I thought it was perfect. I'll never buy store-bought garlic bread again! Thanks for a great recipe!

Wow! What an awesome recipe! I had the same problem as Acadia though- I hand mixed the ingredients and couldn't wait long enough for it to get thoroughly frozen again! An amazingly easy, yet delicious treat! Thanks breezermom!

Comfort food for sure! As other reviewers have, I added a little olive oil to moisten the pasta. I also added cherry tomatoes and heated gently until the cherry tomatoes popped slightly and the juices poured out. Beautiful flavour! Thanks for a lovely recipe!

I have been craving mushrooms and this hit the spot! I'm afraid I'm a bit of a garlic addict, so I crushed the garlic and obviously left it in! A really easy comfort food dish that I'll definitely repeat! Thanks!

This little gem was a total surprise! I didn't expect such a wonderful flavour from such a simple dish! The only thing I added was a chicken stock cube, which I think really boosted the creamy flavour. Thanks for a super recipe that I will certainly be making again.

Wow, what a wonderful indulgent treat! I have always believed that Irish Coffee had to include Baileys, so it was enlightening to try this authentic version. Thanks French Tart for this super treat, and for all your work with the Everyday is a Holiday tag game.

This is so refreshing! The flavours work together very nicely and this really brightens up a hot day. I also agree with Kim127 that the colour is stunning. Thank you so much for a lovely new way to use watermelon!

A really lovely iced coffee drink! I loved the scoop of ice cream on top- perhaps next time I will blend it in to mix the flavours together. This would be lovely with chocolate or white chocolate ice cream as well! Thanks for a super summer treat!

Really enjoyed this type of drink during my summer in KY so thank you so much for the trip down memory lane! This is a very refreshing summer treat. I really liked the addition of the carbonated lemonade- gave it a little something extra!

I had never tried the sour cream/ brown sugar combination before and I have been seriously missing out! The flavour combination was absolutely wonderful. This would be sublime over fresh peaches. Certainly one I'll be making again and again! Thanks!

Superb sausage gravy recipe! Made this for breakfast today and we really enjoyed it. I used Lincolnshire sausage which worked very well as pepper was already in the sausage. It took slightly longer than I expected to thicken- about 10 minutes, so be patient! It's well worth the wait!
An excellent blend of flavours- the brown sugar and vanilla made it extra special. I also used instant coffee and it worked very well. Thanks Boomette for a fantastic warming treat!

Really enjoyed the tartness in these tomatoes from the red wine vinegar. I used fresh basil- I would recommend always using fresh herbs with this dish, rather than dried. This is a recipe I'll certainly be using again! Thanks!

We really enjoyed this fruity summery drink. I have never tried adding club soda to a fruity iced tea and it worked beautifully. The only change I made was to add a little more juice after tasting to increase the fruity flavour a little. Thanks for a winner!

Loved the garlicky flavour of this sauce. I used 2 cloves and didn't find it too strong at all. For 3 servings, I used 2 cups of dry pasta and the rest of the ingredients as listed and I'm glad I made the extra sauce as some was soaked up into the pasta. I used milk rather than cream to cut the calories and it thickened up just fine. Thank you for a super make-again recipe!

This was a wonderful treat after a long day. I really liked the milkiness of this drink. The coffee and cocoa flavours were nicely blended with the liqueur and the whole thing had a creaminess that was very satisfying. Thanks for a super recipe!

What an excellent recipe! I really enjoyed the blend of flavours- so much healthier than garlic bread but just as tasty! I also brushed on the olive oil to spare the calories. Thanks for a definite keeper of a recipe!

Simple yet so effective! I love these flavours put together so this dish is a winner for me. I put the butter on straight after straining the potatoes so it melted in nicely, then added the sour cream. I experimented by using Cavenders Greek seasoning in place of the herbs which worked really well. Thanks for a lovely recipe!

Absolutely loved this recipe. Grilling/ roasting the vegetables gives a lovely smoky flavour. I used chicken stock to cook the couscous, rather than water, as I love the combination of that with lemon. A brilliant couscous recipe- thanks!

Made this for my bf to enjoy with a bean and cheese burrito and he was very pleased with the extra flavour dimension that this added. I used fresh chillies as that is what I happened to have, so continued to cook the dish for a few minutes after adding them so they wouldn't be raw. A lovely addition to our regular Mexican family favourites! Thanks Noo!
This is much better than my usual way of making iced tea. Thanks for a new keeper! I used Splenda instead of sugar which worked just fine.

Really enjoyed this recipe, both for its simplicity and good taste. We added some diced chicken breast and this was a very satisfying weeknight meal. Thanks PAC mom for this super recipe as well as for adopting me!

Excellent recipe- we absolutely loved these and I'm already planning to make them again next week! I made it as written but left out the pepper as I'm not too keen on it and we used a dark brown sugar which gave a gorgeous caramelised flavour. Thanks so much for a new favourite!
In response to another review- I would really recommend cooking in a single layer as in step 5. That said, I was too bowled over by the delicious flavour to notice any sogginess!

This was very easy to throw together and made rice much more interesting. Next time I would add garlic somehow- roasted garlic would be wonderful and make this a more than 5 star recipe! Thanks Boomette!
Loved the range of flavours here, especially the garlic! Thanks for a flavourful but easy side!

Wish I could give this more than 5 stars. I did add 2 cloves of crushed garlic with the onions. It needed a while to thicken up but once it did the result was oh so good! Definitely making this repeatedly through the winter- thanks Noo!
So simple and yet so good! I used vine tomatoes and fresh basil. A really wonderful recipe that I'll certainly remember when summer comes around again!

Brilliant flavours in this lovely salad! I often make a similar dish but have never added the balsamic vinegar and boy was it good! I was recently lucky enough to visit Italy and this brought back great memories so thanks!

Loved loved loved this soup! BF hates mushrooms so I added 2 chopped carrots instead and it had a lovely flavour and colour. It's very thick so can be thinned to your taste by adding milk or broth, or left as is. I used light cream cheese with herbs and loved the subtle herby flavour. Thanks gailanng for a lovely new soup!

This has so much more flavour than my usual cinnamon sugar which has been just that- cinnamon and sugar. I love the addition of the nutmeg especially. This will brighten up my porridge so much this winter- thanks!

Loved this recipe! I always enjoy broccoli with cheese sauce more than plain broccoli but this took the guilt right out of it! I did throw some parmesan into the sauce right at the end to boost the cheese flavour- think the cheddar I got was very mild. Thanks for a lovely recipe!

Certainly enjoyed this different way of doing potatoes. Mine were large potatoes so needed an hour to cook even though I halved them lengthwise. May I suggest brushing with butter immediately before sprinkling with the parmesan and breadcrumbs to help them stick- a lot of mine slipped off and ended up in the pan. Really liked the flavour of these though- BF especially enjoyed them with cheese sauce on top! Thanks LM!

Very easy and really added some crunch to the dish. I used this with Recipe#394230. It's worth adding these late in the cooking stage as it looked like they could get overdone more quickly then regular breadcrumbs- having already been cooked! Will definitely use this recipe again!

What a brilliant little appetizer! Couldn't find neufchatel cheese so used herb and garlic cream cheese. This is definitely a repeat recipe, and so versatile. You could take this along when visiting friends and warm it through when you arrive. Next time I'll sprinkle pine nuts over the top! Thanks SarahBeth.

This is my newest diet saver! I used raspberry sugar free jello and 1% milk. I especially loved the thickness from the jello without the calories of a syrup- it was substantial enough to tide me over until a late dinner. Next time I'll try adding a little frozen yoghurt! Thanks for a keeper!
What a way to jazz up leftovers! I really liked the alfalfa sprouts (I believe it's the same as what we call cress) as they gave a nice texture alongside the creamy cheese. Thanks breezermom!
Lovely flavour from this sauce. I also reduced the sugar as I'm watching calories and simmered it for 30 minutes. Thanks for a great spaghetti sauce!
5 stars for the new technique! I used the blender method- much neater than scraping the crumbs from stale bread. Thanks for posting Deb!
Fantastic! I used frozen berries and low fat vanilla yogurt. This will be a great diet saver! Thanks for posting!
I also used my regular ratio of coffee to water and the flavours came out beautifully. Thanks for a lovely winter treat!
My instant cinnamon hazelnut coffee is my favourite and this was a great new way to have it. I'll be adding cocoa to it more often! Thanks!
This is the healthiest way to cook bacon so it's my method of choice. I used foil to make the clean up easier. Thanks for reminding me how much I like bacon!
Simple but great! I served this with sugar free syrup. Thanks for a great breakfast!

Simple, quick and easy. I cooked mine on high for the first few minutes to reduce the water. Personally though, I prefer zucchini with a hint of garlic or Cavenders greek seasoning. Thanks for posting!
I couldn't find fudge ripple ice cream this side of the pond so used vanilla. This was still excellent and a real treat. I'll have to try it with my almond coke next!
Loved the flavours of the olive oil and balsamic vinegar paired with the herbs and seasonings. Grilled indoors this time but can't wait to make it properly in the summer!
Great winter treat! I used Splenda rather than sugar and light whipped cream. Super indulgent recipe!

This was my first attempt at gnocchi and I'll definitely try it again! I used 1 (15oz) can of pumpkin puree and unlike Wish I Could Cook, I didn't saute it first to dry it out (I will next time), so my dough needed 2 1/2 cups of flour. My dough was still a bit sticky so I pulled it out of the bowl and put it on the countertop in rope-shaped batches, sprinkling the countertop and dough with flour, then it was relatively easy to make a sausage shape. Thanks Loula for introducing me to the world of making gnocchi!

Wonderful flavour in this recipe! I used Splenda and sugar-free syrup and it made a wonderful accompaniment to pancakes, and only 1/2 Weight Watchers point per apple! I'm planning to make a larger batch for take-to-work lunches next week! Thanks Andi!
Loved this twist on oatmeal! I used low fat butter spread and no salt. Thanks for a lovely breakfast treat!
This is just my kind of meal! Loved the flavours and the fresh basil gave a lovely fresh taste. Definitely one to make over and over again!

Absolutely love this sandwich! You can't beat the combination of egg and tomato in my opinion. Personally though, I prefer to mash up the egg and mix it with the mayonnaise, but it's a great flavour combination this way too. Thanks Starry!

5 stars for its simplicity and how quick it is to make. I added some spring (green) onions to give it that bit of extra flavour which worked really well with the dish. Thanks Realtor for another lovely recipe!

Wow! Who knew diet food could taste this good! I used Weight Watchers creme fraiche as the sour cream and Splenda in place of the confectioners sugar and it tasted just like a cheesecake! Loved the hint of vanilla too! I'll be coming back to this recipe over and over again!
Loved the flavour in this dish, particulary the dressing. I used creme fraiche as the plain yoghurt and the dressing had a really fresh light taste. Thanks for a lovely recipe!

Lovely basic recipe here with the option for so many variations. I really liked the flavour of the chicken stock and pine nuts together. Next time I'll try adding some italian seasoning. Thanks UmmBinat!
Loved the flavour of the ranch in this dish. I left out the mustard as I don't like the flavour too much and wanted the ranch to shine through. Will come back to this recipe often. Thanks Boomette!

Lovely egg salad! I liked that there wasn't too much mayo in this one- it let the egg be the real star! I spread this over white bread, topped with sliced tomatoes and another piece of bread to make a yummy sandwich! Thanks Nif!

Scaled this down to serve 1. My BF doesn't like his onions overcooked so I put them in at the same time as the tomatoes and olives. His comment was "the flavours blend together really well". He really liked it, so thanks Sarah_Jayne, AKA PAC mom!
Really nice flavour and very healthy! I added some dried garlic towards the end of cooking to boost the garlic flavour and this was lovely with some grated parmesan sprinkled over the top.
Loved the flavour combination here! Unfortunately we couldn't get sourdough bread but it would be even better with the sourdough. A brilliant sandwich- thanks Debbwl!
Loved the flavour in these steaks! We used Bourbon whiskey and Splenda brown sugar blend and didn't find them too sweet after marinating for 2 hours. Thanks for another winner Noo!

Love this recipe! I've made a couple of variations of the fillings- my favourite is onion, red pepper and chopped cherry tomatoes (drained on kitchen paper so they don't made the egg too soggy). I also make mine healthier by adding salsa and not using cheese. Thanks for a keeper!
Wonderful flavour! We had these onions with burgers- they tasted great on top of the burgers and as a side dish. We'll definitely return to this recipe!

The flavour of this smoothie is really lovely! I used canned pineapple chunks and couldn't get the pineapple completely blended in despite blending for ages- probably more to do with my blender than the recipe. I included some juice from the pineapple chunks so omitted the water. I'll definitely try this again, with fresh pineapple. Thanks diner!

I was torn between 4 1/2 and 5 stars but as these are healthy I'm rounding up! We cooked these on the grill outside, on a sheet of foil to help them stay together and not fall through the shelf. I loved the flavour of the veggies in these burgers but BF and I both thought the topping could be changed to bring out these flavours more. He wants to try blue cheese on top, I think some kind of lemon & garlic mayo would work really well. We'll definitely try these again, playing around with various toppings. Thanks for a lovely recipe Noo!

This rice has brilliant flavour. I used 2 teaspoons of a Korma curry powder and it was flavourful but not spicy- just how I like it! I used half a red onion which gave the dish a nice colour. Thanks for a recipe I'll return to often!

This certainly made potatoes more interesting and was really easy! I liked that the sauce added flavour without too many extra calories- good for Weight Watchers. Next time, I'll probably add some garlic. Thanks for a lovely recipe!

I loved the flavour of this dessert and it's got hardly any calories! I used raspberry sugar free jello and Weight Watchers brand vanilla yoghurt. This has endless possibilities! Thanks for a great recipe! Made for PAC Spring 2010.

Loved the flavour combination in this frittata- it was tasty and easy. I loved that it included garlic as many frittatas overlook this (for me) vital ingredient! I didn't have a pan with an ovenproof handle so I flipped the frittata using a plate. Definitely one I'll make again. Thanks!

Oh wow! I absolutely loved this! I doubled the recipe and it served 2 as a main meal. I cooked the rice with a chicken stock cube to give it more flavour, used 4 scallions, nut oil and lots of soy sauce. I added the scallions and eggs at the same time to let the scallions keep some of their flavour by not overcooking them. BF suggested peas and finely diced carrots for next time! I'm not getting egg fried rice from the Chinese takeaway ever again! Thanks for a great recipe!

I love chip sandwiches so this was a great idea! I tried mine two different ways- the first as directed, when I found the juice from the tomato made the chips go soft quite quickly. So the second time I put the chips under the burger and they retained their crunch a lot better this way. Thanks for a lovely idea and a thoroughly enjoyed recipe!

This was very refreshing on a hot day! This drink is very easy to vary to personal taste- personally I found the chocolate too strong and the coffee too weak so would change the amounts of those next time. Thanks for this lovely diet recipe!

Loved this as a healthier alternative to beefburgers. I used havarti cheese as I couldn't find smoked anything at the supermarket. This was a good cheese to use as it doesn't go too gooey when heated but holds its shape well. I'll be using this recipe again! Thanks Starry!

We loved the flavour combination in this dish. I used Cavenders Greek seasoning in place of the salt and pepper and I used "Mini Cheddars" cheese crackers. The eggs sank to the bottom and the zucchini rose to the top but that's no big deal. Thanks for a lovely recipe!
I loved the combination of flavours in this drink- the warm rose flavour perfectly matched with fresh bright lemon. Delicious! I'll make this often. Made for ZWT6.

We couldn't get the burgers to come out properly, with the filling staying inside! So we mixed the filling throughout the burgers and they were very tasty! I particularly liked the oregano so upped the amount a good deal! The ranch worked very well with this recipe. Thanks for a lovely treat! Made for ZWT6.
This recipe worked a treat! I had no idea roasted garlic was so easy! I didn't see where to add the salt and pepper so happily left them out! This added a great flavour to bolognese. Made for ZWT6.
A British classic! Personally I prefer it plain and simple without the eggs on top. And you're right about tea being absolutely essential! Made for ZWT6.

This quick and easy recipe incorporates all my favourite flavours! Next time, I'd probably leave the basil leaves whole and skewer one with each toothpick to ensure each one has some basil on it. Loved it! Made for Everyday is a Holiday tag game.

Thanks for this tasty little recipe! I halved the recipe but still used 1/2 teaspoon of cumin and found that to be about right for my tastes. I loved the way the cumin blended with the tomato for a really flavourful dish!
I love this flavour combination! I used fresh basil and really enjoyed this omelette with toast. Thanks!

We really enjoyed this comforting cold-weather dish! The flavours blended together very nicely. I personally would have prefered more mushroom soup in the mushroom soup- canned tomato ratio so would use more soup or less canned tomatoes next time. But there will definitely be a next time!

I really enjoyed having a change from plain egg salad with just mayonnaise. The mustard was a particularly nice addition and this was much enjoyed. Personally though, I'm not too keen on raw red onion so will probably use spring onion next time to soften the flavour. Thanks Debbwl!

I really enjoyed this healthy meal. To reduce the calories I used Weight Watchers creme fraiche which worked well in place of the yoghurt. The mustard really made this dish great and worked with all the other flavours. I'll make this often, thanks!

Made this for breakfast today- loved the combination of flavours! It was thick and creamy and the lime juice gave it a lovely tangy flavour. I used Splenda in place of the sugar. We'll be making this again!

Really liked the simplicity of this recipe! I love the taste of almond extract, although the one I use has a sunflower oil base, so I just skimmed the droplets of oil off the top! I added bourbon as the liquor and thoroughly enjoyed it!

This was different from most salads we usually have but we loved it! The flavours blended together nicely. DH doesn't like tomatoes so he had his without them and we both really enjoyed it. Made for ZWT7.

We absolutely went crazy for this recipe! If I could give it 10 stars I would! I used low fat sausage and couldn't find dried basil so used italian seasoning. I also added a courgette/ zucchini that I had spare, grated into the potato mixture. Not sure if it was the flour but it had a nice slightly crunchy top to it. I sprayed the pan with a 1 calorie spray. I can't wait to try a Greek version- feta, courgettes, black olives, red onion! Made for ZWT7.

We loved this fried rice recipe! The salty ham went really well with the sceet pineapple. I've also never used garlic in a fried rice recipe but it really added something. Thanks for posting! Made for ZWT7.

We really enjoyed this fresh, light salad. The dressing was lovely but with English cherry tomatoes never being very ripe, I had to add a tiny pinch of Splenda to reduce the tartness. I will definately be using this recipe again, probably adding some finely diced red onion to lift the flavour. Thanks for a keeper! UPDATE: I made this again using baby plum tomatoes which are sweeter. No Splenda was needed! I'd definitely recommend using baby plum tomatoes in this recipe as they really lift the sweetness of the corn.

You're right, this adds a subtle taste which is just right- not as sweet as juice but healthier and more refreshing. This makes a lovely change and I'll be making this whenever I have some pineapple around! Made for PRMR.

Wow! We loved this recipe! The marinade smelled so good as I was making it that I made half as much again, then added just a little flour at the end of cooking to thicken the sauce. This might be too lemony for some but we loved the tangyness! Next time I'll try this over rice- this is my new go-to diet curry recipe! The combination of garam masala and fresh coriander really works! Thanks for another great recipe Noo!

I had never had sloppy joes before but this recipe was delicious! Really easy to make, very tasty and still great with extra lean beef. My DH doesn't like celery but couldn't taste it in this recipe at all! I'm making it again next week!

I had never had cinnamon in hot milk before but it was absolutely lovely! I am a huge fan of vanilla so I pretty much doubled the amount I used as initially I couldn't taste it over the cinnamon. I'll come back to this recipe often!

What a lovely, healthy treat! I used Weight Watchers creme fraiche and extra light cream cheese so there's no guilt! I've boxed the rest up to take to work tomorrow and will really look forward to it. Next time, I'm going to try 2Bleu's idea and use coconut extract!

This was a nice treat to try something different and healthy. I used bacon medallions to cut the fat and left out the cheese as I was looking for a true BLT flavour without the fat. I used iceberg lettuce and it was easy to roll and not as messy as I expected. Thanks for a lovely new healthy treat!

This is a very refreshing salad with bright flavours and the yogurt dressing really cuts the fat from my normal mayonnaise-based dressings. For me, there was possibly a touch too much cumin but that's just personal taste. I could see using this dressing for all sorts of recipes but next I'll try it with turkey burgers. Thanks for a lovely salad recipe! Made for PAC 2012.
We love this recipe! I've made it a few times, sometimes with lettuce and sometimes with rice. It tastes great either way! Thanks for posting!

We loved this recipe! I sliced the onions rather than chopping them small and DH doesn't like celery so I used extra onion instead. I'd definitely recommend making a double batch as 3/4 cup servings would just leave us wanting more! Thanks so much for posting!

We definitely enjoyed this salad and will make it again. I added baby plum tomatoes, a red bell pepper and cooked chicken to make a meal out of it. Next time, I would mix the taco seasoning and ranch dressing earlier to let the flavours blend and mellow a bit as I personally found the taco spice a little too strong. This would also be great with coriander/ cilantro as another reviewer recommended!

This is a simple dinner that still tastes great.  I found that the onions needed to cook for a big longer to get soft after the patties were done.  I served with mashed potatoes for some extra comfort food goodness.  Thanks for posting!
These are probably some of the best roasted potatoes that I have ever had.  They are so simple and have a lot of flavor.  Thanks!

Wow, I never would have thought that simmering the meat would make such a huge difference, but it does!  These tasted absolutely delicious.  I used your spice mix and your topping suggestions.  I often make ground beef burritos and tacos, and I will always simmer instead of brown from now on.  Thanks so much for the recipe!

I am so glad I tried this sauce!  Not only was it delicious, it also surprised me by tasting exactly like the sauce at this little restaurant in San Diego that I used to go to all the time back when I lived there.  I added twice as much sesame oil since I love the stuff.  I used the sauce with stir fried chicken and Chinese vegetables, and it worked great.  I can't wait to experiment with using it with all sorts of different meats and veggies.  I will definitely make this sauce often.  Thank you so much!

Wow, this is wonderful!  I have a couple different varieties of flavored mayonnaise that I use for artichokes, but this was way better.  It had a lot of great flavors which really complemented the artichokes very well.  Thanks for the great recipe!

Wow, these are great!  Definitely one of those recipes where simple ingredients come together well to make something terrific.  I made mine with bacon and used homegrown tomatoes sprinkled with a bit of sea salt and pepper.  This made for a lovely, rich lunch.  Thanks for the recipe.
Oh my, these were seriously delicious!  You are right, Jen, the eggs and avocado are an incredible combination.  It was such a lovely breakfast treat.  I can't wait to make this again, thanks!
Delicious!  The combination of cheeses is a nice twist on the usual grilled cheese.  Thanks!

Seriously good eggs!  They were so different, but in a very good way.  I was definitely skeptical about this recipe, but it came together beautifully.  All of the ingredients seemed made for each other in the end.  Thanks for the great recipe!
Fantastic!  I used a cup of skim milk and it was still great.
You forgot to add some gravy and nuke it for 2 minutes...  yumbo!
I used apricot all fruit spread. Simply delicious!  Thx. for posting.  I just love easy, economical and healthy offerings!
This was really full of flavor!  I added some Tabasco chipotle sauce to the butter for a little extra zip...
I added 1/4  tsp of hot pepper flakes and 1/2 cup of grated ramano cheese.  Perfect!  Thx. for sharing this tasty, quick and simple recipe.
This was refreshing and delicious!  I am big tea drinker and sometimes drink it with lemon but never thought to add o.j.  The sugar/o.j. ratio was perfect.  Thx. for posting.

These came out perfect!  I agree, the  more color the better.  The taste is so much better than steamed or boiled.  
Thx. for posting this great recipe.
These are excellent.  And no butter!  Think of all the calories saved...  Thx. for posting.
I'm sorry I haven't reviewed this yet. I have been making this for ages now. I love this stuff, and my husband loves it as well! It's easy and good and I could eat it just about every day! Thanks!

Yummy, Boomette! These wings are so good, and really quite simple. I usually have everything on hand so I don't have to go out after anything. I made 12 servings and was a little concerned that the small amount of marinade wouldn't be enough for the pound of wings, but the flavor came through really well. I pre-baked these about 15 minutes in the oven, and then finished them off on the grill for that nice grill char. I used buckwheat honey since that's what we had, and I loved the spice and honey combo. Thanks for a great recipe!!

This was so good, my carnivore husband loved it! (and I did, too). Best of all, my picky 3.5 year old and 18 month old loved it. I did sub in taco seasoning instead of the seasonings (I used about 1/8 cup bulk taco seasoning, and the 4 bouillon cubes) so good! I have wanted to try this for weks, but was afraid we wouldn't like it...I wish I had tried it sooner, it is great. We used this for burritos with refried beans, cheese, sour cream and some salsa. Thanks for this great cheap recipe!

Yum! I bought some Tzatziki from our local Greek restaurant, and we ate this with that and Greek salad, warm pitas, feta, and kalamata olives. I baked the chicken, and I can't wait until summer so we can grill this, it will be even better grilled! Thanks for a great new (for me) way to fix chicken. It's so quick and easy!

I can't say enough nice things about this punch, it was the hit of the party! I served with frozen raspberries, and the color and flavor they gave were fantastic. I served in a pitcher, rather than a punch bowl, and it was very pretty. I think I'll keep these ingredients on hand, just for a refreshing drink any time. Thanks for a great (easy) drink!

Such  a cute idea!! I used 4 colors, and layered them in a 9x13 pan. Then I cut that into graduating squares for a 3-tier cake for my daughter's personal cake for her 2nd birthday. the gel food coloring works very well, just make sure you mix it really well, I had a few "pockets" of color that I didn't mix in well enough. This was a great idea, and now my son wants a rainbow cake for his next birthday, too!! Thanks, I love the idea!!!

I had this for breakfast nearly every morning when I was visiting a farm near Lyon in the middle of France. The milk came straight from the goats and went into big wide mug/bowls where we added the chocolate to taste. The bread was delivered fresh every day and kept in a tall bread box on the floor. Dipping the bread was definitely the way to go. Thanks for posting this "recipe". It brought back such great memories for me.

Wow, this was delicious! I bought tri-tip steaks because they weren't very expensive, but I had no idea what to do with them! I chose this recipe because of a comment that said it was one of the few non-asian tasting recipes (nothing against asian style food, I just wasn't in that mood last night). I was a little concerned because of all the ingredients (especially all the garlic and onion variations) but I subbed a few ingredients for what I had on hand (lime juice instead of lemon, specialty onion spice mix instead of  onion) and marinated overnight. My DH grilled it to rare/medium rare.  The flavor was so good, I didn't need steak sauce (I *always* use steak sauce). I want this again for dinner tonight, that's how good it was! It was so tender and flavorful. The sugar made a tasty crust and the flavors came together to make a delicious steak with no particular flavor overpowering any of the others. Thanks for sharing your recipe, I don't think I'll need to look for another!
This was so good!  I left out the onion and cilantro as a matter of personal taste but left everything else the same.  This was so easy to throw together that I will be making often.  Thanks!!
This was pretty good.  Made as is, DH did not care for the sour cream so probably will subsitiute something else for that next time. Thanks!!
Very Good!! Made exactly as is, these were easy and tasty.  Thanks!!

This was really good. I used nonfat sour cream, 1/3 of the taco seasoning, and halved everything but the greens. I added to it carrots for a little crunch, the optional olives, and some cilantro. I also used a light sprinkling of apple cider vinegar on top to give it a little tang. Yummy!
Quick, easy and delicious! I used a bit more basil in mine. Fed 4 vegetable lovers. Perfect accompaniment to any meal.
I really liked this recipe. I used chicken breasts and skipped the food coloring. It was very flavorful and a bit spicy -- well enjoyed.

Perfect name for these pancakes, they are fluffy and citrus scented! I love the floral flavor the blood oranges give to them. And the syrup really enhances that flavor. I did halve the syrup amount, but still used the 1 blood orange for the segments in it (we might have liked 2 even!). Other reviewers are right, the batter is thick, it should not be a problem cooking them though, if you stretch it out as you spoon it on to the griddle (or you could quickly and gently spread it right after you lay it on). The positives to the thick batter are 1) the fluffiness and 2) you can make snowpeople or other shapes easily with it! For us, this served 2 people. These pancakes are delicious and something you might expect to be served at an upscale B&B!

Wow, we loved your chili! The cocoa powder gives it a nice depth of flavor. I used very lean turkey, just a teaspoon of sweetener, half the salt, and skipped the cheese. I simmered it about 45 minutes total. Portions are generous. Yummy - you have our vote in the contest!

This was a great soup! It has a high veggie to broth ratio and a little kick to it, which is nice. I used 2 teaspoons of oil (2 tablespoons for the butter must be 2 teaspoons also?). I assumed the hot water in the ingredients were for soaking the tomatoes. I put the tomatoes in the food processor after soaking them, since the only sun dried tomatoes not packed in oil I could find are whole. I also skipped the cheese, which worked for us, since the tortellini already contained ample cheese. Served 3-4 as a meal. The ingredients in this soup work very well together!

Very good, but potent! If you don't drink a lot, this will make enough for 4 people. I skipped the honey, since I used sciacchetra, a sweet wine from Cinque Terre. The flavors here work very well together.

Very good muffins! I liked the strawberry butter with them too, but it certainly is not necessary, the muffins stand by themselves. I used Smart Balance and subbed a little as applesauce. I also cut the powdered sugar in half (in the butter). Still wonderful! I baked them about 20 minutes.

The pancakes were fluffy and really good, but the sauce is the best part! I might cut back the cornstarch just a little bit in it. I also subbed sugar in the sauce, since I was out of honey, but the amount of sugar was just right for us. I halved the butter in the pancakes, and used smart balance for both. I did not have any problems with the batter. We had 16 ounces of strawberries, so used them all; we enjoyed having enough to put on each pancake. Enjoyable breakfast!

Wow! I made a light version of these (less oil and cheese, no butter, used low fat turkey bacon), and they were still absolutely fantastic! I added some garlic, used a chili pepper instead of the cayenne, and just a sprinkle of salt. It took only about 8 minutes for me for this to brown pretty well. The combination of flavors really works here, and the balance of veggies to potatoes is just right. We topped this with nonfat sour cream, which enhanced the flavor nicely, but it certainly does not need it. Great for breakfast, lunch or dinner!

The flavors and method are quite good here. I did also try Recipe #107440 to test out the extra spice and flat version. The twisted are fun (though I did have to weigh down the edges with ramekins for it to stay curled - not sure if that is because I used extra lean turkey bacon), but I think I like the crispier texture of the flat better. The minimum amount of black pepper does give this a bit of heat, which is nice. Yummy recipe!

This was also our first time trying Isreali couscous. We really liked it! It is very much like pasta. I could only find it in a Middle Eastern market. I cut the oil down to a half tablespoon, which was still plenty. I also decreased the amount of garam masala in the recipe (for DH), but added more to mine. Next time I will cook this a few more minutes, it was still a bit al dente after the 10+5 minutes cook time. Two of us ate the whole recipe as a side dish -- we kept going back for more!

This was a good, easy, one dish meal. The only thing I really did different was to use chicken breasts and red wine instead of white. I was afraid it wouldn't be enough liquid and the potatoes would stick, but it worked out perfectly on both accounts. Thanks, Pneuma!

Great salad! I also used turkey bacon and subbed goat cheese. I added some sweet and spicy pecans to this, and it provided a nice crunchy counterpart. The flavors are balanced and all went together well. The dressing wasn't too tart for me, but if you think it would be for you, add some oil to the dressing to balance that out. Thanks for this recipe!

This is an innovative idea, as well as yummy! I added the higher amount of lemon curd, as we are lemon lovers. We tried different bowls with different toppings -- the gingersnaps, as well as raspberries, blueberries, sliced almonds, and walnuts. We liked it topped with the nuts the best, though the raspberries and nuts together also made a nice combination. If you are a big eater, you might want to make 50 percent more than the recipe calls for. The amount of liquid and cooking time produced the perfect consistency for this oatmeal. Thanks for the great idea and recipe!

These tasted really good, though I think that it takes some practice to get them to look like the photos from 2Bleu's clan. Mine were much flatter, and more of the consistency of foccacia. The first four steps are quick and easy, the boiling is the trickiest part. Even though 3 bagels fit comfortably in my large wok, I think it would have been easier to flip them, have them keep their shape, and get them in and out of the boiling water with only one or two bagels. I chose the refrigerator option, which worked well, they rose a little bit more overnight. I used nonstick cooking spray for the glaze, which gave it a nice little crunch. I made it easy on myself and just used the same pan and silpat for the rises, shaping, storing in the frig, and baking (with no problems). Of the flavors I made, sun dried tomato was the unanimous first choice, other favorites were kalamata olive and everything, with dried onion and (fresh) garlic ranking behind those. As a first timer bagel maker, this took me about 2.5 hours from start to finish, including rise time. So it takes a bit of time, but they do taste yummy.

WOW!! This was amazing! You guys obviously went to great lengths to test this to get all the ratios/flavors right with the 5 almond components, etc. I halved the sugar in this, since we don't like things too sweet. I used crumbled rather than crushed amaretti, using your photos as my guide. I also substituted milk, which is common in gelato (and also how I make all my ice creams). Even the low fat version is to die for! I didn't have any problems with the directions. The only thing to mention there is in step 1 the almond paste did not become smooth until after I added the eggs. Even with some teeny weeny bits left, I would not strain that out, as I LOVE almond. I would keep the berries fresh for sprinkling over, and not freeze them. The raspberries especially do freeze up very hard. An almond lovers dream -- thank you!

Yummy potatoes! The squashed appearance might be best suited for your family, but they do taste great. I liked the crispness the oil gave to them. Like another reviewer, I also microwaved mine initially to save time. Served these plain as a side dish, but I could see guacamole and nonfat sour cream being good on these too (like a potato skin).

I have made a lot of baked oatmeals, but none with maple syrup, which really makes this recipe special! I also used walnuts and doubled them. I ended up tripling the maple syrup by accident (big heavy jug), but it really wasn't too sweet (and I don't like things very sweet). The major thing I did differently was to halve the milk and bake it for 30 minutes (I have made baked oatmeal with this high of liquid ratio before and it was very loose). Thanks for such a delicious breakfast, this will definitely be made again!
This is a good oatmeal. I used tangerine marmalade and got the idea from other reviewers to add a little maple syrup. The orange, cranberry and maple tasted good together with the walnuts.
Delicious! I used vanilla bean and less cinnamon. This is easy and tasty and gives you a different flavor!

This is an amazing drink, maybe our new favorite! You wouldn't know it has maple syrup in it. It has the perfect balance of sweet and tart, and was not too sweet for DH, who doesn't like sweet drinks. YUM! Can I go make another one?

What a great salad! A lot like an antipasto salad. I love hearts of palm on salad, and marinating them is a great way to inject flavor. I used Italian parsley, only half the dressing, and less artichokes. I also subbed balsamic vinegar and arugula, and added a little bit of basil and proscuitto. This makes 4 huge (and delicious) salads!

Delicious! I used fat free sour cream and half the margarine (light Smart Balance). I also halved the artichokes and spinach, since I was afraid it would be too much. The combination was wonderful, I could taste each of the individual components. I did heat the artichokes, spinach and milk first, so they wouldn't cool down the potatoes.  Great side dish -- very addicting!
These were yummy! Mine came out more like regular pancakes than crepes. I used nonfat milk and cooking spray. I really liked the lemon juice, powdered sugar and cinnamon on them too!
We really liked this combination, and especially the relish. The tomatoes and basil are very important to it, don't leave them out. I halved the oil, and used more basil and wild king salmon.
Yummy! I used less syrup and more coffee, and added a tad of Frangelico. Had this chilled since it is too hot right now!

Wow, this IS a chocolate lovers dream! I thought the serving size seemed small until we started eating it, it is very rich!  I did what it is normal for me for making ice creams/gelatos: used egg yolks instead of whole eggs, all milk, tempered the eggs, and added the Frangelico after it is off the heat. I subbed amaretti for the biscotti (estimated 12 would equal about 2 biscotti). I also used 6 tablespoons of the Frangelico, it wasn't too much, still quite subtle. I thought the amount of sugar was just right, and I don't like things too sweet. This is like a fudgey bittersweet brownie!

This makes for some yummy salads. I made half the original way, and half the Yemenite way. Dh liked the former better, I liked the latter better. But both were very good. I used just a pinch of salt, 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, and 2 large tomatoes. I did not puree the second version, so it would still be like a salad, rather than a dip. I also decided to halve the parsley in that version and not add the extra lemon. We love lemon, but it was already quite tart with the tahini. Thanks, Susiecat!

This a really good soup. I halved the cayenne pepper, and it was still fairly spicy. I also subbed celery seed and 1/4 tsp of salt for the celery salt, since I didn't have any. I topped this with cilantro and squeezed lime and lemon over it at the table, and that definitely brightened up all the flavors. Served 4 as an entree. Here is my video of the soup being made: http://www.recipezaar.com/sitenews/post.php?pid=944&pn=1&pageref=Photo_Video-927138&vw_arrange_order=DESC&vw_sort_order=MOST_RECENT

I love potatoes, eggplant and Indian food, so this is the perfect dish for me! I followed your advice and doubled all the spices (except the salt, just used a pinch). I also added a little of sharon's Recipe #174350. I halved the oil and did add a few tablespoons of water the few times I stirred this (our potato dice was pretty big, so I think this was done at 20-25 minutes). Squeezed a little lemon on top, and yum. As 2 adults, we ate almost all of this!

Delicious! Great way to serve brussel sprouts. I used uncured bacon bits, double the mushrooms, and just a light sprinkle of salt and pepper. I also microwaved the sprouts to retain nutrients. The flavor of the onion, mushrooms, bacon and sprouts are wonderful together.

I made this to be used for your Recipe #297430, but also tasted some plain with baked chips. I used fresh tomatoes and ended up adding the avocado from the salad to it, so it wouldn't brown. That would be a great variation, like guacamole with black beans and corn. It was really good plain, but even better on the salad.

Great corn! I used fresh oregano and just a teaspoon of Smart Balance, which is plenty for us, since we usually eat corn plain. Nice to have something a little different, and a good cooking method as well.

This is such a fun way to eat your veggies. I used garden cucumbers and fat free feta. The flavors go very well together, and it is an enjoyable dish. Goat cheese would probably be really good in these too.

These are monster smores! I thought the amount of filling and banana was a lot for one smore, but it is perfect, as long as you do not mind getting all 10 fingers messy! I think it would also work to split the filling in half and have them as two open face smores (if you did not want to wash up afterward). The flavor combination in this dessert is great, who can resist peanut butter, chocolate and bananas together! Note: 1 graham cracker in the ingredient list is 1 sheet of graham crackers, or 2 crackers.

We rarely eat beef, so I am rating only the potatoes. They sounded just too awesome to pass up - and they were - and I don't give out 5 stars that easily! I would rename them truffle mashed potatoes instead of mascarpone potatoes though, since you could not specifically taste the mascarpone, but could really taste the truffle oil. They were so delicious and very addicting. I used only one tablespoon of Smart Balance and nonfat milk in these. The amount of potatoes served at least 4. Highly recommended!

Very good pancakes. I thought the graham cracker crumbs imparted a nice subtle taste, and were an innovate use of a contest ingredient. I like your tip for the graham crackers in the ziploc, much less messy than doing them in the food processor. This makes a very thick batter (I decided not to add any extra buttermilk). I had no problems flipping them or with burning. Prep and cook time are a little off though, it took me about 20 minutes for each. The pancakes served 2 people, and were great with coconut syrup!

We really liked these, but they didn't quite live up to what I was expecting being a chocolate peanut butter fan. I couldn't taste the peanut butter in the brownie, even with chunky peanut butter. There's also a lot going on with the 3 components of this, and with the texture. One thing I did love was the extra chocolate chips that were stirred into the batter. Fresh out of the oven, they melt in your mouth, liquidy chocolateness! This makes a very thick batter that turns into a dense brownie, almost like a flourless chocolate cake. I think I would have preferred a little more flour and leavening, so they would be more cakey, but that's probably personal preference. We don't like things too sweet, so I cut out one third of the sweetener in the brownies, and half of the sugar in the topping (I wouldn't call it frosting). I did step 2 in the microwave, and step 8 by hand. Mine also puffed up unevenly after baking, but they mostly flattened back down once cooled, and it is undiscernible once the topping is on them. I did not store these in the refrigerator, and I think they actually got better the second day. Overall, we did really like these, but would need a little tweaking to become a 5 star recipe for us.

This is a great bread! I doubled the dill, and could not really taste the onion, but that may be because I decided to saute it first. I ended up adding the amount of flour that was half way between in your range, and it was just right for our climate. The texture and flavor in this bread is very nice!

We really liked this chicken. We also liked that it was nice and crispy with no added oil. I made the sauce for me (since DH isn't a big peanut sauce fan) and thought it was great too. I used only one teaspoon of sugar, half of the sesame oil, and subbed sweet chili sauce and two cloves of garlic. I thought it had a rich balanced flavor, and lived up to its thickness in it's title "dipping sauce". I also really liked it over the brown rice and broccolini we had with the chicken. I  made my own seasoning salt, using only a pinch of salt with turmeric, celery seed, onion powder and Italian seasoning. I think the baking time will vary with how thick you cut the chicken strips. Ours were pretty thin, so 15-20 minutes was plenty of time in the oven. The only thing that confused me on this recipe is in the description where it says "crispy rice cereal flakes". It made me wonder if the cereal should be like Rice Krispies or like Special K. I went with Rice Krispies, since that was one of the required ingredients for RSC. Serving size is spot on. Yummy chicken and peanut sauce!

Great pancakes! Surprisingly light for being half whole wheat and having mashed banana in them. The nutmeg gives them a slightly different flavor. I found 3/4 cup of blueberries to be plenty, and I usually load my pancakes with them! We tried these with both syrup and topped with banana slices, but they kind of overwhelm the delicate flavor. We liked them plain for that reason. They were also good with a tad of lemon curd too. Feeds 2-3 people, depending on how big of an eater you are.

This is a nice way to do something different with your regular corn on the cob. I used just a tad of Smart Balance and had to use the oven for these. It's sweet and I really enjoyed the change of pace. Thanks!

This was quite yummy on its own, but I ate the leftovers with a little homemade Recipe #174350, which was also nice. I could see how another reviewer ate this for breakfast, since it really is a skillet potato dish. I did pack the spinach in the measuring cup, but would have liked about 3 times the quantity, so it could be more in balance with the amount of the other ingredients. I did not boil it, just added it at the end and let it wilt a little. I used 2 tablespoons of oil, which was more than enough. Delicious, Zurie!

Wow, is this ever delicious! It is mild, but don't confuse that with bland - it has great flavor. I halved the salt, tripled the mushrooms, and used a teaspoon each of the soy and vinegar. I loved the fish and the method in this, and the flavors were nicely balanced. I decreased the fish to half a pound (but kept the rest the same) and it was perfect for 2 people.

We loved this ragu! We chopped the veggies finely, omitted the sugar, and doubled the pasta and basil. It was great with turkey, but I am sure you could use other meats as well. I was worried about putting the ground meat in raw, but it broke up easily upon stirring, and worked just fine. I used a Malbec in this -- which I will increase next time. Very easy with a great method and a great taste - I definitely recommend trying this bolognese!

This is a wonderful way to fix your greens - it had a great flavor. I used chard, less oil, more garlic, and just stir fried it. I also drizzled the soy and oyster sauces over it, so the amounts were maybe half. We'll definitely be making this again!

This is a delicious and spicy side dish! I loved the addition of the water chestnuts. I stir fried the green beans instead of steaming them, so it came out much like the kind you get in a restaurant, a little browned and a little crisp - perfect. Next time I will double the sauce since it barely coated the veggies.
This is a great soup! The pearl couscous is wonderful in it, and the slow cooking allows it to develop a nice richness.

These would be delicious with just the almonds and banana - add the other stuff, and wow! I followed others and reduced the sugar (to 6 tablespoons) and subbed applesauce for half of the oil. I also halved the coconut to make it lighter and omitted the maraschino cherries (personal preference). These flavors are great together - very yummy!
Fast and delicious! I used only 2 tablespoons of the vinegar and took your lead on the peanut oil (omitted it, actually). I used a 12 oz. bag of broccoli, so this fed two of us. It was very yummy!
Delicious! I love the combination. The peach schnapps really makes it.

Simple, but delicious and satisfying! I used a little olive oil for sauteeing, in lieu of adding the butter. I like that you just warm the sauce, so it retains all the fresh flavors. I agree with Boomette, a double recipe feeds about two people, if this is the sole entree. Yum!!

This would be really great cocoa with just the first two ingredients! I did add the butterscotch schnapps, and it was present, but subtle. I like how the salt enhances it, but you don't specifically taste it. I also made the light version of this with fat free whipped cream. We ended up stirred in the toppings, since we kept missing them as we sipped and just got the cocoa!

I tried these based on Bird and Wigal's recommendations in the top 2008 game and was not disappointed. I totally agree with Bird, the tomato with the potato is what makes it sing! So I would make sure you stick to cherry tomatoes, unless you can get garden or other very flavorful ones for the regular kind. I used more of the fresh herbs - they really make this dish too. I halved the butter (1/2 tablespoon - about 7.5 grams), and just followed step 3 and coated/warmed the potatoes (did not fry them til cripsy). These are delicious and could even be eaten for breakfast like homefries!

These were good, but didn't really strike us as "really good". I expected so much more flavor given the nature of the ingredients in the marinade (and I love sherry vinegar!). I think either doubling the marinade or maybe trying it with balsamic vinegar might make the flavor come out more.

Holy cow is this delicious! I think the cake flour and creaming method really make this light and fluffy. I cut back the sugar 25% (I usually do, since we don't like things too sweet) and used Smart Balance. I added a piece of parchment under the long way of the loaf pan so it would be easy to remove. I thought the syrup looked like a lot, but it all got absorbed, and makes for a VERY nice lemon flavor. Scrumptious!!

Oh, this is an awesome salad! It strikes the perfect balance of flavors. I halved the cayenne and cumin for DH and used just a pinch of salt. I have made similar salads to this before, but they were never this good. I think the walnuts and small amount of feta add a nice touch. I can see why this made it into the best of ZWT and the best of 2008 game!

This made a great pasta sauce - very lemony. I used 1/2 tablespoon of oil, and just sprinkled the salt and pepper over it. We kept with the lemon yellow theme and used yellow cherry tomatoes. I think it would work well over chicken or fish as well.
We love roasted broccoli and we love balsamic, so this was a great pairing for us. Made for a very yummy side dish!

This might just be the best green bean stir fry we have ever made! The flavors are harmonious and delicious together. I halved the sugar and red pepper flakes (it was still quite spicy!). I also used probably 1/2 tablespoon of oil, which was ample. The two of us ate this all as a side dish (we love our veggies). I could also see this being a wonderful entree with the addition of tofu or ground pork.

Very yummy! I didn't use baking squares of chocolate, but with a little detective work I figured out each square is equal to one ounce. I also used natural crunchy peanut butter since that is what we have in the house, and it worked fine. Two of us shared a (heart shaped!) ramekin, instead of turning it out onto a plate. If you love peanut butter and chocolate together, this one's for you!

Originally reviewed April 12, 2008. This made it into my book#207955. This was so incredible! It contains some of my favorite ingredients, and I love how you get chocolate chips in every bite (even with the lower amount). I used quick oats, just a pinch of salt, double the nuts, and about half the sugar (I do not like things too sweet). I only cooled it 2-3 minutes, I was afraid it would get cold if I waited 5-10 minutes. You have a winner here! Thanks for incorporating my suggestions. :)

I tried this both with chai and some other teas. I liked the vanilla almond and green tea versions better than the  chai, though they are definitely more subtle. It opens the door to try all kinds of other teas in your oatmeal. It is a nice change to have some differrent flavors in there.

This is a good oatmeal. I used fresh squeezed orange juice and one fresh mandarin orange (ie. tangerine) per person. I followed another reviewer and used 1/3 of the sugar, and the sweetest was just right. Next time I would halve the cinnamon and mix-ins. Thanks!

WOW - this is my kind of dinner!! This is very similar to my favorite dish at Hobee's (De Anza browns with black bean chili), but better and much healthier. I used pico de gallo instead of the chilies and tomatoes, plus the optional toppings in step 8. We also ended up using most of the can of black beans, since we had it open already. This is super super SUPER! ETA - I made this again the super quick way by microwaving the potatoes. It was almost as good that way as well!

This has a very good flavor, but the pudding makes it very sweet. I wasn't sure what another reviewer meant by using only one box of pudding, until I noticed the box I had was only 3.4 oz (I only had/used one box).  Also, I did use instant pudding because that is all we had, and it worked fine. This is just as easy as making quick oatmeal on the stove, and definitely worth trying! ETA - We tried this a second time using 1.25 oz. pistachio pudding and the artificial coloring was much less bright, as well as the sweetness being fine. The flavor didn't come through as much though, so I added whole pistachios, which brought that flavor up. This recipe serves 2.

I loved this - it's different, in a good way! I especially liked the coriander and cumin seeds on the sweet potato (which I would not omit - that's what makes it unique). I used less oil, fresh tomatoes and black beans. I also made this with baked chips and without cheese to make it healthier. My sweet potato chunks were done in about 20 minutes. This serves 3 at most, if it's an entree. These flavors really sing together!

I thought this recipe was great. The leeks and tiny bit of yogurt really make it. I used the cooking method from Recipe #315371, so only used about half the broth and wine (I also omitted the salt). I think arugula would be nice in this as a substitute for the spinach. Thanks!

We love chorizo, it gives the beans a great background flavor in these tostadas. I think next time we would double it to make that flavor more prominent. I baked these to make them healthier. Thanks for sharing your creation!

We really enjoyed this soup and were surprised it didn't need any spices. The lemon and wine really carried it. I did adjust the amounts a bit, using less oil, lentils, broth and wine and more vegetables and dill. I also added garlic, decreased the cooking time, and cooked the wine into it a little bit. It has a nice flavor.

This was really good. I always use less salt. I also added more ginger, doubled the red pepper flakes, and finished it with some lemon. Also didn't know if the amount of oil was wrong, I used 1/2 tablespoon so that the seeds had enough to sputter in. I liked having the daal and cauliflower together in one dish.
Nice dressing! I used buttermilk for the milk since I had it.
These are very good, though mine didn't crisp up. I don't know if it is because I only used the oil and omitted the butter.

I LOVE these pancakes! They are fluffy and really showcase the fresh taste of the cranberry since they aren't cooked too long. The amount of sugar and orange juice perfectly balance the tartness of the cranberries, and the finished product isn't too sweet, which is perfect for me. The only change I made was to decrease the butter to 1 tablespoon. The first time I made these I had a harder time flipping them. The second time I tried to correct this. I let the batter sit 5-10 minutes before starting to cook them. I sprayed the skillet well. I made sure they were adequately spread out. And I waited to flip them until they were a little drier/cooked a little longer on the first side than normal. These yielded perfect results! Fed 3.

Absolutely delicious, and it does taste like tacos! I have made these several times now, sometimes using ground turkey, other times using soy crumbles (and both are really good). We usually omit the cheese, and also top them with cilantro, guacamole and tomatoes (or pico de gallo instead of salsa). You will be licking your plate with this one if you love tacos and potatoes like I do!
Wow, these are super! And such a great cooking method, which I will use again and again (cook them before caramelizing them). Tons of delicious flavor without all the time to get there!
I love savory popcorns, and this one is just spot on! Really good.
This was good. I think adding some Amaretto or something to it would make it better.

We loved this crisp! Especially the crispy chewy topping. I halved the margarine and decreased the flour by 2 tablespoons. The second time I made this I made it only with the cranberries and baked it 15 minutes, then broiled it 2 more minutes. We decided that this is the best crisp we've ever had! Great served warm with low fat vanilla (or eggnog) ice cream.

What an awesome topping for fish! I halved the garlic and reduced the fats to just one tablespoon. I ended up having to omit the roasted red pepper since it had gone bad. The mediterranean flavors are just wonderful here. I used the sage, but I think the basil would be great in it too.

Oh, these are so good! More like cake than banana bread. I took other reviewers' advice and added 1/4 cup chocolate chips and used an 8x8 pan (which was still spread very thin, so I would not at all recommend a 13x9). I baked them for 35 minutes, and the top layer was much browner than Marra's. I also subbed half the Smart Balance as applesauce and used sugar, but reduced it by 25%. I think the chocolate chips really add something special to this. I thought about another's suggestion of nuts, but am glad I didn't add them. I sprinked some toasted almonds on one piece, and it kind of overpowered the delicate flavor. These are super, especially the chocolate and banana flavor together, and are definitely recommended!
These have a very nice flavor, and are healthy too!
This is a very good soup. I liked the addition of the red wine. I added some lemon, red pepper flakes and spinach (because I had it) and saved the basil for serving. Comforting on a cold night.
Great rice! I followed another reviewer and used 2 cans of tomatoes with 3 cups of broth. Portions are generous, served 10-12 as a side dish.

This is a good pasta salad - different and interesting. We subbed half of the mayo with homemade ranch, used romaine lettuce and less salt and pepper. DH thought avocado would be great in this. If you are making this as a main dish instead of a side, it would feed 3 people.
These have great flavor. We used the BBQ instead of broiling. I think setting some of the marinade aside to use as a sauce is key.

Great (and healthy) take on macaroni salad! The chipotles give this a very smoky flavor. You can definitely control the hotness by the salsa you use. We used medium salsa and it was pretty hot, but perfect for me. I ended up doubling the beans, lime and garlic. All nice flavors. Portions I would say are for a side dish, halve the number if this is your sole entree.
These were really good pancakes. I used 3 egg whites to make up the half cup. They don't need any syrup (IMO!).

I followed other's suggestions and only browned the onion first. I thought the eggplant was cooked well (not overcooked) after 4 hours on low. I think it might have created more liquid though as it cooked. It would have been good to serve this over rice for that reason. I used less salt and more parsley.

I love home fries, so I knew these would hit the spot. The chilis (which we reduced) and peanuts lend something different and very nice to the recipe. We reduced the oil and salt, and omitted the cheese (personal preference). Good solid dish.

I left the sugar out of the marinade to lessen the chance of burning on the BBQ (based on the photos), but it still did, so maybe the oven would be better suited for this dish. I think it has great potential with all the flavors we love, but somehow it didn't taste as good as it sounded.

Being the scientist that I am, I had to do a side by side comparison of this with my usual method of storage (kept enclosed in a plastic produce bag). I checked/used them with the same frequency and found both methods to yield comparable results. They both lasted (and smelled fresh) for 3 weeks, following the directions to remove any yellowing or rotting stems/leaves along the way. We get very fresh produce here, so I am not sure if this method would make more of a difference if the cilantro you purchased weren't as fresh.

This was delicious, moist and dense like a pound cake. I doubled the recipe to make a regular loaf size and was surprised that it did need to bake 65 minutes in our convection oven to be done. I followed other reviewers in adding more lemon juice (1.5 lemons) and 1/2 teaspoon of vanilla. I also did my usual cutting back of sugar by 25%. It was wonderfully lemony and the sweet tart ratio was perfect for us.
This was great! I followed other reviewers and used low sodium broth and added lemon and fresh spinach to it. I also used much less of my Indian chili powder, as it is very hot.
Delicious combination! I also added some cucumber for a little crunch. Everything went very well together.

Different and very good chili. I really like the potatoes in it, and it does taste like chili! We made an even healthier version with Morningstar veggie crumbles, which work so well in recipes like this. I also followed other reviewers and doubled the cumin and oregano, and added a red pepper and garlic. Ate the leftovers with some lime, cilantro and nonfat sour cream and that was even better.

Great flavors. I used less salt, more cilantro and the optionals: corn tortillas and nonfat sour cream. Loved it as a taco! I did have to cook it an extra 4 minutes past the cooking time (covered) so that the sweet potatoes were all the way cooked through (which were cut into french fry shape).
This was pretty good, especially the sauce. DH thought the chicken without the sauce tasted like fajitas. Thanks!
Loved the crispiness of these, but the liquid burnt black around the potatoes. I used fresh oregano, just a sprinkle of salt, and extra lemon at the table. I am not sure why they burned...
These were good, but the cheese and the sauce get a little overpowered in them. I left out the bouillon so it wouldn't be too salty, and used 4 whole wheat tortillas. One each was very filling.

This was a really good bread. I think if fresh cranberries were in season, it would be even better. I tasted it with and without the glaze and definitely liked the lemon boost (it was very subtle without it). I used the almonds and added a little vanilla. When I checked (the regular loaf) at 45 minutes it was done. Thanks!
This was really good. We had the odd craving to put peanuts on it, and it actually worked nicely! I also cut the cayenne in half.

What a great base for a pizza! We loved the goat cheese. With fat free cream cheese, this was super low fat.
