Dh loved this soup and said 5 stars.  I loved the ease of making the soup and taste was very good.  Thanks Chili Spice.  Made for my 3 chefs.

Very good.  I did pepper my chicken and used fresh salsa.  Next time I think I will also add a can of chilies to the chicken mixture.  I did not use fat-free half-and-half; I used regular half-and-half.  Don't like the ingredients used in fat free stuff.  Thanks for a great recipe.  Made for Ausie Swap Days of Christmas.

Good eggs!!!  We had these for lunch today.  The two of us ate the whole serving.  I did butter the toast before adding the cooked eggs.  I divided the eggs between 2 pieces of toast.  Made for teammate for 12 Days of Christmas.
A great snack that I made for my gift trays.  I had trouble getting the cranberries to adhere to the pretzels.  Very easy to make.  Thanks for posting Brooke.
Excellent.  We enjoyed these today.  I did sprinkle some cajun spice on ours before I sprinkled the sea salt.  Very good.  Thanks dreamer.

I absolutely loved these rolls.  And, the added bonus of being extremely easy.  I did not measure but just sprinkled on the parmesan cheese.  I did not add the seeds.  We also halved the recipe for the two of us.  Thanks loof!  Made for Best of 2008 Cookbooks Swap.

Excellent.  Quick and easy and most of delicious.  I cooked in 2 tablespoons butter instead of oil.   I doubled the garlic and only used 1 tablespoon of fresh lemon juice.  Great recipe.  Thanks Karen.  Made for Ausie Swap #26.

Fluffy and delicious potato.  I made as directed but did sprinkle the potatoes with sea salt before rolling in foil.  Mine baked in one hour and I used canola oil.   This is a great baked potato!  Made for The Best of 2008 Cookbook Swap.
Great potatoes.  I made with regular mayo - don't use the light or diet stuff.  Mine were done in 45 minutes.  I halved the recipe easily.  Thanks Jackie.  Made for The Best of 2008 Cookbook Swap.

Very Nice Appetizer. I halved the recipe easily for the two of us.   I think next time I would like to try them with white cheese such as Jack or Provolone along with the cream cheese.  Thanks Shelby Jo.  Made For The Best of 2008 Cookbook.

Great Sandwich.  I made as directed but cooked my sandwiches an extra 4 minutes before adding the cheese and bacon.  Tomatoes are not in season but they would be an excellent addition.  Thanks AD!
Made as a prize for The Best of 2008 Cookbook Swap.

We enjoyed this tonight for dinner.  Being a meat lover, DH suggested adding crumbled sausage or bacon and I do believe that would taste great.  To fix 2 servings, I used 2 medium brown potatoes and put them in a zip lock bag.  I added 1 T olive oil and mixed well and then added the cumin and black pepper and put on greased baking sheet.  I did not double the onions.  I left out green pepper due to personal preference and the tomato as they are not in season. Made 4 over easy eggs.   Made for Starry's win in The Best of 2008 Cookbook.

Dh loved this meal!  I used a pork roast as my tenderloins were right at 2 pounds.  My roast was just under 3 pounds.  I put on high for the first hour and then on low for time as indicated.  The meat just fell apart when carved and was so tender.  We topped with the juices. I used Baby Ray's as that is our favorite. Very tasty and easy meal.  Made for Spring PAC 2009.

Nice treat!  I used Pillsbury Creation Dough instead of crescent rolls and made then into 12 verses 24.  Mine baked in 14 minutes.   Next time I might put a small layer of italian dressing on each roll before adding feta mixture.  Thanks for a nice treat M2R!  Made for M2R's win in The Best of 2008 Cookbook Swap.

This made us a nice meal.  I doubled the red pepper flakes and made as directed. We served over nice.  Next time I would add chopped onion.  Thanks Barbry for sharing this recipe.  Made for her win in The Best of Cookbook 2008 Swap.

Very good brownie.  I made as directed and mine cooked in 26 minutes.  We like ours a bit more fudgey.  I liked the fact that they were made in a small pan since there is the two of us.  Thanks AP for a nice treat.   Made for AP's win in The Best of 2008 Cookbook Swap.

Excellent!  We had breakfast for dinner tonight and enjoyed these pancakes immensely!  I used all all-purpose flour.  I did not have buttermilk so I put 1 tablespoon white vinegar in 2% milk and let set for a bit. I then made as directed.  Thanks KCM.    I made this recipe as a thank you for kittycatmom adopting for Spring Pac 2009.

Very Good.  I just threw everything into a big baggie, mixed well  and then put in greased baking dish.  I did use less salt and doubled the olive oil.  I added mushrooms since I had some that I needed to use up.  Did not add the green pepper.  Thanks Sharon.  Made for Ausie Swap #28.

Very good.  We served over pasta.  We enjoyed this for dinner last evening and next time I will add some spice to it.  I think the addition of red pepper flakes would be wonderful. I believe I could cut down the butter for us also.  I did add the optional bread crumbs and recommend adding them. Nice and easy.   Thanks for a great meal 2Bleu!

Very Good.  I was pushed for time but I think this would be good over rice or pasta as Flying Chef suggested.  We just served with a vegetable.  I made as directed but used cream of mushrooms soup, added fresh garlic and used boneless chicken breasts.  Very good.  Thanks M2R.  Made for Auzie Swap #30.

Excellent!  We enjoyed this for dinner tonight.  I doubled the onion and used 1 1/2 large Arkansas tomatoes.  For the dressing I squeezed 1/2 of a lemon used Baby Ray's Hickory Brown Sugar b-que sauce.  Next time I will try Chipolte b-que sauce.  I think a little spice would be great.  Thanks CBM.   Made for Aussie Swap #30.

Very Good. I used hot chili sauce and at first just doubled the amount. We thought it was too bland so I added more; approx. 3/4 teaspoon or more. It was just the way we like it. Next time my husband would like me to add a jalapeno pepper. My battery was dead so I couldn't take a pic. Next time. Made for Ausie Swap #31.

Very Good WiGal.  We had for dinner with eggs.  Next time I would not cook the potatoes all the way done before adding to kielbasa mixture  -- they were a little mushy for us.  My husband added a few drops of hot sauce and said he thought that added to the recipe.  Thank you for a great meal.  Made for Ausie Swap #31.

Excellent!  We had these for dinner tonight.  I halved the recipe easily, using the whole can of chiles.  I used ground beef.  Since there were no instructions for the beef, I lightly browned it and then added the diced bacon and onions and finished until all were cooked and followed as directed.  Next time I would like to use shredded chicken vs. the ground chicken and add some mexican corn.  Didn't get to take pic.  Very good.  Made for Ausie Swap #33.
Very good.  We had for dinner tonight.  I had  4 large boneless chicken breasts so I doubled everything.  Thanks KK for a great dinner.  Made For Ausie Swap #33.
Nice Burger!  I made as directed except I used 2 yolks instead of 3 and 1/2 t. kosher salt since I had 1.25 pounds of meat.  Made for Ausie Swap #34. Thanks LIG.
Nice drink.  Made as directed.  We enjoyed this as an after dinner drink.  Thanks FT.  Made for Aussie Swap.
Eggs turned out nicely.  I did have trouble peeling the first egg but that rest peeled easily. So, it must of been the egg.  Thanks!  Made for the Best of 2009 Cookbook Swap.

Nice Soup!  I used all chicken broth, doubled the garlic and added crushed chili flakes.  While it was simmering I did have to add an additional can of chicken broth.  Tasty.  Made for Ausie Swap #37.

Very Nice.  I used about 2 pounds of bone-in chicken breasts and made the sauce as directed.  Kept some of the sauce aside for dipping. Chicken was very tender and flavorful  Yum!  Made for the Best of 2009 Cookbook Swap.

Very good.  We enjoyed with dinner tonight.  I made a few modification.  Since tomatoes are not in season I used 3/4  of a 10 ounce can of Rotel diced tomatoes w. chilies, in place of the tomato and chilies.  I  sliced the potato instead of using wedges.  I placed the potatoes in a baggie to mix ingredients instead of using a bowl.  Thanks for posting.  Made for The Best of 2009 Cookbook Swap.

Nice salad!  I added grilled chicken.  I just piled the ingredients onto 2 plates for DH and I for dinner.  I used Chipotle dressing and we just each added our own to our plate.  I don't like as much salad dressing as DH. Next time I would add some drained and rinsed black beans.  Made for The Best of 2009 Cookboook Swap.
Very good.  I like the cinnamon in the batter.  Used oat bran bread.  My husband put maple syrup on his.  Made for the Best of 2009 Cookbook Swap.

My husband really enjoyed this dish.  We both did agree that it was too saucy for us.  Next time for this amount of pasta, I will drain one of the cans of clams.  We used penne instead of ziti.  Maybe we are big eaters but this only made 2 servings for us.  Made for the Best of 2009 Cookbook Swap.

How easy is this?  My kind of recipe:) We enjoyed these rolls.  I didn't read the reviews and I thought, oh no, with the first rise but after the second rise they turned out wonderful.  Made for the Best 2009 Cookbook Swap.

We had this for dinner tonight and loved the ease of the recipe.  For us, 8 hours was too long - the veggies were over done. Next time I will probably cook 6 to 7 hours. I cut my meat into slices verses chunks.  I will defintely make again.  Thanks for posting.

Very good.  We had this dish with tuna steaks tonight.  I used canned black beans and canned corn as that is what I had on hand.  Did not add the green pepper but added the whole can of black beans.  Made for Ausie Swap #35.   Thanks for posting.
We enjoyed these for dinner.  I liked the addition of he flour.  I halved the recipe for us you 3 baking potatoes and used steak seasoning.  Nice.  Made for Ausie Swap #39.
We enjoyed this bread.  I thought it tasted like a cornbread.  Next time I would increase the dill weed.   Nice and easy to make.  Thanks Syd. Made for Ausie Swap 39.

Very nice drink.  My DH thought the oj was overpowering so next time I will get cut it to 1/2 cup.  I think this would be good with low fat milk also.  Thanks for posting.  Made for Auz/Nz Recipe Swap #40.
Nice side dish.  I used Italian seasoning instead of rosemary.  Next time I will cut back on the butter to 1 tablespoon.  Great recipe.  Made for Ausie Swap 41.

In a word - fantastic!  I did not think I would like this very much because I was worried it would be too lemony.  Definitely not the case.  I made as written but with just 3 T of oil and added some fresh thyme.   Thanks for posting, this is truly tasty!

Wonderful!  I made this a while back and loved it.  I did not use the feta or red pepper and used a bit less oil.  I loved the bright flavor from the lemon but not too sour or acidic.  Served over greens and really enjoyed it.  Thanks for posting, TeresaS, this is great.

Really good and simple recipe, took no time at all.  I followed it exactly and enjoyed it.  It's really rich so serve it with something to counteract the ultra rich flavor, maybe something with tomatoes.  Thanks for posting, BakinBaby!

I bought a lot of cans of hearts of palm after having a salad at a friend's dinner party - silly me, I forgot how much I love them.  I made this salad this week and followed your advice, JanuaryBride, I used 2 tablespoons each of oil, lemon (didn't have lime on hand) juice and orange juice.  This was so excellent!  And I loved how it did not need to marinate to develop the flavor.  I loved it so much I ate the entire thing myself in one sitting!  Easy and delicious, JanuaryBride, thank you for posting this terrific recipe!

I was impressed.  I didn't use cajun seasoning (didn't have any), but chili powder, season salt and onion powder, and cayenne.  I dried off the chickpeas, sprayed lightly with cooking spray and then sprinkled the spices on.  I had them on a jelly roll pan with parchment paper (no mess!!).  I did end up keeping them in for 60 minutes.  Very good.  Btw, if you want something crispy do not close it in a bag or tupperware or anything like that until thoroughly cooled.  Else, as others have stated they will soften.

This is a fantastic salad.  I did not change any ingredients, but I had read somewhere to massage it 5-6 minutes--so I did that.  My kale was not young, so I was a little worried about it.  Delicious!
Loved it! Followed the recipe exactly...Will make again. Would more finely chop onions....like mince...
We loved it!! Hour before it was cooked l added onion cut into wedges and half hour before it was cooked l added red caspcium.
This is wonderful. I would rate it 10 stars if l could. Will be making this again and again!!!!!
Loved it!! Quick and easy to prepare.

I tweaked the recipe a bit by:
a) using 4 cups leftover roasted chicken
b) doubling all the other ingredients (except oil)
c) adding 1/2+ cup greek olives

Then we put it all over farfalle. It was wonderful!

YUM!! I'm not sure that I used quite 2 pounds of potatoes and I skipped the onions, but I did everything else to the measurements specified. I used fresh squeezed orange juice too. The sauce was absolutely incredible, and we'll be making this often -- thank you for posting it!!

I skipped the cajun seasoning and added extra garlic. These were great and disappeared fast! It was a huge added benefit that I could make the a couple of days ahead, so party day prep wasn't so hectic! Served them with yummy Philadelphia Dip! http://www.recipezaar.com/recipe/Philadelphia-Dip-303945

Fantastic! Served with homemade garlic bagel chips http://www.recipezaar.com/recipe/seasoned-bagel-chips-392849

Yum!! Update: I made this again, but this time I didn't have time to chop everything up, so I just threw it all in the food processor. I did the tomatoes first, then added the onions and olives and processed again, then added the softened cream cheese and sour cream. Worked like a charm!

This was smooth, creamy, light and delicious! I used a variety of 5 small (4"-6") eggplants (I have no idea how much this weighs) and added a touch extra lemon juice and parsley, but otherwise followed instructions exactly. I also peeled the eggplants. I will absolutely make this again and again - it's so great!! The only other note is that the prep/cook time isn't correct if you count in the cooking time of the eggplant for 20-25 min first. Next time I may double and roast the garlic too.
Made these last night for a BBQ - followed directions using whole wheat tortillas.  They were a HIT - all were eaten!  SUPER RECIPE!  Thanks!

This was good!  I followed the directions as written except I didn't have any carrots on hand.  Also, I added a medium thinly sliced onion.  Flavor was wonderful.  My husband LOVED this and says he prefers it to our local Chinese take-out.  My only complaints (small as they may be) is that it made way too much sauce, which was thin, & it wasn't nearly spicy enough for me.  These small things are easy enough to tweak to my preference the next time that I make this dish (which I will).  Thanks for this healthy recipe!!!!

This was very good!  I made exactly as directed except I substituted turkey kielbasa for the beef.  We had company over for supper, and this was filling and hearty and everyone loved the flavors.  It was not soupy or goupy - it was thick and rich.  As suggested, I served with cornbread.  I also served with cauliflower and green salad.  This wasn't terribly spicy, which I appreciated.  Those who like spicier foods may want to add some red pepper flakes or hotter peppers.  Thanks for a great recipe!  I took a photo while it was still in my pot!

This was delicious!  I LOVE Brussels Sprouts (as does my hubby), so this was a great veggie to have with a sandwich for lunch.  I used a whole jalapeno, and this dish was VERY spicy (I like spicy).  I would suggest modifying what kind of pepper you're using to control the heat factor.  I followed the recipe exactly as written (jalapeno for chili pepper) and I wouldn't change a thing.  Made for Please Review My Recipe Tag Game 1/7/09.
SOOOOO good!  I used homemade meatballs and left-over spaghetti sauce for the filling, and this was delicious!  I WILL MAKE THIS AGAIN!  Made for PRMR Tag Game.  I wish I had made more!

REALLY enjoyed this meal - it was simple to throw together, made the house smell fabulous all day as it cooked, and was tender, delicious and filling!  Hubby has already asked me to keep this recipe and to make it again.  I followed the directions exactly - cooked on low for 7 hours - came out perfectly!  Made for 1-2-3 Hits Tag Game 1/14/09.

Super-dooper scrumptious chocolately peanutbuttery goodness!  These brownies were GREAT!  Made with common household ingredients, quick to put together, these will be made again in my kitchen.  I did have to cook about 5 minutes longer than the directions stated, but they were well worth the wait.  Fabulous recipe, thanks for sharing!  Made for 1-2-3 Hits Tag Game 1/14/09.

Very easy meatloaf to put together.  I appreciated that it only used 1 lb of hamburger as it was just my husband and I eating (instead of one of the huge meatloaves) as we still had left-overs.  I followed as directed except I added some tomato sauce to the outside of the loaf.  Made for New Kids On The Block Tag Game, 1/15/09 - NELady.

This was very good.  I made a couple of changes - I used steak strips instead of ground beef.  Also, I forgot about the red pepper until after the pizza had already come out of the oven, so I chopped it up and put it on top raw.  I rather liked the crisp crunch of the raw pepper, but I think next time I would pay more attention to the recipe when I was cooking.  Also, I added green onions to the onions because I love green onions and I had a bunch to use in the refrigerator.  I served the garlic yogurt on the side as a dip.  It was very flavorful!  I used whole wheat pitas.   All in all, a treat for lunch!  Made for Please Review My Recipe Tag Game, 1/17/09 - NELady.

Easy to put together & tasty.  I didn't have any grape jelly, so I made three different kinds of cookies with raspberry, strawberry & blueberry jelly.  Yum!  Made for Please Review My Recipe Tag Game, 1/16/09 - NELady.

This recipe had great flavor, but I couldn't get a thick gravy out of it - it was more like chicken soup (which is still good) with dumplings.  Very labor intensive (I started from the beginning) so I don't think I would make this very often.  I loved the green onions in the dumplings - the dumplings were very good.  I made exactly as directed.  Made for Please Review My Recipe Tag Game 1/19/09 - NELady.

These were very good... great little burgers. I used toasted whole wheat dinner rolls for buns and omitted the tomato paste - other than that, I followed as directed. I served with a vegetable medly and salad. I LOVED all the onion in the burger! Made for 1-2-3 Hits Tag Game, 1/21/09 - NELady.  REVISING - I had extra cheeseburgers and sent them over to my hubby's Uncle's house (single guy) - about 20 minutes later he called to say they were the best cheeseburgers he has ever eaten - and he's eaten a lot!  I previously rated these burgers a 4, but after hearing everyone else ohhh and awww over these I am raising my rating to 5 stars! 1/22/09 - NELady

This was delicious!  I used whole wheat tortillas instead of regular flour tortillas, and added some onion into the chicken mixture.  Other than that, I followed the recipe as directed.  I used a mild salsa but next time will use a medium or hot (since this is so cheesy, it will balance out the heat).  Great stuff!  Made for PRMR, 1/26/09 - NELady.

These were very good ribs.  I used Kraft Hickory Smoked BBQ Sauce (it was in the pantry), and the ribs just about fell off the bone.  They were as good as any pork rib I've ever eaten.  Made for 1-2-3 Hits! Tag Game, 1/26/09 - NELady.

This was quite good.  The hamburger patty was flavorful.  I didn't really like the sweet & sour onions on first taste, but as I kept eating them, they really grew on me.  Good stuff!  Made for 1-2-3 Hits! Tag Game, 2/5/09 - NELady
This was good chicken - a little spicy, lots of flavor.  I made as directed except I used parmesan instead of romano cheese.  I would recommend this dish.  Made for Newest Tag Game.

I never use taco seasoning packets from the store because they're too expensive and I can't control the ingredients.  This is one of many seasoning mixes I've tried on 'Zaar, and I wasn't disappointed at all!  It was very good - you could really taste the cumin.  I didn't use the cumin seed, but did use the cayenne pepper for some heat.  Also, I doubled the dried onion flakes (personal preference for all things oniony).  Made great taco meat for my taco salad.  Made for Photo Tag.

This was very good and very simple to make.  Next time I would add a little cinnamon (don't know why I think that apple sauce should always have cinnamon - must be a personal preference).  Made for Newest 'Zaar Tag.

Fabulous!  I love the nutty crunch of the pistachios on the pork chops... really a nice way to amp up breaded pork chops.  I, like another reviewer, cut the recipe in half as I was only cooking for 2.  I followed the recipe as stated and wouldn't change a thing!  Made for 1-2-3 Hits Tag Game.

These taste delicious - even if they are kind of labor intensive.  A great project when you're home all day with nothing to do but bake up a tasty treat!  I didn't use any walnuts (I'm cooking for my in-laws, and they won't eat them).  The second layer (caramel) was much easier for me when I used my hands to spread the mixture over the chocolate layer - I got it to spread pretty evenly.  I dyed my icing green (for St. Patrick's Day) and TRIED (emphasis on tried) to draw a shamrock with the chocolate garnish. Made for PRMR Tag Game.

These mashed potatoes were very creamy and very good - and SUPER filling (I could only eat a couple small spoonfuls because they were so rich).  Next time I would cut back on the cream cheese a little bit because I found them just slightly too rich for my tastes.  They went wonderfully with meatloaf!  I followed the recipe exactly (using fat free cream cheese) and I sprinkled a handful of cheddar over the top after I had mashed them (less than 1/4 cup - just what was left over from a different recipe).  Thanks for sharing this great mashed potatoes recipe!  Made for PRMR Tag Game,.

These were good nuggets - I made them over the weekend.  Perfect munchie food for a snow storm!  I made as directed, and wouldn't change a thing except suggesting to bake the nuggets a little longer so they get crispier/crunchier!  Thanks for a fun recipe!  Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders Tag Game.

Fast, easy, inexpensive and filling - a great quick, crowd-pleasing meal!  I made as directed, omitting the green pepper as I didn't have any and couldn't make it through the snow to the store.  Good stuff!  Made for PRMR Tag Game!

Wow - what is not to love about this recipe?  DELICIOUS!  I used real pepperoni instead of turkey as it was what I had on hand, and regular mozzarella.  Gooey and cheesy and I'm thinking about picking up the ingredients to make it again next time I go grocery shopping!  Made for PRMR Tag Game!

I love the texture of this bean dip - it is very, very creamy.  I used my blender to process this smooth, and am glad that I did.  I used organic pinto beans, omitted the cilantro (we don't like it very well) and doubled the spice mixture.  I think next time I would add more of the spice mixture.  I used Pace Organics Medium Salsa.  Made for Photo Tag.

I had to try grilled watermelon - which, hubby and I decided, isn't for us (though it isn't disgusting or anything). I had a little left-over pineapple and decided to throw it on the grill with the watermelon (I've never grilled any fruit before) and it turns out that we LOVE grilled pineapple - so I'm delighted that I tried this recipe! Made for ZWT5, and I'm a Groovy GastroGnome!
DELICIOUS!  What a groovy way to cook corn!  I made as directed - I wouldn't change a thing!  I'm making this one again, and passing along the recipe to my mom! Groovy GastroGnomes, ZWT5.

Easy marinade that made for a great steak!  I subbed fresh snipped chives for the green onions (as I didn't put green onions on my shopping list earlier today), but other than that, I followed the recipe to a T - I even used the reduced sodium soy sauce.  YUMMY!  I let my steaks marinade for about 3 hours, turning them every once in a while.  It was nice to cook a recipe designed for two people.  Spraying the grill with non-stick spray really worked - I was worried that with the honey it was going to stick and burn on the grill, but it didn't (I used high heat Canola oil non-stick spray).  I liked the hint of sweetness the honey brought - plus, I love the beautiful glaze the marinade gave to the steak (my picture really doesn't do it justice).  I made this while touring Australia on ZWT5 for the Groovy GastroGnomes.  Thanks for a nice recipe!

I used this marinade for top sirloin steaks I was grilling - I marinated for about 5 hours.  I halved the recipe, but other than that, followed the directions exactly.  This was very flavorful (smelled wonderful) and I liked the combination of herbs - I don't usually use basil and rosemary on steak.  The lemon juice helped tenderize the steak and gave a nice citrus zing.  I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this marinade.  Groovy GastroGnomes, ZWT5.

Enjoyed this grilled corn very much.  I cut down on the spice & hot sauce a little bit (I'm a chicken!), and added some chopped parsley.  I wrapped the corn in tin foil before throwing it on the grill.  Great side dish!  Made for The Groovy GastroGnomes, ZWT5!

YUMMY!  I made these to go along with recipe #177849.  Since the oven was already going to be on, I baked these potatoes instead of grilling them (350*F for 70 minutes - they cooked along side the meatloaf).  I only cooked 2 potatoes (2 of us eating) and wrapped each potato with 2 slices of bacon.  Other than that, I followed the recipe exactly.  I really enjoyed the subtle hint of cilantro - I was worried the herb would overpower everything else, but it didn't.  A nice change of pace for baked potatoes, simple to prepare, and really pretty on the plate (please see my picture of the "final product").  Great recipe!  Made for the Groovy GastroGnomes of ZWT5!

I halved the recipe, stirred in some fresh chopped cilantro right before serving - but other than that, followed the recipe to a "T".  Delicate and flavorful, this was a perfect side to my cajun soft tacos!  YUMMY!  Made for the Groovy GastroGnomes of ZWT5!

I don't eat deviled eggs (I know, I've heard it before, everyone loves deviled eggs - except me!), but I had extra eggs and made these for my husband, who is a deviled-egg-kinda-guy.  He said they were good (ate them all, too) but said he preferred deviled eggs with mustard vs. butter.  Next time I will sub out the butter with mustard.  He liked the addition of the stuffed olives.  I followed the recipe as instructed except I sprinkled the eggs with paprika (old habits die hard!) and garnished with some chopped green onion.  Made for the Groovy GastroGnomes, ZWT5.

These were a breeze to make and flew off the plate!  We ate all of these potato wedges.  I used olive oil instead of canola oil (I misread the ingredients), but they were still fantastic.  I was hesitant about using a lot of the creole seasoning, but they turned out just about perfect with great flavor and a hint of spice.  I will make these again - and soon - I have a 10 lb bag of potatoes sitting in the pantry that need to be used up soon!  Made for the Groovy GastroGnomes, ZWT5.

Simple to prepare, yummy to eat.  Good combination!  I subbed chicken broth for white wine & omitted the cornstarch.  I had some left-over white rice I stirred in before serving, and that was delicious.  I chopped up some green onion and threw it on top for garnish and a little zing.  Good stuff!  Made for the Groovy GastroGnomes of ZWT5!

I'm typing this review as I'm munching on chips and salsa.  I REALLY liked this salsa - but I had to make a couple of changes to suit our tastes (and what was in the refrigerator).  I omitted the tequila - I don't drink so I didn't have any in the house.  Second, I subbed jalapenos for the habanero peppers (we are much too timid for habanero heat!).  I threw everything else into my blender and pulsed it to do the chopping for me.  Loved the olives, cumin & lime.  Made for the 2nd part of the Salsa! Challenge of the ZWT5, representing the Groovy GastroGnomes.

Delicious!  I cut the recipe down to 1 lb of flank steak (which was one pretty large steak).  I used Wyoming grass-fed free-range beef.  I followed the marinade exactly (other than cutting it in half).  Wowzers!  Does this pack a lot of flavor!  I marinated overnight and let the steak sit out on my counter for about 3 hours until I was ready to grill it up for lunch.  I have another flank steak in the freezer, and I'm planning on using this recipe again to prepare it.  I did forget to add the salt and pepper to the steak while I was grilling it, but it came out wonderfully despite of my error.  I'm a Groovy GastroGnome travelling the ZWT5.  Thanks for posting this tasty recipe for the tour!
Nice, simple classic!  Loved this for a quick snack!  Served with Recipe #372013.  Easy to switch up with chicken or beef, too.  Thanks!  Made for the Groovy GastroGnomes of ZWT5!

I followed the recipe as directed and was very pleased with the result - they were creamy and delicious.  My hubby said he preferred my "regular" mashed potatoes.  I thought these were nice for a different approach to mashed potatoes.  Made for the Groovy GastroGnomes, Family Picks ZWT5.

Loved this french bread!  I dusted mine with garlic powder after I brushed on the olive oil and I sprinkled some parsley over it, too.  DELICIOUS!  Five stars all the way!  I will use this recipe all summer long.  Made for the Groovy GastroGnomes, Zingo ZWT5!

I used bone-in thighs (trimmed of the fat).  I subbed chicken broth for the bouillon/water, added some green onion, subbed corn for hominy, and threw in a jalapeno pepper that needed to be used.  I loved the hit of lime at the end - yummmm!  I served with recipe #308361 & recipe #321401.  Made for the Groovy GastroGnomes, Zingo ZWT5.

Very easy to prepare and quite tasty.  I made exactly as directed except I garnished with parsley and chopped green onion.  I used free-range salt-free chicken broth, so I had to add a quite a bit of salt after I mixed it. Hi Chef in UK

Kudos to you for posting this recipe.  It is long and involved the first time you make it.  But incredibly easy and just wonderful bread.  .This is the BEST way to make bread.  I found the book while browsing in a bookstore about a year ago.  It is tremendous.  No matter what I did to bread it came out hard and rather tasteless.  Fancy flours and additions, bread machines, hand , or mixers.  Nothing helped.  Until I tried this recipe.  Have not looked back.  There are just 2 of us and often I simply halve the recipe.  The longer it sits in the fridge the more like sourdough.  Don't forget to let the bread sit for at least an hour after baking. Hard to do lol-- The crumb will be much improved.  I have made many variations on this bread. Sweet, savory, fruit and nut , whole grain, multi grain and seed, rye.  It seems that it really can't be ruined as long as you follow the basic proportions of flours and liquids salt and yeast.  I also find that if the dough rests in the fridge for at least 6-12 hours that improves it overall.  Panetonne had always seemed daunting until this recipe came along.  

The book is very helpful at debunking old ideas about flours and breads.  Simply explains the science, their journey in coming up with this method, and, as you said, wonderful varieties of sweet to savoury to just "plain" white bread.  
Thank you again for posting.  I do hope lots of people will try this.  Saves time and $$$ and with great results almost guaranteed.
Judy in CA by way of WA

It took me longer to get off the wax paper and wrapped that it did to make it.  I have another batch cooling - this time in quick release tin foil that has been sprayed.  Hopefully that will work better.

This was really good.  My DH, who doesn't eat cooked broccoli had two dishes and said - this is good.  Believe me that is ten stars coming from him.  Mine curdled a little too, don't know why unless I simmered it on too high a heat, but didn't affect the taste at all.  I also made this on the stove.  I will be making this again and again.  May add chedder cheese soup in place of the velveeta sometime.

Can't believe I forgot to review this.  This stuff is great.  I love that you don't get that greasy feel like when you eat tacos.  I made taco salad.  Even my carnivore DH liked it.  Somebody suggested using this for ground beef stroganoff.  Can't wait to try it.  Thanks Dixon.  Just made this for about the 4th time.  I still haven't had the nerve to tell my DH there's no meat in his taco salads, but he raves about this every time I make it.  I make dog food for my three furbabies, however, tonight I didn't have any made up for them, so gave them a heaping spoon of the taco "meat" mixed with their dry dog food and a little water and they all scarfed it down, even my pickie little Yorkie.  So this not only gets five stars, but 12 paws up also.

This was pretty good.  I think I'll add garlic next time and maybe cut down on the lemon.  I'm not sure I liked the lemon, but loved the chickpeas.  May add some mushrooms also.  Thanks for the recipe Mirj.  I'll be making this again.
Oh wow - this is great.  Perfect for when you just gotta have some chocolate.  We ate it right out of the microwave with a little butter (I know not quite vegan).

This was really good.  I added the tomatoes and green chilies and cheese.  I used Ragout sauce instead of Marinara as that is what I had on hand.  It smelled amazing while it was cooking and tasted even better.  Thanks for a great recipe.

OMG this is so good.  I used low sodium soy sauce and added 1/4 cup water as some reviewers said this was too salty.  I loved it.  Even ate the leftovers cold.  I could have eaten the whole 16 ounces in one sitting easily, but thought I probably better not. I also didn't add any oil, as I didn't have sesame oil, but will add it next time. Can only make it better.

I made this with turkey bacon.  I think it would have been better with regular bacon, but was still amazing. DH said - this is good and believe me, that is huge praise.   I made this  for Pammyowl's Cookathon.  Pam I  wish you were here to read your reviews.  You will be so  missed.
Another yummy recipe.  Loved the mustard and honey together.  I did omit the cayenne pepper though.  Made for Pammyowl's Cookathon
My rice turned out perfectly.  Thanks for a great recipe

Wow, this recipe is amazing!  I've been trying to find a good banana recipe for a while (I keep ending up with the remains of the kids' fruit trolley at school, lol), and this is definitely the best.  I like the banana layer so much that the second time I made it, I didn't even use the cocoa powder!  The only change I made was to use low-fat vanilla yogurt instead of margarine (because I didn't have any) and it still turned out really nice and moist.  Thanks for a great recipe!

I'm so glad I'm not the only person who does this- everyone at uni thinks I'm really weird when I bring oatmeal with me for lunch and just add boiling water!  I love it though, it really gives you energy.  Thanks for posting :).

These were delicious!  They're my favourite thing to order at Chinese restaurants and they tasted even better homemade.  My whole family loved them, thanks for posting.  I also wanted to thank you for trying and reviewing my recipes, I'm really glad you enjoyed them.  Thanks again!

Great concept! Made this for dinner last night. My bf and I are both huge mushroom lovers so you can't go wrong there, but we felt the sauce was a bit to sour for our tastes. (I know, what do you expect with sour cream, right?) He suggested that next time I add cream cheese to make it a little creamier.

I have never made gnocchi before and was kind of intimidated to try it but this couldn't have been easier! I cooked them as directed then tossed in a pan with garlic, butter, fresh thyme and baby Portabellas. SOOO GOOD! This is definitely going into regular rotation.

This was definitely a step up from regular instant mashed potatoes. The simplicity of this recipe alone makes it worth making again. Next time I will probably add more garlic for a bit more flavor. I ended up having to use a total of 3 Tbs butter to get the creaminess I wanted. Overall, great dish.

I've been making this for years. Not sure where I got the recipe but it is super simple to throw together for lunch or a late dinner. The flavors speak for themselves. Great to see that others enjoy it as well.

I'm not kidding when I say these are the best red potatoes we've ever had! This recipe has the perfect amount of everything... lemon being really important and I highly recommend squeezing a little extra lemon when the potatoes are done. Also, perfect amount of garlic and oregano, which can be overdone. Thank you for a keeper!
Thanks for coming to my rescue! This made a nice dinner. I didn't have any mushrooms but it was great without them. Thanks!
Very good. Two of my favorites-black beans and avocados. Very healthy, too.

This was very good. We BBQ'd the chicken thighs first because it sounded good then just sliced the chicken and threw it all in to simmer for 15 minutes. I liked the extra flavor but still needed to add a pinch more spice as it was a little flat. Maybe next time I'll put in less coconut milk and more chutney.

These were really good. I adore string beans so I'm always thinking of different way to serve them. I left out the salt for the hubby and they were still really good. I only had to blanch them for six minutes. Thanks for posting this recipe.

This is a winner. I took it down to my neighbors house last night and we munched on them while drinking margaritas. The cinnamon added a great litle sweetness.

I accidently dropped one on the floor and called there Chocolate Lab "Reble" over to eat it, Robbie (neighbor) was fast to say that he wouldn't eat it because he didn't like Sweet Potatoes. I replied he likes mine. Reble ate it and then promptly asked for more.
I did mess up because I addedd a little more oil because I thought the seasonings weren't coasting the potatoes enough. Next time I will know better.
Awesome! Very easy and quick. I am fixing again next week for company.

Another winner. The suace on this is great. I might add a little more sun-dried tomatoes and pancetta next time but definately will do this again. It was a little dry so I will just not cook as long next time. Perfect for a brunch. Made for Fall PAC 2008.

I made this as directed, except I used parmesean instead of asiago since it was what I had on hand! This is a very versatile dish. I can make it fast on a weeknight after work, but it tastes "fancy" enough that it would be appropriate for guests as well! Thanks!

It is August in Memphis ladies and gentlemen and it is HOT HOT HOT! This is the perfect beat the heat beverage! I made it with unsweetened tea, that I had in the fridge and vanilla ice cream as well! So good! Thanks for sharing! Next time I make it I will use raspberry sorbet for a raspberry tea shake! Can't wait!

This was very simple and straight up good! We used penne pasta since it is what we had on hand and it was just sooo good! It came together in about 20 minutes for me (I used peeled deviened frozen shrimp) and it was greatly enjoyed! DH loved it; I loved it and we will be making this many many times in the future! Also, although it is simple to make, the colors are so pretty together -- this is a perfect dish for guests too! [Made for Newest Zaar Tag]

I made this last night for dinner and it was perfect! I also used chicken tenders and they cooked for about ten minutes. We like things on the spicier side so I used about 5 generous shakes of the cayenne pepper shaker! Other than that, made exactly as directed! Thanks for a great recipe! [Made for I Recommend Tag]

I made this with left over egg noodles from our beef stroganoff last night -- very simple and easy! The taste is simple too -- but just enough to be a delicious dinner side -- or pasta salad lunch the next day! :) Thanks for a great recipe! Made for newest zaar tag!

This is an amazing potato dish! I made it last night for my DH who can only eat soft foods right due to surgery so I made it with instant potatoes to avoid any lumps! He at every single but of it (a feat right now) and asked for seconds! I snuck a few bites in as well and I have to say yum yum! This is such an excellent alternative to mashed potatoes! Just a little something extra and I love the little crust that forms on top! Mmm mmm good! [Made for 1-2-3 Hits tag game!]

I made this last night for dinner with a serving of Recipe #387727 so I did not use the egg coating. This was a wonderful blend of sweet and salty together! Mmm... I loved it! I made it with my favorite strawberry peach preserves my friend Libba makes and gives me! So perfect.

I made this to enjoy this weekend during the college football madness that ensues in our house every Saturday in the fall! These were delicious! It is great because my DH is very picky and I am not! I added a little bit of turkey chili I had leftover to the top of mine and turned the plain avocado into guacomole! Yum! Made for Holiday Tag 2009!

This was very good! I also used low-sodium soy sauce. I doubled the garlic added some crushed red pepper and some cayenne to give it a little kick! Next time I will add some ginger as others have suggested! This is a nice recipe to have since I can make on a Sunday with little monitoring and freeze it with some stir fry veggies then reheat later on in the week. Thanks for a recipe I am sure I will use again! [Made for PRMR recipe tag]

This is delicious! Peanut butter and honey has always been a favorite of mine, but I love the addition of the cinnamon! so good! I left the apple juice out since I was spreading mine on toast and not apples! This is great comfort food with tea! Thanks for posting! [Made for Potluck Tag 2009]

This gets four stars for simplcity and ease. I used homemade pizza sauce (I don't like raw tomatoes) and I used a small amount of pizza dough b/c I had the time. This will be a staple for me. DH travels a lot for work, so this is a great "dinner for one" recipe as well as a wonderful lunch recipe. I might try bringing the basil garlic salt pepper in a container and the cheese in another and the sauce in a third (small of course) and assembling at work and microwaving! Thanks for a great recipe! [Made for HolidayTag Fall 2009]

I finally gave in and tried this sandwich last night for dinner. I used wheat bread and I added a little squirt of mustard (can't eat a sandwich without it). I like neither eggs nor tomatoes and this was a delicious sandwich! I was so excited when I bit in and it was just so yummy! Something about the combo is just amazing! I will be eating this very often! Thank you so much!!!

I am not sure who or what Raising Cane is -- but his sauce is delicious! I made homemade chicken nuggets last night and they tasted sooooo good with the sauce! I love also that this is made with simple ingredients I always have on hand in my kitchen! Thanks for a great sauce! [Made for Potluck Tag]

I made these for a surprise last night for DH -- we normally don't have dessert on weeknights. These are easy to put together and they taste delicious. I topped with strawberry jam instead of pine nuts. I also halved the recipe since it is just two of us. Thanks for a great recipe!!! [Made for Holiday Tag Fall 2009]

I do something very similar to this as well -- about once every two weeks I cook a big box of penne noodles and some sort of veggie (usually peas or broccoli) that I throw in during the last few minutes of boiling -- then we have it available in the fridge throughtout the weeks for quick lunches, sometimes we throw together alfredo, or just butter and parm cheese. So this group is a great way for me to get new ideas. Which I love. For today's lunch I had the mediterranean option, and this weeks pasta has peas in it so I left the arugula out, added a wee bit of mayo, red wine vinegar and some oregano! Mmmm! This was sooo good! Thanks for posting all these yummy options! :) [Made for 123 Hits]

Great way to dress up a boxed stuffing! I love these kinds of recipes! Sometimes I like the time/labor intensive "real" stuff, but this is great! You never would guess it came from a box and it is nice enough to serve to dinner guests! I did not use celery as we are not huge fans and I did not have any on hand! I left out the butter and used half the oil and this was still perfect! Thanks for posting! [Made for Holiday Tag]

Easy peasy lemon squeazy! We had this for dinner last week and since I made the noodles the night before and left them in the fridge, I dumped the noodles in cold (cooked the shrooms all day long with the chicken) and turned the crock pot up to high -- for about 25 minutes. Perfection! This is a DEFINITE keeper meal I will make again and again! Thanks!

This salad is (I fear) simply addicting! The only change I made was to omit the sugar and add one packet of the pink fake sugar stuff! We had this last night with spaghetti for dinner and it was a perfect little side salad! DH did not eat his -- so guess what I get to have for lunch today? mmmmm! HIghly recommended! Thanks for posting! [Made for Holiday Tag Fall 2009]

Super simple -- great for a weeknight and we loved the flavor! We omitted the tomato and added some sweet basil before we cooked it. I cooked in a 425F oven top rack for 12 minutes and it came out perfectly. Made for Holiday Tag October 2009

Sour pink is right! :) Lip puckering and sooo good! I really really enjoyed this! I also added about 1/2 tsp raspberry liquer to this b/c I only had regular cranberry juice! I will definitely make this again... tonight possibly... Made for THINK PINK event for Breast Cancer Awareness, October 2009!

This is a very delicious bread. I used my batter to make muffins. They are perfect, and in my opinion just the way a muffing should be! Kind of crusty on the outside but fluffy and tender on the inside! I might add some red food coloring to the batter next time to make it more "pink". This gave me 12 muffins perfectly cooked after 23 minutes! Thanks Starry!!!
Ole!!! These are so good and so easy! I think I might try making these and then freezing them, then when you want taco night - thaw and bake! Perfect! Thanks for posting Coffee!

This was a nice drink! DH liked it a lot more than I did, it was a little bitter for my taste, so I added about 1/2 of a packet of sweet-n-low to it and that made it a lot more palatable for me! I think it had a lot to do with the orange juice I used, a brand tha generally tastes bitter to me, so next time I will try it with a sweeter juice. DH loved this though! :) Thanks for posting Boomette! Made for Holiday Tag Fall 2009!
This is warm and delicious goodness! We actually had this as a desert instead of breakfast! It is great warm with some vanilla icecream! Thanks for posting!

These are super! I really loved them! I made four of them (2 of us) and I used swiss = cheddar and I added minced garlic between the layers (we LOVE garlice)! I love all of the different possibilities!!! Thanks for posting! [Made for Holiday Tag October 2009!]

I loved these Loula! Crunchity Crispity! Perfect for dunking in a glass of ice cold milk (which I propose can and should only be done with a cookie of a certain texture!)! Made for Holiday tag October 2009!

This was great this morning on the way to work! I made as directed except made 2 cups of coffee, since it was only for me! I loved the smell of the cinnamon coffee and the taste! I can't wait for it to get really cold so I can enjoy a steaming mug of this under a cozy blanket! Thanks for posting Hokies! Love it! Made for Sweet Traditions Tag Game November & December 2009!

This was a really great dish. I used chicken broth in place of the wine as well. I also sprinkled my chicken breasts with a little flour, salt and pepper before cooking. We really enjoyed this dish. It is light tasting and not heavy at all. I served mine over penne pasta with broccoli. Thanks for posting! Made for Holiday Tag November 2009!
Perfect! I cut this down to about a quarter. This was perfect bed time treat to enjoy while watching some TV and snuggling under the covers! Thanks for posting! Made for Sweet Traditions tag game!
I enjoyed this immensely as a breakfast shake this morning! The other portions have been frozen for next week! :) I added one scoop of protein powder! Thanks for posting! Made for 1-2-3 Hits Tag!

20 Stars! This was awesome! I used some four cheese & garlic bread I had made earlier in the week, I sliced it very thin and then in half to make small pieces of bread. Then I put a scoop of the cheese/onion/chive mixture on each and toasted them in the same pan I used for the onions. I used a mix of shredded swiss and sharp cheddar cheese and added about 1T of mayo to the mix. These were amazing little bites and I wish I had made more. The flavor is rich and oustanding. Perfect! Thanks for posting Kate! Made for Holiday Tag November 2009!

These we sooooo good! We had them with some beef stew and the really made a great pair for that! I used the dough for regular french bread (about a 1 pound loaf cut in half) out of my ABM. I kept all the seasonings the same. I will make these again and again and again! Thanks for posting Diner!

We had these with our steak dinner last night. I made four potatoes resulting in 8 halves and cut the amounts of the filling ingredients down accordingly. We ate one each with dinner and the rest are in my freezer for a busy night! Thanks for posting! Made for Holiday Tag November 2009!

This was so easy and sooooo good. I subbed Lima beans for the fava beans, because I could not find them (and to be honest I am obsessed with lima beans). I love the use of the chicken broth here. It adds a whole different dimension. I subbed Cavender's Greek seasoning for the S&P and we ate the whole entire dish! I will be making these a lot! Thanks for posting! Made for Holiday Tag 2009!

I made these over the Thanksgiving Holiday weekend to take to my mom and dad's house. These were very good and as the recipe states -- very sweet. I used cherry faloverd craisins for the glace cherries. These are very good! Thanks for posting! Made for Sweet Traditions game November 2009.

Oh goody goody gum-drops! This was one delicious pizza! I used whole wheat flour and bread flour, about 2 cups whole wheat and 1 cup bread and then added water and olive oil as needed. I also dumped about two TBS of italian seasoning into the dough mix as well. This made enough for two pizzas - we have half the dough frozen for later.  We did omit the zucchini as we are not big fans, and added some mushrooms (can't get enough of these). I used mozzarella, gouda and mix of romano and parmesan cheeses for the third. I loved the fresh sliced mozzarella especially! Mmmm. Such a nice change from our normal Turkey Pepperoni! Thanks for posting Loula! Made for Holiday Tag 2009!

I am not sure on the coffee to water ratio. I think that is fairly subjective depending on how strong you like it! :) I Just used the same amount of coffee and water I normally use to make my coffee (8 cups water to about 4 heaping TBS of coffee and then brew on the strong setting my machine has) and added the other ingredients before brewing! This was absolutely amazing! Chocolate peppermint is the one type of flavored coffee I really enjoy! I LOVE the peppermint mochas from Starbucks -- but can only get them at Christmastime! Now I can have them all year long! DH loved this too! :) I did not use the whipped cream (this was to-go in the car this morning) but added a little halfandhalf as I normally do! Thanks for posting this amazing coffee recipe! I love it! Made for Holiday tag December 2009!

Gosh this is so lip smacking good! This was a wonderful dinner for a cold rainy night! I subbed in prepared salsa, but when I have more time I will make the salsa fresh because it sounds so yummy! I took the recommendation to use lime juice while pan frying the chicken! It is so good! Just a hint of lime! Served as directed with the addition of a smally dollop of sour cream. Oh yeah, I am enjoying this for lunch right now again! :) Thanks for posting! Made for 1-2-3 Hits December 2009!

This was the perfect salad. Other than skipping the tomatoes out of personal preference I made this as directed, including the anchovies, which I LOVE! The flavors were perfectly balanced and the anchovies added just a bit of saltiness here and there (although I admit I will double them next time because I seriously LOVE LOVE LOVE anchovies)! I ate so much of this I barely had room for the chicken and mashed potatoes! I am having it again for lunch today!!! Thanks for posting this tremendously outstanding recipe Andi!!! Made for Holiday Tag 2009!

Umm I am glad this recipe makes a lot (just the two of us, should have cut it in half) because SHOOIE this is good stuff! Made as directed, except with russet potatoes (had on hand) and I left the peels on b/c we love em. I would not change a thing! And we will be eating these a lot! I really can't see making "fancy" mashed taters another way now that I have eaten these!!! Thanks for posting this amazing recipe! Made for Holiday tag December 2009!

Yummy Yummy Yummy!!! I used ground turkey instead of the ground beef (trying to eat healthier) and used whole wheat bread crumbs that I seasoned with Italian seasoning and whole wheat buns! These were perfect, just a hint of sweetness that we loved! We will be making these again and again, by far our favorite way to eat turkey burgers because the marinade that we use for the ground beef burgers usually just does not translate well to the turkey for some reason, but this did! Can't wait to make again! Thanks for posting! :) Made for Holiday Tag 2009!

You really don't get much better than this on a FREEZING cold morning to keep you running throughout the morning! I added a sprinkle of cinnamon and topped with a sprinkle of raisins! Thanks for posting! Made for Holiday Tag December 2009!

This was really an easy five star meal. I used Recipe #35805 for the pizza dough, crushed pineapple (drained well on a paper towel), and I pinched the ends shut with a fork. I made four and froze two for DH to take for work lunch! Thanks for posting Shuz! Made for Holiday Tag December 2009!

Ok I admit it, it was freezing and rainy and plain yucky here this past weekend, so I drank this hot. It warmed me right up! I might try it with camomile tea next time to drink before bed time! I can't wait until the summer time so I can make the iced version! Thanks for posting! made for Holiday Tag December 2009!

I have been thinking all morning about how to rate this recipe -- I have had several things come to mind: 10+ stars, you know that Food Network show, Best Meal I Ever Ate?, the words divine, delicious and delectable don't begin to describe this. Ok, enough raving! I made as stated -- subbing peas for broccoli and 1% milk for the whipping cream. This was perfection in every warm and creamy amazing bite. Thanks for posting! This will become a regular in our household as both DH and I ate and ate until we could not eat anymore! Then we both snuck in a few more bites while cleaning up ;) [Made for Holiday Tag December 2009!]
These were so good and easy to make! I had never made them myself before and I had not had them in years! Thanks so much for posting! These are delicious, simple and easy!
Mmmmm! I used light mayo and added some salt and pepper! Went great over a green salad! Really perked it up more than my normal bottled dressing does! Thanks for posting!

Loved this variation on Chex-mix! made for DH to take to work for Christmas goodie bags so I quadrupled the recipe! And I did have to bake them in a rotation, but that's ok I was glad I made so much so I could keep some to munch on at home! We used something called wasabi bites. They worked well! Thanks for posting! [Made for Holiday Tag December 2009]

Easy peazy! Loved it! I used country ham (the real salty kind :yumy:) and shredded cheddar cheese! Loved that I had time to put this together -- stick in the oven and then finish my make-up before work and when I was done voila -- breakfast is served! My picky DH loved his too! Thanks for posting! Made for Holiday Tag December 2009!

I made two portions (the whole recipe but only divided into two) for lunch for DH and I last week! It was too cold for him to grill -- so we used the good ole George Forman which worked just fine. We left out the radish, tomato and potato simply due to personal preference! I also used splenda in place of the sugar! This was a great hearty salad that, with the addition of a french roll, kept me full until dinner time, but didn't make me feel so full I needed a nap during the work day! By the way -- I sent lunch packed this way: Salad in a big tupperware bowl, chicken (already sliced) in a zip lock to re heat in microwave and dressing in a separate container in order to keep everything as fresh as possible! Thanks for posting we will enjoy this many a time to come! Made for Holiday Tag 2009!

I made this to go with a pork tenderloin for dinner last night and it went perfectly! I have been making almost this same recipe for a long time and you are right -- the addition of the pickle juice and the worcetershire sauce makes all the difference. Thanks so much for posting! I will add these oh so important additions in the future! :) [Made for Holiday Tag December 2009]

Great flavor -- left in marinade for about 18 hours (bed time to dinner the next night in the fridge). This gave our meat (a nice pork tenderloin) a nice sweet (but not too sweet) flavor. I also added a bit of liquid smoke. This was great for both dinner and lunch today! Thanks for posting! Made for Holiday Tag 2009!

These are light and tender. I made these for our office holiday dinner last night (we do it at the boss's house every year between Christmas and New Years) and I was told in no uncertain terms that these would be repeated next year! Made as directed (in little balls) and they turned out great! Made for PRMR Tag December 2009!

Made this to go with our New Years Day brunch -- we used it to dip pieces of fresh fruit and our waffles (in lieu os syrup). The only change I made was to directly quarter the recipe, which worked out perfectly for the two of us! Thanks for posting! Made for PRMR tag January 2010!

We had this for our desert last night! Yum yum! Both DH and I loved it -- I left out the flaxseed because I couldn't find it at my local store (veeeeery small!) but I will go to the whole foods and check there and definitely have this again! I can't wait til it gets warmer and we can have this for breakfast! Thanks for posting! Made for Holiday Tag January 2009!

I won't be using any other egg salad from now on! I love the zip from the lemon and the flavor of the basil! Although, I admit I used dried basil. I did let this sit for about an hour in the fridge to let the flavors really blend since I did use the dried and it was just perfect! I used the whole wheat bread and lettuce, but no bean sprouts! Thanks for posting Andi! Made for Holiday Tag January 2010!

I too was a bachelorette for dinner last night and I really enjoyed this pizza for one! I made it on a Flat Out brand whole wheat flat bread. I left off the tomato for personal preference. So I did add a wee bit of marinara. I loved the sliced olives and mozarella!!! I also added a TON of basil because it's like catnip to me -- I can't get enough of it and about a tsp of minced garlic sprinkled over top of it! The rest I made as directed using low fat feta and about five spinach leaves. This was yummy! Thanks for posting this new combo! I will make this often even when DH returns from business! :) Made for Veggie Swap January 2010!

This did a great job! The only thing it did not get off is some cooked on coconut pecan frosting that boiled over about a month ago, that is like fossilized on there now. But it did get some of it off, so I think I will spend about 10 minutes a day with this stuff cleaning it and eventually it will come off. I also really enjoyed the lemon smell. It is my favorite way for my kitchen to smell, it's just a super clean scent! :) Thanks for posting! Made for Holiday Tag January 2010!

Perfect quick dinner last night. I used my own pizza crust I make in my ABM and used browned hamburger instead of the deli meat (it makes me sick for some reason) and this was yummy and cheesy and delicous! Thanks for posting! Made for PRMR Tag January 2010!

Oh. My. Goodness. This is so wonderful! Made for a wonderful Friday night dinner with DH! I used siracha (sp) hot chili sauce, not sure how much (just to taste) and used dried basil and fresh cilantro and used light coconut milk! I will say if you use the dried herbs, after you add the milk, make sure to simmer it for about ten minutes to let the flavor develop because it changes a lot! At first the coconut was very overwhelming and after simmering everything just blended perfectly and the flavors really shimmered in and out in a perfect blend! Served with sticky rice and can't wait to make again! :) Made for PRMR Tag January 2010!
Easy? You betcha? Delicious? Absolutely! Loved the grapes! I used rotisserie chicken! Thanks for posting! This is sure to be a lunchtime fave from now on! Made for Holiday Tag January 2010!

These were absolutely fantastic! These were perfect for a snowy morning when we couldn't get out of the house! I used pumpkin pie spice with a little extra cinnamon. Served with honey butter and cinnamon butter! They had a perfect texture and tasted a little like pumpkin pie! Can't wait to make them again! :) Made for Veggie Swap January 2010!

Great comfort food for a cold winter night! I steamed my chicken instead of frying (to save on fat) and sauted the veggies in a non stick pan with a spray of canola oil cooking spray and I used reduced fat-sour cream. This is a simple tasty easy peasy weeknight meal! Next time I think I might try brown rice! :) Thanks for posting! :)
Delicious! Made in the microwave, with 2 packets of splenda in place of the sugar! Great afternoon pick me up! Made for Holiday Tag February 2010!

I toasted my bread, left off the tomato and bean sprouts (we don't like them) and added a sprinkle of dill and oregano to the mayo/mustard. This was a yummy (and light) dinner last night with some baked chips! I did add some turkey to DH's per his request. I had mine straight veggie though and I really look forward to having this in the summertime! Thanks for posting --this will definitely become a staple sandwhich in our household! [Made for Holiday Tag February 2010]

This was enjoyed by all at my super bowl party! Added a little ranch dressing with the italian. And I cut up the onions into smaller pieces. Also I doubled the recipe for a larger bunch :) Thanks for posting! This will definitely be enjoyed again in our house! [Made for PRMR Tag Februaruy 2010].

Wow! This is closer to 10 stars! I never eat bread without butter (not big on the taste) and I could eat this bread plain all day long, in fact it is so good i have not even tried it with butter! It is dense and moist with a soft crust. Just perfect! I made the 1 1/2 lb loaf option on the dough cycle and then divided into two loafs (which I will not do again because this bread does not rise very much) and baked at 400F for 17 minutes. It was perfect! Thanks so much for posting this gem! This will be our new standard bread in our house! [Made for Veggie Swap February 2010]

Great super easy weeknight dinner. I doubled the recipe (so as to have some leftovers) added some garlic to the mushrooms and added some lightly steamed broccoli in with the cream and cooked about 5 minutes instead of two to get the broccoli a little more tender! This is a great keeper recipe! We will be eating this often! Thanks for posting! [Made for PRMR tag February 2010]

Great light lunch for a rainy Sunday afternoon! Made exactly as directed except instead of cilantro I added just a few green onions finely chopped. We loved the spinach in here! Thanks for posting Brooke! [Made for Holiday Tag February 2010}

This was great alongside sandwiches for lunch on Saturday. We dipped carrot sticks into it! Taking another reviewers suggestion I added a bit of dill! Thanks for posting! I am glad we have leftovers for lunches this week! :) [Made for Veg*n Swap March 2010]

MOVE OVER STARBUCKS!!! ;) This was a great sneaky treat (I say sneaky because I am not supposed to have more than 1/2 cup of coffee per day and I cheated this afternoon hehe). This was very easy to make. I made the rice in my rice maker while I made the dressing part and then just combined it all together! This was a wonderful side for grilled chicken and reheated wonderfully! Thanks for posting! Made for Holiday Tag! :)

Halved the recipe and used a combo of raspberries and strawberries, used splenda and FF plain yogurt. It was great and I am sure we will continue to make this all summer long! [Made for our VIP Chef for the April 2010 Veg*n Tag]

Made this using vanilla low fat organic soy milk! Otherwise as directed (except cut in half). Very tasty and healthy and I loved the cinnamon banana combo! :) Thanks for posting! [Made for Veg*n Swap April 2010]

Seriously? Ten Stars!!! The flavor was incredible and the ease of this recipe is just unbelievable! I did use dried rosemary and added a sprtiz of lemon juice over the top of it! Made for Holiday Tag April 2010 and for Herb of the Month Tag in the French Forum!

We took this to a friends house last night for dinner and it was a huge hit! We served it with tortilla chips alongside some hot spinach and artichoke dip another guest brought! Thanks for posting! [Made for PRMR tag April 2010]!

This was so easy and filling! I had this for breakfast twice last week and I am going to the store for more apples and yogurt today. Super easy! Super delicious! Five stars all the way!

Great! Not too sweet and not too peachy! Made this for a family cook out tonight, and after a sample and I expect not one drop to be left. :) I made the tea in my iced tea maker! Thanks Syd! Made for PRMR.

yummy! I made as directed except using diced tomatoes. I did use kalamata olives (my favorite!!!). I took previous reviewers advice and added a little red wine vinegar to the oil. It was delicious, tangy and fresh! Can't wait to have this again! made for Veg'n Swap August 2011!
Very very good! A friend and I dipped pita chips into this like a dip! Very good! I love the spicy from the cayenne! I garnished with a teeny bit of mint! Thanks for posting! Made for Veg'N Swap 37!
Simple and delicious! This was the perfect ending to a lunch for a friend and me! Thanks for posting! Made for Veg'N Swap 37!

This was just like at the restaurant. Very pretty salad and very filling. We had it as a main dish and it was plenty, had leftovers for tomorrow's lunch. Definitely will make again. It was a little more labor intense than I anticipated, does require some prep time.

I do not drink coffee, so I am taking everyone else who had it at my brunch's word for it - they said it was great and they want me to make it again. Made for ZWT4

These are wonderful burritos. The use of pork was a nice switch. Will make these again.

This is a great recipe, everyone really enjoyed it, great snacking. As I didn't have a double boiler on hand, I used the chocalates that are in a coin shape that can be melted in the microwave. Worked great.
This was a quick and easy supper. Served it with a salad and bread. Perfect for a chilly evening. I only had spiraled noodled mac and cheese, worked fine.

This was surprising good and it does give you a lift. It has a very good flavor and is a nice healthy drink. Only thing is it seems a little watered down, think next time I will cut back on the water a little. But will add it to my regulars.
This smelt so good while it was shimmering. I loved the spicey tea flavor and the rum made it special. Only change I made was I left the butter out. Great recipe!

This is a wonderful smoothie. I liked the cranberry flavored, had some fresh cranberries left from Thanksgiving and they worked nicely. I really have a thing for tostadas, it is what I order when we eat out at a Mexican restaurant, these were great, I liked the addition of the sausage.
Easy, fun and just like the old days. Great recipe. When I was growing up we had root beer floats all the time, this brought back memories. thanks

This were so quick and simple. I did one thing different I actually baked them and then used the broil function on the oven for just a few minutes to brown them and they were great. What a great combination of ingredients.

This was very quick and easy. The flavor was fresh and light, would be good foor a warm summers day. However, on a cold, rainy day I felt it needed a little more punch - we actually heated it up and enjoyed it better that way.

This was a quite yummy recipe. It also makes a huge amount of spaghetti, my husband asked if we were feeding the neighbors - ha! ha! Only thing I would change the next time around, would be to use more sauce, I think I would two jars instead of the 1 1/2 jars, just felt it needed more sauce.
I really enjoyed the marinade, it gave the beef a very nice flavor. I did use a bag of Asian stir fry veggies, which besides green veggies it had carrots. Nice stir fry.

We really enjoyed these sloppy joes, I did use a little more tomato paste and a little less water, also cut the amt of chili powder in half after reading others reviews. We thought they were a whole lot better the can stuff!

Yum! Is all I can say. I had to make these inside on my small grill, but they still turned out great, I loved the rub, it was great, will definitely try them again this summer on the big grill outside.

I really like squash, but my husband doesn't, so I am always searching for recipes that will convince him that squash is a great vegetable. He even liked this recipe - I liked it because it added a little variety with the cheese and nuts.

This was so easy to prepare and it turned out great, chicken was tender and the flavor was nice. Only change I made was I did cook the meat, before baking and I baked it a tad longer to compensate, but it turned out great. thanks

These were great, I actually made tostadas instead of tacos, because that is what I had in the house. Don't think it makes a lof of difference. We really liked the peach salsa, it was a nice combo with the fish. Made for everyday is a holiday.

This had a nice subtle taste, a nice mix between sweet and tangy. I had to grill it indoors, but it turned out just fine, plenty leftover for tomorrows lunch. I did add a little cheese, just couldn't resist.

This was so good, I liked the citrus flavor to it. I also added just a little feta cheese as they were in with the deli black olives I purchased. The dressing makes the salad. Made for ZWT5.

This is a very nice refreshing salad. I enjoyed the combination of cucumbers and tomatoes. The dressing was great. Made for ZWT5

Simple, quick and very good. I used fresh cilantro from my herb garden and fresh corn from the farmers market. Nice summer salad.
Great veggies, can't wait to try it later in the season when we have more fresh veggies at the Farmers Market. Did cut out the yellow pepper, it was just a little too many peppers for me.
Nice salad, something different, quick to prepare and yummy!

My husband loves blue cheese and I am not as fond of it as he is, but these simple and quick sandwiches are quite good and simple to make. Served with a lettuce salad, was a quick lunch.

Yum! Yum! Very good burger - it was a nice "hot" change from the usual burger. The mango and pineapple were a great additional.  A little messy, but well worth the taste.
This was super simple to prepare and provides one of those meals that reminds you of mom. I felt it could have had a little more tomatoes, next time might add more or cut back on the amount of pasta.
