Bubble up pizzas are a favorite at my house. This was a very good one. Loved the fresh veggies in the meat sauce. A delicious, filling, satisfying meal.
A fun breakfast. I used ham with cheese on top. Would like to try with bacon or sausage. Sprinkle a little salt and pepper on the egg.

I wouldn't call it a tweak as I never add salt to my cooking unless it is to make pastry last longer. This recipe as written has a HUGE amount of salt! Ham, stock, Cajun seasoning, sausage, a Knorr cube, liquid smoke & TWO forms of salt, a garlic & plain salt, a whole 2-3 tsp in all!!! And if plain salt is not added to beans as it hardens the skins as they cook, why is garlic salt added? Then no doubt loads would be added to the rice too. Why so much salt? I appreciate manual workers in Southern states may need more salt, but it's otherwise an unhealthy overload. I was also concerned that no mention was made that red kidney beans should be boiled vigourously for 10 minutes to neutralise the food-poisoning toxin. And that you didn't clarify where the hot water tap was drawn from to up the temperature of the crockpot - fine if direct from a main like mine but not fine if from a tank in the attic fed into an electic immersion heater where the water is stale, I would only ever use that water boiled. I don't call it a tweak either as I would be forever doing it because I don't eat mammals - so later I used vegetarian bacon in lieu of ham hock & fried at the same time as vegetarian sausage. I used an extra garlic clove instead of using garlic salt & found the 'liquid smoke' flavour, as Americans say, AWESOME!!! I used green peppers like in the picture & served with a recipe for Collard Greens but using a similar cabbage found locally. I don't like losing beans either but I do sometimes mash a few as I like that creamy texture, just a few though, I like to keep my beans too! I love your 'humble beans' & will cook again, amazing flavours.

This is an amazing dressing!!! I have regularly bought Feta salad dressing or just added feta to a standard dressing. This will be a rare occasion from now on. This is restaurant quality & I cannot wait to try it with the one ingredient I didn't use this time for authenticity's sake. I wanted the dressing to make at the same time as Kittencal's Famous Greek Salad (& that dressing too) & corn syrup is not sold in UK supermarkets (not in large ones in my city anyway). I could only order online so I googled for a substitute: as stated here, sugar & honey would alter taste as would Maple syrup, which I had, but I could use Golden Syrup (made from sugar cane). All shops sell this as it's popular as a sauce on sponge puddings & on pancakes. A quick visit to my corner shop & my salad was ready with a yum factor 100! (I did order corn syrup from Amazon as I'm curious to see what it's like)

This was extremely cheesy & needed some research. I cannot buy Velveeta in the U.K. (though it used to be sold here) . I learnt too that 'sharp' Cheddar refers to mature/aged cheese. (I don't find Cheddar at all 'sharp' myself, what is called 'mature', I find very smooth, but it may be different in the U.S. I attempted to melt Kraft Dairylea, but it does not really make a sauce, doesn't melt right. Some websites say it does, but again, it may be differently processed in the U.S. Tried Laughing Cow, same story. We don't have branded 'Swiss' Cheese in the U.K. either which I've often seen on cooking websites. SO! I have some Velveeta Cheese on its way to me from GERMANY!!! (Presumably sold to US servicemen there). Meanwhile, I made this with Mature (very) Cheddar & 'Mexican' cheese (in our supermarkets, Mex cheese is orange, spicy & flecked with multi-colour peppers & onions). I made again with various cheese blends; Gouda, Emmenthal, Gorgonzola, Blue cheese etc. I've normally used a shop jar for this, but fresh is so much better. I usually serve this tasty cheese-fest with grilled chicken/veggy-chicken fillet or a veggy burger (shop or homemade) of many variations with lots of different salads to 'cut through; the fat.

I grilled them (broiled in US?) and didn't bother with skewers, just put in all on a plate under there. I used half red/half green pepper though as it was screaming for some colour. The fresh pineapple was really dense with a good texture (though I made an unholy mess getting the fruit de-cored/cubed) - a very intense flavour completely different to the lazy (and tempting) way of opening a tin. I had to, just had to, add mushroom too & red onion, but I cooked them separately for authenticity. Served with brown basmati, pitta/naan & salads from this site; creamy macaroni salad, creamy potato salad, both from Karen, Colorado; also, Spiced Marinated Tomatoes, which is wonderful. Green salads too. Very versaltile. The pineapple was thick texture like potato. The sauce was awesome.

Had to guess 'Pizza Sauce' as we don't have that in the UK; after a good think re sauce/mince quantities I decided on Passata (plain sieved tomatoes without seeds); (rather than tomato puree or jarred Bolognese Sauce, the latter more usually for a saucy pasta meal. I fried veggy mince in olive oil first then continued as written EXCEPT I wondered if 'Pizza Sauce' meant that garlic & basil had been added, so I added them too to the cups. (Just one clove to try as garlic can be very strong when roast like this). Like the top review, I haven't served at a party, but a knife/fork dinner; having smaller portions would be wonderful for smaller children & they are also for lunchboxes, for children & dieters. If this is not a consideration & perhaps huge masculine workers have to be catered for, another contributor to this site suggests jumbo muffin cups! Also a lovely snack with a little salad for my lunch at home (too much & I don't get any work done lol).

Absolutely wonderful!!! I didn't serve with spaghetti, not good to eat in public & I had company; so jacket spuds & penne pasta. Served fried mushroom & onions separately & sweetcorn (just thawed & briefly microwaved. Went well with all salad stuff served too. I made asparagus guacamole from this site & will make 248096 too next time as it is quite herby. It was very tender & I like 'cuzincuzin' suggestions too, yum Factor 98 for me!!!

I grilled (uk) which is under heat between the hob & oven so didn't need all the oil mix (thought I kept it for next time). The mushrooms (with gills) were gorgeous & moist. I served with 'hot German salad' from this site as well as grilled asparagus like the pic above & sprialised courgettes & spaghetti verde (in case I had it wrong). Also had chicken & red peppers as per pic, served with lots of salad veg too,mushrooms are yum factor 80!!

I don't have a BBQ so I grilled it, that space with an overhead grill between the hob & oven in British cookers. There was a lot of marinade, I think because some is lost on BBQ's, so as an experiment to see which I preferred, I grilled half & fried half. I browned the chicken in oil first before continuing to fry. I also have a dry-pan (saucepan with a central funnel (with a lid).) Next time, I'll try that. I didn't use my oven, still the easiest for this quantity (I froze half) because I had jacket spuds there & plus 2 pasta dishes. Served with the spuds, peas & mushrooms/asparagus from this site. Sauce went over everything.

I couldn't get 'corn chips' unless they are Doritos Crisps - if they are made of corn? I'm in the UK so I used Cheese Crisps (crisps are called chips in the US). They a bit soggy as they are made from potato & I don't know if corn ones would be better, would have had to go to town but it was too late to go for Doritos. Another reviewer said she cooked the chicken over rice instead of crisps, I wanted to try it, I will still try again with corn, but I am serving rice with it, as well as broccoli & carrots. Can't say anything about 'copycat' as we don't have Applebee in UK. Supper looks wonderful, sauce is brilliant, yum, I delay no more...

I'm not sure what is supposed to be 'African-style' about this, other than it's served with the bones still in it. Mayonnaise & Sherry (or wine) are not African at all. Lime juice & coriander are Mediterranean to South-East Asian, as are peppers. Plantains, Cassava, Palm oil & Maize Porridge are traditional African foods, though I have found a reference to peanut sauces in West African cuisine. I've never met Africans who cook with them though other than using groundnut oil. Did you mean Arab, rather than Black Africa, as in, say, Morocco? It does seem more like Middle-Eastern cookery. It is lovely though, I never buy peanut butter, not a popular item in Britain, unless I'm making a sauce, I used the coarse-ground (and next time I'll make my own as I regularly make peanut burgers - mixed with maizemeal as it happens!). I used fillets as I never buy boney pieces & don't want fatty skin, & they were lovely. I grilled them (British grill is the space between the oven & hob, not an outdoor BBQ - most people don't have them). I made a spicy tomato rice as pictured & Recipes 406859 & 368435 (Black-eye-bean salad & Grilled Coconut Pineapple as well as suggested by another reviewer below. Onion, Tomato, Cucumber & Coriander Leaf Raita (yogurt) & Garlic Naan Bread completed the spread. I shall make this again soon.

Gorgeous & refreshing, just what I make in the early hours when I can't sleep. Like another reviewer, I am always on the prowl for unusual/different dressings - yum! (used veggy bacon too) & sprinled with sultanas.

Great flavor but didn't make much. Next time I would double the recipe so there would be plenty for seconds!

Wouldn't recommend jumbo biscuits as they took up all the space in the muffin pan and then I had enough left over meat and veggie mixture that I could make a pie tin of crustless meat/veggie, mashed potatoes and cheese casserole. Flavor was good but even with the 1 teaspoon of garlic powder and onion powder instead of the tablespoons recommended, I probably would lessen even more since I had chopped up onion and minced garlic already in the mixture. Even with omitting the mushrooms (since someone in the family doesn't like them), this was a very tasty dish and easy to prepare.

The family loved these mashed potatoes! Even though I had some gravy as a result of something I prepared for the same meal, these were eaten without any additional adornments. A definite repeat at our house.
Delicious. I served it over Mexican rice. Next time I try this I plan to shred the chicken, and then serve this on tortillas.

Delicious and easy to make. I used more onion, cheese, and pineapple than called for in the recipe, since the family likes all of those. I also had some Canadian bacon, so I cut up two slices and added that as well.

Got this recipe from the Weight Watcher's website original. We absolutely love it! We've made it with tilapia, but we've found we prefer it with hake loin. I modified this recipe by making it on the stove top instead of the crockpot.  I kept all the measurements the same.  This was easy to put together, and on the stove top, took about 1 hour from start to finish.  I would definitely make this soup again :)

This was easy and delicious, so my DH says, which is a terrific testament to the recipe...he usually says, "it was alright."  i don't eat roast.  I will make again.  JacquelynLee, thanks for posting a good recipe.  Sue

too much ground ginger and too much red pepper flakes and we are not wooses. Next time I make i will use 1/4 of the ground ginger and cut the red pepper flakes in 1/2 and then this recipe will be great. update 3/9/14 did not use the ginger, but still a little too harsh, next  time I will cut back on the coriander to 1 teaspoon and a little less brown sugar. We love the pork chops, so moist and juicy and flavorful, but the spices are off a little bit for us. Will keep on trying and will keep on trying.

Lovely flavor and attractive.  Healthy recipe with a favorite assortment of vegetables. I added two pieces of cooked potato for the last 1/2 hour and then fork mashed them with the sauce before serving.  I didn't add any cornstarch. Good with the croutons. Good without. Loaded with flavor. Will definitely make again.

Excellent spice mix, I used it on a pork tenderloin and it turned out delicious with a nice bit of heat.  i roasted the tenderloin as I would normally for about 30 minutes.  Lovely flavourful dinner!
Thanks for posting I will be using it regularly!!
A very tasty cole slaw recipe.  I enjoyed the addition of beans to the recipe.

Very delicious carrot/polenta dish. I loved the sage. The cheese I used was aged Cheddar and 2 tbsp Romano. To the carrots I added a pinch of garlic powder. This was so easy to put together and it baked-up as the recipe said. I made a change: instead of instant polenta, I used regular polenta and all veg broth (4:1) which needed a longer polenta cooking time.. Next time I make this (and I will make this again), I'll cut the carrots into one-inch slices - while eating, we cut them into manageable pieces anyways. Very nice recipe. Now I have a great new polenta recipe for my cookbook!

My biggest complaint about this recipe - Why haven't I been using this for years?  : )  I ran out of red wine vinegar for a creamy garlic salad dressing that I was making.  I remember years ago a coworker telling me that she makes her own red wine vinegar.  I didn't pursue it then but I remembered today.  This turned out great! And now that I know the ratio is 3 to 1, I can mix up as much as I need at any one time.  The recipe says it makes 1 1/4 cups.  But it should really say that it makes 1/4 cup of red wine vinegar.  1 tablespoon red wine + 3 Tablespoons vinegar = 4 tablespoons = 1/4 c.

Wow. Just Wow!  Made with all super fresh ingredients and used organic cannellini beans.  I also used 2 very large garlic cloves, which worked out very well.  I served with black bean tortilla  chips and will use leftovers in combination with sandwich ingredients.  Super!!  Thanks so  much for sharing!
This is delicious! I was after an omelet and found this in the new recipes. I did scale it down but essentially did all the steps. Very tasty easy meal. Thanks for sharing.

We loved it! I'm a big fan of Remoulade sauce and I appreciate the tweaks! We dipped our shrimp in it, and I used it for leftover Cajun chicken sandwiches. Will I make it again.....and again....and again.....an...........Made for Susie's World Tour 2018.

This is SO perfect and SO simple, it's going into my ~Encore~ cookbook, one I reserve for the best of the best.  I experimented with my collection of finishing salts.  YES MA'AM!  The smoked salish, lime flake and herb grey (all from Saltistry.com) were outstanding sprinkled over the fish. Few ingredients, super-fast production, excellent flavor. Can't ask for more. Thank you for posting, Maito!

I loved the ease of these chops. I used all the marinade mix but only 4 bone in pork loin chops. Will be a very useful recipe to have on hand for the summer BBQs.

This recipe is one of those that you wonder why you havent made it sooner.  Very delicious and filling.  Also, I like that this is very easy to make.  Thanks for sharing.
This was very good. We enjoy this as well as many other recipes of Kittencal's.
Very easy, and excellent chocolate flavor. I subbed one snack cup of unsweetened applesauce for the oil, and it still came out moist and delicious.
Made just a single serving of this - fried the egg.  It was quick and easy and my husband enjoyed it very much. May try to make ahead version sometime soon.

Perfect blend of spices which I put under the skin and then on the outside also.  I used my rotisserie oven to roast the 3.75 pound chicken for 1 hour.  The lemon squeezed over the chicken after it was cut, was what helps put this chicken right over the top, for taste and flavor!!     Made for team Soup-A-Stars during ZWT9 2013
This was so nice, easy and a keeper!
WoW  whats better than chocolate and strawberries! Oh and so creamy! I also tripled the recipe to serve three of us!  We all loved it : )

Garlic and olive oil optional in my family?  Not going to happen, it's mandatory!  I had a baguette sitting on the counter since yesterday and this was the perfect recipe to use it.  I toasted the bread slightly, rubbed some mashed garlic into it, then topped with tomato slices and drizzled with the oil.  In our house 4 slices will serve one person, not 4 people as the recipe states, so I just quadrupled the recipe for the three of us, and not a crumb was left!  Tapas, shmapas, this was a pefect lunch with some Moscato on the side.  Made for ZWT5.

A good recipe and I am glad to have found it. The first time I made it to recipe but omitted raisins as we avoid sulphites and I used butter. The only issue I had was the baking soda flavor came through. Since then I have made them omitting the baking soda and increasing the baking powder to 1tbs and omitting the sugar as well. I made this for Sunday dinner. It was enjoyed by the entire family. Served with green beans and yellow rice.
Simple, yes, but more importantly absolutely delicious!  Will go into my "WOW" cookbook and will definitely be made many more times!  Loved it! Thanks so much for sharing this recipe.

This was yummy! I made just enough for 2 so I only used 1 can of mushroom soup. Thought I had Kitchen Bouquet, but guess not so I used some Maggi seasoning instead. I dipped the steaks in seasoned flour fist, then pan fried till brown. Served with rice and veggies, a very delicious dinner!

Mmm, delicious. I skipped all the butter and blackened in 1 tbs olive oil. I used half smoked paprika. I also reduced the cayenne as I made a fairly spicy pico with cucumber.to top the chicken. A keeper, healthy and easy, will make often. Thanks for the recipe.

I made many different Mac & Cheese recipes in the past.  This recipe tops them all.  The combination of the 4 cheese was perfection.

I did not change anything in the recipe, prepared as specified.

"Uncle Bill"
All the flavors I crave. Smooooth and yummy. Thanks for sharing.

"PERFECT" I had a 3 pound eye of round and made as written and I seasoned it all over with "Cavender's all Purpose Greek Seasoning (salt free) and baked for 30 minutes at the 475?F mark before turning the oven off and left it in the close oven for the recommended 2 1/2 hours and as I said it came out "perfect". Wow!  Great flavor - so quick and delicious!  We really enjoyed this and will certainly make it again.  DH suggested adding some caraway seeds next time so we might do that just for fun.  Thanks TLu.  Made for Best of 2010.
So simple and easy to make.  This tasted great and will be great for when the weather turns cooler.  I had all the ingredients on hand to make it which is a plus.  Thanks for posting.  Made for ZWT5.

What a easy simple recipe! and so GOOD too!   I added a dash of ground cloves to the flour mixture for extra flavor and next time I'm thinking on adding some lemon zest. Wow these turned out great! Really easy to make and turned out moist even until the next day. I can imagine adding a lot of different flavors (choco chips, nuts) to it to really make it even more delicious! :)

Much enjoyed! I did cook longer than called for and may cook at a higher temp next time. I liked the combo of veggies. Thanks!

Oh wow these were good!!! Followed the recipe exactly and served with some grilled steaks. They were so delicious and very easy to make!! Thanks for posting and congrats on your football pool win! Made for your Football Pool - Divisional Playoff win!!
Very good - I used less marmalade and forgot the garlic but otherwise made as directed. Used a grill pan on top of the stove. Served with tossed salad and fruit. Great dinner! Thanks for sharing!

Loved this!  I took other reviewer's advice and baked it all together and it worked perfectly.  This would work great as sub for a meat dish.  I used low sodium soy sauce so it wasn't salty at all for me.  Thanks for posting a keeper!

Excellent recipe and very adaptable to personal taste and/or whatever you have on hand. I used cream cheese with chives, sharp cheddar cheese and 12 Jimmy Dean pork breakfast sausage links cut into bite-sized pieces. Excellent panini! Made it for our lunch. The basil gives it great flavor, do not leave it out!
The name says it all ....... very moist and tender, full of flavour! I scaled the coating ingredients in half to cook 2 breasts but used only 1/2 cup of Italian style breadcrumbs. Thanx Carol!

Not having much of a sweet tooth, I used about a teaspoon of sugar (and don't think I even needed to add that).  I think I would halve the dressing ingredients the next time as there was a tad too much dressing for my tastes.  Great tasting though!

Just learning to like blue cheese and enjoyed this quick, easy, healthy, tasty snack!
Just treated myself to this ice-cold frothy good Orange Julius, and am so glad I tried it! I used regular granulated sugar instead of Splenda and halved the vanilla. Thanks!

I wish I had never laid eyes on this recipe.  I am not kidding.  I have been slicing off slivers of it since it cooled enough to cut, because tiny slivers won't ruin my diet...until they add up to the entire loaf!  This is INCREDIBLE!  As other reviews mentioned, 5 stars is really not enough.  I did add about 2 teaspoons of cinnamon to the batter, but that was all I did differently.  I didn't grate the apples, I peeled and cored them, then tossed them into my mini chopper.  If you are making this for the first time, do NOT BE ALARMED when the batter appears thick before adding the apples, it is perfect after the addition of the apples.  This is going to be a new go-to recipe for sure.  My family and I thank you for sharing this recipe, even if my diet does not.

This was really good, easy, and used all stuff that I had easily available (not fresh ginger, which rots in my fridge, or chicken broth, which hides in my freezer and has to be thawed). I gave this 5 stars. This is become my favorite way to make bacon! I discovered the way of making bacon about a year ago and love it! Thanks for posting a great method! Christine

Oh, so good!! The feta & chickpeas give the salad a wonderfully savoury flavour. I made 1/2 recipe, used steamed regular spinach instead of baby spinach, and stirred in all the feta. Wonderful, wonderful! This has been such a hit with my husband and me and also some neighbors that came for dinner last night.  I made a batch on Friday and had a loaf that very night. If it wasn't` for the down pouring rain I would have gone back out for more. 1/2 cup of mushrooms was plenty. I did use all the cheese the recipe called for. As I was making these I thought should I roast the slices first? Thinking they would be tough and not cooked through. As it baked the sauce did fill the pan and and ended up stewing the eggplant. I would have given this 4 stars but the amounts are so off. We found this not to be pizza (not being a crust at all) but more like eggplant parmesan.  You do need a fork and knife. Had overnight guest and made this today. Very simple to assemble with delish results.  The only thing I would change was I ended up browning the tater tots in a separate pan. I have made this coffee several times, and with modifications to the ingredients. After I add 10 ounces of water to my coffee cup, I add 1-1/2 teaspoons of instant coffee, and heat it in the microwave. I then stirred in 1 tablespoon of granulated sugar, 4-1/2 teaspoons of Coffee-Mate Powdered Coffee Creamer, plus the extract. I topped the coffee with a heavy amount of Reddi-Wip Whipped Topping, and thoroughly enjoyed the coffee! I did notice, after some of the Reddi-Wip had melted into the coffee, it made the coffee even more creamy, but oh so delicious! I highly recommend topping your cup of coffee with some sort of whipped topping, it adds just that little bit of something extra which you will enjoy. Thank you Annacia for sharing this recipe, this one's definitely a keeper!

Delicious and a bit of heaven in every bite!!! Very satisfying. Thanks for posting!

I really like the subtlety of the cinnamon in this drink. I can taste it but it's not overwhelming the dark, strong coffee. I didn't add much sugar to the coffee or the whipped cream but there was a little bit in the cinnamon that I sprinkled on top and it was just right for me. Thanks momaphet! :)

This will be my go-to recipe for cole slaw from now on! I used low fat mayonaise, Splenda , 1% milk, rice wine vinegar and added about 1/4 to 1/2 cup finely minced yellow onion. Absolutely delicious!! Even my hubby commented on how good it was! Thanks for posting this- it's a keeper!

I accidentally defrosted chops and chicken instead of just poultry and decided to make both with this sauce.  Surprisingly, it was even better with the pork then the chicken.  I loved how the ginger and soy paired with the apricot nectar transforming a simple sauce into layers of flavor.  Made for 123 Hit Wonders.

I needed something to pack for dinner at work, so I made sandwiches out of this. I used multi grain flatbread wraps, American cheese, lettuce, pickles, tomato and a little bit of honey chipotle mustard (I warmed the wrap/chicken/cheese in the microwave at work, and added all the cold veggies afterwards). For the chicken, I let it marinate overnight before cooking it. I didn't have light beer, so I used Modelo instead. Once the chicken was fully cooked, I removed it from the sauce and continued to simmer the sauce for a while to reduce it and thicken it up (didn't want the chicken to get overcooked). Very tasty chicken, and versatile, too! Thanks for posting this keeper! Made for CQ 2017 Central America

Excellent!  I had a 2 1/2 lb. rump roast....I didn't add the garlic (husband doesn't like it) and used Montreal seasoning in place of the salt, pepper, garlic.  After reading some of the reviews, I used beef broth in place of the water and sliced my onion into quarters....the onions got all browned and delicious!  I roasted the beef until it reached 150 degrees, removed it from the pan and kept it warm, then poured out the juices and added some veg oil to the pan and browned a couple of tablespoons of flour right in the pan over low heat.  I added enough water to the juices to make about 1 1/2 to 2 cups of liquid and poured that back into the pan and whisked with the browned flour.  What a delicious gravy that was!!  This is really a great, simple recipe and I'll definitely use it again the next time rump roast goes on sale as it did today!  Thanks so much for posting this recipe :)

These were so delicious and so easy to whip up. I used low sodium Soy Sauce with great results.   I had them along with Asian Cole Slaw for a fabulous dinner!  Thank you for sharing your recipe with us!  Linda
Fabulous, I love the rosemary in this.  I used some from my garden and it sort of crisps up.  Was lovely and such a change from normal garlic bread.  I served with soup.

Awesome salad, very light and refreshing that brings out such bright flavors.  Glad to have another unusual combination to share at summer meals.  Thanks for sharing!  Made and reviewed for the shady ladies of zwt7!

Tasty meal-in-a-bowl soup and so easy to make in the crock pot. I added 2 teaspoons sugar to cut the acid of the tomato sauce, used potato water from making mashed potatoes instead of the plain water, and added 2 teaspoons beef soup base mix purchased from a Bulk Food store. Cooked as directed and it worked perfectly. Served with thick slices of French bread and a salad for a meal. Will definitely make again and use up my canned diced tomatoes with a Tablespoon or two of tomato paste instead of the tomato sauce.

Ohhhh my! So good! I used 1T of medallion Doro for the coffee assuming you meant instant. So good!
Very good - tasted more like frozen yogurt, though. Thanks for the posting!

Easy and tasty!  I made mine in the crockpot and it worked great -- the spices are absolutely delicious. I didn't have any problems with dryness that others had.  Will make again!
Quick, easy and delicious!  My kind of recipe!

So glad to have found this recipe as I always have the ingredients on hand (sour cherry juice is a 'must' to cool down in the hot, Greek, summer months).  I would never have thought of the combo of the sour cherry juice/mint/rum, but it's the bomb!
Used this as a dressing for Recipe#431877 as suggested and was not disappointed. The quantity listed for each item was just right to my liking. Thank-you for sharing!
We had this last night.  As i never know how to cook asparagus, I thought this was great. Very simply to make.   Served with a side salad.

It has been a long time since I was *wowed* by a salad as I was this one. It is beautiful in taste and appearance. These are so good, so easy and so quick--what more could you want on a week night!  Used shredded lettuce as had no coleslaw mix, added minced onions and some sliced black olives----turned out great.  Also mixed the ranch dressing with some salsa.

We love a good burger, and this is one of the best we have ever eaten. Didn't change a thing. The onions and chipotle ketchup yield a wonderful blend of flavors. This was cooked on the stove top because of the cold weather. Can't wait to try it on the grill. Thanks for the great burger.

I have made this several times and it is always a hit. My daughter ask for it almost every time they come to visit. I made as written except to use peas instead of the green beans. Just a personal preference. Thanks so much for sharing a great recipe.

This dinner made us so happy; thanks for posting something we'd LOVE to eat again soon!

Awesome!  I made this 2 nights in a row... it is that good.  I used the juice of tangerines I had on hand instead of orange juice.  I left out the nuts, too.  I added a clove of minced garlic to the carrots and celery on the second night.  Very nice.  Thanks for posting this recipe, KateL!

I chose this recipe for Kittencalskitchen forum tag game, I love homemade pizza sauce and this one is a winner, I added in seasoning salt and black pepper, we like very spicy so I also added in cayenne pepper, this will be used for my French bread pizza loaf recipe, thanks Bee!

What a great way to serve pork tenderloin. I served them with scalloped potatoes and we enjoyed them very much. Thanks! Made for CQ '17.

This cake is delicious!  I reduced the amount of sugar in the batter but otherwise made it as directed.  Its vanilla fragrance while baking is intoxicating!

Great flavor combo, the lemon juice and sesame oil really hit the spot. Thanks for sharing another yummy recipe.

Yum! This was delicious and satisfying! I cut it down to a single serving, using 2 eggs, 1 t. butter, 2 t. milk (I used evaporated milk) and used a wedge of Laughing Cow Creamy Swiss Cheese. This is a great ham and bean recipe. Just like my mom makes!
Oh yum!  I used a green from the farmer's market that was said to be a lot like spinach but takes the heat better and this was a wonderful way to prepare it.  I only wish I had more!

mr picky loved these moist burgers ,cherry bombers

This was okay, but a bit bland for our tastes.  The basil didn't come through very well, and I had to add onion and salt to give a bit more flavor.  It was easy to tweak, and pretty and colorful, but could have been better.

I found the flavor to be spectacular.  Great idea to add the rosemary!  The only issue was that the veggies were still hard at end of cooking time so next time (and there will be a next time!), I'm going to crank up the heat to 425 for 30 minutes and see what happens.  Thanks for sharing, KateL.

This made for a lovely light weekend lunch, that was enjoyed by all. I subbed chopped basil in place of the parsley but otherwise made as directed.
Thanks for sharing :)

I increased the garlic, salt and pepper in the mashed potatoes, and poached the eggs separately and added them after the casserole came out of the oven. I really wasn't crazy about the texture of the Swiss on top, although I loved the flavor.
Very paleo friendly!  I used almond butter and added 2 TB of ground flax seeds to the recipe.  I will try with cashew butter, too.  Very delicious; thanks!

Easily adaptable. I used leftover turkey from when my Mom visited, and cauliflower instead of tator tots. I totally forgot the bacon. Thanks for sharing a local fave, SarahBeth.
Very good and easy to make. I used 93% lean ground beef.
I've made this several times now. Simple, fast and tasty. Last night I put some tater tots around the fish, no foil over the food, and it came out perfect.
I love this marinade. I added green pepper chunks to the beef on the skewers and served it over steamed jasmine rice.

This is a very good chili the whole family enjoyed on a chilly evening (well, as chilly as it gets in San Diego, which is never overly cool). I followed the ingredients and directions with just a couple of minor exceptions; I used a spicy Mexican 8 oz. can of tomato sauce and a can of diced fire roasted tomatoes with garlic. Since I used the spicier tomato sauce, I eliminated the cayenne pepper. We love spicy food and it certainly was with my small changes. Served with corn bread to round out a perfect meal. Thanks for sharing Chef Lil' Momma Jenn.

Turned these into strawberry shortcake. I thinks these would be good served warm or cold. We served them warm this time, sprinkled with a little bit of powdered sugar. I will make this recipe again, as 3/4 of the family really loved it, and 1/4 ate it with minimal complaints. Thanks for sharing!

Fantastic! Everything,the salad, the dressing. Perfect combination of flavors. We loved it.

Great bread for our pastrami sandwich. I used my KitchenAide and had to add another 1/4 c. flour. easy to make and Very good flavor!

This was so wonderfully fresh.  I love a chopped salad with tons of toppings and this one fits the bill.  Such a beautiful presentation, too.  Thank you for the recipe!

This is a great alternative to a wheat flour pizza crust, it bakes up nicely, doesn't stick to the pan and tastes great. Corn Bread like my Mom used to make.

So easy and so yummy!! No frosting required, these came out beautifully! I did, however, use the bottom of a glass to press them a little - more round, pretty, uniform look :) (presentation is EVERYTHING!).
Thanks for posting!

Wow!  This is a home run!  I iced the cake while still in the pan, next time I will take the cake out of the pan first before icing for a better presentation.  My house smells delicious.  This is so easy and so delicious. Thank you for sharing this great recipe.
Vibrant colors - a beautiful tropical salsa or condiment.

Made as directed.  Only one problem. Doesn't make enough for my family, so I had to make a second batch and have been told to save this recipe.  I used coconut verses the sugar.  Thanks for a great, delicious AND easy cookie.  Made for Football Pool 2013.
Enjoyed this casserole, great comfort food! Added more red pepper flakes for my taste, love it spicy.

made this as a side to go with steaks. It was very good. We didn't use the 2-3 cups of soup but made the packet according to directions. We used provonle cheese instead of swiss (personel prefence). thanks for the post
Jules

This recipe was a hit with my family.  They loved the flavor of the chicken.  I had some liquid still in the bottom of the pan but most of the chicken browned nicely.  Would post a photo, but can't get it to load from my phone.  Thank you for posting.  Made for ZWT9

The kids sure loved the wait time on these treats! And thank goodness because they crowded around me like a bunch of wild animals and grabbed for them before I even had them cut nicely from the pan. I was gifted a bag of marshmallows from someone cleaning their pantry so this worked out nicely as I noticed the expiration date was forthcoming. Thanks for posting, Mary.

Oh yum!!!! Based upon other suggestions, I just eyeballed the amount of corn to potato. I LOVE this flavor combination of sauteed onions, corn and creamy potatoes. I also chose not to puree he corn and onions. Love the texture of the veggies whole!! Made for the Quest!

Wow, this was incredibly delicious. I had high hopes and they weren't disappointed in the least! I made a few modifications. I replaced 6 tbsp of the fat with chicken stock, added 1/2 tsp of ground coriander and 1 chopped cubanelle pepper since I had one on hand to use up, and used just a couple pinches of saffron. I also first browned the chicken and then sauteed the onions and pepper before adding the remaining ingredients and letting it simmer on the stove top for 45 minutes. It was perfect served over rice. I'll definitely prepare this again. I only cooked up 4 chicken thighs (2 servings) so if I cook up more chicken in the future, I'll double the sauce ingredients to be sure there's enough. Thanks for posting!

I can see this dish making a fabulous breakfast, brunch, lunch or dinner!  In order to use up our ham, I put shaved pieces in the ramekin, rather than a slice, and I think for ease in eating right out of the ramekin with just a fork, I will continue to do that in future.  I used just one extra large egg with only one tablespoon of fat free sour cream and omitted the parsley.  My husband and I are so taken with your recipe#344386 Nif, that we drizzled it on the cooked ham and eggs, and that took the whole dish over the top.
Delicious!!  I made 1 and 1/2 times the recipe and used 2 cups of blueberries.  I baked in an 8x11 pan and these turned out to be fabulous bars.  Thanks so much for sharing your yummy recipe!!
This was delicious and so easy.  I used half romano and half  parmesan cheese and grilled them on a stove-top grill pan.  I left out the salt, also. I will be making this recipe often in the future.

I made this today with a few variations. Very delicious served with steamed broccoli and mashed potatoes! My mods - I added some minced garlic and paprika to the salmon marinade. I also added a tiny bit of salt and chili powder to the flour and reduced the oil/butter considerably. I skipped the sauce because I wanted everything crispy. While the salmon turned out fantastic, it is the onions I want to rave about. I love crispy, caramelized onions and don't much enjoy deep frying. The technique used in this recipe is simply terrific - very quick, simple, no mess, much healthier and very very tasty. Thanks for posting the recipe, Elmotoo!

Oh my! This is wonderful! I've never had the "meat" version, but I'm hooked on this version! I'm not a lentil fan, but absolutely love the combination of this recipe!<br/>Made as written, might add more seasoning the next time, as a personal choice. Thank you so much for sharing! Update-forgot to give it stars!

This was really a great soup! Baking the potatoes made a big difference in the flavour, much deeper. Very simple to put together, we had this for a very filling meal along with some crusty bread. Thanks for posting :) Made for Aussie Reunion Tag!
Very good, very easy, great for a busy week night. Thanks for a great addition to "my family likes it" recipes!

WOW these are great and addictive! They were gobbled up and everyone wants them again so I think I will be making this recipe again this week. Thank you for posting. It went straight into my favorites folder!! ZWT6

Kittencal, you are my favorite chef here for such simple and tasty dishes like this one!  I am one of your biggest fans!  This was simple and so super tasty.  Thank you for yet another wonderful recipe!  xo LA :-)
This was amazing!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  I omitted the pecans because I didn't have any....and for the chocolate glaze I added some peppermint extract...it was divine!!  Made for Photo Tag

Saw this one on the PAC 2008, looked so good I had to dash to the kitchen and make one.  Yes, I had frozen coffee ice cubes waiting for what come what may. Enjoyed it, even though you are not one of my adopted babies.

Made for Week 16 Football Pool win and I was pleasantly surprised and how good this quick and easy recipe turned out. I used the basil in place of dill and added a little extra parmesan than the recipe called for. This is a good recipe and I will use it again.

CONGRATS AGAIN on your win!!!

I used a sweet potato in this recipe, instead of a regular potato.  My husband thought it would have been better with a regular potato, as written.  It was a simple breakfast, and the leftovers kept nicely for a quick weekday morning breakfast.  Reviewed for the "For your consideration" game.  :)

No better flavor combination than cranberry and orange! I boiled the water on the stove then added the tea bags and orange rind to steep. Did not make the ice cubes so added slices of the orange to my pitcher along with the cranberry juice and sugar. I like a bit of tart so didnt add all the sugar. Made and reviewed for the Think Pink - 2018 game.
Made this for PAC Fall 2012, my better half gave it a 5 but I think it is a 4.  Easy fast week night one pot dish.

Keeper - thanks for posting!

Just what I've been looking for! My cook time was under 10 min as I used a pressure cooker, so I will be making this often. I used pre-cut butternut squash, which was SO much easier. Roxygirl

Very tasty. The only thing I changed was to sub the Worcestershire sauce (did not have any) for Ketjap Manis. The drumsticks were good hot as well as cold. Easy to make. Yes, a good recipe. Thanks for posting.

YUM! Makes a wonderful Sunday omelette, Sonya.
I used some sharp cheddar cheese in place of the Swiss (to use it up) Delicious breakfast!
Thanks for posting! :)
This is so simple!  BUT my condensed milk & lime was so loose that I folded in the coolwhip.  It was still soft but held up.  ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS!

Bf said this looked good and asked me what it was.  He took a bite and said, "Hmm, pretty good."  Then he took more bites and said, "Mm, this IS good!"  My chicken breasts weren't large, but they did take an extra 6 mins after the original 7 mins.  I followed this recipe exactly, using prepacked baby spinach and more penne. I call this poverty food - as you can grow most of it. We loved it. I used our own canned beans and canned caramelized onions. That helped speed up the progress. I couldn't find a ham hock so I used a ham steak that I added after the potatoes cooked. Thanks for a great dinner - I can't wait to make this when we have everything fresh.

This was great!  I used pork medallions and let them marinate in the rub for 3-4 hours.  DH loved the flavors which made me chuckle to myself as he claims he HATES ginger and coriander!  I want to try this on chicken next.  Thanks.

SO tasty!  Thank you!  I was looking for a sugar free and caffeine free iced tea for my kids and me.  I used 6 of the Good Earth sweet and spicy tea.  It's perfect. I love green beans and these were delicious. Loved the flavors and it was really quick and easy. Made for ZWT8 for the Diners, Winers and Chives team.

Made for Groovy GastroGnomes, ZWT5, Zingo. Thanks for posting!
Wow this is good!  I made it last night with low carb penne.  I tripled the amount of garlic, added pepper when I was cooking the shrimp and grated parmesean over the top.  It was out of this world!

Excellent.  I cooked a blend of zucchini and yellow crookneck squash with a lid, making my own vegetable stock.  I did add a little more liquid and some bullion.  We stirred some Greek yogurt in the bowls as garnish.
Loved this recipe! Very easy.

Made this using steelhead trout and will admit that I was just a tad bit unsure of the sour cream. There was no need to be as it came out marvelous. Lovely flavors that play very nicely together. If fact, I would happily serve this to guests. Used Panko crumbs and they worked well. Thanks Lynn for another way to serve fish.

I cajun-ized this recipe, and the result was awesome.<br/><br/>I sautéed an onion, then browned some Andouille sausage, then beat some Cajun seasoning into the eggs before adding the eggs to the skillet.<br/><br/>Try it. You won't be disappointed.

This salad was awesome! Even our 6 year old devoured this one! The combination of the cranberries and broccoli with the dressing was delicious. I used less bacon but followed the other amounts. Thanks Syd!
We all loved these!  The flavor was amazing and they were not as heavy and gloppy as many other asian noodle recipes out there.  I served them with Lettuce Wraps and it was perfect!  Delicious!!!!!!

Being diabetic and craving Italian fare is the pitts! But this recipe rescued me from my cravings. I did omit the pasta completely, used fresh broccoli and sliced some cherry tomatoes cut in half. This is fantastic! The whole family loved it and even went back for seconds. Thank you so much for this easy and delicious recipe!
Delicious! Prepared exactly as written and wouldn't change a thing.
love these as a light dinner or appy. thanks so much!
This is a wonderful tasting recipe.  Will make from now on.  Thanks for posting.

Good! Was in the mood for a creamy but easy casserole to serve alongside steaks and potatoes. Will make again. Thanks for sharing the recipe!

Thanks for a great soup and an easy method !
Perfection! I loved the ease of this recipe and that there wasn't any butter or oil used.

The blueberries and banana make a delicious pairing of flavors, while the bright citrus note from the lime juice takes this smoothie to the next level. Thanks, loof, for sharing this enjoyable smoothie with us!
This worked out perfectly!!! Thanks :)

This was the BEST! I doubled the recipe and seved it as the main dish with a side of tomatoes and onions with Peter Luger Sauce. Really good, BUT a bit salty for my taste, so I knocked off a star. Might make again, but only use half the packets. Also, I did not use any butter and can't imagine it is really needed.

I LOVE this cake!  I followed some reviewer suggestions--added a chopped apple to the batter, doubled the vanilla. Really tasty.  I made a few modifications due to what I had on hand.  Instead of rosemary I used a bit of marjoram and dill.  I used green bell pepper and added one seeded and chopped jalepeno.  I used feta instead of goat.  I will try again with the goat cheese next time.  Thanks for sharing.

This was awesome. I was short on gin, so I used half gin and half lemon-thyme infused vodka, along with fresh lemon juice and rose's lime. It tasted very similar to a lemondrop but a little less sweet. I would definitely make this again! Made for ZWT 8 - British Pub Crawl Challenge.
Made this for dinner and everyone loved it. I used whole chicken breasts and doubled the seasonings. The chicken really was moist. Made for the cookathon in Judy's memory.

This versatile recipe made a nice loaf of bread, and the credit goes to Gerry for providing her usual personal touch with directions and helpful hints.  Made using Gerry's suggested amounts and it came out perfect.  Thanks for making us look like accomplished bakers--if guests only knew how easy it really was.
This was exactly what I needed in a pinch.  I was making cornbread with corn casserole but realized I didn't have a box of jiffy mix.  Thank you

What an easy recipe! I made this last month, but I forgot to review it and post my pictures. I made this for one serving. The parmesan cheese was added the last 15 min of baking.  It turned out super, and I served it with stuffing and beans.

I really loved this recipe.  I cut it in half, and it made 2 very generous portions.  Served it instead of potatoes with our leftover turkey dinner. Good luck, and thanks for your contribution to the RSC Potion #18 Contest

Ah, the poor, under-rated Lima Bean. :( Well, in OUR household, they sure are loved!) Saw this recipe and a great photo posted over at Kittencal's site and knew it must be made within the week. GREAT recipe, Chef Shapeweaver!
This worked perfectly for my Pan Burritos recipe that calls for dry enchilada mix. Love that I didn't have to run to the store for it! Will file this to use again.

Simply wonderful! Great flavors, and super-easy to put together. I used half the amount of chicken and two cans of black beans, but otherwise made as directed. This was a huge hit with all of us. Thanks for sharing!

We liked these, and they are simple to make.  I made these to go with an Asian soup, so I added an Asian spice blend into the batter.  I used one small zucchini and it made a total of 5 small pancakes.  I look forward to making these again.
I left out the lime and I used garlic salt instead of minced garlic. I let them marinate in a ziploc bag for about 2 hours and then baked at 375 for 20 mins (for thin cut boneless pork chops).
Perfect recipe, I would give more stars if I could. Will forever cook my Eye-Of-Round Roast this way.
This is absolutely amazing!!  I added 1 pound of meat filled tortellini.
Excellent! I made this in a glass pyrex bowl; 25degrees lower than the biscuit tube specified. Took a little longer to bake, but made the nice pretty shape that I was looking for! :)
Made this with my own frozen peaches. It's great! Thanks.

I took Toni's suggestion to cook the carrots about 10 minutes longer.  That definitely worked well.  Loved the scallion and and rosemary on this dish.  Great way to prepare two delicious veggies that look beautiful together.

The only change I made to this was to use one cup of Skippy chunky peanut butter as I didn't have regular peanuts.  Whirled it all up in the food processer and let my pork loin cubes marinate all day. This was soooo good. DH loved it and when I asked him what he liked best about it he said: It is very flavorful without any one flavor standing out, it all blends together. Thank you for sharing.

We made these for our New Years Eve supper.  First time cooking mussels.  We both enjoyed them for something new, the recipe was easy to follow, the only thing I would do differently is up the garlic and maybe my cloves were smaller and I think I would step it up from plain old parsley and add the recommended taragon or something for a bit more flavor, we played it simple the first time around.  Definately will make again now I know how easy they are to make.  Thanks for a great simple recipe.

I don't really know how to rate it since when I printed out the recipe the cornstarch, splenda and topping was yet added to the recipe. So, as I made it it was very good. The cookie crust was crisp and softened without being soggy the next day. I was worried it would be too sweet, but the sugar free jello powder added great favour, some sweetness and the tartness of the rhubarb still was there. I can only imagine this would now definietly deserve 5 stars with the topping!  Thanks for a keeper Brooke! Reviewed during ZWT 4.

I can't believe I forgot to rate this recipe! I've been using your technique for over a year Nan, and you're right, it comes out perfect every time. I use it as a OAMC recipe by making a double batch.
I freeze the rice in one cup portions, using my Food Saver. Whenever I need rice for recipe I just toss a bag or two into hot water to defrost. I use the microwavable bags for a quick side. Thank you so much for posting. Your recipe makes it easy for us to eat healthier.

Great treat! We are getting cooler nights now, and this was great after a beef stew dinner.  The hazelnut makes the coffee less sweet, a nice nutty flavor. I used half and half in mine, but my DBF wanted whipped cream on  his. Thanks for posting.
This is a very good sauce, and very easy.  Loved it!!

We love mushrooms and spinach so I knew we'd love this recipe.  I used fresh mushrooms and spinach and sauted some fresh onion - with some garlic - as I've never bought canned French-fried onions and I'm not even sure if they're readily available here.  Delicious!  And very pleasingly low in calories so that it can be enjoyed often!  :) Thanks for sharing.

We had some baby red potatoes and garlic chives in our basket of goodies from the farmers market. A great way to use both. We love garlic so we used the garlic salt and pepper grinder instead of plain table salt. Served as a side to grilled chicken and Italian green beans.

Yum!!! I blended 1 banana with 1 cup of spring water in my Vitamix. This is delicious! I first had "banana juice" in the Dominican Republic, and this could be it. Great way to kick start my diet, too! Thanks!

I made these for Valentine's Day, and served with ice cream and hot fudge sauce. So chewy and chocolatey. My favorite Valentine's dessert! I sprinkled some sea salt on top, right before they were done baking..delicious!

Let me start by saying I'm a seasoned baker...I baked 4 dozen cupcakes yesterday, two of which were this recipe.  The cupcakes didn't dome - and as I filled the cupcakes fairly full the flat muffin top cracked and broke and fell off after taking the cupcakes out of the muffin tin.  Also - they were hard to get out of the muffin tin (used papers - didn't grease).  So, the cupcakes, while flavorful were ugly and basically falling apart.  The other frosting recipe I made started with two sticks of soft butter + 5 C powdered sugar.  Many of the reviews discussed too much sugar in the frosting.  Would consider / suggest starting with two sticks of room temp butter - and then adding 4 - 5 C powdered sugar... that might fix the frosting situation ... also because I felt that there wasn't enough frosting - used a bag to pipe it on.  Needed more frosting to cover and hide the falling apart muffin tops...   While I was super excited to make a cupcake out of Guinness and frost with baileys butter cream - I'm disappointed in the results and will either need to find a new recipe or tweak this one.  So confused about the other so favorable reviews...  Now - the super important part - they do taste very good. If you look at the pictures,  mine are the ones that look ugly... ;)

We enjoyed this nearly fat free gravy with a whole lot of onions. I did feel it needed some pepper. The rosemary was nice. It would be so much nicer with the onions fried first but this suited my diet better. My husband thought adding in some mushrooms would take it over the top but they, alas, would also need to be fried. With all that said, we did enjoy the treat of having gravy and not feeling guilty about it.;) Thanks for sharing your recipe. Made for ZWT - Xtra Hot Dishes.

Fantastic mashed potatoes.  This makes mashed potatoes much less ho-hum and yet doesn't take a whole lot more effort.  I made this just as written, using an extra sharp white cheddar.  I doubled the recipe and I'm so glad that I did.  I may have to make even more next time.  Thanx for sharing!

I did not have shallots and used chopped onions, which look like mushrooms in the photos!! :-) Thanks!!

Reduced to 2 servings and made for lunch today. Very rich and thick. I will be baking extra potatoes every once in a while so I can make this again. Thanks for posting Nancy. Made for Pick A Chef Spring 2011.

Thinking to give some of this as gifts, I made 1/2 the recipe and can hardly believe my taste buds.  It's wonderful!!!!  I've had it on a turkey burger, on crackers, and on a spoon.  I also mixed 1/2 Tbls of it into 1/2 lb of ground beef and had the best beef patty ever!  Thank you so much.  Those who receive this at Christmas are going to go nuts over it!
This was a big hit.  The only thing I did differently as to add extra Tobasco.  We love it spicy!
Great selection of flavors. This was very tasty in our Smothered Cube Steak recipe.
This was a wonderfully dense and moist cake!  Perfect servings for 2.  Hubby and I devoured this after our dinner.  Made for ZWT5, thanks for the great recipe!!

I made this for Cinco de Mayo, and it was very good!  I was curious about the mint and margarita/lime combo, but it turned out to be something that my roommates and I really liked.  Thanks for the twist on the traditional margarita!

Delicious! I followed the directions exactly. We loved it. Thank you for posting.

Made as posted except I parboiled the potatoes for about six minutes earlier in the day to give them a head start on the cooking time. Just wrapped them in paper towels and put in the fridge to cool. I used Greek seasoning from the recipe #61579, and it worked great! I can get yummy grilled potatoes without using all that butter, who knew? Will definitely make these again, thanks so much! Oh, and they were done in just under thirty minutes.
Seemed to do a job job on the stuck on stuff but left a haze that took several wipes to get rid of and lots of elbow grease. Did I use too much baking soda?

Mmmm. This made for a delicious afternoon treat. I thought the coffee flavor to be subtle yet noticeable. I may have to make this one of my regular weekend treats!  Garnished with whipped cream and chocolate covered coffee beans. Made in memory of Jim.

While I liked this dish, the beans were a weird addition for our family.  All of the other textures seemed to go together, but then you would get a bean and it seemed out of place.  The taste was good, but I think I will omit the beans next time.  Thanks for posting!

What a fabulous recipe.....I am no scone baker, but these little lovelies came out beautifully!<br/>So light and fluffy, but full of flavour!<br/>I grated half of my cheese, and cubed the other half...the grated to distribute throughout the mixture a little more evenly, and the cubed for that extra cheesy punch every now and then.<br/>Fresh garlic chives from the garden complimented it perfectly.<br/>I used the trusty KitchenAid, to bring it all together, adding around another 2-3 tbsp. cream to the dough, top get it all to stick together.<br/>I threw it straight onto the silicone paper lined baking sheet, and patted it into shape on there, moving it around to prevent it sticking as I did so.<br/>I baked for just under 20 minutes in a fan forced oven, and the results were absolutely wonderful.<br/>DH is loving them with soup for his lunches at work, and I am loving them just as they are.<br/>Definitely a repeat recipe. Thanks Annacia!<br/>Made for PRMR.

Not sure if this is authentic or not, but it really doesn't matter.  It was good and I'll definitely keep making this.  I much prefer to make my own spice mixes since most of the store bought mixes have ingredients in them that I can't have or don't want to have.  Thanks for posting this.

I have used this method for a very long time. With, our ultra pasteurized cream it is the only way it works. I would like to add a hint. I am able to buy a Product, called "Whip it" by Dr.Oetker. It is a German Product and when added to your cream before whipping it will keep it from breaking down. It will literaly stay stiff in your fridge for days. I buy it at World Market/Cost Plus, but have also seen it in some of our grocery stores in the baking as well as international isles.It is a small Blue and white packet with red trim. :-) If you cann't find it, add !-2T of instant Vanilla Pudding. It gives a lovely flavor and helps to stabalize it as well.You might want to leave out the vanilla and powdered sugar though..
Cut everything in half, since there's only two of us, and it worked out fine. I added a small can of sweet peas and about half a cup of chopped celery. An excellent, tasty dish. Thanks for sharing.

Yummy chocolate in a pinch! Simple ingredients and perfect for late night cravings! I overcooked this I think so it was tough and brownie-like. I made 1/2 recipe for the small mugs we have, and didn't decrease the time enough. Will definitely try again. Great chocolate flavor, I liked the added chocolate chips.
Really tasty combination of flavors and easy to prepare.  The family loved it!  Another for the favorites file!  Made for Pink Panthers on the Prowl for ZWT9.

5 stars is not enough. My children  loved this, even the spicy sauce. Next time I will double the sauce, there was not enough. They thought they were at a restaurant ... Well, sort off lol Made for the AUS/NZ Swap # 42
Simplicity is the best.

Followed the directions pretty exactly with a touch extra green beans and feta.  We really enjoyed this!  I used the oven method, baking for 20 minutes, and then I let the packets rest a bit while I finished everything else.  Made for ZWT6 Zingo for the Whine and Cheese gang.

My husband loves to mix corn with his mashed potatoes, it's one of his very favorite things, so this recipe was well liked! We loved the sweetness the corn gave to dish. I used white corn, so it doesn't show up too well in the picture, but I pureed half of it with the onions and put the other half of whole kernels in. I did make more potatoes than called for in the recipe. This is going into my keeper file. Thanks, Karen! (SWT)

This is a very good marinade, but we will be making some alterations next time we make it, and we WILL make it again! We would like some salt and a more assertive amount of cinnamon in it, but the harissa and orange is what makes it delicious. We have some extra marinade to try on some fish later in the week. It's not too spicy, so give it a try, you'll like it! We had it with a Moroccan couscous salad and Recipe #493013.

This was so aromitc, when I was baking it in the oven, I almost didn't want the cooking to end. But it turned out really good. All the spices blended really well together, and nothing was overpowering.

I love this recipe. I used Southern Pepper Sauce in place of the Balsamic Vinegar and it went perfect. I think next time I will fry some Bacon and use some of the Bacon fat in place of the Olive Oil and add some of the Bacon Crumbles in with it like some people do with Greens. I know that is not the healthiest for you but I it would go well. Thanks again for a keeper.

Thanks to My-3-Chefs June 2012 I picked this recipe to try.

This was a nice corn muffin mix. For us we felt it needed something to it. On my second attemp on this recipe I chose to add maple syrup which made out turn our better.
Great idea! I've used the cold oven method before with a rack although often that comes out a bit too crunchy. This was an ideal in-between and certainly makes a lot less mess.
Tasty dish! I parboiled the potatoes first, to reduce the baking time by about half.

Yummo!  The flavours all worked well together and the chicken was outstanding.  I marinated the chicken overnight and since we love mushrooms I used the mushrooms.  Thanks for posting your recipe Leggy Peggy.

Nice ribs.  Very easy recipe.  The flavors work nicely together.  I just had a problem with getting the sauce to glaze.  I don't know why.  But I still spooned the sauce over the meat and enjoyed.  I will definitely try this again to get the glaze.  Made for ZWT 6.

I used the yellow can of El Pato tomato sauce (almost 8 oz can) which has chilies in it. I don't eat very spicy food & the heat level for me was mildly warm...hotter than green chilies but nice. Absolutely magnificent.  I cooked mine for 4 hours.  I covered it with tin foil for the last hour of cooking.  It is devine.  There is nothing else to say.  Thanks French Tart.

Used Heinz veg baked beans over 2 slices of homemade white bread.  Also fried up a couple of eggs to go alongside.  Love the yolk and beans together.  Topped mine with a little HP sauce.  Made for PAC fall 2009.
We made these for our weekend breakfast and they turned out delicious! Quick and easy to make, with a nice thick batter. Thanks for sharing! Made for Susie's World Tour 2018.
Flavor was great, but I forgot to put in the lettuce, so I unrolled the tortilla to stick in the lettuce and that didn't work too well! I'll pay more attention next time!! See... Made for Think Pink

Made it this morning and I practically inhaled half the thing!  The sugar was so right on target and it tasted excellent right out of the oven.  And so easy to make!  Thanks for sharing.  BTW, I made this because of the lovely picture you posted on the photo forum that just said to me make me you will not be sorry!  And it was true!
This was VERY good.  I used sliced smoked sausage.  I will make this over and over since it was soo easy.  Made for ZWT for the Golden Gourmets
Hi, thanks for this amazing recipe. I think I might add a bit more sugar as I needed more sweetness, and add a bit of cinnamon just for the flavor profile. Thank you!

This was such a simple yet tasty soup. The broth is so tasty, I'm so glad I tried it. I topped ours with some leftover cubed beef and sliced button mushrooms, and it was really good (even tough those ingredients don't photograph very well). Thanks, Nif. Made for SWT 2018 (Hawaii).

This is delicious! The seasoning is wonderful, though if I get in that curry mood, I may make it with a bit of curry powder as well. The green onions at the end are a superb touch, too, adding a little touch of freshness to the dish.

The 5th star comes from my 5 year old, who was disappointed when the pan was emptied because he *needed* more! All of the meat eaters in the house enjoyed this very much, and I loved hearing DH's contented sigh at the end of the meal! Made for ZWT 9, for a fellow Gourmet Goddess!

WOW!!!!!!  This was so good!!!!!!  Lots of flavor. Used soy sauce with less sodium.  Also used  cinnamon applesauce since I didn't have any apple juice. Yummy dish!  I added half a chopped purple onion and used chicken broth.  Served it as a side dish with seasoned chicken thighs and avocado slices.

Can't believe I forgot to rate this! This recipe is wonderful. Used it on WW & now low carb as well. I used bagged shredded 3 color coleslaw, and added some matchstick carrots, then doubled the dressing!! YUM!

Being Brits, we don't know about cornbread but this was delicious! Added more paprika & oregano as we love the tastes, and served with fresh green beans. Many thanks!

These are so good and easy.  My teenage son wanted to help with dinner and this was his project.  He couldn't believe how easy and we all thought they were delicious. (I used dried parsley - about a tablespoon in each pie plate)

This is a wonderful soup!! All who tried it raved. I made exactly as the recipe was written with one exception, I used fat free half and half. It turned out wonderful. Thank you Anne for posting this recipe!

This was, simply put, divine. I am SO glad I took the plunge! We halved the recipe (just the two of us) with no difficulty. We added plenty of extra Parmesan for garnish, but aside from that, this needed no tweaking at all. It's very good - I grilled my hamburger brushed with this paste, and it was awesome!  I agree with littlemafia - I love how you get the flavors from everything in this paste.  Thank you so much for sharing!

This was super simple and good.  I also did not drain the tomatoes. I thought the mustard level was fine, it gave the dish a nice tang for my tastes.  I also used cavatappi pasta rather than penne as again, I used what I had on hand.  Very yummy.  Made for PAC Spring '11.

Hi Starrynews, WOW, were these awesome! I love Deviled Eggs and so we tried them one day when there were visitors here at the home. I used 1/2 garlic & herb flavor cheese and 1/2 Boursin pepper with a small shot of hot sauce. They were very creamy & looked lovely! I used a pastry bag on some and a plastic bag with a slit on others - not one person noticed the wrapping, they went for the gusto! Also added some chopped parsely for color - thank you Starrynews for a wonderful recipe, Manami ;)

What more can I say than THANK YOU!!  This was fast and easy to make. basil from the garden freshly picked and chopped, organic chicken, a side salad, and of course a glass of wine. A really lovely meal, quick and easy thanks for posting this Pat,

This was quick and easy to throw together and comes from one of my all time favorite cookbooks.  I followed the recipe exactly and felt it was a bit on the bland side.  Next time I'll take more liberties with the spices for sure.  Good basic recipe to play with though.  Thanks for posting!

Wonderful combination of flavours. The only time-consuming part of this recipe is roasting the peppers but that can be done ahead of time. I sliced the roll-ups into 3/4 inch slices for appetizer servings. Thank you for a repeater!

I made this as a soup for the Inn I cook at and it was very well received, all the staff demanded it for lunch!! (Customers loved it too), thank you for posting this recipe will be made again. Made for ZWT6  challenge.

We loved this!  Made it for our baked fries.  I did 1/2 a recipe and it was enough for the 4 of us and 4 taters and still had a little extra, too. :)  Thanks for posting!
These were excellent and easy. I added white chocolate chips...Yummy.

Scrumptious! Everyone enjoyed this! I used non-stick spray instead of butter when cooking the eggs. Didn't have onions on hand, so I steamed frozen mixed veggie and added to the wok. Very nice flavor.  The marinade reminded me a lot of Yoshi's.

These beans had lots of flavor even though there were not many ingredients. I used the sour cream option, and cooked the onions in garlic infused olive oil instead of the butter. Also, I added some salt and fresh cracked black pepper. **Made for Susie's World Tour 2018**

So tasty and healthy, too!  As I usually do when slow cooking pork, to get a richer color I brown the meat in grapeseed oil first but will try skipping that step next time. Instead of adding individually, I combined soup mix with water, wine and less-sodium soy sauce and poured mixture over pork then added garlic on top and sprinkled with pepper. Threw in some fingerling potatoes the last hour.  Excellent!

I cooked a 3 pound pork loin and it just ended up being so tender and just shredded to pieces with two forks. Only reason I didn't give this 5 stars is I thought it was lacking some spices. A nice rub on the loin I think would of really put this over the edge for us.

First thing you should know is that this makes a lot!  Perfect for parties cuz everyone will love it.  I used whole wheat pasta(accidental purchase) and let pasta chill in fridge for two hours and then finished the sauce and veggies. Don't like napa cabbage so I used green cabbage instead.  Very good!!!

Well, this could never replace my regular chicken and dumplings recipe, nor did I find it comparable to "Grandma's"--but it is a very good crock pot recipe.  Very quick and easy recipe for those days when you just need some comfort food.  I added a little extra water and was glad I did because the biscuits absorbed a lot of the liquid.  I would definitely make this recipe again.
My mushroom were big so I cut them in half Very nice Id make these again Made for Susies world tour 2018

A definite keeper!  Quick to put together and very tasty. This will be going into our weeknight rotation!  Thanks for sharing.

This was a good salad. I've been on such a beet kick lately, just love beets in salad! I also love feta and avocado so this sounded like the perfect salad for me. Thanks for sharing a great, easy recipe many people can benefit from!!!

Delicious. I made this the other night and it was wonderful. I never had homemade tomato soup before and it was so worth it. I made it exactly as posted...wouldn't change a thing.
Aussie Swap #85: Outstanding!! This dish highlights one of my favorite veggies perfectly and the savory feta cheese - YUM!! We loved this!
Awesome pancakes! Served mine with blueberries. I look forward to a second round with strawberries from the garden. Thanks!  Made for the I Recommend tag game.

I made this recipe to go with a turkey sandwich recipe I wanted to try also..OMG this was so good the sandwich was fab..I made to loaves,one I gave to my daughter..I used 1/4 tsp total ,used my KA for mixing and kneading otherwise followed recipe exactly...What a great sandwich bread,or even with a hearty soup..I will definitely be making this again. I recommend trying #116193 bacon turkey bravo to go with this bread, delish..Thank U......

Great cookie! I echo the other reviewers about the dough being a little dry, but a drop or two of water did the trick. My house is warm and that's probably the reason. I bought a variety of kisses, and Hugs, so they were all different. My favorite is the Kisses with the cherry in them, OMG, they are so good! Thanks Dreamer for a great recipe! Made for "24 Days of Cookies" at KK's forum!

Wow! This recipe is simple, fast to prepare, and good golly delicious. I use corn tortillas.
Love it, Love it!!

This dish is going straight to my favourite folder. I made two thirds of the recipe, and added just a tiny bit of sugar as my beef got a little bit burnt. My children loved it. Thank you so much for posting.

AMAZING!!  This salad is a treat to eat.  I used navel oranges as that's what I had, dried cherries, and toasted pecans.  It is a VERY sweet salad, and I think next time  I'll leave the brown sugar out.  I may play with the amount of sugar in the dressing as well simply to make it healthier~~but I could literally drink the dressing it's so yummy!!  Thanks SO MUCH for sharing!  :O)

PAC Spring 2008 ~ What's not to like!?  As I do not own a blender, I doubled the amounts on everything and shook with ice.  I sprinkled a bit of sweetened chocolate powder on top.  I was afraid the tequila was going to be overpowering in this but it was not.  I will be making this one often!

very nice!!!  i have made this many times to go along with my own copycat chicken mcnugget recipe and fries.  this is a keeper for sure, and very easy to whip together with help from the microwave !!  thanks for posting!

Wonderful.  My DH, the meat eater, loved this.  I spread a little of the enchilada sauce on the bottom of the pan before I put the enchiladas in the pan.  Added the sauce on the top and then sprinkled 2% shredded Mexican Blend cheese on the top.  So so good.  I am moving this into my "Tried and True" file.

Winner winner chicken dinner! This is fancy enough to serve guests and easy enough to devote your time to other side dishes. I made the mushroom/wine topper and the only thing I'd do differently is add some cornstarch, like another reviewer, to thicken the sauce. I also let the chicken keep cooking on low heat while the topping prepared. My chicken was thick and I didn't want to take the chance of having it not be done completely.

4 stars! These are very quick and easy to put together. The batter is quite runny so I found them sticking to the waffle iron.  They also didn't take as long to cook as other waffles do.  Next time I would probably add a bit more flour.  They had a nice flavor though, and we enjoyed them. Made and reviewed for RSC#11.

This recipe is a keeper. I heated chick peas only today with this recipe's ingredients, sans the rice and extra water of course. I also used cilantro in place of marjoram for a different flavor. I heated all of the ingredients for 15 minutes, uncovered. The chick peas were soft, had a slight orange color because of the turmeric and were delicious. Three cheers for this recipe!

Great tasting shrimp and it went so well with your glazed grilled salmon tonight. I didn't use as much red pepper flakes as called for, but the flavor was still really nice. Loved the sherry addition.

OMG, this was so good.  I couldn%u2019t find 10 count shrimp, so I used 20 count.  Shelling and butterfling the shrimp was a bit time consuming, but so well worth it.  I served at Easter dinner and it was a big success.  Thanks for posting.
wonderful, so cheesy! I especially liked it more the day after since it got creamier. Love the idea of breadcrumbs in it too. Thank you!

Followed the recipe exactly (with the exception of poppy seeds) and served with Recipe #265727.   It had a moist quick bread texture.   Not sure if it was the tomatoes I used or what but it was a little bland for our taste.   Wonder what some sun dried tomatoes might add to it.
Comfort food at it's best.  I loved this and dinner guest sopped up left over gravy with bread.  I did double the amounts of broth to make extra.  I did not do the potato step.
Loved the cola in this recipe and it tenderized the steak. Very delicious - the whole family gave it 2 thumbs way up. Great comfort food. I served it over a split baked potato. Made for ZWT 7.

A delightful, simple recipe that scores not only on taste, but also by showing how inferior store bought products are. Even the typical excuse of convenience falls by the wayside, particularly when the results are this good.

This didn't go over like I thought it would.  We didn't care for the flavor of the sauce.  I did love the spinach adding part though.  I subbed kale since my neighbor gave us a ton.  Next time I would use a different sauce - more to our liking.  I love the general idea that the recipe takes.  Thanks so much for sharing!  Made for the September 2010 Aussie/NZ recipe swap.

What a decadent cookie! I doubled my recipe completely and omitted nuts. I used half wheat/half white flour with fine results. Mine baked in about 8 minutes, so watch your time carefully. They are an absolute keeper!
This recipe is easy and delicious.  I precooked the potatoes as directed and used the cheese.  It was delicious and I plan to make these again.  Thanks for posting!

Super yummy and super easy.  I started using Zip N Steam bags about a year ago.  I use them for lots of things; potatoes, veggies, even shrimp stir fry.  Thanks so much for sharing.  Made for PRMR tag game.
This was a quick easy weeknight dinner.  I used boneless and skinless thighs and still had a fair amount of grease floating on top BUT after 6 hours on low they were still moist.  Thanks for posting.

What a yummy dish...I cooked my carrots al dente and they came out perfect once I did the sauteing for...I would say 4-5 minutes while the rest of my meal was cooking...the hubby raved about this...so that means it a repeat...made for FYC tag game...

This is a winner for sure, nice blend of flavors. I love anything with pumpkin pie spice in it. Very moist. I used 1/2 cup of brown sugar and 1/2 cup of white. I found this was not overly sweet and perfect for us. I baked it in a loaf and it took 1hr 13 minutes. I will be making these again and making the jumbo muffins. Thanks for sharing this recipe. Made for Fall PAC/09

These were WONDERFUL!! My kids, who know good cookies :), were even impressed!!  Yum, these were so delicious I could eat the whole plate of them!  A real keeper.  The only change I made was to add  little more brown sugar, in place of some of the regular sugar called for.  Made for ZWT4 Zingo for the CAFE ZMAKK Gypsies team!
Delicious and easy.  I cut in half for 4 servings.  If making for a party next time, I'll try the other reviewers' suggestion for putting in the crockpot to keep warm.

This was so easy to prepare, we were having roast for dinner, and quickly prepared the sprouts and just popped them in the oven with everything else. DS commented on how good the sprouts were, with everyone else agreeing. The flavours just go so well together and the sprouts were just perfectly cooked.<br/>Wonderful recipe for the brussel sprout lovers of this world.
Michelle, This is a FantasticChocolateSauce recipe. We loved the smooth consistency and rich flavor.. Used it on vanilla ice cream...  Putting this in my use again soon file..
Yummy topping for a burger, even without a bun!  I used fresh mushrooms instead of canned and loved the topping!
